name: 100 Sails Restaurant & Bar
description: 100 Sails is the main restaurant of the Prince Waikīkī hotel, looking out over the Ala Wai small-boat harbour at the western edge of Waikīkī. Its stated position is that mocktails belong on the same level as the cocktails, and the kitchen backs that with method rather than assertion: the zero-proof drinks are built on house-made syrups and local ingredients, running to ginger lemongrass, hibiscus and ube. Ube — the purple yam that anchors a great deal of Filipino cooking in Hawaiʻi — is an unusual thing to put in a drink and gives it colour and a mild nutty sweetness. Mocktails are included in the daily happy hour rather than excluded from it.

name: 16-Bit Bar+Arcade
address: 110 E New York St, Indianapolis, IN 46204
description: 16-Bit is a 21-and-over retro arcade bar on East New York Street downtown, where the cabinet games are free to play and the money is made at the bar. That model happens to make it one of the easier nights out in Indianapolis for someone who is not drinking, because the reason to be there is the arcade rather than the round. The non-alcoholic list is longer than most bars manage and every drink is named in the same register as the cocktails: Kissed By A Rose is built on Seedlip Garden 108 with hibiscus, lemon, rose and mint, Gym Class Zero runs desert pear with lime and tonic, and Pinky and the Brain, Optimus Prime and Lisa Simpson fill out the simpler end.

name: 1833 Craft
address: 1398 S 1100 E, Salt Lake City, UT 84105
hours: Temporarily closed for summer renovations; the bar says it reopens in the fall (checked 5 October 2026). Normal hours Thu-Fri 5pm-10pm; other times by special request
description: Closed for renovations since summer 2026; the bar says it will reopen in the fall, so check before you go. Salt Lake City's dedicated non-alcoholic speakeasy, opened in December 2024 inside a restored century-old Sugar House home known as The Eclipse House and run by sibling team Matthew and Kelly LaPlante. The entire menu is zero-proof — "0% Alcohol, 100% Heart" — built by co-owner and lead bartender Matthew, a former Salt Lake Tribune reporter who quit drinking but never left bar culture, with his sister Kelly, a designer, styling the room as a forest-green, 1920s-inspired lounge. The duo have developed 50-plus craft NA cocktails on premium spirits like Lyre's, Dhōs, Trejo's and Kentucky 74, finished with herbs from their own basement hydroponic garden. The name nods to 1833, the year of the Latter-day Saint "Word of Wisdom," and because nothing on the menu contains alcohol, no ID is required — a genuine cocktail experience for people in recovery, designated drivers, never-drinkers, and the sober-curious.

name: 1923 Prohibition Bar
address: 3930 S Las Vegas Blvd, Suite 200B, Las Vegas, NV 89119
description: 1923 Prohibition Bar is a hidden, 1920s-style speakeasy tucked inside The Shoppes at Mandalay Place at Mandalay Bay on the Las Vegas Strip, reached through a concealed door and known for its bourbon-and-burlesque atmosphere with live music, piano players, and weekend entertainment. While the menu is whisky- and cocktail-forward, the bar keeps a dedicated "Zero Proof" section for non-drinkers, anchored by Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits. The signature zero-proof builds are the Zer-Old Fashioned (made with Lyre's American Malt), Summer on the Wagon (Lyre's Pink Gin), and the Kats Meow. For non-alcoholic beer drinkers, the bar pours Lagunitas IPNA NA on draft. The speakeasy is open daily and offers a genuine cocktail-lounge experience without requiring guests to drink alcohol. A second 1923 location operates at The Venetian's Grand Canal Shoppes, but the Mandalay Bay original is the flagship.

name: 1Watson
description: 1Watson is the rooftop bar at the AC Hotel San Antonio Riverwalk on Soledad Street, and its named non-alcoholic drinks are the Pina Breezy and the Spicy Pal No Ma — the latter a zero-proof play on a Paloma, which is the right instinct in Texas, where grapefruit and salt are already the local drinking grammar. It runs late for a hotel rooftop, to midnight midweek and 1am at weekends, and adds a third downtown rooftop option for anyone not drinking, in a district where visitors substantially outnumber locals. Weekend brunch service from 10:30am extends the window further, and it is a few blocks from both other rooftops in this guide.

name: 20 Stories
address: No.1 Spinningfields, 1 Hardman Square, Spinningfields, Manchester M3 3EB
description: 20 Stories is a glamorous rooftop restaurant and cocktail bar nineteen floors above No.1 Spinningfields, wrapping an elegant dining room, a statement illuminated bar and an expansive terrace planted with silver birch trees around a firepit, with 360-degree views over the Manchester skyline. It is the flagship of The Evolv Collection — sister to 14 Stories in London and 24 Stories in Birmingham — was named Best Restaurant in Manchester at the British Restaurant Awards, and its menus are led by executive head chef Daniel Scott on regional Northwest produce. The non-alcoholic side is genuine: a varied alcohol-free spirits list built on brands like Caleño and Everleaf, plus a dedicated zero-proof section of the cocktail menu using the same house syrups, with a Mediterranean and tropical bent. It is a rare high-end Manchester rooftop where a non-drinker gets a proper printed list rather than a token mocktail.

name: 2nd Shift Brewing
description: 2nd Shift Brewing became the first brewery on The Hill, St. Louis' storied Italian neighborhood, when founders Steve and Libby Crider moved their 2009-vintage operation from New Haven, Missouri into an 18,000-square-foot warehouse in December 2016. Alongside the craft beer, the taproom pours Busy Bees N/A, a house line of non-alcoholic drinks crafted and packaged at the brewery: hop water, root beer, grape soda made with real cane sugar, and tangerine or unflavored sparkling water. With Central State Sandwiches in-house, dogs welcome inside and on the patio, and kids allowed with adult supervision, it's a laid-back neighborhood hangout where, as the brewery puts it, there's 'an option for everyone.'

name: 330 Main
description: 330 Main is a non-alcoholic bar and coffee house on East Main Street in Chattanooga's Southside, owned and run by a husband-and-wife team, and it introduced the city to kava cocktails. The drinks list is built on kava extract in place of alcohol — cocktails and shots rather than the ceremonial shell-and-bowl service most kava bars offer — alongside yaupon tea carbonated and poured on draft, plus rotating house creations. The female owner's Filipino heritage shapes the food and drink; her partner came up through craft coffee, craft beer, cannabis and hospitality across the Southeast, and created Kavanooga, a kava tincture developed locally. Guests may bring in food from neighbouring businesses.

name: 36 Below

hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 4pm-12am; Fri 4pm-1am; Sat 3pm-1am; Sun 3pm-11pm
description: A hidden underground speakeasy beneath Sip Coffee & Beer Garage in the Arcadia Lite neighborhood of Phoenix, 36 Below pairs a transportive, candlelit room with a dedicated 'Zero Proof' section of non-alcoholic glasses built with the same care as the cocktails. The menu rotates around immersive themes; on the current Midnight in Paris list every zero-proof drink is a $14 alcohol-free twin of a signature cocktail — Kiwi's Nest, Château de Chambord, Epernay, Monet's Garden, and Palais Garnier — built on N/A spirits, house cordials and foams. Earlier spirit-free builds such as the Artemis, Earth, and Foam on the Rim retired with the previous theme. DiningOut Phoenix listed it among the metro bars worth visiting specifically for a mocktail in May 2026. Entry is via the coffee shop above; reservations are advisable at weekends.

name: 3rd Space Kava
description: 3rd Space Kava on South University Drive is a fully alcohol-free bar open from noon until 2am, and to 3am on Friday and Saturday, built around pool, board games, gaming stations and a dense events calendar — karaoke nights, Guitar Hero tournaments and Magic: The Gathering play on the first and third Wednesday of the month. Dogs are welcome. Traditional kava comes as noble-root shells at three strengths: the lighter White Sand for sipping, the nuttier King's Kava, and the Ceremonial shell, the strongest of the three, plus a house watermelon Kokkaido shell made fresh daily and a concentrated kavalactone shot called The Roman. IMPORTANT: a large part of this menu is kratom, not kava — six kratom cocktails plus kratom shots, sodas and seltzers, all restricted to 21 and over. Kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries dependence risk that kava does not; order deliberately.

name: 4 Hands Brewing Co.
description: 4 Hands Brewing Co. has anchored St. Louis' LaSalle Park neighborhood since 2011, and its lineup now includes three house-brewed non-alcoholic beers: NA City Wide Hoppy Pale, NA Full Life Lager and NA Incarnation, a Mosaic-hopped IPA — all under 0.5% ABV. The tasting room at 1220 S. 8th Street backs them up with a mocktail list built on zero-proof spirits, Athletic Brewing Lite and local Excel sodas, plus food from Hi-Pointe Drive-In's kitchen and an upstairs arcade with Skee-Ball. City Wide, the brewery's civic flagship, donates $1 from every case sold to local nonprofit partners — a program that has generated close to half a million dollars.

name: 4 Noses Brewing Company
description: 4 Noses Brewing Company runs a Denver taproom on Dahlia Street in Northeast Park Hill alongside its original Broomfield brewery, and in 2025 it launched Camp Zero, its first non-alcoholic beer. The brewery describes Camp Zero as "our easy-drinking adventure into alcohol-free beer", crafted with full flavour and made for trail breaks and mellow nights; the second batch is a tangerine guava blonde that Westword characterised as brewed with real fruit, lightly tart and plenty refreshing. Camp Zero is poured at the taproom and stocked by other Denver bars — Briar Common in Jefferson Park keeps it on its guest non-alcoholic can list. The Dahlia Street room opens from noon or early afternoon daily and closes by 9pm, and is family-friendly.

description: 8th Day is a small-batch distillery, bottle shop and cocktail bar in the Circle City Industrial Complex on the Near Eastside, run by Matt and Jaime Lamping. They signed the lease in 2015 and began filling bourbon barrels, launched gin and rum into Indianapolis bars and shops, and opened the bottle shop and cocktail bar to the public in 2018. The room is deliberately living-room-ish, with a new local artist's work shown every quarter and regular pop-ups with other Indianapolis businesses. Mocktails sit on the rotating seasonal menu alongside the cocktails as a matter of course — the Overalls. is lemon with a lavender-thyme simple syrup and soda water.

name: 967 Coffee Co.
description: 967 Coffee Co. is a Yemeni coffeehouse on Alpharetta Highway in Roswell, named for Yemen's international dialling code. It opened during Ramadan in early 2025 and is fully alcohol-free. The trading hours make it one of the latest-running rooms of any kind in north Fulton County: 7am to midnight Sunday through Thursday, and 7am to 2am on Friday and Saturday. The drinks list runs Yemeni preparations and espresso side by side — Iced Adeni Chai and the Iced Yemeni Latte are the house pours, with qishr, Biscoff and pistachio lattes and a set of dragon fruit and strawberry refreshers filling out the board. Desserts sit alongside the coffee, and the seating is arranged for groups staying several hours rather than for takeaway trade.

name: A La Mousse
description: A La Mousse is a Chinatown dessert cafe and tea house that opens at noon and runs to eleven at night, midnight on Friday and Saturday, with no alcohol on the premises at any point. The drinks are the reason to go rather than an afterthought to the cakes: fruit teas including a mango lychee and a passion fruit peach, a pomegranate strawberry lemonade, a lemonade mint tea, and milk-foam teas built on rose and on oolong. The matcha list runs to a cherry blossom matcha latte alongside peach, coconut and almond milk versions. For a city where almost every late option has a liquor licence, a Chinatown room serving properly built tea drinks until midnight is a genuinely useful address.

name: Absinthe Brasserie & Bar
description: Absinthe Brasserie & Bar has been the pre-theatre anchor of Hayes Valley for decades, a French-Californian brasserie on the corner of Hayes and Gough with a long marble bar and a classics-heavy cocktail list. Its alcohol-free drinks are printed under their own heading, n/a cocktails, and are all $12 against $16 to $18 for the full-proof list. Four are named: Coda Leger, built on pomegranate with lemon, lime, vanilla and seltzer; Mister Rogers, a lighter build of lime, mint and ginger beer; Absinthe Lemonade, made with lemon, cranberry and ginger; and Bright Red Shirts, which uses a house non-alcoholic Campari-style syrup with orange, lemon and seltzer to reproduce a bitter aperitivo. The kitchen serves lunch and dinner Wednesday through Sunday.

name: ABV
description: ABV is a Mission District cocktail bar that opened in summer 2014, founded by Erik Reichborn-Kjennerud, Ryan Fitzgerald, and Todd Smith (a founding Bourbon & Branch bartender). It was named Imbibe Magazine's 2015 Bar of the Year and ranked #39 in the inaugural North America's 50 Best Bars (2022), the only San Francisco bar on that list. The menu is organized by base spirit, with dedicated "LOW ABV" and "0% ABV" sections that make the no/low offering a standing, structured part of the program rather than an afterthought. The non-alcoholic cocktails ($14) center on a house "n/a aperitif" and bright, fresh builds — the N/A Negroni (n/a aperitif, charred grapefruit tonic), Flightless Bird, Green Dream (tarragon, lemon, ginger, tonic), and Jumpstart (carrot, ginger, turmeric, lemon, soda) — alongside Lagunitas Hop Water and IPNA. ABV makes drinks to order and runs a late kitchen until midnight.

name: Accent Wine Parlor
description: Accent Wine Parlor is a wine shop and tasting room in the historic Citizens Building on North High Street downtown, opened in August 2021 by sommelier Gregory Stokes with chef Joshua Dalton of Veritas. It works as both retail and a room to sit and drink in, running daily tastings, weekly classes and local delivery across the Columbus metro alongside bottles from $10 to collector prices. For non-drinkers the relevant part is a maintained non-alcoholic collection rather than a token bottle or two — alcohol-removed still and sparkling wines from producers including Leitz, and Copenhagen Sparkling Tea, the Danish tea-based alternative that behaves like wine at the table rather than like a soft drink. The shop also makes its own syrups. Open Tuesday to Saturday afternoons and evenings.

name: Adam Reid at The French
address: The Midland Hotel, 16 Peter Street, Manchester M60 2DS
hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed-Thu 6pm-8:30pm; Fri 5pm-8:30pm; Sat 4pm-8:30pm; Sun closed
description: Adam Reid at The French is one of Manchester city centre's most decorated tasting-menu restaurants, set in the Edwardian dining room of the Midland Hotel on Peter Street. Chef-patron Adam Reid, a BBC Great British Menu winner, took over the room in 2016 following Simon Rogan's departure and has built a reputation for bold, playful modern-British cooking rooted in Northern ingredients; the restaurant holds four AA Rosettes and a listing in the Michelin Guide, and its courses are finished and explained tableside by the kitchen team. It earns a place in a non-alcoholic directory for its drinks programme: alongside the traditional wine flight, it offers a full non-alcoholic flight designed to pair with each course, positioned as a direct alternative rather than a token substitute, and the sommelier team will build bespoke soft or zero-proof pairings on request. It is one of the few tasting-menu destinations in the city where the alcohol-free option is a designed part of the experience.

name: ADRIFT Mare
description: ADRIFT Mare is a Mediterranean restaurant and cocktail bar from Michelin-starred chef David Myers, perched on the 25th floor of Hotel AKA Brickell with terrace views over Biscayne Bay. The kitchen draws on the French Riviera, the Balearic islands, Italian produce, Levantine hospitality, and the Greek isles, serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner daily. The cocktail program was built by acclaimed bartenders Moe Aljaff and Juliette Larrouy, whose résumés include Himkok and Two Schmucks. Its zero-proof side is small but real: alcohol-free cocktails such as Chai Life and Palm Paradise lean on spice, citrus, and freshness, alongside Lyre's-based non-alcoholic aperitivo classics that mirror the bar's spritz-forward sensibility. Resident magazine featured the mocktails in its 2025 Dry January roundup. It's a polished hotel-rooftop option for a sit-down dinner with credible non-alcoholic choices rather than a dedicated NA bar.

name: Adrift Tiki Bar

description: Adrift Tiki Bar is an immersive Polynesian and Caribbean-inspired tiki bar on South Broadway in Denver, established in 2011 and bought in 2016 by current owner Loren Martinez, who also runs Little Man Ice Cream. The room is a full tropical build: a totem-pole-flanked bar, pufferfish lights, and an outdoor patio with a firepit, with a kitchen turning out spice-route Polynesian and Caribbean plates to match the rum-forward list. The menu carries a dedicated "On Dry Land (No ABV)" section — Anchored Tides (ginger, lime, demerara, Leopold Bros non-alcoholic aperitif), the N/A Mai Tai and N/A Painkiller (both built on Ritual N/A Rum), and the P.O.G. of passion fruit, orange and guava — plus a Mash Gang non-alcoholic IPA. A separate "In Shallow Water" section lists low-ABV cocktails for guests moderating rather than abstaining. Vince Polizzi is bar manager.

The bar runs a dedicated "Spirit-Free" section on its printed drinks menu, with four named, ingredient-listed alcohol-free cocktails served alongside the full bar list. Executive Chef Binit Pandey has described the kitchen's unhurried, technique-forward approach as built for the room's views.

name: Affäre
description: Affäre is a modern German restaurant at 1911 Main Street in the Crossroads Arts District, opened in May 2012 by chef Martin Heuser and his wife Katrin Heuser, who moved to Kansas City from Germany in 2007. Martin learned to cook at his family's restaurant Im Steinhaus in Bonn — a 15th-century stone building his family has owned for nearly two hundred years — earned a Master Chef Diploma and worked in two Michelin-starred kitchens; Katrin completed her sommelier diploma through the International Sommelier Guild in Calgary. The Pitch, reviewing it two months after opening, described a menu of small and exquisitely presented plates which arrive at the table arranged like tiny sculptures. The dining room occupies the cavernous former Bar Natasha space. Dinner runs Tuesday to Sunday, 4.45pm to 9pm, closed Mondays, with a children's menu and high chairs available. Affäre keeps non-alcoholic house drinks and a non-alcoholic beer alongside its wine list, but does not publish its drinks menu online, so ask what is being poured.

name: Agency
description: Agency is the nation's first fully hybrid cocktail lounge, set inside the restored Dubbel Dutch Hotel in Milwaukee's Yankee Hill / Cathedral Square area. Every drink on the menu can be ordered full-proof or completely spirit-free — guests flip a two-sided coaster (gold side up for non-alcoholic, black for alcoholic) to signal their choice, so ordering a zero-proof round never requires a conversation. Founded by Ryan Castelaz of Discourse Coffee, the bar was a 2025 James Beard Award finalist for Best New Bar — one of only five nationwide. Because the spirit-free and spirited builds are made with equal craft, it is one of the strongest zero-proof-friendly rooms in the country.

name: Aguasal by José Andrés
description: Aguasal by José Andrés opened in June 2025 inside the Andaz Miami Beach in Mid-Beach, the first of the José Andrés Group's planned dining takeover of the oceanfront resort. Named for agua salada (Spanish for saltwater), the all-day coastal-Mediterranean restaurant draws on Mallorca and Mykonos, with dishes like Kumamoto oysters, mussels saganaki, and whole snapper served indoors or on the terrace. The bar program carries a small but intentional zero-proof selection: two named spirit-free cocktails — the Cardamom & Ginger (cardamom, citrus, sakura, ginger beer) and the Mediterranean Milk Punch (lavender-cardamom tea, pomegranate, fenugreek, mint, dairy-clarified) — alongside Athletic Brewing's Free Wave non-alcoholic Hazy IPA, fresh juices, Per'la coffee, and Art of Tea infusions. A separate upstairs bar, Bar Centro, extends the group's spirit-free options. Aguasal sits steps from the sand on Collins Avenue.

name: Albert's Schloss
description: Albert's Schloss is a cavernous Bavarian bierkeller and cook-haus on the ground floor of Manchester's Grade II-listed Albert Hall, pouring tank-fresh European lager beneath near-constant live music, cabaret and its trademark 'Bongdays'. It is no dedicated sober bar, but it is genuinely well-versed in low and no: the fridges hold alcohol-free Paulaner Hefe Weisse and Jever Fun, alongside Hip Pop kombucha and a small named 'No Alk' list of spirit-free cocktails built on Lyre's. Open daily from 9am until 2am, it is a rare big-room party venue where a non-drinker is properly looked after rather than handed a lemonade.

name: Alcove
description: Alcove is a waterfront restaurant and bar at 50 Lovejoy Wharf in Boston's West End, a few steps from TD Garden and North Station, with a patio on the Charles River that is one of the few genuinely water-facing terraces in the neighbourhood. The kitchen runs a coastal New England menu of line-caught seafood, farm vegetables and locally sourced meats alongside an extensive wine list. The drinks menu prints a named spirit-free section holding five drinks between $11 and $13 — roughly half the price of the house cocktails — including a shandy built on Athletic Brewing's Free Wave non-alcoholic IPA that can be ordered in pitchers for four. Two non-alcoholic beers are stocked at $7.

name: Alden & Harlow
description: Alden & Harlow is chef-owner Michael Scelfo's New American restaurant at 40 Brattle Street in Harvard Square, opened in 2014 in a basement space and known for a vegetable-forward, small-plates menu and an off-menu burger that has drawn national attention. Scelfo also runs The Longfellow Bar upstairs in the same building. The bar keeps a printed Mocktails section of three house drinks, priced $9 to $10, built from the kitchen's own techniques rather than from bought-in zero-proof spirits: cold-smoked passionfruit, ube coconut water, lapsang souchong and a non-alcoholic Giffard aperitif all appear. The result is savoury and smoke-inflected rather than sweet, and reads as an extension of the kitchen rather than a bar afterthought.

name: AleSmith Brewing Company
description: AleSmith Brewing Company, founded in 1995 and owned since 2002 by Peter Zien, is one of San Diego's flagship craft breweries. Its large Miramar tasting room — a two-story space with a patio, games, and a Tony Gwynn memorabilia museum — pours the brewery's own house-brewed non-alcoholic line alongside its full beer lineup. The NA program centers on AleSmith NA IPA (tangerine and pine, under 0.5% ABV, 75 calories) and NA Speedway, a non-alcoholic take on the brewery's iconic Speedway Stout with dark chocolate, espresso, and roasted-malt notes, plus a Nelson Sauvin hop water on tap — a zero-proof, zero-calorie option. The NA IPA has earned real recognition, taking medals at the California Craft Brewers Cup and the San Diego Beer News Awards.

Its drinks list carries a standing, clearly labelled Zero-Proof section rather than a single token option, and it is one of the deeper spirit-free lists on the Strip: the Zero Royal (Lucano N/A amaro, pomegranate juice, Owen's ginger beer, lime juice), the Flora Botanica (Seedlip Grove 42, grapefruit juice, tart cherry syrup, lime juice), the St. Zita Spritz (Giffard N/A aperitif, non-alcoholic sparkling wine, soda, orange), and a Michenada built on Athletic Brewing's Atletica with michelada mix. Athletic Brewing's Free Wave hazy IPA and Atletica pour alongside them, and the same section carries a matcha green tea latte, freshly squeezed orange juice, the Garden Glow cold-pressed juice (apple, celery, cucumber, spinach, kale, parsley, ginger, lemon) and Ghirardelli hot chocolate. The restaurant serves from 7am daily through to 10pm, and to 11pm on Friday and Saturday.

name: Alibaba Lounge & Kava Bar
description: Alibaba is an alcohol-free lounge and cafe on Linebaugh Avenue that pairs a hookah programme with fruit-infused kava and an organic wellness drink list, open from noon to midnight and to 2am on Friday and Saturday. It is worth being clear about the balance: this is a hookah lounge first, and the kava is genuine but sits alongside that rather than at the centre. For anyone avoiding alcohol who wants a late, social, dressed-up room, it works — the space is clean and carefully arranged, the music is good and Thursday is Ladies Night. For anyone avoiding smoke, it will not, since hookah is the main draw and the room is not smoke-free. No alcohol is served at any point.

name: All Purpose Pizzeria (Shaw)
description: All Purpose Pizzeria is an Italian-American restaurant at 1250 9th Street NW in Shaw, opened in 2016 by chef Michael Friedman, also behind The Red Hen, and known for crunchy Jersey-style pizza, house-made charcuterie and red-sauce classics. The Shaw original anchors a small group that also includes a Capitol Riverfront outpost near Navy Yard. In January 2025 the restaurant added a dedicated dry cocktail menu at both locations, moving its non-alcoholic offer well beyond the usual sodas. The two named spirit-free drinks are The Golden Boot, made with pineapple juice, basil, lemon juice and soda, and the Positano Punch, built from pomegranate and apple with rosemary simple syrup and grapefruit bitters. It is a lively, social room that hosts a popular weekend drag brunch, and it was named to Washingtonian's 100 Very Best Restaurants 2025 at number 69.

name: Alley Brews
description: Alley Brews is a small women-owned brewery and coffee shop hidden in the alley between Tennyson and Stuart Streets in Berkeley, taken over at the end of June 2025 by longtime friends Liz Hess and Chelsea Rhoads — Rhoads helped open 4 Noses Brewing in 2014 — who rebranded it from Berkeley Alley Beer Company. The room is designed to work all day: coffee and matcha from the morning, small-batch beer and draft cocktails later, and a stated non-alcoholic line of "non-alcoholic beers, kombucha, coffee, matcha & in-house crafted mocktails". Rhoads told Westword in October 2025 that entire groups had been drinking N/A beer on a Sunday and that there was no stigma around it. Gluten-free brews are also part of the standing offer.

name: Alley Cat Lounge
description: Alley Cat Lounge is a basement cocktail bar reached from Broughton Lane, the service alley behind Savannah's main shopping street, in an 1870s brick cellar. Its menu is a newsprint broadsheet — the Alley Cat Rag — reissued in numbered editions with the whole list rewritten each time, and the bar's standing commitment is that whatever the edition, it carries a minimum of ten low- and no-alcohol cocktails alongside alcohol-free beer and cider. That is the deepest running alcohol-free selection of any licensed bar in the city. It is open from 4pm to 1am Monday through Thursday, to 2am on Friday and Saturday, and closed Sundays.

name: Alley Cat Oyster Bar
description: Alley Cat Oyster Bar is a waterfront seafood restaurant on Old River Road in the Flats East Bank, pairing New England coastal cooking with a Southern Californian lightness and panoramic views over the Cuyahoga. Its mocktails are shaken and built to order rather than pulled off a soda gun, and they are priced deliberately low: the Kitten's Pajamas, a spirit-free take on a classic bubbly lemonade served in strawberry-jalapeño or blueberry-basil, costs $6 — less than half what most composed zero-proof drinks run in the city. It opens at 11:30am Wednesday through Sunday.

Owner Shannon Healy and his bartenders hold experimental sessions on Thursday mornings building syrups and tinctures specifically for zero-proof drinks, and the bar keeps around twenty house-made tonics that underpin both sides of the menu — the same blood orange or cinchona-bittered tonic that sharpens a gin drink gives a zero-proof build its backbone. The current "Non-Alcohol" section runs four builds, two of them tea-based, and is refreshed seasonally; Best Day Brewing's non-alcoholic Kölsch and hazy IPA sit alongside. Discover Durham credits it with non-alcoholic cocktails with layers of flavour, house-made syrups and real presentation. Open Tuesday to Sunday from four until midnight.

The drinks list is the substantial part of the business rather than a sideline to the food: matcha built to order including the house Aloha Matcha Latte, smoothies made with fresh organic fruit, and cold drinks served alongside açaí bowls and a plant-focused menu. The Waikīkī room on Kaiulani Avenue opens daily from 7am to 7pm, which makes it one of the few genuinely alcohol-free options inside Waikīkī itself — a district otherwise dominated by hotel bars and resort restaurants where a non-drinker is always ordering around the menu.

Its own reservations page states the kitchen offers "a refined non-alcoholic pairing" as a standing alternative to its wine pairing across both the six- and ten-course tasting menus, built to deliver "the same level of creativity and balance." A June 2026 review documented that pairing in practice: guests are offered a choice of Champagne or a welcome pour of sparkling Saicho hojicha, a single-origin roasted green tea served chilled and lightly fizzy.

name: Aloha Beer Company
description: Aloha Beer Company is a brewery and taproom on Queen Street in Kakaʻako, and it keeps a named mocktail list rather than the token soda option most breweries offer. The Cucumber Smash and the tropical Lilikoi Cooler are the two the bar is known for, alongside a house iced tea and a Virgin Mojito. That combination — a working brewery that has bothered to write a zero-proof list — is what makes it useful, because a taproom is the default social venue in most cities and the place a non-drinker is most likely to be stranded. Happy hour runs daily from 2pm to 6pm and brunch at weekends from 10am to 2pm.

name: Amal Miami
description: Amal is a modern Lebanese restaurant and bar in Coconut Grove, opened in 2022 by Ink Entertainment Group, the hospitality company led by Beirut-born founder Charles Khabouth. It is the U.S. counterpart to the original Amal in Toronto, with executive chef Wissam Baki overseeing a menu of shareable mezze and coastal Lebanese dishes in a 180-seat dining room known for live music and a lively evening scene. For non-drinkers, Amal keeps a named zero-proof list built on Seedlip Notas de Agave and Martini & Rossi non-alcoholic aperitivo: the Habibi Mule (Seedlip Notas de Agave, prickly pear–lime, hibiscus ginger beer), the Yalla Spritz (Martini & Rossi Vibrante, cranberry-mango, Fever-Tree soda), and the Secret Garden (parsley-infused Seedlip Notas de Agave, lime, orange blossom, rose water, tonic). The kitchen also serves Lebanese brunch and a daily happy hour.

The cooking is coastal Latin American, and the bar keeps two documented alcohol-free builds that are designed to sit with it rather than to stand apart: the Pathfinder's Hand, made with The Pathfinder Hemp & Root, fresh tangerine, lime and soda, and the Miami Mockarita, a margarita-style pour of coconut water, lime, agave, orange bitters, pineapple and coconut. The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau lists the restaurant among the city's dining destinations with exceptional alcohol-free drinks. Service runs from 11:30am daily and the room sits directly on Biscayne Bay.

At the chef's counter, selecting a pairing (wine or non-alcoholic) is required, putting the zero-proof list on equal footing with the cellar.

description: Amazonia occupies a converted house on Hopkins Avenue in Birdtown, the small Lakewood district a few streets from LBM, and pairs a cocktail bar with a wood-fired pizza kitchen and a short menu of small plates. The rooms are domestic in scale — you are drinking in someone's front parlour, which is much of the appeal — and the bar leans tropical without tipping into tiki kitsch. Everything on both menus is made from scratch, and the zero-proof drinks get the same construction as the full-proof ones: house-made syrups, Seedlip and Lyre's spirits, and the same smoking and charring work. The alcohol-free Coconut Song is $15, exactly what the original costs. It opens at 4pm daily except Monday, runs to 2am on Friday and Saturday, and is 21-and-over, with an early-week happy hour taking $2 off cocktails and half off pizza.

name: Amba
description: Amba sits on West 28th Street in Hingetown, the compact Ohio City block that also holds Jukebox, and is the Indian-influenced restaurant in Douglas Katz and Todd Thompson's Edgewater Hospitality group — the same operation behind Zhug in Cleveland Heights. Chef Cameron McCaulley runs the kitchen, and the cooking works through spice, acid and fermentation rather than heat alone, which turns out to be the same logic driving the drinks list. Three named non-alcoholic builds sit as a standing section, each written out with its ingredients the way the cocktails are: the cumin-and-black-salt Nimbu Masala, the colour-shifting Blue Bergamot, and the Spiced Nectar at $13 on a citrus-forward zero-proof spirit. Best Day Brewing's non-alcoholic kölsch is $7 alongside the full-strength taps. Dinner only, Monday through Saturday.

name: American Bar at The Savoy
description: The American Bar at The Savoy, on the Strand, is London's oldest surviving cocktail bar (open since 1893) and a long-standing World's 50 Best Bars name, crowned the World's Best Bar in 2017. Its 2025 'Liquid Moments' menu — 17 cocktails marking the Savoy's 135th anniversary under head bartender Angelo Sparvoli — carries a set of genuine non-alcoholic cocktails, among them the King's Cobbler and Homecoming, mixed with the same craft as the spirituous list. For a landmark grand-hotel bar of this stature, that makes it a rare high-value zero-proof option in central London.

name: Analog Coffee Bar (Carabello Coffee)
description: Analog is the fully non-alcoholic "slow bar" tucked inside Carabello Coffee's roastery-cafe in historic Newport, where baristas apply craft-cocktail technique to zero-proof drinks. Seating just six at a wooden counter, it runs like a chef's table for beverages: the espresso and pour-over gear sits behind the bar so guests watch every step. A brand-new themed menu drops every six weeks — a recent literary-inspired lineup featured The Hobbit, Bear, Blueberries for Sal and Anne of Green Gables — spanning coffee builds, tea-based signatures, hot chocolate and coffee mocktails like the Cold Fashioned (cold brew and bitters, sans the bourbon). Everything is alcohol-free; the venue's own FAQ answers the alcohol question with a flat "No." Open Thursday–Saturday, 10am–5pm, with reservations encouraged, especially on Saturdays.

Its non-alcoholic menu is not a handful of substitutions but a named list, the Ikenice Choice, built entirely on Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits. The standout is the alcohol-free espresso martini, frothy and bitter without the syrupy finish most versions carry, and there is an amaretto sour given texture with aquafaba. The bar's own site puts it simply: it has cocktails for those who do not consume alcohol.

name: Andra Hem
description: Andra Hem — Swedish for "second home" — is a Scandinavian-inspired cocktail lounge that opened in November 2022 in a four-story black-painted townhouse at 16th and Chancellor in Rittenhouse. Founded by art collector Paige West, with interiors by designer Ghislaine Viñas built around a fictional Swedish proprietor, the bar deliberately launched with no public-relations push yet landed on Esquire's Best Bars in America list in 2023. Lead bartender Patrick Jennings runs a cocktail program that leans Nordic, alongside snacks like warm bread, pickled herring, and caviar. Its menu carries a dedicated "Low ABV & Non-Alcoholic" section with three named zero-proof builds at $11 each: the Squirt Gun (bitter soda and espresso), The Linc (cucumber water, dill, lime, soda), and Touch Nothing But the Lamp (jasmine tea, fruit, citrus, soda). The NA list is small but real and house-made.

The section holds four drinks: a St Agrestis Phony Negroni, a Ghia Spritz labeled Lime and Salt, the Root and Bloom built from Seedlip Grove with tonic and lime, and an NA 75 of passionfruit and Roots non-alcoholic vermouth. A Gruvi Golden Lager is stocked at $10 for anyone who wants a beer with the grill. The program has been part of the restaurant since its early days and has grown rather than shrunk.

Its practical advantage over almost everything else in Portland is the clock: it opens at 11am on weekdays, 7:30am on Saturdays for breakfast, and runs to 1am every night, which is a longer useful window than any other venue in this guide. At least one local guide attributes specific mocktail names here that another assigns elsewhere, so ask what is actually on when you arrive.

name: Animae
description: Animae is an Asian-inspired fine-dining room on Pacific Highway downtown, led by executive chef Tara Monsod, a three-time James Beard Award semifinalist, and its drinks list prints a Spirit Free section of four. Spirited Away is built on Pentire Adrift with elderflower, honey, Thai basil and black peppercorn; The Malarkey uses a Thai chilli and tamarind syrup with pineapple and lime; and two tea drinks follow — a melon milk tea with jasmine, oat milk and boba, and a cold-brewed single-source iced tea. Prices run from nine to thirteen dollars, against nineteen for the alcoholic cocktails, so a non-drinker is not paying a premium for the absence of alcohol. The Malarkey is the one to order if you would rather avoid spirit analogues entirely. Dinner is served nightly from five, until half past nine on Friday and Saturday, in a dining room built into the base of the Pacific Gate tower on the waterfront edge of downtown.

The kitchen draws from across the Mediterranean coast with mezze and shareable plates, and the wine program is the centerpiece — roughly 30 wines by the glass, 10 on tap, and about 135 total. Its published Zero Proof section is short rather than deep: the Underserved ($8), built on sweet plum, ginger and lemon with Fever-Tree Mediterranean tonic, alongside a fresh ginger ale ($4) and Heineken 0.0 ($6). It has built a reputation on inventive, produce-driven drinks, and its standing zero-proof list is repeatedly named among Cincinnati's best mocktails. Two roughly $10 alcohol-free cocktails anchor the menu: the citrus-forward Schamer '94 (non-alcoholic spiced spirit, lemon, grapefruit, honey and NA bitters) and the warmer, aromatic Once An Island (masala, pomegranate, spiced maple, ginger, house yuzu, NA bitters and smoked cinnamon). A lighter Spencer, built on mint, lime, seltzer and a pineapple-mango shrub, has also appeared. Anjou rounds out the option with zero-proof wine and beer, making it a genuine choice for an alcohol-free date night.

Its specialty mocktails are scratch-made, and the house build is the Rowena Moore — named for the Omaha civil-rights organiser and community leader, which places the alcohol-free drink in the bar's own naming scheme rather than in an annex. description: Anomaly SF is an intimate tasting-menu restaurant on a quiet block in Lower Pacific Heights, opened by chef-owner Mike Lanham in January 2023 after nearly five years as a word-of-mouth pop-up, with the buildout funded partly via Kickstarter. Lanham — a Culinary Institute of America (Greystone) graduate who cooked at Spruce, the Michelin-starred Commis, and Bird Dog — calls his Georgia-rooted cooking "Southern-Inspired Modernism," and the restaurant earned a Bib Gourmand in the 2024 California Michelin Guide. General manager and beverage director Francis Kulaga runs a full non-alcoholic pairing alongside the multi-course tasting menu, priced comparably to the wine pairing (roughly $99). Rather than a fixed zero-proof list, Kulaga builds the pairing to each guest's taste across the courses, leaning on dealcoholized and spirit-free products including Free AF, Proxies, and Leitz Sparkling, with an option for a few standalone spirit-free cocktails.

description: Antidote is a three-storey cocktail lounge and coffee bar that opened in 2018 at 151 Coxe Avenue in the South Slope, built as a turn-of-the-century apothecary and attached to the Chemist Spirits distillery next door. Mountain Xpress described it on opening as aiming for a cosy, quiet, upscale vibe with Prohibition-style décor in the manner of a traditional gentleman's cigar bar — though, as the paper noted, happily free of cigars and sexism. The award-winning cocktail team turns the same craft to zero-proof drinks, served all day: an apothecary-inspired menu of espresso, coffee, tea and non-alcoholic mocktails, with the Cold Brew Old Fashioned and Cold Brew Mojito among them. The all-day format is what makes it useful — it works as a morning coffee stop and an evening cocktail room in the same seat, in Asheville's densest brewery-and-bar district.

Its non-alcoholic offerings are modest but genuine and appear by name on the current seasonal menu: "Double Time," a shaken build of zero-proof tequila, strawberry, vinegar, and sparkling water, and the "Phony Negroni," a bubbly non-alcoholic Negroni served on tap.

The winter card added a No-Jito and a hot Apple of My Pie, so the section moves with the season. description: Aperitivo is an Italian-inspired bar and cafe inside downtown Milwaukee's historic Pritzlaff Building, built around the European ritual of the pre-dinner drink. Alongside its wine, amari and vermouth, it keeps a standing lineup of house zero-proof cocktails built largely on Great Lakes Distillery's non-alcoholic Junipre spirit. The alcohol-free list runs from a berry-forward Dry Spritz to the winter-favorite Teetotal Toddy, plus an off-menu Lavender Espresso Martini that local press has singled out. The Mock Trial balances bitter Stappi, the Italian red soda that has become a bartender's shortcut to real bitterness, against fluffy pineapple; there is a Watermelon Mojito, and a Coffee Tonic built on nitro cold brew with Fever-Tree tonic and cane syrup. Its own menu index bills the section as inventive cocktails without the booze, and Discover Durham names it beside The Velvet Hippo for a dedicated non-alcoholic menu that rivals anything with a proof. We do not name the drinks here on purpose: the section's individual builds do not render on the bar's website and the menu images it hosts date from 2023, so the honest position is that the programme is real and the list changes with the season. Ask at the bar. Open six to midnight most nights, from five on Friday and Saturday, closed Mondays.

name: ARCO Cocktail Lounge + Coastal Fare
description: ARCO is a cocktail lounge and coastal-seafood room set inside an 1860 Victorian building on Bay Street, entered off Factor's Walk and framed by the brick arches and vaults that give it its name, with the Savannah River below. It is part of the Ele & the Chef restaurant collection. The cocktail menu is organised into four named categories — Classics, Signature, Light and Moderate, and Non-Alcoholic — so the alcohol-free drinks are a standing section of the list rather than a request, and the low-ABV tier sits between them for anyone moderating rather than abstaining. The room opens in the late afternoon and runs to 10pm, or 11pm on Fridays.

name: Ardsley Station
description: Ardsley Station is a neighbourhood restaurant on Victory Drive at the edge of Ardsley Park, away from the tourist blocks, serving Southern plates with local produce from 11am to 10pm every day of the week. Its drinks list prints a section headed Zero-Proof carrying three built cocktails between $8.90 and $9.90 — a rosemary-and-orgeat citrus drink, a seasonal-fruit build on Amethyst's blueberry-ginger botanical, and a cucumber-shrub spritz — alongside Athletic Brewing's New Dawn alcohol-free beer at $4.90 in the beer and seltzer section. The all-day hours make it one of the more reliably open zero-proof lists in the city.

name: Arizona Wilderness Brewing — DTPHX
description: The downtown Phoenix pub from one of Arizona's most acclaimed breweries — and one of the few anywhere that brews its own non-alcoholic beer rather than stocking someone else's. Arizona Wilderness released ARIZO[NA], billed as the state's first non-alcoholic IPA, with bright citrus, balanced bitterness and a snappy finish, and donates 2 percent of its sales to the Arizona Trail Association every year. The taproom also pours Wild Water, a zero-proof sparkling water hopped with El Dorado and Mosaic. Founded in 2013 by Jonathan Buford and Patrick Ware and named Best New Brewery in the World by RateBeer within months of opening, the company built its identity on water stewardship in a drought state — its slogan is "Drink Like You Care".

name: Armadillo Den
description: Armadillo Den is a three-acre outdoor entertainment complex on Menchaca Road in far South Austin, opened in December 2020 by partner Brett Berry. The two-story bar is a neighborhood gathering spot known for live music seven nights a week, five rotating on-site food trucks (including Biggie's Yardbird, Via 313, and Los Danzantes), a large off-leash dog park, yard games, and a 13-foot LED TV wall for watch parties. Visit Austin recognizes Armadillo Den for its award-winning draft mocktail program — a relatively rare commitment in Texas, where most NA options are made glass-by-glass rather than poured from a tap. Signature NA cocktails include the Frescadillo Paloma (pink grapefruit, sea salt) and Ford's Ranch Water (Thai basil sparkling water, cucumber). The space is kid-friendly until 6pm Monday through Friday, and the dog-park-and-food-trucks setup makes it one of South Austin's most family- and group-friendly bars regardless of whether you're drinking alcohol.

name: Around the Kava Bowl
description: Around the Kava Bowl is a fully alcohol-free kava bar in Captain Cook, twelve miles up the hill from Kailua-Kona, serving fresh Hawaiian and Pacific kava since 2019. It operates from the back of the Hoʻo Hui wellness centre — the old Captain Cook courthouse building on Mamalahoa Highway, across from the NAPA auto parts store — and trades on being the cooler, quieter alternative when the Kona coast is too hot. Its own stated purpose is to create and nurture ʻohana through community, culture and oneness around the kava bowl. Posted hours are not reliably published, so call ahead. Kava contains no alcohol but is psychoactive and mildly sedating.

Orange blossom water and cardamom are the giveaway: they are perfume-adjacent ingredients used in small measures for scent, and reaching for them signals a bar solving the real problem with zero-proof drinks, which is that removing alcohol removes aroma as much as it removes warmth. Note that some local guides list a Grove Street address; the Main Street location is the one recorded here. Open Wednesday to Saturday only.

Head bartender Giulia Cuccurullo's "Ultimo" menu includes dedicated non-alcoholic serves: Currant, a booze-free paloma with Smiling Wolf agave and London Essence raspberry-rose soda, and an effervescent Apple built on Lyre's American Malt and Amaretto with Wignac cider.

name: Arwa Yemeni Coffee
description: Arwa Yemeni Coffee is a late-night Yemeni coffeehouse in Brookline's Coolidge Corner, opened in March 2026 as the first Massachusetts outpost of a small Texas-based chain. No alcohol is served, and the room is built for staying: the kitchen and bar run past 10pm every night of the week and to midnight on Fridays and Saturdays. The list is anchored in Yemeni coffee tradition. Jubani is a spiced blend brewed with coffee husks; mofawer is a kettle-brewed medium roast infused with cardamom, cinnamon and fresh ginger and finished with milk; qishr is the caffeine-light husk brew. Adeni teas are milk-based black brews carrying a warm spice blend and a frothy cardamom syrup. Modern drinks sit beside them, including pistachio, salted caramel and Fruity Pebbles lattes, blueberry matcha and limeade, alongside sweet and savory pastries.

Arwa's rooms are designed for sitting and staying, several of them built around jelsa rooms for traditional floor seating. The Strawberry Ginger Smash at $12 muddles strawberry with ginger and lemon over ginger beer; the Cucumber Mint 'Gin' Spritz at $14 runs cucumber and mint with lime and lemon-lime soda. A rooftop is one of the better settings for an evening without alcohol, because the view supplies the reason to be there and nobody is standing at a bar.

Its documented alcohol-free build is the Almond Blossom, which layers Seedlip Grove 42 with orgeat, yuzu juice and yuzu soda — the citrus expression of the non-alcoholic distiller carrying the almond sweetness rather than being buried by it. The seasonal, chef-driven menu is gluten-free, organic, and locally sourced where possible. Note for anyone avoiding all intoxicants: the same drinks menu also lists THC beverages.

The house pours fresh 'awa — the Hawaiian name for kava — farmed on Moku o Keawe and Molokaʻi and hand-pressed on site, alongside dry kava sourced from across the South Pacific. It is halal and serves no alcohol, and it opens at 2pm on weekdays and noon at weekends and runs to 10pm every night, which makes it a genuine evening destination rather than a lunch counter. The kitchen works from traditional Yemeni recipes: lamb mandi and haneeth served over rice, fahsa cooked and brought to the table still bubbling in its stone pot, and bread baked to order in a tandoor. The drink to know is the Yemeni cocktail, a layered non-alcoholic blend of mango, banana, dates, strawberry, milk and Vimto, served in a tall glass. Adani tea, the spiced milk tea of Aden, closes the meal.

It seats only 39, takes no reservations, and has collected an unusual run of accolades for its size: Boston Magazine rated it the city's best bar in March 2020, Time Out included it among the 28 coolest bars in the world in August 2021, and Wine Enthusiast named it Best Overall Bar in Boston in November 2024. Its non-alcoholic list is a full themed menu that rotates rather than a token section; the current one is Studio Ghibli-themed and headed "Rated NA: Non Alcoholic!", with every alcohol-free drink priced at $11.

Its documented alcohol-free build, the Dirty Marti-No, is an unusually savoury build — a spirit-free take on a dirty martini made with Osco Original and layered with olive, thyme, grape and rose tea. The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau describes it as balancing briny depth with subtle floral notes and calls it an option for guests who prefer their drinks less sweet and more complex.

name: Baia
address: Level 4, Esplanade Mall, 8 Raffles Avenue, Singapore 039802
description: Baia is a Roman-inspired rooftop dining lounge above Esplanade Mall with sweeping Marina Bay views, where the Proof & Co-curated cocktail list carries a genuine set of four dedicated zero-proof drinks at S$22 or below. The standout is 'As Good As Corona', built on Seedlip Grove 42 with yuzu and sage, alongside 'Not a Sunken City', the alcohol-free take on the house Sunken City that swaps gin for a non-alcoholic spirit and holds the tomato relish. Bar manager Adonis E. Reyes builds each spirit-free drink to mirror the flavour architecture of its full-proof counterpart, and the team will craft bespoke zero-proof serves on request.

name: Bait Shop
description: Bait Shop is a kitschy tiki-and-tackle bar at 606 Broadway E on Capitol Hill, known for frozen cocktails and a room styled after a port town. It opened in 2012 under Linda Derschang, and Mike Leifur and Jonah Bergman — then working for her — bought it in 2016. STATUS, BECAUSE IT IS ON OUR WATCHLIST: the century-old building is slated for demolition and the owners have been looking for a new Capitol Hill home since their demolition clause was triggered; they "technically" lost the lease in December 2025. But no demolition permit has been filed for the address as of today, and Bergman has said construction is not expected before the first quarter of 2027 at the earliest. It is open and trading normally. Its printed non-alcoholic section runs Athletic Brewing Run Wild IPA and Upside Dawn ($6 each), a Phony Negroni and an Amaro Falso ($10 each), a Recess zero-proof margarita ($8), and soft drinks. NOTE: a Rogue CBD ($6) and a Recess Mood soda ($7) also sit under that same heading, with no dosage printed. Open 4pm–2am daily.

name: Bakaris Pizza & Kava Lounge
hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 5pm-11:45pm; Fri 12am-2am & 2pm-2am; Sat 2pm-12am; Sun 5pm-11:45pm
description: Bakaris Pizza & Kava Lounge has operated in Atlanta's historic West End since 2013, billing itself as the area's original pork-free halal and plant-based pizzeria paired with an alcohol-free kava bar. The venue is fully zero-proof: its entire beverage program centers on kava, the South Pacific root traditionally used for relaxation. Bakaris serves traditional ceremonial kava, instant kava shots, and tropical "kavarita"-style blends, alongside wellness-oriented kava drinks marketed for "calm, clarity, and social vibes without alcohol." To-go ceremonial and instant kava packs are also available. The kitchen turns out halal turkey pepperoni and turkey bacon pizzas plus build-your-own vegan options with plant-based cheese, making it a draw for the Muslim community and sober-curious crowd alike. The lounge runs late-night, doubling as a community and wellness gathering space in Southwest Atlanta.

name: Baladi Coffee House
description: Baladi Coffee House is a Yemeni coffeehouse on Lorain Road in North Olmsted that describes itself as authentic Yemeni coffee and tea, with tradition in every cup. It serves no alcohol and keeps the latest hours of the three Yemeni cafes in the suburb, open until 11pm most nights and 1am on Friday and Saturday. The shop says its beans come from a single farm in Haraz, Yemen, are never blended and are roasted to order. Its ordering menu runs from a Baladi House Latte and pistachio, Spanish, Biscoff and tiramisu lattes through matcha, frappes, smoothies, refreshers and tea, with sandwiches at the counter, and it sells its Jubani and Turkish blends and Adeni tea to take home.

name: Baladi Coffee
address: 3061 George Busbee Pkwy NW Suite 2000, Kennesaw, GA 30144
description: Baladi Coffee is a family-owned Arabic coffeehouse on George Busbee Parkway in Kennesaw, run by Sarah and Allen, who describe it as "a Middle Eastern/Arabic coffee shop with influences from around the world". Baladi means "my homeland". It is fully alcohol-free and trades 7am to 10pm seven days a week, extending to midnight during Ramadan. The tea programme is the distinguishing feature: Adeni tea, Arabic tea, Yemeni tea and Pakistani chai are listed separately rather than folded into a single chai. Alongside them sit signature espresso drinks, a matcha list, and Peach Mango, Strawberry Acai and Watermelon Kiwi refreshers. The food counter runs to milk cake, kunafa and traditional and modern Arabic pastries, and there are further Baladi locations in Marietta and Athens.

name: The Lounge at Balanced Being
description: Billed by its own team as Dallas's first plant bar and non-alcoholic lounge, The Lounge at Balanced Being is a fully alcohol-free social space on Lower Greenville — a room to relax and connect, in its own words, without alcohol. Access runs on reservations and memberships rather than walk-ins, with a first-visit fee. It is explicit that plant medicines are part of the offer, including kava and mushrooms, and that intentional cannabis use is welcomed within legal guidelines: alcohol-free, but emphatically not substance-free.

name: Baleia
description: Baleia is a Portuguese-inspired, seafood-forward restaurant at 264 East Berkeley Street in Boston's South End, opened in 2024 as the fourth concept from Coda Restaurant Group, following CODA, The Salty Pig, SRV and Gufo. The restaurant describes itself as a love letter to Portugal — its seafood cooking, its easy-drinking cocktails and bold wines, and the soft lines of its sun-faded architecture — with a global influence layered over it. The drinks list prints a standing Low + No Proof section split between three house mocktails at $8 to $12 and three non-alcoholic wines by the glass at $13 to $14. The zero-proof cocktails are built on real non-alcoholic spirits including Almave and a zero-proof rosso vermouth.

description: The Ball & Biscuit opened on Massachusetts Avenue in June 2010 and is generally credited as Indiana's first craft cocktail bar. It was founded by local attorney Trevor Belden with bartender Zach Wilks, who later left to build the Wilks & Wilson syrup line, and takes its name from the 1930s ribbon microphone nicknamed the ball and biscuit — vintage mics and music gear are part of the fit-out. For a bar of that vintage the non-alcoholic list is unusually developed: seven named zero-proof drinks stand alongside the full-proof menu rather than in a footnote, including the Spritz AF built on Lyre's Italian Orange and Aperitif Rosso with Fre sparkling brut, the Twist of Fate, the New Fashioned and the floral Whole Garden.

name: Bantha Tea Bar
description: Bantha Tea Bar, on Penn Ave between Garfield and Bloomfield, is a solar-powered tea house built largely from recycled materials and an explicitly alcohol-free space to hang out without drinking. The menu runs deep on loose-leaf black, green and herbal teas, joined by Sweet Unity Farms coffee, matcha, ceremonial cacao, MUD\WTR and house lemonades — no alcohol is served at all. It has also been the closest thing Pittsburgh has to a kava bar: Keystone Newsroom's February 2026 survey of the city's kava scene found that Pittsburgh has no dedicated kava bar and named Bantha the only cafe in the city with kava on its menu, mixed with almond milk, coconut milk, ginger beer or lemonade, or taken as a shot of house concentrated extract. Bantha's own published menu does not currently list kava, so call ahead if that is why you are going. The room runs poetry readings and regular community events.

name: Bar 473
description: Bar 473 sits on Admiral Boulevard in Tulsa's Kendall-Whittier neighbourhood, open from 3pm and running to midnight midweek and 2am on Friday and Saturday. Its alcohol-free drink is the Horchata Colada — pineapple, coconut, lime and cinnamon — which builds a piña colada on a horchata base rather than a rum one, using cinnamon and the creaminess of the coconut to supply the weight the spirit would otherwise carry. It is a dessert-leaning drink and honestly so, and a good answer for anyone who wants something substantial rather than another citrus highball. Kendall-Whittier puts it a short drive east of downtown rather than within walking distance of the other rooms here.
signatureDrinks: Horchata Colada — pineapple, coconut, lime, cinnamon

name: Bar Banane
address: 227A Ossington Ave, Toronto, ON M6J 2Z8, Canada

description: Bar Banane is a lively cocktail bar on the Ossington Strip in Toronto, pairing an elevated, French-inflected small-plates menu — lobster croustade, smoked sturgeon rillettes, steak tartare — with an ambitious twelve-drink signature cocktail list. Its non-alcoholic beverages get a standalone "Non-Alcoholic Beverages" section on the menu, priced at the same $14 as the house cocktails rather than tacked on as an afterthought: Optional Side Quest (elderflower, clarified grapefruit, genmaicha tea, tonic), Pear-odactyl (mango aloe, pear juice, lemon) and Extremely Safe for Work (passion fruit, clarified lemon, orange, chili). Destination Toronto, the city's official tourism organization, singled the bar out for showing "just how far and creative you can go when building a non-alcoholic beverage."

The cocktail program — developed by Jason Lee (n/soto, Baroo) and beverage director Chad Austin — is known for elaborate, food-driven drinks, and the non-alcoholic list is a genuine priority rather than an afterthought: Austin, who is five years sober, builds the zero-proof cocktails with the same rigor as the full menu. Named NA drinks on the current menu include the Smiley Face (a mango-margarita riff with yellow bell pepper syrup, fermented mango, acid-adjusted pineapple, Wilderton Citrus Bitter, and Optimist Smoky), plus Aura Farm, Bangkok Dangerous, and Tepache Bird. Most of its non-alcoholic drinks pair Seedlip spirits with house-made syrups, producing layered, low-sweetness builds like the citrusy Vinifera Spice and the herbal Mariposa Milk. Phoenix New Times has singled out that Seedlip-and-housemade-syrup pairing as exactly what separates the list here from the sweetened juice most restaurants hand to non-drinkers while they wait for a table.

Young, an accomplished Twin Cities beverage director, anchors a serious drink program — and that extends to one of the metro's deepest zero-proof lists. The "Free Spirit" menu currently runs six house non-alcoholic cocktails spanning smoky to sweet — White Fox (coconut water, orange blossom, banana, egg white, cherry-bark vanilla), Up In Smoke (coconut water, grapefruit, jalapeño, basil, smoked salt), Hibiscus Punch, Fruit of the Desert, Devil in the Garden, and Lucky Me — alongside bottled St. Agrestis Phony Negronis in both the classic and mezcal styles. Axios Twin Cities named it the most expansive non-alcoholic list in its January 2026 Dry January roundup. The food leans elevated-comfort, from Coney Island dogs to fresh oysters.

It was named a winner of the inaugural NYC's Best Bars for NA Awards 2025 for its deeply experimental non-alcoholic menu, and its drink list carries a few low-ABV and no-ABV options alongside its $21 craft cocktails and creative small plates.

name: Bar Esmé
description: Bar Esmé is the à la carte bar adjoining Esmé, the one-Michelin-star Lincoln Park restaurant opened in August 2021 by chef Jenner Tomaska and his partner Katrina Bravo. Where the flagship serves a tasting menu built around rotating collaborations with artists, the bar is a smaller, more casual route into the same kitchen without committing to the full format. Drinks are led by beverage director Stevan Miller, who also oversees Esmé and the group's French brasserie Petite Edith, and whose stated approach is the reverse of the usual order: non-alcoholic cocktails, he told Third Coast Review in 2026, are something he thinks of before every other part of the menu. A current zero-proof example is Apple Island — apple with habanero and agave, force-carbonated so it lands with the bite of a hard soda. Note that the bar does not publish a working drinks list online, so the rotating menu is best read on arrival, and any zero-proof drinks named in pre-2026 coverage predate the current beverage team. Service runs Wednesday to Sunday from 5pm.

description: Bar Franca is a Euro-style cocktail and sound bar on South Main Street in the Historic Core of Downtown Los Angeles, open only Thursday to Saturday from 9pm to 2am. It is licensed, and its drink menu carries a titled Zero Proof and Low ABV section: Bonfire Water, made with fresh-pressed watermelon, hibiscus and Lyre's Italian Spritz; Espresso Esplatore, built on Pathfinder Hemp and Root with espresso, tonic and citrus; and Palomanada, with grapefruit, citrus, agave, soda and salt. Estrella Galicia Zero Proof is stocked in cans alongside two low-alcohol Stiegl radlers. The room has tall ceilings, floral wallpaper, a long bar and semi-separate lounge seating, and the music programming is the point as much as the drinks.

name: Bar Hygge
description: Bar Hygge is a Fairmount brewpub open since 2016, run by owners Stew and Julie Keener, Tom Baker, and Peggy Zwerver. Named for the Danish concept of cozy contentment (pronounced "huu-guh"), it houses Brewery Techne, a 10-barrel brewhouse pouring rotating house draft and cask beers alongside contemporary American boards and comfort-food entrees. The venue is recognized for an inclusive, sober-friendly approach: alongside the bar's cocktails and draft wines, it stocks alcohol-removed wine, a zero-proof amaro, and signature non-alcoholic cocktails. Visit Philadelphia's zero-proof guide highlights two named mocktails — "Amateur Jazz," built on Ritual's gin alternative with cinchona bark, herbs, citrus, and soda, and "Spice Up Your Life," made with Seedlip Garden 108, caramelized pineapple, strawberry oleo saccharum, jalapeño, lemon, and soda — plus a lavender lemonade and a Ritual/Seedlip spritz. Located near Eastern State Penitentiary, it's a neighborhood favorite for drinkers and non-drinkers alike.

The program leans on Japanese spirits and long, seasonal ingredient lists, and its non-alcoholic offering is unusually deep: the bar keeps a standalone alcohol-free menu that currently runs nine N/A cocktails named for Japanese places, from the Kyoto — a non-alcoholic martini of Amass and Dhōs N/A spirits with Aplos Arise, narazuke brine and tsukemono — to the Yakushima (Okinawa purple yam, Wilderton Earthen, kalamansi, li hin mui), alongside a bottle list of dealcoholized sake, sparkling wine and riesling. Several cocktails on the main list are also marked as available non-alcoholic, and The San Francisco Standard has reported that more than half its cocktails can be made without alcohol.

description: Bar Julian is the rooftop bar on top of Thompson Savannah in the Eastern Wharf development, the tallest roof in the city, looking straight down the Savannah River. Its cocktail list prints a section headed Booze-Free carrying four drinks between $12 and $14, all built on non-alcoholic spirits — a zero-proof agave, a zero-proof London dry, Lyre's cane spirit and a zero-proof aperitif — rather than assembled from juices. There is no fixed zero-proof list, so nothing is named here — but the stock behind the bar is real, and one of the team describes themselves on the bar's own site as a sober bartender who makes their own amari. Seatings run from half past five, closed Tuesdays, to ten most nights and eleven on Friday and Saturday.

The menu, titled the Kapitan's Archives, is arranged in four eras of the house's history, and each era carries one drink printed at zero strength. Last Call is built on oolong, roasted barley, honey and chenpi; Sister Act on white tea, cucumber, coriander, rojak flower and quinine; TCM Drawer No.3 on soy milk, ginger, honeydew, chestnut honey and gula melaka; and Gong Fu Merchant on aged tea, black date and rock sugar. It is open every day from 5pm to midnight.

description: Kindred is a vegan cocktail bar and restaurant in South Park, open since 2015 and styled as "equal parts evil lair and Victorian cocktail salon," pairing plant-based fare with craft drinks and a death-metal soundtrack. Voted Best Vegan Bar in the U.S. by VegNews and a Tales of the Cocktail honoree, it keeps a dedicated "Zero-Proof" menu its team treats "just as intentional and special as any other part of the menu." Named alcohol-free options include the Kiss of Steel (cold-brew, oat milk, cinnamon, coconut, orange twist), the Zombie Prescription (pineapple-turmeric shrub, grapefruit, lemon, cinnamon, ginger, agave), the tropical-goth Miracle Cure (pineapple, lime, coconut, passionfruit, Thai basil, lemongrass, charcoal), and a Phony Negroni. It ranked among Yelp's Top 25 U.S. mocktail spots.

name: Bar Lina
description: The basement aperitivo bar beneath Lina Stores' Brewer Street delicatessen, the Italian grocer that has anchored Soho since 1944. Upstairs is all fresh pasta and hanging salumi; downstairs the green-and-brass bar pours a negroni-led list with an unusually well-built page of virgin cocktails. Three zero-proof drinks are constructed with the same cordials-and-bitters seriousness as the boozy side: Essenza on Amaro 0% with lemon balm cordial and a strawberry and lavender soda, Euphoria on Amaro 0% with raspberry, mint and tonic, and Ananas & Menta on Gin 0% with pineapple cordial and a pepper bitter. Aperitivo snacks come from the deli, and the room works as well for an early evening as a nightcap.

description: Bellwoods Brewery is a longstanding Ossington Avenue brewpub and bottle shop that brews its own line of named, in-house non-alcoholic beers rather than carrying outside NA brands. The lineup centers on the 0.5% — which started as an internal Dry January joke before becoming a real release — alongside the dry-hopped Stay Classy IPA and several Jelly King non-alcoholic sour and seltzer variants. Co-founder Luke Pestl says the NA beers use controlled, stopped fermentation rather than dealcoholization, an extension of the brewery's long-running interest in low-ABV brewing.

description: Beneath Driver Lane is a subterranean CBD cocktail den hidden in the vault of the old GPO Money Order Office, down a lane off Little Bourke Street. Alongside its whisky-heavy classic-cocktail program it keeps a genuine run of 100% alcohol-free builds - a zero-proof Negroni, a spiced pineapple Daiquiri, a Winter Paloma and an Americano - documented by Time Out as being 'just as lip-smackingly good' as the full-strength list. Time Out lists four fully alcohol-free builds here — a Negroni, a spiced pineapple Daiquiri, a Winter Paloma and an Americano — so the zero-proof order is a named drink rather than a request.

name: Bern's Steak House
description: Bern's Steak House is Tampa's most storied fine-dining institution — a SoHo landmark open since 1956, known worldwide for its dry-aged steaks and a legendary upstairs dessert room. Its bar carries a dedicated "Zero Proof" cocktail section built on Ritual Zero Proof spirits, currently the Lil' Miss (dark cherry, cinnamon, ginger ale), the Solé Sunrise (Ritual tequila, orgeat, tangerine, lime, grapefruit), and the Watermelon Crawl (Ritual aperitif, watermelon, lime, mint, honey). It means a non-drinker can sit down to one of the country's great steakhouse experiences without settling for a soda.  Reservations are essential and often booked well ahead, and the upstairs dessert room is a separate seating after dinner.

name: Better Beverage
description: Better Beverage is a fully non-alcoholic bottle shop serving the Columbus metro, founded by Mary LaPlaca and based in Westerville. It has no storefront: the shop trades through pop-ups, event bars, tastings, local delivery and a wholesale programme for bars and restaurants, with orders taken by email. Everything it stocks is alcohol-free, and the buying policy is unusually explicit — LaPlaca curates ready-to-drink brands that are women-, LGBTQ+-, veteran-, minority- or family-owned, or that work to a sustainability standard, rather than simply carrying whatever distributes into Ohio. LaPlaca has written that Al-Anon changed her life and that she started the business after realising Columbus had no shop dedicated to non-alcoholic drinks, bringing two decades of work as an artist to the venture.

name: Better Luck Tomorrow
description: A Heights neighborhood cocktail bar from chef Justin Yu and bar operator Bobby Heugel with a genuine six-drink spirit-free list — including a Seedlip Grove Sin & Tonic and a Jungle Birdie garnished with a hand-folded origami bird — built by head bartender Sarah Crowl.

name: Beyond Proof
description: Beyond Proof is a fully alcohol-free craft cocktail bar at 597 Centre Street in Jamaica Plain, opened in April 2026 by Krista Kranyak, who converted her own long-running restaurant Ten Tables into what is widely reported as Boston's first zero-proof bar. Every drink is built at 0% ABV and the list is organised into sections headed Florals, Groundings, Rewritten Classics, Awakenings and Simple Sips, with straight $9 pours of zero-proof tequila, gin, vodka, bourbon and mezcal for guests who want something plainer. The kitchen serves a Lebanese and Mediterranean mezze menu of hummus boards, fire-roasted carrots, saffron tahdig bites, knafeh and slow-cooked pots. One drink, the Settle, is made with kava, a psychoactive root, which the bar names openly on the menu.

description: Beyond the Bar is DFW's first alcohol-free bottle shop and dry bar, and by its own account the only one in Texas — a zero-proof shop and tasting room in a 1958 mid-century building in Richardson's Core District. The range runs past 280 products, from Athletic, Seedlip, Lyre's and Ritual to Almave, Ghia, Pathfinder and De Soi, alongside dealcoholised wines and functional drinks. The bar pours its own builds, including the Italian Spritz that won the Dallas Observer's Best Mocktail award, and the room hosts tastings and zero-proof cocktail classes.

name: The Biergarten at Anheuser-Busch Brewery
description: Few sober-curious flexes beat ordering a Bud Zero at the brewery where Budweiser is born. The Biergarten sits inside Anheuser-Busch's historic St. Louis campus — a National Historic Landmark since 1966 — and is open to the public daily, no tour ticket required. Alongside 18 draught beers in signature glassware, the current menu lists five non-alcoholic beers: Bud Zero, Michelob Ultra Zero, Michelob Ultra Lime Zero, Mango Cart NA and Stella Artois Liberté. Add a full food menu, a pet-friendly outdoor patio and a heated tent in the winter months, and this Soulard beer garden is one of the easiest zero-proof outings in the city.

Non-alcoholic Best Day IPA and Fremont Dark are $8 each. Open from 8 or 9am daily.

name: Big Mini Putt Club
address: 70 Ionia Ave SW, Grand Rapids, MI 49503
description: Big Mini Putt Club is an indoor mini golf bar and lounge at 70 Ionia Avenue SW, billing itself as the Midwest's indoor mini golf bar. It is included here for a specific structural reason: the activity is the point of the visit, so a guest who is not drinking is doing the same thing as everyone else at the table rather than watching. The bar backs that up with stock rather than improvisation, carrying six zero-proof drinks, three mocktails and two non-alcoholic beers. Named builds include the Mulligan Margarita and the Ube Tee, both listed among downtown Grand Rapids' best non-alcoholic drinks in October 2025. It sits directly between Max's South Seas Hideaway and One Twenty Three Tavern on the same block of Ionia.

name: Bijou
description: Bijou is a neighbourhood cocktail bar in Browne's Addition, Spokane's oldest residential district, with a menu split between house specialties, classic cocktails, warm winter drinks, seasonal coffee blends and a standing mocktail section. The alcohol-free drinks are made from the bar's own components rather than bought mixers — butterfly pea flower tea, house elderflower and lavender syrups, fresh citrus — and the bartenders build to taste, asking which flavours you like and dislike before making something rather than pointing at a list. Open every day from 3pm, to midnight most nights and 1am on Friday, which makes it the most reliably open room in this guide.
pressQuoteSourceLabel: The Inlander, on mocktails becoming a menu standard

name: Bike Dog Brewing
description: Bike Dog Brewing's East Sacramento taproom carries three genuinely different alcohol-free options: locally made KC Kombucha on rotating flavours, hop water in passion fruit, orange and guava, and Untitled Art non-alcoholic beer. Hop water is the interesting one in a brewery — sparkling water dry-hopped with the same aromatic hops as an IPA, bitter and citrusy with no alcohol and no calories. Ordering one in a taproom gets you the flavour everybody else came for, from the same tap wall, without the beer. The East Sacramento taproom opens Tuesday to Sunday, from noon at weekends, and is closed Mondays. Three genuinely different options in a brewery is unusual; most manage one dusty can.

name: Billy Sunday
description: Billy Sunday is an award-winning craft cocktail bar that opened in 2013 in Chicago's Logan Square, part of chef Matthias Merges' Folkart Management group. The bar is best known for one of North America's largest collections of vintage fernet and amaro — bartender Alex Bachman's deeply researched back bar earned a place in James Beard Award-winning author Brad Thomas Parsons' book on amaro. While the cocktail list is spirit-forward, the menu also carries a dedicated "Spirit Free" section. Named zero-proof options include the Lupine Lady (lavender- and thyme-infused verjus, lime, mint, basil, and sparkling water) and an Italian Cream Soda (cola reduction, stewed cherries, cream, nutmeg, and Perrier). The bar also pours a rotating Athletic Brewing non-alcoholic beer alongside house-fermented sodas (note: the house sodas contain trace amounts of alcohol).

name: Binge Bar
description: Binge Bar is Washington DC's first 100% alcohol-free bar, in a lower-level space at 506 H Street NE in the Atlas District. Filipina entrepreneur Vergie "Gigi" Arandid founded the concept in June 2020 and opened to the public on 11 February 2023. It works as three things at once: a zero-proof cocktail bar, a Filipino bistro serving traditional bites alongside plant-based Mediterranean plates, and an events room. The drinks are built rather than poured - a Cucumber Mangorita, an Espresso Old Fashioned on Bare Zero Proof bourbon, a Passion Fruit Ginger Sour, a Hibiscus Reposado Margarita - alongside craft NA beer, vegan wines and canned mocktails. It won Best Craft Mocktail in Washington City Paper's 2024 Best of DC reader poll, and runs monthly sober comedy nights and vegan brunches. Nothing alcoholic is served.

description: Set in the historic Luhrs Building downtown, Bitter & Twisted is one of Phoenix's most decorated cocktail bars — open since 2014, and a top-ten finalist for Best U.S. Cocktail Bar at the Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Awards. It takes its zero-proof side as seriously as the rest. Alongside a dedicated spirit-free menu, the team says roughly 60 percent of the full cocktail list can be built without alcohol, and the bar has developed non-alcoholic versions of a dozen or so menu staples rather than a token pair. Named NA drinks have included the Nada Colada, the fizzy hibiscus-sage-cinnamon Miss Nightingale, the Rhubarb-Ba-Arandas, RUM DMC, an NA Pornstar Martini, and Hasta La Vista, Berry! — zero-proof mezcal and Martini & Rossi's non-alcoholic aperitif with a triple-berry shrub and soda.

name: Black Pearl
description: Black Pearl is a Fitzroy cocktail institution on Brunswick Street that has been named among the World's 50 Best Bars, and its bartenders extend the same craft to their alcohol-free builds. Broadsheet's best-non-alcoholic-bars guide singles it out for giving zero-proof drinks equal billing, from a savoury shaken number with lacto-fermented tomato, lemon juice, honey, ginger and Lyre's Italian Spritz to fruit-forward mocktails. Non-alcoholic beer such as Heaps Normal is also poured alongside the celebrated cocktail list. Time Out rates the alcohol-free cocktails as impressive as everything else the bartenders mix, running from a savoury build on lacto-fermented tomatoes to fruitier work.
