name: Blackbird
description: Blackbird is a literary-themed neighbourhood cocktail bar on Market Street at the Castro end of Upper Market, open since 2009 and trading to 2am on Friday and Saturday. Its menu carries a section headed Low ABV & Zero Proof, and two of the five drinks in it contain no alcohol at all: Nearly February, at $10, built from fig-infused balsamic with orange, grapefruit and soda water, and Salty Puppy, at $12, made with Aplós Calm, grapefruit, lime, honey and orange blossom water over a salted rim. Aplós Calm is a hemp-derived non-alcoholic spirit and the bar also stocks Wyld CBD cans, which is worth knowing for anyone avoiding psychoactive ingredients as well as alcohol.

It describes itself as equal parts wine bar and conversational destination, and its non-alcoholic drinks are made from real NA spirits rather than soft drinks: the Citrusy Glow is Seedlip Citrus with fresh lemon, and the Spice Girl works berries against Seedlip Spice. DiningOut Phoenix named it among the metro bars worth visiting for a mocktail in May 2026. Open from 11am on weekdays, with a nightly Rebel Hour from 7pm seven days a week, and quiet enough to hold a conversation in.

Set among lush plants, floral wallpaper, and a deep vinyl collection, it serves craft cocktails, beer, wine, and a seasonal small-plates menu. Its non-alcoholic program is genuine and built in-house: the menu's dedicated "Non-Alcoholic Cocktails" section runs about half a dozen drinks at $10, using house-made botanical syrups, house tea blends, coconut milk, vinegars, and rosewater rather than juice-and-soda shortcuts. Named zero-proof drinks include the Cat Nap N.A. (bitter botanical syrup, chamomile, sherry vinegar), Orange Dream Machine N.A. (orange, vanilla, rosewater, oat milk), Rose Darling N.A. (hibiscus, rose and green tea, lime, coconut milk), and Vacation (coconut milk, passion fruit, lemon, lime, orgeat). NA beer, hop water, kombucha, and CBD soda round out the list.

Regulars include a trio of fully alcohol-free cocktails made with Three Spirit Livener or Nightcap, plus zero-proof takes on the Martini, Margarita and Manhattan. The team's obsessive, ingredient-led approach applies just as much to the drinks without booze.

Alongside its rotating lineup of up to 26 taps, the brewery brews and cans its own dedicated non-alcoholic beer line — a 0.5% ABV Zero IPA and several Paradise Lost sour variants — sold through a standalone "Non-alc" collection on its own site. Narcity singled out the brewery's non-alcoholic options as "equally as fun" as its beer, pointing to an in-house strawberry-kiwi lemonade sparkling water and "the occasional non-alcoholic craft beer."

name: Bloom's
description: Bloom's is the late-night cocktail lounge just off the lobby of Hotel Ulysses, the maximalist 116-room hotel that opened in the 1920s Latrobe Building on Mount Vernon's Read Street in September 2022. The room commits to the look — crimson banquettes, purple stools, a mirrored ceiling and bar counter — and the list draws on Prohibition-era classics and 1970s revivals like the Midori sour and French martini. The menu carries a short but genuine Zero Proof section: the No Negroni builds Seedlip Garden 108 with Earl Grey tea and Giffard's alcohol-free aperitif bitter, alongside the Naquiri, a daiquiri-shaped mix of Seedlip Grove 42, guava, lime and orgeat (it contains almonds); the earlier Apple Blossom has rotated off, and Peroni's non-alcoholic lager sits on the beer list. It is a two-drink program rather than a deep one, but both are built cocktails on a named menu section, not mocktails improvised on request.

description: Bloomsday is a small wine bar and cafe near Headhouse Square, and it does something almost no other bar in Philadelphia does: it runs a $6 non-alcoholic happy hour price all the time, year-round, rather than only in January. Cuddles on the Beach pairs pomegranate with orange; there is a house-made ginger beer, which is worth ordering because a genuine ginger beer is fermented and hot rather than sweet; and the fridge carries Well Being's non-alcoholic IPA, Collective Arts Hazy at 0.5% and Athletic's golden ale. For a wine bar — the venue type where a non-drinker is usually offered the least — a permanent zero-proof price is a meaningful commitment.

name: Blue Atlas Restaurant and Market
description: Blue Atlas is a restaurant and market in Fulton, east of downtown Richmond, and its bar does two things that separate a real alcohol-free offering from a token one: it makes its own shrubs, and it stocks non-alcoholic wine. A shrub is a drinking vinegar — fruit, sugar and vinegar macerated over days — and it exists precisely to give a soft drink the acidity and length that alcohol normally provides, so any kitchen making one has committed real prep time to the non-drinker's side of the menu. Combined with the market operation and a Wednesday-to-Sunday schedule, it is a genuine destination rather than a convenient stop.

description: Boca is Chef David Falk's flagship fine-dining room, set behind a famous red door in the storied Sixth Street space that once held Cincinnati's legendary Maisonette. Its Italian-French menu is matched by a beverage list carrying a genuine dedicated "Zero Proof" section: five alcohol-free cocktails, each $12. The lineup pairs house builds — the Caribbean Queen (coconut milk, pineapple, demerara, cherry), the Blueberry Basil Fizz, The Cure (ginger, basil, honey, citrus, ginger beer) and the strawberry-jalapeno Fragola Pazzo — with a St. Agrestis Phony Negroni served over big ice with orange. It's a real menu section rather than an afterthought, letting non-drinkers order with the same intention as the wine-and-cocktail crowd in one of the region's most decorated dining rooms.

It is women-owned and family-run, with a pan-Thai menu built from recipes passed down through the three of them. The bar treats zero-proof as a build rather than a substitution: the Water Lily Dessert layers Lyre's Dry London Spirit and Fre Rosé over coconut water, strawberry shrub, lychee jelly and soda, and the rotating Secret Garden leans on seasonal fruit and vegetables. Seedlip appears in the seasonal list. The kitchen closes an hour before the bar does.

name: Boia De
description: Boia De is a Michelin-starred Italian restaurant opened in June 2019 by chef-partners Luciana Giangrandi and Alex Meyer, who began as a Miami food-truck and pop-up before going brick-and-mortar. Tucked into the Bravo Supermarket Plaza on the Little Haiti/Upper East Side line — marked by a neon pink exclamation point next to a coin laundromat — the intimate room seats roughly two dozen and earned its first Michelin star in 2022, retained through 2026. The kitchen pairs precise small plates and pasta with a curated wine list and a genuine no/low-ABV cocktail program. The menu's dedicated "Zero Proof" section brings the same precision to alcohol-free drinks: the Sober Surfer leans into tropical Miami flavors (coconut, pineapple, Pathfinder), while Strawberry Fields Forever is a clarified, layered build of strawberry-cucumber oleo, lemon, and basil oil. An Aplos Cup and a non-alcoholic Untitled Art IPA round out the options.

The lounge blends island ambience with a modern space and programmes live Polynesian music — the kava is affordable, available in to-go containers, and the draw is as much the shows and the company as the drink. Kava is a South Pacific root drink, alcohol-free but genuinely relaxing and mildly intoxicating in its own right, and it is served to adults. Hours shift with the events calendar, so check the lounge's social channels before travelling.

name: Bonifacio
description: Bonifacio is a modern Filipino restaurant on King Avenue in Fifth by Northwest, founded in 2016 by Krizzia Yanga, a Columbus native who had earlier introduced the city to Filipino cooking through her Red Velvet Café and who was named a Columbus Monthly Tastemaker in 2021. The restaurant is best known for its Boodle Nights, communal kamayan feasts eaten by hand from banana leaves piled with sticky rice, longganisa, lumpia, pickled vegetables and shrimp. The drinks list is written to match those flavours rather than to sit apart from them, and the non-alcoholic side draws on the same pantry: the Ube Colada is built from ube simple syrup with lime, pineapple and coconut cream, using the purple yam that runs through Filipino desserts. It backs up its cocktail reputation with a genuine, separately published non-alcoholic menu of five named mocktails plus a stocked zero-proof bar (Giffard NA aperitif, Lagunitas Hop Refresher, Athletic Lite and Guinness N/A). The bar runs on an order-at-the-bar model with the on-site Taco Moto truck for food and shares its address with sister event venue The Cooperage. Each Dry January it anchors Milwaukee's sober-curious scene by hosting the free after-party for N/A Day, the non-alcoholic beverage festival held next door.

name: Border Brewing Company
description: Border Brewing Company is the original brewery and taproom in Kansas City's Crossroads Arts District, founded by owner and lead brewer Eric Martens, who opened the business after a career as a chemical and process engineer. Open since 2015, it pours a rotating lineup of house-brewed beer, cider, seltzer, and cocktails. In December 2024 the brewery launched Baseline, billed as Kansas City's first locally-owned craft non-alcoholic beer series, brewed in-house to the same standards as its flagship beers. The series debuted in two styles — Baseline Amber, a malt-forward beer with toasty caramel character, and Baseline Pale, a citrus-forward hoppy style — both under 0.5% ABV. The Baseline beers are available on tap at the Crossroads taproom and in to-go four-packs and crowlers. Because the NA beer is house-brewed rather than a stocked national brand, it is a genuine local zero-proof program.

The bar prints a dedicated non-alcoholic menu headlined 'Clear views.': five $13 signature mocktails built on craft NA spirits, from the Ash & Fig (Cut Above zero-proof mezcal, caramelized fig, lime) to a pine-laced Mountain Forager and an NA Espressotini made with Lyre's Amaretti. Best Day Brewing's hazy IPA, Weihenstephaner's NA weissbier and alcohol-removed Mionetto prosecco round out the list. It is an alcohol-forward retailer rather than an alcohol-free one, but its non-alcoholic range is organised as a proper department rather than a single shelf: the shop's own catalogue breaks non-alcoholic stock into beer by style, including pilsner, IPA, sour, dark and cider; wine by colour, including red, white, rose and sparkling; and spirits by category, including gin, whiskey, tequila and mezcal, rum and vodka. Non-alcoholic aperitifs, digestifs and vermouths and ready-to-drink zero-proof cocktails sit alongside them, plus bitters, syrups, mixers and bar tools for building at home.

Its non-alcoholic side is a defined "Zero Proof Libations" menu ($13–$15 per drink) of crafted, mixology-style mocktails rather than token sodas. The list runs four drinks across the dinner, lunch and brunch menus: the Fiori Nero (Fever-Tree Sicilian lemon soda, hibiscus syrup, mint), the Amore Giardino (Fever-Tree cucumber tonic, mint, basil, lemon, orgeat), the Whata Peach (white peach purée, rosemary, lemon-lime soda), and the Grazi 75, built on Almave non-alcoholic blue agave spirit with agave nectar, lemon and seltzer; earlier seasonal options such as Pomelo Paradise, Lavender Lemonade and a non-alcoholic Milano Mule have rotated off, and Michelob Ultra Zero sits on the beer list. Open daily 8am to 2pm for brunch and lunch, it's one of St. Louis's most reliable spots for a booze-free morning out.

Three builds run on Ritual's alcohol-free spirits: the No-jito pairs Ritual rum with fresh mint and soda, the Spicy Paloma runs Ritual tequila against jalapeño and grapefruit, and the French "O"-75 rebuilds a French 75 on the same alcohol-free base. Houston Press named all three in its January 2026 zero-proof guide. In a room whose identity is built on wine, having three spirit-based alternatives that are ordered by name rather than described to a bartender is the difference between being catered for and being accommodated.

The dining room mixes neighbourhood warmth with special-occasion polish - splashes of gold, a living moss wall - and the cooking pairs French technique with local and international ingredients. The bar extends the same care to its non-alcoholic list as to the cocktails: a Citronnade a la Menthe built on a cardamom-lemon cordial, a Pear Collins on zero-proof gin with pear, lemon and ginger beer, and an Old Fashioned riff on American malt with orgeat and aromatic bitters. name: Bright Nights Social
description: Bright Nights Social is an alcohol-free pop-up bar and events platform founded by Sam Bail, running sober dance parties, mixology classes and social gatherings at rotating venues across New York — there is no permanent location, and its own line is that all of NYC is its venue. It has been going since 2022 and has hosted more than 100 events. It was called Third Place Bar until January 2026, when Bail renamed it, writing that three years and nearly a hundred events in, Third Place Bar had grown into many things, just not an actual bricks-and-mortar bar. Her framing of the mission is precise: it is not about sobriety as an identity, but about creating a space where alcohol isn't the default. Events have included tea bars, bagel-making classes and full dance parties with DJs and a complete non-alcoholic bar. Bright Nights Social also presents the NYC's Best Bars for NA awards, which judge the city's non-alcoholic drinks programmes. name: Brooklyn Kava
description: Brooklyn Kava was the borough's first kava bar and remains its defining one — a full-service cafe on Suydam Street in Bushwick, a short walk from the Myrtle-Wyckoff subway hub, open late and serving no alcohol. It opened around 2015; Brooklyn's other early kava bar closed in 2018. The menu runs traditional kava alongside fresh coffee, teas and other non-alcoholic drinks. TWO THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE VISITING. First, its website (brooklynkava.com) is dead — the domain returns a Squarespace "account has expired" error — so Instagram is the only channel it maintains, and current hours and prices are best confirmed there or in person. Its Instagram remains substantial and active, and third-party listings were still being updated in mid-2026, so this is a lapsed website rather than a closed business. Second, it is alcohol-free but not necessarily substance-free: an older directory listing describes kratom being served in hot and iced teas and in mocktails, by red, green, white and yellow vein. We could not confirm that against any current source, and no dosage guidance or age policy is published anywhere we could find. Ask at the counter.

name: Brooklyn Tea
description: Brooklyn Tea is a loose-leaf tearoom in Castleberry Hill, the second location of a specialty tea company founded in Bedford-Stuyvesant in 2017 by tea sommelier Alfonso Wright and his wife Jamila, an Atlanta native. The Atlanta shop opened in February 2022 and is run by Kerri-Ann Thomas, a Spelman graduate and long-time friend of the founders. It carries more than fifty loose-leaf teas served hot or iced, alongside coffee, vegan and non-vegan food, and the company's Notorious B.I.G. cookies. Masala chai lattes, the Cucumber Melon iced tea and the Cold Killer detox blend are the regular orders. No alcohol is served. The company's stated mission is to open tea shops in predominantly Black neighbourhoods where loose leaf has not been readily available. (The Atlanta tearoom appeared to be temporarily closed from early September 2026, with no announcement from the company. Check before you go.)

name: Brunswick Aces
description: Brunswick Aces is billed as Australia's first permanent non-alcoholic bar and bottle shop, an attached distillery in Brunswick East that produces its own zero-proof botanical spirit, Sapiir. Founded by CEO Stephen Lawrence and co-founder Cameron Hunt, the bar pours a 0% cocktail list built on the house Hearts Sapiir - a juniper-forward, wattleseed-scented gin alternative - alongside NA beer from Heaps Normal, and zero-proof wine and spirits from Ovant, NON and Sweden's Gnista. The room has since reopened to serve a small full-strength selection, but the menu and identity remain firmly non-alcoholic-first. It is Australia's first non-alcoholic bar, and it inverts the usual ratio: the menu carries exactly one alcoholic drink, a single gin and tonic, and everything else is alcohol-free.
signatureDrinks: King Louis - coconut water, cucumber-mint cordial and house-distilled Hearts Sapiir (0%)

name: Buena Vida Tea Bar & Garden
description: Buena Vida Tea Bar and Garden is a fully alcohol-free loose-leaf tea bar on Montana Avenue in Santa Monica, founded by Mayra Vazquez, who styles herself and her staff Tearistas. It serves organic loose-leaf teas brewed to order, including on a teapresso machine, alongside sweet and savoury treats, and it has an outdoor tea garden terrace. Named pours include Dragonwell Longjing, China's best-known green; Jasmine Silver Needle, aromatic with floral and citrus notes; Persian Delight, a blend of premium black tea and rose petals; and Rosa de Jamaica, a hibiscus iced tea. The shop also sells teaware, runs a tea club and makes TEArrariums and plant arrangements. Reservations are recommended, and it is closed Mondays. No alcohol is served.

name: Buffalo Traders Lounge
address: 950 Fulton St E, Grand Rapids, MI 49503
description: Buffalo Traders Lounge is a cocktail bar at 950 East Fulton Street in East Hills, describing its remit as bringing the art of cocktail culture to the local community of Grand Rapids. It is routinely named among the better cocktail bars in West Michigan, and it takes zero-proof drinking seriously enough to stock for it specifically, keeping Little Saints and Tor's Tonics behind the bar for non-alcoholic builds. Named options include the Mock Mule, made with lime, simple syrup and ginger beer, and the Better Spritz, built on a non-alcoholic aperitif and soda. The bar will also make a Zero Proof Dealer's Choice, handing the decision to the bartender in the same way its full-proof list does.

name: Builders Arms Hotel
description: This landmark Gertrude Street gastropub, run by chef Andrew McConnell's Trader House group, backs its wine and cocktail program with a genuinely built-out non-alcoholic list. The zero-proof offering spans AF beer, alcohol-free cocktails, AF red, white and sparkling wine, AF spritzes and mocktails, letting a non-drinker order across the full menu rather than settling for soda. It's one of the reasons the pub earns a place on Australian no/low guides Pub With No Booze and NoLo Life, the latter awarding it a full five-star rating for its range of AF and LA drinks. The Gertrude Street pub keeps a well-considered non-alcoholic list of beer and cocktails, under the same Andrew McConnell and Anthony Hammond stewardship the kitchen has had for over a decade.

name: Bula Kafe
description: Bula Kafe is St. Petersburg's original kava bar and coffee house, open in Historic Kenwood since 2009 and tracing its roots to Nakava — North America's first kava bar. The founder, from Vanuatu, built it around noble kava from Vanuatu and the Solomon Islands, served alongside locally roasted coffee, matcha, and ethnobotanical teas in a fully alcohol-free nakamal. A repeat "Best of the Bay" kava winner, it anchors St. Pete's claim as the country's unofficial kava capital — a title earned by dozens of kava bars across Pinellas County. Open 7am to 2am most nights and to 3am at weekends, it is one of the few rooms in the region genuinely available across the whole day without alcohol. Kava is alcohol-free but psychoactive and mildly sedating; alcohol-free is not substance-free.
pressQuoteSourceLabel: Creative Loafing Tampa Bay, Best of the Bay 2021

name: Bula Kava House
description: Bula Kava House opened on 22 March 2011 at 3115 SE Division Street and is one of the oldest kava bars in the United States, marking fifteen years in 2026. Owner Judd Rench's reasoning still heads the site: kava makes a safe alternative to alcohol and other intoxicants, and he figured a Pacific Northwest kava bar would be a great place to socialise or to use something that has been used medicinally for pain, insomnia and anxiety for thousands of years. Kava varieties change daily and are listed on a blackboard rather than published online, so prices for the traditional shells have to be seen in person. What is published: kava shots at $3.50 for 2oz, or a flight of four for $12 — The Glow Up, Dragonfuel, Coconut Kiss and Guava Kava — plus smoothies at $8.25–$9, cold-pressed juices at $6–$9, açaí and yogurt bowls at $10–$16, and $3 wellness shots. NOTE: we found no kratom, kanna, blue lotus or THC anywhere; CBD is sold only as a $2 tincture add-on. But no dosage guidance, age policy or health warning is published anywhere current. Open to midnight, 1am Friday and Saturday.

name: Bula Kavananda
description: Bula Kavananda is a fully alcohol-free kava bar and coffee house in Seminole Heights — the Tampa-side outpost of St. Pete's Bula tribe. It pours kava sourced from Vanuatu alongside ZEAL coffee, botanical and hemp teas, kombucha on tap, yerba mate, and cacao shots, in a community-minded room built for winding down without alcohol. First-timers get a shell of kava on the house.  Open daily 7am to 2am — a nineteen-hour day, and very little else in Tampa is available at either end of it without alcohol as the organising principle. Kava is alcohol-free but psychoactive; alcohol-free is not substance-free.

name: Bundobust Brewery
address: St James Building, 61-69 Oxford Street, Manchester M1 6EQ
description: Bundobust Brewery is the working brewery and 150-seat taproom of the celebrated vegetarian Indian street-food group, set in a converted car park beneath the glass atrium of Oxford Street's grand St James Building. It brews its own beer on site, including KOPRA, a 0.5% alcohol-free double-dry-hopped pale made in collaboration with Manchester's Cloudwater, which pours on the taplist beside a proper Desi non-alcoholic range of iced masala chai, Alphonso mango lassi and Indian sodas. All the food is Gujarati-inspired and fully vegetarian and vegan, so the no-and-low drinker is genuinely catered for rather than an afterthought.

name: Bungalow by Middle Brow
description: Bungalow by Middle Brow is the Logan Square brewery, bakery and pizzeria that Middle Brow Beer Co. opened after eight years of contract brewing, and it runs a properly built non-alcoholic cocktail list under an N-A heading on its drinks menu. Three house zero-proof drinks anchor it: a Middle Brow Paloma with Lyre's N/A tequila, sudachi and sparkling grapefruit; an Amaro Negroni with Seedlip 94, non-alcoholic Amaro Lucano and Lyre's Red Aperitivo; and a Dark and Stormy with Lyre's N/A dark rum, Pathfinder hemp root amaro, lime and ginger beer. A house shrub and soda, an Anti-Zero N/A IPA from Chicago's Revolution Brewing and a Domaine Montrose N/A sparkling rose sit beside them. The room opens at 8am for coffee and toast and runs through naturally leavened pizza in the evening.

name: Burden of Proof
description: Burden of Proof is a fully alcohol-free bottle shop and market on Mission Street in South Pasadena, and by its own count it holds the largest non-alcoholic selection in Los Angeles - more than 450 beers, wines, spirits and ready-to-drink cocktails, alongside specialty groceries. It opened in late 2024, the San Gabriel Valley's first shop of its kind, run by co-owners Obreanna McReynolds and Dean Peterson. The stock spans dealcoholized wine and beer, botanical spirits such as Pathfinder's whiskey alternative, and functional drinks built on adaptogens and nootropics. A free tasting runs every Saturday from 1pm to 4pm, which is the practical answer to a category where a $30 bottle can be a $30 mistake. Nothing sold here contains alcohol.

name: Burdock Brewery
description: Burdock Brewery is a craft brewery and restaurant on Bloor Street West in Bloordale Village, one of three Toronto locations for a brewing company that has been making beer in the city since 2015. Rather than stocking an outside brand, Burdock brews its own non-alcoholic beer line in-house: DuckZ, a 0.5% ABV IPA; Deluxe Zero .5, a 0.5% ABV lager; and Salt Lick, a 0.5% ABV lime sour beer, all sold in 355mL cans. ELLE Gourmet named Burdock's non-alcoholic beer among the city's best. The Bloor St. location pairs its beer shop with a full kitchen serving seasonal, locally sourced food.

name: Burial Beer Co.
description: Burial Beer Co. was born in the summer of 2013 out of a renovated transmission shop at 40 Collier Avenue — as the brewery puts it, before it was the South Slope. Three founders moved from Seattle and opened nine months later on a 30-gallon brewhouse producing 150 barrels a year, with no employees, doing everything themselves including tending the bar. It now anchors Asheville's densest brewing district and has opened outposts elsewhere; the original taproom is the one it calls the crypt from which its story was born. For non-drinkers it keeps a Burial-branded non-alcoholic beer on the board — Chaosmachine, a non-alcoholic IPA under 0.5% ABV made with barley and oats and hopped with Citra and Mosaic — often alongside a second rotating NA option. One of the city's most sought-after beer names therefore has a spot for the non-drinker too. Note that Burial's NA cans are contract-packaged rather than confirmed brewed on site.

description: Burial Beer Co.'s Charlotte outpost, House of Relics, occupies a storied Plaza Midwood building and features 36 draft lines across two bars, a rooftop deck, and a downstairs bottle shop. The taproom carries Burial's own Chaosmachine Non-Alcoholic IPA (under 0.5% ABV) alongside third-party NA options from Untitled Art, giving sober-curious visitors real craft options. Opened in summer 2022, it remains one of Charlotte's most design-forward brewery taprooms.

name: Butcher & Bee
description: Butcher & Bee is a vegetable-forward, Middle Eastern–leaning restaurant in East Nashville's Historic Edgefield, on Main Street. It opened in 2015 as the second location of the Charleston original, founded in 2011 by restaurateur Michael Shemtov; both are now run by Nashville's Honest to Goodness Hospitality group (also behind Redheaded Stranger and Fancypants). The kitchen is known for mezze and shareable plates — whipped feta with fermented honey, hummus bowls, shakshuka, and avocado crispy rice. Every menu carries a dedicated non-alcoholic section. Current zero-proof offerings are a rotating Seasonal Gazoz (a macerated-fruit shrub topped with sparkling water — apricot, rosemary and cardamom at the time of writing) at $10, the Tin Lizzies (Lucano NA Amaro, Crema espresso, Giffard Aperitif Syrup, orange oil) at $12, and Untitled Art's 'American Gold' non-alcoholic lager at $6, plus Boylan's sodas; a Papaw's Punch on earlier menus has been dropped.

name: Butter Bar & Kitchen
hours: Wed-Thu 4:30pm-8:30pm; Fri 4:30pm-9pm; Sat 9am-2pm & 4:30pm-9pm; Sun 9am-2pm & 4:30pm-8pm; Mon-Tue closed
description: Butter Bar & Kitchen is a neighbourhood gastropub in Burlington's New North End, well away from the downtown bar strip, serving burgers, fried chicken, salads and a full weekend brunch with espresso drinks and baked goods. Its ordering menu lists Mocktails as a category in its own right, printed alongside Specialty Cocktails rather than folded into the soft drinks — a small formatting decision that reliably signals a kitchen has actually built the drinks. It is one of very few options for a considered alcohol-free drink outside the city centre. Open Wednesday to Sunday evenings from 4:30pm, with brunch from 9am on Saturday and Sunday.

name: Butterjoint
description: Butterjoint is a bar and restaurant at 208 North Craig Street in North Oakland, serving Pittsburgh comfort food and French bistro classics. It opened next door to Legume in late 2012 under Trevett and Sarah Hooper, and absorbed that restaurant's space when Legume closed for good in February 2020; the Hoopers sold the business in November 2023 to George Austin, who had been their executive chef since 2021 and still runs it. Its non-alcoholic drinks sit under a menu heading called "Hold the Booze" and run across all three lists. There is one house zero-proof cocktail at a time, currently the Concrete Jungle bird ($12) built on house-made non-alcoholic rum and non-alcoholic Campari with pineapple, lime, cinnamon and jalapeño; Leitz sparkling Riesling is poured as the non-alcoholic wine ($10); and the beer list carries Guinness Zero, Bitburger Premium Pils and an Aslin blackberry-and-blueberry sour at $6 a can. The cocktail slot rotates several times a year, so the name changes even though the section does not.

name: The Butterscotch Den
description: The Butterscotch Den on Broadway is the third of the Irish Hospitality Group's Sacramento bars, stocking the same St. Agrestis Phony Negroni and Guinness 0 as the others and staying open to 2am on Friday and Saturday. Its value is location: Broadway and Oak Park sit south of the downtown and Midtown cluster where nearly every other venue in this guide is concentrated, so this covers a part of the city that would otherwise require a drive to drink anything decent without alcohol. It opens at 4pm every day and is the southernmost venue in this guide. Broadway itself has gained restaurants and bars over the past decade, so a night out here no longer means heading into Midtown.

name: Cabin Boys Brewery
description: Cabin Boys is a Tulsa brewery in Kendall-Whittier that keeps Big Drop Brewing Co.'s Pine Trail Pale Ale on for anyone not drinking — a genuine non-alcoholic pale ale at 0.5% from one of the best-regarded alcohol-free brewers in the world, rather than a token domestic lager. In a brewery taproom the specific choice of NA beer matters more than the fact of having one: Big Drop brews to be alcohol-free from the start rather than removing alcohol afterwards, which is why its beers taste like beer. Open from 4pm midweek and noon at weekends, closing at 9pm early in the week and 11pm from Thursday.
signatureDrinks: Big Drop Brewing Co. Pine Trail Pale Ale — non-alcoholic, 0.5%

name: Café Beermoth
description: Café Beermoth is an award-winning independent craft-beer café-bar in Manchester city centre, tucked off Spring Gardens with its public entrance on Brown Street. Run by the team behind the long-running Beermoth beer shop, it was named Central Manchester CAMRA's Pub of the Year 2026 and pours rotating cask and keg alongside a 450-strong bottle-and-can list. Crucially for non-drinkers, its fridges hold a genuinely deep alcohol-free bank led by around eight fresh options from dedicated no-alcohol brewery BRÜLO. A coffee bar by day and a beer café by night, it is an easy alcohol-free choice at any hour.

name: Café Hollander Hilldale
description: Café Hollander sits in the Hilldale shopping district on Madison's west side and works the Belgian café format — a long beer list, mussels and frites, a big terrace. Its relevance here is narrow but real: the kitchen pours non-alcoholic sparkling wine and will build it into a mimosa with orange juice, which sounds slight until you have tried to order brunch without alcohol in a room where everyone else is having one. Madison Eats Food Tours names it in the metro's must-try non-alcoholic round-up on that basis. It is the west side's most convenient sit-down option and one of the few with genuine weekend brunch service.

name: Cafe Jazzy Rose
address: 44 Ionia Ave SW, Grand Rapids, MI 49503
description: Cafe Jazzy Rose is downtown Grand Rapids' first fully alcohol-free cocktail bar, opened in January 2025 at 44 Ionia Avenue SW by hospitality veterans Joseff VanHorn and Ben Kaja. The room is built on a Jazz Age conceit, with a menu organised around iconic jazz locales, and the drinks are botanical zero-proof builds the owners call elixirs rather than mocktails. They are made with adaptogens including lion's mane mushroom, ashwagandha, tulsi, valerian root, hemp and ginseng, and non-alcoholic beer and wine round out the list. The kitchen serves Southern comfort cooking with Cajun and global touches: shrimp and grits, mahi tacos, smash burgers, bowls, soups and salads, alongside vegetarian-forward plates such as lion's mane "crab-less cakes" and the Sun Ra Nut Burger. Nothing on the premises contains alcohol.

name: Cafe La Trova
description: Cafe La Trova is the Calle Ocho bar and Cuban restaurant that put the cantinero tradition back on the international map, ranked #42 on North America's 50 Best Bars in 2024, 2025 and 2026 and #82 on the World's 50 Best Bars list in 2025, with co-founder Julio Cabrera named Roku Industry Icon in 2023. Its bar menu carries a short mocktail section of two named builds, both priced at $10: the Yumislaidy, a long pour of pineapple juice, agave syrup, lime juice, cucumber juice and soda water, and the Mexican Cooler, which uses the non-alcoholic agave spirit Almave Blanco with spicy agave syrup, lime juice and ginger beer. Service starts at 4pm daily and the room stays open to 2am on Friday and Saturday.

description: Café Roze is an all-day café and restaurant in East Nashville's Lockeland Springs area, opened in 2017 by chef-owner Julia Jaksic (a longtime New York chef, formerly of Employees Only and Jack's Wife Freda) with business partner Eric Lincoln. The vegetable-forward kitchen runs from morning coffee and breakfast through afternoon wine and dinner, and was named a Recommended Restaurant in the inaugural 2025 Michelin Guide American South. Its beverage menu carries a genuine, clearly labeled zero-proof selection rather than an afterthought: dedicated "N/A Wines & Kombucha" and "N/A Beer" sections list a Lyre's Classico non-alcoholic sparkling, the St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, Walker Brothers citrus kombucha, and Athletic Brewing's Cerveza N/A. Alongside the bottles, the bar makes a short list of house fizzy drinks at $6 — a Turmeric Cooler, a Beet Root Soda with carrot and lemon, a carrot-and-habanero Firewater, and a cold-brew Coffee Fizz with orange shrub. The Florentina Spritz built on Ritual NA tequila that appeared on earlier menus is no longer listed.

Its drinks card prints a section headed mocktails with five named alcohol-free drinks at $9 to $11, well below the $14 to $16 cocktails. Still in the Bus is fresh blueberries, lavender syrup and club soda; the Ochoa Save is described on the menu as everything you love about a margarita, minus the booze; Le Carre Magique layers pineapple, basil and orange with a coconut-strawberry lime foam; DKR Sunrise combines orange juice, bissap, passion fruit and club soda; and Parisian Sakura is lychee, ginger syrup, lime and club soda. description: Cairo Cafe is a family-owned Egyptian coffee and dessert house on County Road 10 in Blaine, established in 2026. Everything it serves is halal and it holds no liquor licence, so the whole room is alcohol-free; it is also open until 11pm on weeknights, 1am on Friday and Saturday and midnight on Sunday. The drinks board runs an Arabic-coffee section with Turkish coffee, a tea and chai section carrying Adeni black tea with cardamom, Cairo tea with mint, Somali chai and karak, and a long list of specialty lattes. description: Calico is a New American neighbourhood restaurant and bar on Main Street with a seasonal menu built around local farm partnerships, and it prints its non-alcoholic drinks as named cocktails rather than burying them. Three mocktails hold the list: the Midnight Sun on non-alcoholic tequila with acidulated blood orange, cherry, pomegranate and lime; An Orange Lovely with orange, vanilla, lime and cardamom bitters; and the Hat Trick, built on house strawberry coconut water with lemon and nutmeg demerara. name: Callie
description: Callie is a Mediterranean restaurant on Island Avenue in East Village whose drinks list gives non-alcoholic drinkers three separate sections rather than one token line. Five N/A cocktails are priced at sixteen dollars alongside the full-strength list and built on named alcohol-free spirits — Pentire Adrift, the agave distillate Almave, the Scottish spirit Feragaia and a non-alcoholic Amaro Lucano. There is N/A wine by the glass from Lyre's and Leitz, and two Best Day Brewing beers at eight dollars. Every one of those is priced within a dollar or two of its alcoholic equivalent, which is the clearest signal a bar can send about how seriously it takes the category. The kitchen runs Tuesday to Sunday from five until ten and the bar stays open until eleven, so a drink without dinner is a reasonable plan. A four percent service charge funds staff wages and health benefits, stated plainly on the menu.

description: Camellia Tea Bar is a specialty Chinese tea bar in Katong Square, out in the east of the island and well away from the central bar districts, and it is entirely alcohol-free. The house sources premium leaf directly from farms in the Wuyi Mountains in Fujian — the origin for rock oolongs such as Da Hong Pao and for lapsang souchong — and the room is built around unhurried brewing rather than takeaway cups. The stated intention is calm tea culture: quality brewing, an emphasis on slowing down, and no pressure to turn the table. It is a daytime and early-evening venue, open Tuesday to Sunday from 10am to 8pm and closed on Mondays.

name: Camellias at Hotel Bennett
description: A pink, Faberge-inspired champagne lounge on the lobby level of Hotel Bennett on Upper King Street, with an etched-mirror ceiling, crystal chandelier and reclaimed marble. Alongside its champagne, caviar and afternoon tea, Camellias keeps a printed list of non-spirited cocktails built on zero-proof spirits, including The Charleston (Seedlip 108, celery, pistachio, citrus, smoked salt) and The Waring (Seedlip 42, apple, citrus, Codorniu N/A Brut). Each non-spirited build is $16, and the menu notes a rotating selection of non-alcoholic beer and wine alongside them. Standard service runs Monday through Saturday evenings on a walk-in basis, with afternoon tea seatings Thursday through Sunday by reservation. It is one of the more polished settings in Charleston for a serious zero-proof drink.

name: Campfire
description: Campfire is a live-fire New American restaurant in Carlsbad Village, opened in 2016 by restaurateur John Resnick inside a converted mid-century Quonset hut with a 12-foot wood-burning hearth at its center. Executive chef Eric Bost leads a seasonal, communal menu organized into "Trailhead," "Kindling," and "The Fire," and the kitchen earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand and remains in the Michelin Guide. The bar program extends to thoughtful non-alcoholic cocktails: San Diego Magazine highlighted Campfire's zero-proof "Thank You, Please," built from yellow corn, jicama, hoja santa, lime, and koji. The NA offering is culinary-driven and intentional — a fine, ingredient-forward option alongside acclaimed wood-fired food.

name: The Campground
description: The Campground is an intimate aperitivo cocktail bar and restaurant in Kansas City's Historic West Bottoms, opened December 3, 2018 in the former Genessee Royale Bistro space. It grew from a 2012 backyard cocktail-party hangout into a brick-and-mortar known for woodsy, foraged-leaning craft cocktails, a natural-wine list, and seasonal small plates. Its zero-proof program is genuine and built into the printed menu: a dedicated "N/A Options" section mirrors the bar's spirit-forward style. The non-alcoholic Gimlet pairs an N/A blood-orange aperitif with wild mint, white sage, and lemon; the N/A Spritz layers that aperitif with non-alcoholic sparkling Pinot Noir and soda; and the N/A Margarita and Paloma are built on Strongwater (Denver) zero-proof spirits. Best Day Brewing NA lager, Topo Lupo hop water, and Casamara Club soda round out the lineup. The Campground was a 2024 James Beard Award semifinalist.

A working farm is the ideal pantry for alcohol-free drinking, because the produce is the point and the spirit was never carrying the flavour. Free live jazz runs every Tuesday, the kitchen serves until 1am nightly, and rotating food pop-ups take over several nights a week.

Named builds include the Safe Harbor (a smoky zero-proof negroni on Pathfinder NA aperitivo), the Just Like a Spritz (Giffard non-alcoholic aperitif cordial, sparkling, citrus), the savory-fruity Funky Fresh (strawberry, pineapple, NA beer, black pepper), and a house passionfruit ginger lemonade.

The all-day menu of coffee, tea and specialty drinks (OJ & Kush, Cucumber Frost, Riverwalk and more) is built to be ordered straight, spirited, or botanically infused. name: Cannon Ball Lounge
description: Cannon Ball Lounge sits six floors up on the roof of Hotel Indy on East Washington Street, and is the only indoor-outdoor rooftop bar downtown — which matters in a city with four distinct seasons. It is named for Erwin "Cannonball" Baker, the Indianapolis motorcyclist who rode in the first Indianapolis 500 and set transcontinental records for decades afterwards, and the drinks list leans on local reference points throughout. The non-alcoholic drinks are a printed zero-proof section rather than an afterthought: I Miss My Spritz is built on DHOS Bittersweet Aperitif and non-alcoholic sparkling wine, Good Graces runs lemon, guava and honey against New Orleans non-alcoholic bitters and ginger beer, and the Tail of Thyme uses a house plum-lavender syrup.

name: Canon
description: Canon is a 32-seat cocktail bar and small restaurant at 928 12th Avenue on Capitol Hill, opened in 2011 by Jamie Boudreau, and it holds one of the largest spirits collections in the world — over 4,000 labels, around 2,500 of them whiskey, shelved along the hallway and even in the bathrooms. Boudreau designed the back bar so guests would feel utterly, lavishly wrapped up in bottles. ACCURACY NOTE: Canon is frequently credited online with winning the 2019 James Beard Award for Outstanding Bar Program. It did not — that award went to Bar Agricole in San Francisco. Canon was a James Beard semifinalist in the same category in 2014. Its non-alcoholic drinks sit in their own printed section headed "Sans", each prepared without alcohol at $20: POG the Magic Dragon (passion fruit, orange, guava, black "horchata"), I'm Longan Ver-Jus (longan, pear, verjus blanc, sparkling rosé), Tropical "Julius" (mango, pineapple, starfruit, passion fruit, orange, vanilla, milk, frozen) and Cascadian Norteño (Pathfinder amaro, Mexican vanilla cold brew, chicory, sarsaparilla). It sits at 5230 S Harper Ave, steps from Williams' other Hyde Park spots, Virtue and Daisy's Po-Boy & Tavern, and was developed with longtime collaborator Jesus Garcia, with the tiki-leaning cocktail menu consulted on by veteran Chicago bartender Paul McGee. Tequila and mezcal anchor the drink list, but the bar runs a genuine "Spirit Free" section that gets the same fresh-juice, house-syrup and garnish treatment as the alcoholic menu. Named zero-proof options include the Verdita (pineapple, lime, mint, jalapeño) and the Horchata Fizz (coconut water, in-house almond orgeat, cinnamon, ginger beer), plus a spirit-free Margarita and non-alcoholic Corona. The room, designed by Erin Boone with nods to architect Luis Barragán, features pink accents, terracotta tiles and mesquite woodwork.

name: Cardellino
description: Cardellino is the Italian-American room in chef Brad Wise's group, on Goldfinch Street in Mission Hills, making handmade pasta and pizza alongside a bar that prints a Spirit Free section. Four entries run from a ten-dollar cantaloupe and mint limeade made in house, through Bella Vita on a non-alcoholic aperitif with orange and raspberry at thirteen, to Solar Flare at fourteen — aplós arise with lemon, ginger and turmeric — with Athletic Brewing's non-alcoholic golden ale at eight. The limeade matters as much as the two spirit builds: it is the one drink on the list for a guest who would rather avoid spirit analogues altogether, and it is made to order rather than poured. Dinner runs Tuesday to Sunday from five, until ten on Friday and Saturday, with a happy hour in the first hour of service. The room is small and pasta-led, so weekend reservations are advisable.

name: Casa Cacao
description: Casa Cacao is Columbus' first kava and cacao bar, opened in 2024 by Ayala Wolak on East Hudson Street in Old North Columbus. No alcohol is served. The menu is built around two plant ingredients — kava, a root native to the Pacific Islands that is prepared as a drink for its relaxant effect, and ceremonial-grade cacao, ground to a paste and spiced. Alongside them sit a full espresso programme, loose teas, kombucha, hot chocolate and alcohol-free wine. Kava is a psychoactive botanical rather than an inert soft drink: Wolak has said each drink carries roughly a tablespoon and a half of kava powder, and concentrated shots are sold alongside the milder 12-ounce teas. The room occupies a long-dormant building that has been a theatre, a barbershop and a church, and it runs $5 kava on Thursday and Saturday evenings.

name: Casadonna
description: Casadonna is the coastal Italian restaurant on North Bayshore Drive at the southern edge of Edgewater, with a dining room and terrace facing Biscayne Bay. Its documented alcohol-free build is the Donna d'Oro, made with Almave Ámbar — a distilled blue agave spirit with no alcohol — balanced with pineapple and lime, which puts a genuine agave backbone under a drink that would otherwise be a fruit cooler. Secret Miami described the restaurant in December 2025 as an ideal destination for booze-free sips, and RESIDENT wrote that the drink channels coastal Italian ease while maintaining structure and depth. Dinner runs nightly from 5pm, with lunch on Saturday and brunch on Sunday.

name: CASBAR Lounge

description: CASBAR Lounge is the 24-hour cocktail lounge on the casino floor at SAHARA Las Vegas, at the quieter north end of the Strip, with live music every evening and a room built for sitting rather than passing through. Its non-alcoholic menu is unusually developed for a casino bar: rather than stripping the spirit out of a cocktail and serving what is left, the bar reaches for low- and no-ABV substitutes and rebuilds classics properly, working largely with Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits so that the juniper of a gin drink or the vanilla of a whiskey drink is still there. Documented builds include an N/A Old Fashioned made with Lyre's American Malt and an N/A Raspberry Mojito made with Lyre's White Cane Spirit. The Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority named it among seven must-try spirit-free stops in the city, and Best of Las Vegas awarded the lounge Bronze for Best Cocktail Bar in 2024. Because it never closes, it is one of the few genuinely round-the-clock spirit-free options in Las Vegas.

A printed section rather than an off-menu favour is the distinction that matters here: it has to be stocked, trained on and kept through every menu redesign, which is why so few restaurants on this strip bother.

It's craft NA to order rather than a separate printed list, but the builds are executed to the same standard as the full-proof menu.

The kitchen runs a half-pound Ditka Burger at $18, seafood tagliatelle with bay scallops, lump crab and shrimp at $26, and a Sonoma chicken salad at $21, with happy hour weekdays from 3pm to 6pm and oysters at $2.50. Its printed "Zero Proof Cocktails" section holds four drinks at a flat $11: Almost Rita (Lyre's non-alcoholic blanco, cold-pressed lime, agave), No-Jito (Lyre's non-alcoholic white cane, mint, cold-pressed lime), Hibiscus Rose Fizz (hibiscus-infused water, rose, ginger beer) and Lavender Lemonade (lemonade, lavender-infused syrup, cold-pressed lemon, fizzy water). Best Day Brewing's non-alcoholic Kölsch is $6.

Heineken 0.0 is on the beer list. The section is offered the other way round too — any of the three can be made spirited for a small supplement, which is a rare and genuinely useful courtesy for a mixed table where one person is drinking and another is not.

Alongside kava it pours teas, coffee and ginger kombucha, and blends smoothies with kratom, kava and CBD. name: Ceremony
description: Ceremony is Hampton Roads' dedicated dry bottle shop and the anchor of the region's alcohol-free scene — a curated wall of non-alcoholic beer, wine and spirits alongside mixers, bitters and sustainable bar tools, run on a zero-waste model. It was founded in Virginia Beach in 2022 and has since grown to multiple locations across Virginia and into North Carolina, which makes it one of the few alcohol-free retailers anywhere to have proven the format can scale. The Norfolk shop on Baldwin Avenue is the flagship, and the company has extended beyond retail into a non-alcohol pop-up bar inside a local coffee shop.

name: Châm Pang Lanes
description: Châm Pang Lanes is a bowling alley, bar and Vietnamese-leaning kitchen on Harney Street in downtown Omaha, and it is listed in the city's own curated drinks guide for its spirit-free offerings. The format is the argument for it: bowling gives an evening a structure that is not the round, which is consistently the single most useful thing for someone who does not drink, and the room is busy and social without the pace being set by anyone's glass. Open from 4pm, to midnight midweek and 2am on Friday and Saturday, with a noon start at weekends. Lanes book up at weekends, so reserve ahead if bowling is the plan.

name: Char & Stave
description: Char & Stave is an all-day cafe and cocktail bar in Ardmore, opened March 21, 2022 by Jared Adkins, owner and master distiller of Phoenixville's Bluebird Distilling, with head distiller Scott Gilbert. The concept — "coffee made by whiskey people" — uses Bluebird's spent bourbon barrels to age coffee beans, drawing vanilla, caramel, and spice notes into the roast. The 42-seat space pours espresso, nitro cold brew, barrel-aged espresso, and signature lattes by day, then shifts to cocktails in the evening. For zero-proof drinkers, the menu carries a dedicated, clearly labeled section, "Handcrafted Non-Alcoholic Options, for here or to-go," that mirrors the cocktail list. Named alcohol-free builds include a Barrel-Aged "Old Fashioned," a Matcha "Mojito," an Espresso Tonic, a Chai Blossom, Espresso Y Amaro, and Flora & Fauna. A second location operates in Chestnut Hill.

name: Charlie was a sinner.
description: Charlie was a sinner. is an all-vegan cocktail bar and small-plates restaurant in Philadelphia's Midtown Village, opened in 2014 by Nicole Marquis, the restaurateur behind the HipCityVeg and Bar Bombón plant-based ventures. The dimly lit, candle-lit room — brass bar top, button-tufted banquettes, antique fixtures — is fully plant-based across food and drink. Its craft cocktail program runs deep, and alongside the spirited list it keeps a standing "Zero Proof" section of roughly four non-alcoholic cocktails around $11, built on house-made syrups, cordials, and even a house-made zero-proof gin rather than off-the-shelf substitutes. Current zero-proof pours include No Regrets (house zero-proof gin, lemon, sparkling water), Spicy Pineapple (pineapple, agave, lime, house spice blend), a Basil Fennel Lemon Soda, and a Blackberry Ginger Soda. Visit Philly highlights it as "an upscale respite" on alcohol-heavy 13th Street that "always has several zero-proof options."

description: Chartreuse Sisters is a French-American fusion patisserie and dry bar at 800 Wealthy Street SE, owned and run by sisters Alyson and Mallory Caillaud-Jones. Alyson heads the beverage program and Mallory is head pastry chef, and the shop's own tagline lists what it sells in order: pastries, NA cocktails, espresso. No alcohol is served. The pastry side is French-American — eclairs, large macarons, savoury galettes — on a menu that rotates monthly around local seasonal fruit and vegetables, made in house and sourced locally where possible. The non-alcoholic cocktail list rotates alongside it. The pair started out baking in their parents' home kitchen before opening the storefront, which occupies a preserved historic building on Wealthy Street.

name: Chattanooga Culture
description: Chattanooga Culture is a fermentation lab on Vance Avenue with a kombucha and kava lounge attached, established in 2022 as a holistic wellness-led food and beverage company. It brews its own kombucha locally and works across cultured foods more broadly, serving that alongside kava and handcrafted mocktails in a small lounge space, and it sells at the Main Street Farmers Market as well. Nothing it pours contains alcohol. The lounge keeps limited but genuinely social hours — noon to 6pm on Thursday and noon to 10pm on Friday and Saturday — and programmes events including sound baths in the room.

name: Cheeky & Dry
description: Cheeky & Dry is Seattle's first and only fully alcohol-free bottle shop, a 750-square-foot family-owned store at 6120 Phinney Ave N opened in November 2023 by Kirstin and Yura Vracko. Kirstin started it after her husband went to rehab for alcohol use and she stopped drinking in solidarity with him, looking for products that would carry her through the ritual of a drink at night — she has said she built the shop she wished existed. Its own rule is absolute: every bottle is 0.5% ABV or less. The catalogue runs to roughly 250 products across non-alcoholic spirits (gin, whiskey, agave, aperitivo), wines still and sparkling, beers, ready-to-drink cocktails, mixers and bitters, with brands including Pathfinder, Three Spirit, Little Saints, Parch, Aplos, Free Spirits, Leilo and Opius. There is a counter for tasting samples before you buy. NOTE FOR ANYONE AVOIDING ALL INTOXICANTS: we checked the full catalogue and found no THC at all, but it does stock kava products, one kava-and-kratom elixir, and one CBD coffee at 25mg per serving.

name: Chelsea Corner
description: Chelsea Corner is a long-running Knox-Henderson neighbourhood bar with a big patio, and it keeps a printed Zero Proof / Mocktail Menu that is deeper than most dedicated cocktail bars manage. Ritual Zero Proof does the heavy lifting: a zero-proof espresso martini, a Tommy's margarita and a cucumber mint spritz that adds Lyre's Classico. Beyond the cocktails there is Lyre's sparkling by the glass or as mimosas and bellinis, a michelada built on Heineken 0.0, and several Athletic Brewing varieties. It opens at ten on weekend mornings and runs to two on Friday and Saturday nights, so it works as an actual night out rather than a dinner reservation.

name: Chez Maggy
description: Chez Maggy is the ground-floor French restaurant of the Thompson Denver hotel on Market Street, and the first restaurant outside Los Angeles from Michelin-starred chef Ludo Lefebvre. It is named for Lefebvre's late mother-in-law Margaret, a Colorado native who was killed by a drunk driver in 2019 — context that gives the restaurant's zero-proof list more weight than a hotel bar's usual courtesy offering. Visit Denver describes a delectable selection of zero-proof cocktails, naming the Earl Grey Bliss, built on tea-infused Ritual zero-proof gin with lemon and honey, and a St. Agrestis Phony Negroni made with the brand's non-alcoholic mezcal. The kitchen applies the same approach to the food, cooking classic French dishes with Colorado ingredients. Bar M, in the hotel lobby, is the companion cocktail room.

name: Cholita Taqueria
description: Cholita is a Los Angeles-style taqueria on Broad Ripple Avenue serving tacos and Mexican street food, with a bar that takes its non-alcoholic drinks seriously enough to build them from a proper base. The Fauxjito is the drink Indy Maven picked out: Seedlip Garden 108 — the herbal expression made from peas, rosemary, thyme and spearmint — worked into a mojito structure with lime and mint, so the herbal weight comes from the distillate rather than from sugar. In a neighbourhood whose bar scene runs heavily to margaritas and late-night drinking, a restaurant with a competent zero-proof build and a full dinner menu is a genuinely useful thing to know about.

name: Chop Steakhouse & Bar
description: Chop Steakhouse & Bar is a modern steakhouse on Grand Avenue in the centre of Coconut Grove, open from 11am every day and running to midnight from Wednesday through Saturday, which makes it one of the later kitchens in the Grove. Its alcohol-free list runs to three named builds rather than a single afterthought: a Sparkling Yuzu Limeade, a more herbaceous Green Tea Sour, and a Berry Shrub that brings mixed berries together with ginger beer, fresh citrus, cane sugar and a hint of balsamic — a genuine shrub build rather than a sweetened juice. Secret Miami documented all three in December 2025. The restaurant serves brunch, lunch, happy hour, dinner and a late-night menu.

name: Chyna Club at Fontainebleau Las Vegas
address: 2777 S Las Vegas Blvd, Level 1, Las Vegas, NV 89109
description: Chyna Club is an upscale Chinese restaurant and cocktail destination on level 1 of Fontainebleau Las Vegas, a concept from Wagamama and Hakkasan founder Alan Yau set adjacent to the casino floor and high-limit gaming area. Its beverage program, overseen by Director of Beverage Development Juyoung Kang, treats zero-proof drinks with the same culinary rigor as its full cocktails, using teas for tannin and umami, starches for mouthfeel, and oils that coat the palate. The signature non-alcoholic creation, "Heaven," is built from rice-water tea infusion, oleo-saccharum (citrus-infused sugared oil), fig jam and Supasawa, while "Made You Look" pairs jasmine pearl and green tea with cucumber and watermelon, taking its lilac hue from color-shifting butterfly pea tisane. Kang told Las Vegas Weekly that interest in mocktails has grown because "we raised the conversation and we raised their awareness, [so] people are more confident in ordering it." The restaurant is open evenings (typically Wednesday-Sunday, 5:30-9:30pm), with business-casual attire and reservations recommended.

name: Cinderlands Beer Company
description: Cinderlands Beer Company was founded in 2017 by two married couples — Jamie and Joanna Warden and Paul and Emily Schneider — and its Warehouse on Smallman Street in the Strip District is its largest site and main production centre: 17,500 square feet in an 1880 building, two 40-foot bars with sixteen draft lines, a built-in bocce court, dome hockey and shuffleboard, and a covered, heated second-floor patio. Its own non-alcoholic line is Hop Run, a 0.0% sparkling hop water brewed and canned in Pittsburgh that showcases Citra and Mosaic hops, sold as a 12oz can ($4) and used as the base of a small printed section called "Hop Run Mocktails": a Cranberry Lime Refresher and a Hop Run Mule, both $6. Food is smokehouse pub cooking — smoked wings ($12), pulled pork ($13), a jumbo pretzel ($15) — with a kids' menu. The taproom took a Great American Beer Festival gold medal in 2021.

Co-founder Kris Nelson also helped develop Zero Gravity's Rescue Club non-alcoholic beer, which makes this one address responsible for two of the three alcohol-free drinks Vermont producers are best known for. The zero-proof drinks are a full named section of the menu, "Refrescos Sin Alcohol," priced at $11-12 alongside the mezcal cocktails rather than buried at the back. House-made ingredients carry the list: El Curandero blends the kitchen's tres chiles shrub with limon, Topo Chico and chile salt; Malabarista is built on house beet kvass with ginger, tamarindo, pina and a turmeric-marigold salt; and Horchata Real layers house black rice-coconut-pandan horchata with Cafe de Chiapas cold brew and raw wildflower honey. The bar comprises a 38-seat Lounge serving à la carte food and drinks, plus a nine-seat Studio offering a five-course tasting with cocktail pairings. Like EMP, the food is fully plant-based. description: Clio is an Old Market restaurant and bar on Howard Street in Omaha, open 11am to 10pm most days and to 11pm at weekends — the widest hours of any venue in this guide. Its alcohol-free offer covers all three of the things a non-drinker actually wants: a built cocktail in the Apricotta, a low-sugar long drink in its shrub and soda, and a proper beer in Athletic Brewing's Run Wild IPA. Most venues manage one of those three. A shrub — fruit preserved in vinegar — is the component that gives an alcohol-free drink acidity and savoury depth rather than sweetness, and having one on the menu is a reliable sign the bar makes its own.

The bar changes its whole menu on a schedule and publishes each one as a numbered volume rather than a list, so regulars track it by book number rather than by season; the current edition is Book 22, "Whiskey Bent & Hellbound". description: Cobalt Grille is a Laskin Road restaurant in Virginia Beach's Hilltop area whose non-alcoholic drinks are the work of a named mixologist, Windsor Swink, rather than an anonymous back-bar decision. That attribution is the signal worth acting on: when a venue credits a person with its zero-proof creations, the drinks tend to be developed rather than improvised, and they tend to stay on the menu. It shares an address block with Ceremony's Virginia Beach outlet inside Painted Tree Boutiques, which makes the two an easy pairing for anyone on the beach side of Hampton Roads. Note it opens at 3pm and closes entirely on Sundays, which catches people out.

name: Cobra
description: Cobra is an Asian-American bar on South High Street in the Brewery District, opened in October 2023 by four owners — Alex Chen and Jack Bennett, who helped open Watershed Kitchen + Bar, and David Yee and Josh Spiers, both previously of Oddfellows. It bills itself as a "good night bar," pairing a cocktail programme built on Asian ingredients with handmade noodles served late. The non-alcoholic drinks are treated as an extension of that flavour perspective rather than a fallback: the Pool Float is a no-proof build that carries the serrano and cilantro notes of the bar's Above Ground Pool cocktail, and All Gas No Brakes is a no-proof boilermaker pairing Pathfinder's non-alcoholic amaro with a locally owned non-alcoholic IPA. Bar manager David Yee was one of the bartenders Forbes surveyed on 2025 drink trends.

name: Codependent Cocktails + Coffee
description: Codependent Cocktails + Coffee is an all-day cocktail and coffee bar at the base of The Independent condo tower in downtown Austin, opened by Kevin Burns and Merrill Alley of design firm Urbanspace. The concept is Italian luxury meets Austin hospitality — mid-century modern interiors, floor-to-ceiling windows, aperitivo culture-inspired drinks, and an Instagram-friendly aesthetic that doubles as a coworking spot before 4pm (the cutoff after which laptops are no longer welcome). The cocktail program is well-regarded across Austin's bar scene, and Visit Austin's official tourism blog highlights Codependent's non-alcoholic offerings as one of the strongest in town, calling out the Well Manoered Monk (NA tequila, cucumber, pineapple) and Tell Me Something Good (prickly pear, coconut water). The menu also includes Athletic Brewing non-alcoholic beer alongside the broader coffee and cocktail program. A private speakeasy with homemade ingredients sits behind the main bar.

name: Colita
description: Colita is a Tex-Oaxacan restaurant from chef Daniel del Prado's DDP Restaurant Group (the Martina and Bar La Grassa team), open since October 2018 in a converted former gas station at 54th & Penn in southwest Minneapolis's Armatage neighborhood. Named after del Prado's first dog, it pairs Oaxacan-influenced barbecue, creative tacos, and mole-driven dishes with a well-regarded bar program in a fully gluten-free kitchen. The drinks menu carries a dedicated "Zero Proof" section of four house-made, $10 non-alcoholic cocktails built with the same care as its alcoholic list — fruit-, herb-, and tea-forward sodas finished with carbonation. Named pours include the rose-and-raspberry Rosas, the citrus-and-lychee Naranjitas, a cinnamon coconut-milk Horchata, and the honey-sarsaparilla 3leche Miele. The brewery brews its own line of non-alcoholic beers - a 0.4% ABV Non-Alcoholic IPA hopped with Citra, Simcoe and Mosaic, a 0.4% ABV Hazy Pale Ale hopped with Mosaic and Citra, and an under-0.5% ABV Emerald Non-Alcoholic Stout - and stocks them in the on-site retail store alongside its full portfolio of beers, cocktails, spirits and glassware. blogTO has described it as "a popular Hamilton brewer now boasting a Toronto location."

name: Comfort Kitchen
description: Comfort Kitchen is a restaurant and cafe in Upham's Corner, Dorchester, opened in January 2023 inside a restored 1912 comfort station on Columbia Road. The kitchen cooks what it calls global comfort food, tracing ingredients and techniques of the African diaspora from Asia to the Americas. Its drinks program is unusually deliberate about non-alcoholic service: the bar list is split into cocktails and a standing 'Free-Spirited Cocktails' section, and the rotating wine and beer selection includes N/A options. General manager and beverage director Kyisha Davenport built the program around the same pantry the kitchen uses, with Nepali timur pepper, West African suya spice and Middle Eastern sumac appearing in drinks on both sides of the menu. The cafe side pours coffee, espresso and tea.

name: Common Tiger
description: Common Tiger is a hidden speakeasy in downtown Mission, Kansas, opened quietly in August 2024 by Abby Hans alongside her family. The bar is concealed behind a faux neighborhood corner store stocked with chips, cereal, and soaps; guests with the password are led past the shelves into a dim, tiger-themed lounge with red couches, music, and a small dance floor. The cocktail list rotates monthly around seasonal themes, and the kitchen turns out snacks and pizza. Its zero-proof side is small but genuine: bartenders build named mocktails such as the Starlight (a light pear-lemon soda) and the Filthy Chai (a spirit-free dirty chai), pour the dessert-style Pink Pony Club, and will spin up non-alcoholic versions of cocktails like the Bad Blood Mule on request. description: Commune is a wine bar and hi-fi listening room in Avondale Estates, opened May 8, 2024 by Zopi Kristjanson and music producer/DJ Chris Devoe inside the Olive + Pine development. The wine list is curated by James Beard-nominated sommelier Steven Grubbs, formerly of Empire State South, who keeps an esoteric but approachably priced by-the-glass and bottle program. The space pairs that list with seasonal small plates and a nightly schedule of DJ sets and live performances spanning jazz, funk, Afrobeat, psych rock and post-punk. Alongside wine, cocktails, beer and tea, Commune maintains a standing N/A Drinks category for non-drinkers: a St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, an Oddbird Blanc de Blanc non-alcoholic sparkling chardonnay, an Aplos Ume Spritz, Athletic Upside Dawn and sparkling mineral water. The same list also carries an Afterdream Tropical THC Tonic, which is alcohol-free but psychoactive. The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reviewed the room favorably in August 2024, praising its creative, frequently changing food menu, well-trained staff and fair pricing.

name: Community Beer Co.
description: Community Beer Co. is a Dallas brewery, distillery, and taproom-restaurant founded by Kevin Carr in 2013, now housed in a sprawling former ExxonMobil campus near the Design District. Beyond its alcoholic lineup, Community brews its own non-alcoholic beer under the "Nada" label — making it one of relatively few breweries producing zero-proof beer in-house rather than reselling outside brands. The non-alcoholic range now runs to two beers: Nada IPA, hopped with Mosaic, Sabro and Simcoe, and Texas Free, a non-alcoholic lite beer, each roughly 25 calories, 5g carbs and under 0.5% ABV. A Nada Hazy IPA, Pilsner and Bock and a hop-infused "Hop'd Water" were previously part of the family but have been dropped from the published lineup as of August 2026. Note that the taproom also pours THC seltzers, listed on the same beverage menu, which readers avoiding intoxicants of any kind will want to know before ordering. Nada IPA earned a Bronze medal in the Non-Alcohol Beer category at the 2022 Great American Beer Festival. The Nada beers are poured and sold at the family- and dog-friendly taproom alongside food from the on-site kitchen.

name: Compère Lapin
description: Compère Lapin is the New Orleans flagship of James Beard Award-winning chef Nina Compton, opened in June 2015 inside The Old No. 77 Hotel & Chandlery in the Warehouse District. Born and raised in St Lucia and a Top Chef runner-up, Compton melds Caribbean cooking with French and Italian technique; she won Best Chef: South in 2018 and was a Food & Wine Best New Chef in 2017. The name means "Brother Rabbit", a trickster figure from her St Lucian childhood. The restaurant was the first in New Orleans to win a Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Award for Best American Hotel Bar, and it made OpenTable's Top 100 Hotel Restaurants in America for 2025. Its drinks list carries a "Non-Alc and Mocktails" section: a house Sorrel Tea ($8) of spiced hibiscus with ginger, lavender and lime; Silly Songs With Larry ($8) with cucumber, ginger, sesame, rice vinegar, chilli and soda; Athletic Brewing's Run Wild non-alcoholic IPA ($7); and a Unified Ferments jasmine green tea ($10 a glass, $40 a bottle). Dinner nightly from 5.30pm.

The bar runs a root-to-stem cocktail programme alongside natural wine and herbal digestifs, and marks its non-alcoholic options directly on the printed menu: cocktails available zero-proof carry a degree symbol, currently the Vermouth + Tonic at $8, the Alta Highball at $10 and the Comune Sour at $14. Esquire named it one of the 27 best bars in America in 2021. It is owned by executive chef Josh Ross, music curator John Shannon and beverage director Aimee Marshall. The non-alcoholic section carries two built cocktails — an N/A Painkiller with coconut cream, orange, pineapple and nutmeg, and an N/A Mojito ($10) — plus Eins-Zwei-Zero 0% sparkling Riesling ($12), a Bravas non-alcoholic golden ale ($6) and a rotating NA beer. description: Copra is a coastal South Indian restaurant that opened in 2023 in San Francisco's Fillmore / Lower Pac Heights neighborhood, led by Michelin-starred chef Srijith "Sri" Gopinathan, drawing on the cuisines of Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Alongside a full cocktail and wine program, Copra runs a serious zero-proof menu that mirrors its cocktail list, building drinks from the same Southeast Asian-leaning pantry — coconut yogurt, makrut lime, star anise, lemongrass, and orange blossom — rather than treating non-alcoholic options as an afterthought. Several of the zero-proof cocktails are built on non-alcoholic spirits including Wilderton Lustre and Vibrante NA vermouth. The space features a stone bar, a dimly lit lounge, and an open-air rooftop patio, with snacks like black truffle popcorn and tinned fish. The drink menu is organized into Standards, House, and a dedicated Zero-Proof section that co-owner Kristopher Esqueda says "doesn't feel like an afterthought." Confirmed zero-proof options include the Neo-Tropical (Giffard N/A Aperitivo, pineapple, ginger, lime soda), the Chaise Lounge (coconut water, cucumber, lime, soda), a St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, Sanbitter, and Corona 0%.

description: Cordelia opened in 2022 at 2058 East Fourth Street, the downtown block that has carried Cleveland's restaurant reputation for two decades, from chef Vinnie Cimino and co-owner Andrew Watts. Cimino describes the cooking as Midwest melting pot meets modern grandma — a celebration of the region's farmers run through the immigrant home cooking the city was built on — and the recognition arrived fast: Cleveland Magazine named it Best New Restaurant in 2023, Cimino was a James Beard Award finalist, and Food & Wine made him a Best New Chef in 2025. Rather than keeping a token mocktail list, the bar rebuilds cocktails from the main menu using Lyre's and Seedlip and its own syrups, at the same prices as the originals.

Alongside 120-plus hard-to-find wines, vermouths, ciders, and bottled cocktails, CORK has built one of the Philadelphia region's largest non-alcoholic selections, branding itself "Dry Bar Headquarters." Per a 2023 Philadelphia Inquirer feature, buyer Michelle Flisek said the store carries more than 100 varieties of zero-proof items, including Ritual Zero Proof spirits, Lyre's Aperitif Rosso, Spiritless tequila alternative, and canned Ghia apéritifs. description: Cosmic Coffee + Cocktails is a large South Austin garden bar and coffee house built around a landscaped outdoor space with food trucks, native planting and a pond, and it runs from 8am to late every day — which is what makes it genuinely useful to a non-drinker. The same counter that pulls espresso in the morning builds zero-proof cocktails at night, including a Zero-Proof Espresso Martini that bridges the two, and Liquid Sunshine, a pitaya-based energy elixir. description: Cosmic Roots is a fully alcohol-free kava and tea house tucked inside Ferndale's Pavilion Street Market food hall, the only non-food stall among the market's vendors. Its named non-alcoholic cocktails include The Resolution, made with Martini & Rossi Floreal, cranberry, lime, ginger beer, and orgeat, and the Sparkling Conviction, made with blood orange, lemon, Lyre's Classico, and All the Bitter zero-proof aromatic bitters, alongside a spirit-free Aperol-style spritz. Because the whole room is built around bubbles, ordering a booze-free toast reads as native here rather than an afterthought. The zero-proof list was spotlighted by CultureMap and PaperCity for Dry January.

name: The Cowfish Sushi Burger Bar
description: A sushi-and-burger hybrid restaurant at Universal CityWalk known for its 'Burgushi' mashups, The Cowfish runs a small but genuinely crafted mocktail list built around fresh fruit, house syrups, and ginger beer.

name: Craft Lounge
description: Craft Lounge in Nampa keeps a Non-Alcoholic Old Fashioned and a Virgin Mule on its standing list. The Old Fashioned is the notable one, because it is the hardest classic to render without alcohol — the drink is essentially whiskey, sugar and bitters, so there is nowhere for a substitute to hide. A bar willing to put its name on one is making a real claim. With The Sick Stag a few minutes away, Craft Lounge gives the western end of the Treasure Valley a second option rather than a single point of failure. It keeps a sibling location in nearby Caldwell and serves from 3pm, closing at midnight on Friday and Saturday.

name: Crafted Cocktail Bar
address: 116 A S Main St, Greenville, SC 29601
description: Crafted Cocktail Bar is a small room on South Main in downtown Greenville trading on made-to-order drinks, and it surfaces consistently in searches for zero-proof cocktails in the city. It keeps early and short hours for a cocktail bar — 4pm to 9pm Monday through Thursday and to 10pm on Friday and Saturday, closed Sunday — which makes it an after-work stop rather than a late one, and a good first drink of an evening that continues elsewhere on the same block. This entry is graded conservatively: the alcohol-free offer is real but undocumented in detail.

description: CrowBar is the cocktail lounge and tasting room for Voliere Spirits, an all-women-owned distillery that opened in December 2025 in the former blacksmith shop of the historic Hamm's Brewery complex in Dayton's Bluff. Grete Bergland leads the drinks programme, and the zero-proof column is built with the same culinary approach as the rest of the list and priced at $8 — a flat rate across every non-alcoholic drink. The builds are savoury as often as sweet: one runs roasted strawberry and tomato with balsamic and champagne vinegar, caper, basil, aquafaba and prosciutto; another is charred citrus with baking spices, rosemary, lemon and soda water. House-made French and Italian sodas sit alongside.

name: Crumb & Spigot
description: Crumb & Spigot is a gastropub and cocktail bar at 15322 Detroit Avenue in Lakewood, a few doors from Humble Wine Bar and the second room of a Chagrin Falls original. The format is wood-fired pizza with an unusually large share of the menu marked vegan and gluten-free — enough that it works as the default choice for a mixed group rather than as an accommodation bolted onto the end of the list. The bar built its non-alcoholic offering on purpose, the owners describing the aim as providing a different avenue versus just normal cocktails, and the drinks are constructed accordingly. The Sober Clover at $12 is a straight zero-proof reading of a clover club: grenadine, apple cider vinegar, citrus and egg white, shaken hard to a proper foam. Dinner six nights a week, closed Mondays, to 11pm on Fridays.
signatureDrinks: Sober Clover (grenadine, apple cider vinegar, citrus, egg white)

name: Crux Fermentation Project
description: Crux brews the NØ MØ series in house — a genuine non-alcoholic line rather than a bought-in can, made with traditional brewing methods at under 0.5% ABV. The original NØ MØ IPA uses flaked oats, honey and crystal malts with Pacific Northwest Citra and Mosaic hops at about 30 calories, and the range has grown to include a hazy and a seasonal fresh hop release. The tasting room sits in a converted transmission shop with 28-plus taps, food carts, fire pits and a lawn facing the Cascades.

name: Cultured Cheese Shop
description: Cultured is a locally, female-owned cheese and charcuterie bar in Butchertown, now operating inside the Copper & Kings building at the rooftop level after moving from its original East Main Street shop. It builds shared boards from farmstead cheeses and cured meats and serves them with a drinks list that includes named alcohol-free options — a Tart Cherry Old Fashioned, a Turmeric Ginger Mule and a Cucumber Aloe Margarita, built on mixers from the Louisville company Modica. It does not take reservations. Dine-in runs from 11am daily, to 6pm early in the week and 10pm Thursday through Saturday, with a separate to-go counter.

name: Cultured South Fermentation Co.
description: Cultured South Fermentation Co. is Georgia's first kombucha taproom, opened in May 2018 in the Lee + White warehouse district in the West End by Melanie Wade, who had been brewing Golda Kombucha since 2013. The taproom pours Golda on draught by the pint, flight, taste, growler and gelato float, and stocks water kefir and jun, the honey-fermented cousin of kombucha, alongside cold brew coffee and a cultured-foods counter of vegan cheeses, pickles and preserves. Readers should know the room is not fully alcohol-free: Cultured South also brews and serves Grandmother Hard Kombucha and kombucha cocktails, so the alcoholic and non-alcoholic taps sit on the same board and need to be asked about by name.
