name: Cúrate Bar de Tapas
description: Cúrate Bar de Tapas is a Spanish tapas restaurant at 13 Biltmore Avenue in downtown Asheville, founded in 2011 by chef Katie Button and Félix Meana. It won the James Beard Foundation's Outstanding Hospitality Award in 2022, Button has twice been a Best Chef in the Southeast finalist, and the restaurant was recommended in the 2025 Michelin Guide. The kitchen serves gildas, pan con tomate, croquetas, gazpacho, patatas bravas, tortilla española and pulpo a la gallega alongside a jamón counter and paella, with a Cúrate Experience prix fixe at $80. Its drinks list carries a dedicated "Sin Alcohol" section structured like the wine list rather than as an afterthought: a non-alcoholic gin and tonic on Dhos with Franklin & Sons tonic, a Solo Agrio built on Kentucky 74 non-alcoholic bourbon with Le Naturel Zero Zero red and lemon, St. Agrestis's Phony Negroni, and an N/A Sangría made with Le Naturel Zero Zero and an orange oleo. Le Naturel's Zero Zero blanco and tinto are poured as wine, with Estrella Galicia 0.0 and Sierra Nevada Trail Pass IPA on the beer list. Children of any age are welcome. No drink prices are published online.

name: Cure
description: Cure is an Uptown New Orleans cocktail bar opened in 2009 by New Orleans native Neal Bodenheimer in a restored firehouse on a then-storm-damaged stretch of Freret Street — a move widely credited with sparking the corridor's revival. It won the James Beard Award for Outstanding Bar Program in 2018 and has held a place on North America's 50 Best Bars for three consecutive years. Its zero-proof drinks are printed as a section inside the bar's own "Cocktails We Love" card rather than on a separate menu. The current Zero Proof list runs four deep: Partly Cloudy ($12) with Undone Not Rum, coconut, lime and Q ginger beer; Round of Applause ($15) on The Pathfinder Bitter with Q tonic, lemon, strawberry and mint; Needlepoint Sour ($13) with verjus, grapefruit, ginger syrup, honey and egg white; and Second Opinion ($12) with chai tea, Giffard Apéritif Syrup, verjus and rose water. The list rotates, so earlier builds such as Gulfside, The Tide Is High and The Eureka are no longer served. The beer list also carries one non-alcoholic beer, Einbecker ($8). Open from 4pm Sunday to Thursday and 3pm Friday and Saturday.

name: Cutler
description: Cutler (formerly Cutler & Co) is Andrew McConnell's flagship Fitzroy fine diner on Gertrude Street, and it pairs its award-winning cellar with a genuinely deep non-alcoholic offering. Drinkers can choose alcohol-free beers from Upflow and Sobah, aromatic wine alternatives from Melbourne's NON, alcohol-free sparkling, red and white wine, plus alcohol-free spritzes, RTDs and house mocktails. The zero-proof list runs to close to twenty options and is treated with the same seriousness as the wine list, earning the restaurant a top 5/5 rating from non-alcoholic guide No & Low Life. The Grande Dame of Gertrude Street keeps close to twenty curated non-alcoholic options alongside the wine list, so the alcohol-free route through dinner is a real one.
signatureDrinks: Curated non-alcoholic list — close to twenty options poured alongside the wine list

name: Cycene
description: Cycene is a one-Michelin-star tasting-menu restaurant inside Shoreditch's Blue Mountain School, and its non-alcoholic pairing is built by a chef rather than the sommelier. Caitlin Jones and the kitchen make a bespoke flight of house-fermented kombuchas and drinks matched to each course - a double-fermented pear and celeriac kombucha with the opening snacks, a pumpkin, miyagawa and greengage-kernel drink alongside sea-urchin linguini, and honey-fermented milk with dessert. There is also a 'half-and-half' option that alternates glasses of fine wine with the homemade kombuchas, so non-drinkers get a genuine tasting experience rather than an afterthought.

name: Da Cove Health Bar & Café
description: Da Cove Health Bar & Café sits on Monsarrat Avenue between Waikīkī and Diamond Head, and is one of the very few Oʻahu businesses that keeps 'awa on a standing everyday menu rather than as an occasional special. It serves no alcohol. Kava comes as an ice-cold single at $6 for eight ounces or a double at $12 for sixteen, and the house 'awa coconut smoothie blends kava with coconut milk, maple syrup and banana. A chalkboard wall explains what kava is and what it does, which is unusual and useful — it is psychoactive. The rest of the menu runs açaí bowls, fruit smoothies and wild-caught ahi salads, wraps and sandwiches, and live music plays Tuesday through Thursday evenings.

description: Da Kine's Kava is Durham's fully alcohol-free bar, open noon to midnight seven days a week in a unit on West Chapel Hill Street in the Burch Avenue neighbourhood. The house drink is kava — ground Noble Vanuatu root blended with water and served the traditional way, or mixed with juices on tap, still or sparkling — and there is a short mocktail list beside it, led by the Haleakala Sunrise on guava, pineapple, lime and coconut. Nothing on the menu contains alcohol, but read it before you order: kratom teas and hemp drinks carrying CBD and Delta-9 THC sit on the same page, clearly labelled. Discover Durham lists it on the city's official non-alcoholic page as an alcohol-free social space, and it is the only dedicated alcohol-free bar in Durham.

Pours are made in-house rather than pulled from a bottle list, and demand for the option has, per Club Oenologique, 'continued to soar.'

Non-drinkers are treated as VIPs: the bar swaps in AF spirits, liqueurs and sparkling so zero-proof guests get the same menu, and cocktail architect Jacob will build a bespoke NA drink on request. Named AF builds include the Chios Spritz with house-made AF mastiha and AF prosecco, and the theatrical Honey Ginger on Fire with smoked AF bourbon.

description: Caffe Dante is the Greenwich Village original at 79–81 MacDougal Street, named the World's Best Bar in 2019 and famous for its Negroni and Garibaldi programmes. Note that three separate Dante rooms share one website — this is the MacDougal Street original, not Dante West Village on Hudson Street or Dante Aperitivo on Bank Street. CORRECTION TO OUR EARLIER LISTING: we previously described a zero-proof menu called "Temperance" led by a signature "NOgroni". Neither appears anywhere on Dante's site or current menus, and we could not source either name; they have been removed. The real section is headed simply NON-ALCOHOLIC and runs five drinks: an Espresso Shakerato with orange juice and vanilla ($16), an NA Cosmojito with Dante cranberry, mint, lime and orange bitters ($14), a Dante Italian Spritz on Lyre's ($16), an NA Blood Orange Spritz with Seedlip Grove, raspberry and balsamic ($17), and a Forest Highball on Everleaf Forest with clementine and saffron ($15). It was shortlisted, not a winner, at NYC's Best Bars for NA 2025.

name: Dario
address: 323 N Washington Ave, Suite 100, Minneapolis, MN 55401
description: Dario is an Italian restaurant with global influences that opened in Minneapolis's North Loop in early 2024, led by chef Joe Rolle and beverage director Stephen Rowe. Rowe spent nearly a decade as a founding team member of the acclaimed Marvel Bar, and at Dario he runs a dedicated spirit-free program built to stand alongside the full-proof cocktails rather than as an afterthought — the restaurant calls it "a groundbreaking spirit-free offering that mirrors the depth and creativity of the full-proof cocktails." The zero-proof list spans bitters-forward and botanical builds such as the New Age Outlaw (Dhos Blanco, Spritz del Conte, lime), No. 75 (ISH London Botanical, Oddbird Blanc de Blanc, lemon), Botanical & Tonic, and the Naw-groni. The kitchen also makes house sodas, pours an Athletic Brewing NA golden ale, and keeps a de-alcoholized wine list. Known for handmade pastas.

description: Dark Horse Bar & Eatery is a Lowertown, St. Paul neighborhood bar and restaurant that spent a decade serving the district before closing in February 2025 and reopening in July 2025 under new ownership. The relaunch is run by chef Shane Oporto in the kitchen and Sarah McDonough on the floor, backed by Eclective, the hospitality group behind Saint Paul Brewing and Can Can Wonderland. The reopened menu pairs elevated bar food — a signature burger, pizzas — with a cocktail list that gives equal attention to its non-alcoholic side. A dedicated "Zero Proof" menu section ($9 each) features house-made drinks: a Ginger Beer built on house ginger syrup, cayenne, and soda; a Squirt with house grapefruit cordial and soda; and a lightly fermented Tepache of pineapple, piloncillo, and cinnamon. Athletic Brewing non-alcoholic beers (Free Wave, Upside Dawn) are also stocked.

name: Darling Aviary
description: Darling Aviary is a rooftop bar above K Street in downtown Sacramento, named by Visit Sacramento among the city's mocktail venues though without its drinks documented individually. Rooftops are usually the least accommodating format for a non-drinker, since the entire proposition is a cocktail at sunset with nothing else to do — so a rooftop that makes the city's official mocktail list is worth knowing. It runs late, to 1:30am on Friday and Saturday, and opens from 11am at weekends. Because the individual drinks are not documented, ask what is available on arrival; Dive Bar is a short walk away with three named options as a fallback.

name: Daru
description: Daru is an acclaimed Indian-ish restaurant just off the H Street Corridor at 1451 Maryland Avenue NE, opened in August 2021 by chef Suresh Sundas and beverage director Dante Datta in a former neighbourhood grocery. Sundas practises a border-defying Indian fusion that pulls off unusual pairings - reshmi chicken kebab with blue cheese, a creamy spinach lasagna made with paneer, smoky black dal with a dollop of burrata. Datta runs an inventive bar rooted in South Asian technique, and the non-alcoholic side is a properly headed section rather than an afterthought: a mango and peach lassi with dahi yoghurt, salt and sugar; masala chai; a Mango Daisy with lemon, sugar and salt; a fizzy tamarind soda of tamarind tea, lime and soda; plus Clausthaler N/A dry-hopped IPA, Thums Up and Limca. Roughly 40 seats indoors with a patio.

name: Davie Kava
description: Davie Kava is an alcohol-free kava bar on West State Road 84, and its hours are the whole argument for it: doors at noon every day, closing at 1am at the start and end of the week and running to 5am from Wednesday through Saturday. Very little else in western Broward is open at that hour without a liquor licence. The menu is organised into four blocks — traditional kava shells, Happy Teas, cold brew and specialty drinks — with the shells as the anchor. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: the tea side of a Florida kava bar menu is normally kratom rather than kava, and Davie Kava does not publish its ingredient list online, so ask at the bar before ordering anything from the tea board. Kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries dependence risk that kava does not.

name: Daydreamer
description: Daydreamer is a cocktail and Champagne bar on East 6th Street, next door to Suerte restaurant. The venue is a collaboration between veterans of Austin bars including Kitty Cohen's, Frazier's, and The White Horse, and the concept centers on caviar, champagne, and martinis — The Infatuation describes the theme bluntly as just that. The interior is intimately decorated with soft lighting, and the back patio features a swimming pool. A taco truck operates out back. The martini program is the standout, and reviewers note that the bartenders accommodate zero-proof mocktail requests, though specific NA drinks are not publicly named on the menu.

name: Dayglow
address: 3206 W Sunset Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90026
description: Dayglow is a multi-roaster specialty coffee bar at 3206 West Sunset Boulevard in Silver Lake, opened in late 2017 by Tohm Ifergan, formerly of Portola Coffee Roasters. Time Out gave it five stars in 2025, describing it as part neighbourhood hangout and part subscription service, a haven for serious coffee drinkers and dabblers alike — and noting that the standout part of the menu is its house signature drinks, which take a craft-cocktail approach to dispensing caffeine. The multi-roaster claim is real and unusually deep: its retail shelf carries well over a hundred beans from roasters including Tim Wendelboe, Coffee Collective, La Cabra, Prolog, Friedhats, Dak, Nomad, Monogram and Morgon alongside its own house roasts. Its signature drinks include the Military Latte, the Warhol, the Totoro and a strawberry matcha. PLEASE NOTE: Dayglow publishes its bean shop online but not its café drinks menu, and the third-party listings that appear to carry it are stale or fabricated — so we cannot give current prices or ingredients for the signature drinks. Seating is limited and there are few outlets, so it is not a laptop café. Open daily 7am to 7pm. Ours is the Silver Lake location; there are five others.
signatureDrinks: Military Latte|Warhol|Totoro|Strawberry Matcha

name: DC Brau Brewing
description: DC Brau Brewing is a craft brewery and taproom at 3178-B Bladensburg Road NE in Ivy City, co-founded by Brandon Skall and Jeff Hancock as one of the District's pioneering modern breweries. Its non-alcoholic beer, NA Brau, launched in late April 2024 and is billed as the first canned non-alcoholic beer brewed by a DC brewery. It is a 0.3% ABV pale ale modelled on DC Brau's flagship The Public, using the same Centennial and El Dorado hops with Caramel 40 and Munich malts for a pale golden colour. Rather than tunnel pasteurisation the brewery uses a hybrid Lallemand yeast strain plus Chinova Bioworks' Chiber mushroom-fibre extract as a natural antimicrobial, which preserves flavour and carbonation. It is sold in cans across the region and pours on the taproom list Thursday to Sunday.
signatureDrinks: NA Brau (non-alcoholic pale ale, 0.3% ABV)

name: De La Playa Records & Leisure
description: De La Playa Records & Leisure is a fully alcohol-free hybrid record shop and community space in LA's Highland Park, opened in mid-2024 by three co-founders with roots in Long Beach and the Harbor area: John David Preap ("Bles"), Diego "Fuego" Guerrero, and Jon Paul Lourenço. The shop pairs thousands of vinyl records — hip hop, reggae, jazz, cumbia, salsa, funk, house — with a retail selection of 100-plus non-alcoholic beverages, including Greek- and Italian-style amaros, NA IPAs, de-alcoholized wines, and ready-to-drink cocktails. On weekends, the founders run "Bar Non," a made-to-order zero-proof cocktail stand on the patio (think an NA rum build with ube, cinnamon, maple, and black walnut, or a non-alcoholic Paloma with hopped grapefruit bitters), alongside guest DJ sets, listening parties, and vendor events. The founders deliberately chose to stay alcohol-free — one of LA's clearest dedicated-NA anchors.
signatureDrinks: NA rum (ube, cinnamon, maple, black walnut)|NA Paloma (hopped grapefruit bitters)

name: Dear Daphni
description: Dear Daphni is a Greek restaurant on the ground floor of The Laurel in Rittenhouse, and its non-alcoholic drinks draw on the eastern Mediterranean pantry rather than on a generic syrup rail. The Honey Bee combines a non-alcoholic gin with sumac honey, lemon and Pinamor — sumac being the dark red, intensely tart berry that Levantine and Greek cooking uses where others would reach for lemon, and which gives the drink an acidity quite unlike citrus. A second build runs a non-alcoholic rum with pineapple, lime and Persian cucumber. Dinner runs from four in the afternoon to ten, and to eleven on Friday and Saturday.

name: Dear Irene
description: Dear Irene is an intimate downtown room doing small plates and cocktails, and it is the Bend bar most often recommended to people who want a proper night out without alcohol. Its Path Less Taken is built on Pathfinder with bitters and drinks like an old fashioned. Small plates run to Oregon crab arancini and king salmon tartare. Closed Sunday and Monday.

name: Dearly Beloved
description: Dearly Beloved is a self-described "cocktail restaurant" from Machine Hospitality Group, which opened in May 2024 in River North's former Kiki's Bistro space at 900 N Franklin St. The beverage program is led by mixologist and beverage director Aneka Saxon, who sourced ingredients on travels through six countries. Alongside its spirited menu, the venue maintains a permanent "Zero Proof Cocktails" section rather than a one-off list — a commitment Saxon highlights as core to the program. Named non-alcoholic builds include Clearly Cultured (with Seedlip Grove), Understory (Heywell lime adaptogen soda), Fresh Cut Grass (dandelion honey, grasshopper syrup, liquid chlorophyll, lime), and Soda Pop (orgeat, oat milk, coconut soda, orange flower and rose water). A Happy Hour zero-proof option, Zeal Without the Rest, uses the Crodino NA aperitif. In January 2025 the venue hosted Chicago's Spirit-Free Cocktail Fest, pouring eight zero-proof drinks.

name: Death & Co
description: Death & Co Denver is the second outpost of the New York cocktail bar, opened in 2018 inside The Ramble Hotel in Denver's River North Art District. Founders David Kaplan, Alex Day and Ravi DeRossi opened the original Death & Co in a windowless Manhattan room in 2007, where it helped lead the modern craft cocktail movement. The Denver location is a multi-bar complex within the boutique hotel: the marquee lobby bar with 1930s decor and plush velvet seating, the DC/AM coffee and brunch bar serving 7am to 3pm daily, the seasonal outdoor Garden, and Suite 6A, a mezzanine lounge overlooking the lobby bar. The bar keeps a standing Zero Proof section on its Denver menu, currently the Vibe Shift, Porch Swing, Business Casual and Cap Gun, alongside non-alcoholic wine and beer. Opening bar manager Alex Jump, since departed to open The Peach Crease Club, is widely credited as a founding figure of Denver's modern non-alcoholic bar scene.

The main room runs a seasonal menu organised into six sections, from the lightest and most refreshing through the most spirituous, with zero-proof drinks treated as one of those sections rather than an appendix; a separate walk-up Standing Room bar operates Thursday to Saturday. The zero-proof list currently holds three built cocktails at $16–$18 on genuine non-alcoholic spirits including Seedlip, Ritual, Giffard and Wilderton, backed by non-alcoholic wine and beer from NON, Lyre's, Athletic and Suntory.

name: Deep Dive
description: Deep Dive is Renée Erickson's jewel-box cocktail lounge beneath the Amazon Spheres at 620 Lenora Street in South Lake Union, opened in August 2018 as part of her Sea Creatures group, with the space curated by Curtis Steiner of the Ballard home store Steinerlf. It is deliberately theatrical — curios on shelves and under specially lit bell jars, metal grooves overhead that the Seattle Times' critic read as ribs, leaving her feeling she was in the bowels of a sea creature. That same review was not uncritical: it found the energy in the oddly shaped room never quite sparks, and that the glamour ends up stage-set-like. The food has included a much-discussed $18 hot dog. It keeps a dedicated non-alcoholic menu called "Above Water", documented as including the Sinless Sour (Pathfinder, orgeat, lemon) and A Bitter Whisper (Pathfinder with Wilderton Lustre and Wilderton Aperitivo). name: Deir Cafe Antioch
description: Appeared to be temporarily closed as of mid-October 2026, after a fire was reported at its Haywood Lane address on 13 October 2026 - check the cafe's own channels before going. Deir Cafe Antioch is the second location of Yousef Gumiza's fully alcohol-free Palestinian coffeehouse, on Haywood Lane in the Antioch neighbourhood of Nashville, and it is the one that keeps the late hours: before the closure it opened seven days a week from 9am until 1am. It took over the former La Princesa Market space, first reported in January 2026. The menu follows the original in Wedgewood-Houston - Mediterranean-inflected signature lattes including the Baklawa latte and the Golden Lotus with biscoff and caramel, fruit refreshers named in Arabic such as Roman for pomegranate and Ward for rose, matcha, smoothies and pastries. No alcohol is served at any hour, which is the point: it was built as a night cafe for a community that does not drink.

name: Deir Cafe
description: Deir Cafe is a fully alcohol-free Palestinian coffeehouse on Hagan Street in Wedgewood-Houston, open seven days a week from 7am to 6pm. Owner Yousef Gumiza named it after Deir al-Balah, his family's city in Gaza, and built it as a community room as much as a cafe: it keeps a dedicated prayer space alongside the counter. The drinks are Mediterranean-inflected rather than standard third-wave - a Baklawa latte, a Golden Lotus latte with biscoff and caramel, a Strawberry Dubai Chocolate latte, a Banana Spice latte - plus fruit refreshers named in Arabic: Roman for pomegranate, Ward for rose, Khokh for peach. Matcha, smoothies and pastries fill out the list. No alcohol is served. A second Deir Cafe on Haywood Lane in Antioch appeared to be temporarily closed as of mid-October 2026, after a fire was reported at that address.

name: Delafia
description: Delafia is a small natural wine bar and retail shop on South Roxboro Street in Durham's Hayti neighbourhood, pouring low-intervention wine from small producers by the glass and selling it by the bottle, with a short food menu and coffee alongside and the feel of a speakeasy more than a shop. Its own invitation is to come in for a nibble and a pour from a rotating menu of low-intervention wines, beer and non-alcoholic bevs, which puts alcohol-free drinks on the same rotating list as everything else rather than in a fixed section; Discover Durham lists it among the shops curating non-alcoholic products locally and beyond, in the same group as LouElla and Beer Study. There is no published list and no named zero-proof cocktails, so call or ask what is open this week. Open from four, to ten early in the week and midnight Thursday through Saturday.

name: Delah Coffee (Sansome Street)
description: Delah Coffee's Financial District cafe sits at Sansome and Clay, on the edge of Chinatown, and pours the same alcohol-free Yemeni list that the group's original SoMa shop opened with in 2022. It runs 6am to 8pm on weekdays and 7am to 9pm at weekends, an earlier close than the SoMa flagship but still well past the point where most downtown coffee counters shut. The traditional preparations are the draw: Sana'ani, the house black coffee with cardamom; Jubani, a light roast cooked with cardamom, ginger and cinnamon; Arabian Qawah, light roast boiled with cardamom; and Adeni chai, Yemeni black tea simmered with cream and the house spice blend. Turkish delights, honeyed pastries and savoury turnovers are baked daily.

name: Delah Coffee (SoMa)
description: Delah Coffee is the original San Francisco Yemeni coffeehouse, opened in SoMa in July 2022 by Omar Jahamee, then eighteen, with his uncle Majed Jahamee. KQED credits it as the first Yemeni coffee shop to open in the Bay Area, ahead of the wave of more than twenty that followed. The Fourth Street cafe is entirely alcohol-free and trades from 6am to 11pm on weeknights and to midnight on Friday and Saturday, which makes it a genuine late option rather than a morning-only stop. The drinks are traditional: Sana'ani, the house black coffee with cardamom; Jubani, a light roast with cardamom, ginger and cinnamon; Arabian Qawah; and Adeni chai, Yemeni black tea cooked with cream and Delah's own spice blend. Turkish delights and turnovers baked daily fill the counter.

name: Delbar
address: 870 Inman Village Pkwy NE, Suite 1, Atlanta, GA 30307
description: Delbar — Farsi for "heart, captured" — is a Persian and Middle Eastern restaurant opened in Inman Park in May 2020 by owner Fares Kargar. The flagship sits in the Inman Quarter development and has grown into a small Atlanta group with additional locations in Buckhead and Old Milton; the restaurant is recognized in the MICHELIN Guide. The food leans on shared mezze, kebabs, and family recipes rooted in Iranian cooking. For non-drinkers, Delbar maintains a real, named zero-proof section on its beverage menu rather than generic sodas. Signature options include the Sharbat e Zereshk, a barberry-and-lime sharbat described as tropical and refreshing, and an Iced Coconut Chai Tea built on Persian tea and ginger. The NA program is house-made and culturally grounded in Persian sharbat tradition — a smaller, curated list at a full-service restaurant.

name: Delilah Miami
hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 5pm-11pm; Fri-Sat 5pm-12am; Sun closed
description: Delilah Miami is a 1920s-themed waterfront supper club from the h.wood Group, the Los Angeles hospitality company co-founded by John Terzian and Brian Toll. It opened in December 2023 inside The Four Ambassadors on Brickell Key, with a terrace and yacht slips overlooking Biscayne Bay. The concept pairs elevated American cuisine with art-deco styling and nightly live entertainment that builds into a late-night lounge. The bar is cocktail-forward, and Delilah carries a short but genuine non-alcoholic section on its menu, building zero-proof serves with the same approach as its full cocktail list. The two named alcohol-free drinks are the Sun's Out (Lyre's N/A rum, elderflower, lime, mint, on the rocks) and the Peacemaker (Lyre's Italian Spritz, grapefruit, lime, topped with tonic), each $16. It is the Miami outpost of the wider Delilah restaurant group.

name: Demi
description: Demi is James Beard Award-winning chef Gavin Kaysen's intimate North Loop tasting-menu restaurant, opened in early 2019 next to his flagship Spoon and Stable and operated under Soigné Hospitality Group. With roughly 20 counter seats wrapping an open oval kitchen, it serves a seasonal, reservation-only multi-course menu and is a Relais & Châteaux member. Alongside the wine pairing, Demi runs a parallel non-alcoholic "Temperance Pairing" (around $85, about eight curated zero-proof drinks) built from teas, juices, shrubs, and fermented or infused preparations designed to match each course. Beverage director Jessi Pollak leads the program. Mpls.St.Paul Magazine called the non-alcoholic pairing "just as good and wildly original" as the wine, citing a hibiscus, beet, apple, black pepper, and black trumpet mushroom "red." Demi is regularly cited among the few U.S. tasting menus doing non-alcoholic pairings seriously.

description: DENMARK on High is a second-floor cocktail lounge in the restored Yankee Trader building — now Yankee on High — at the southern gateway to the Short North, overlooking the Columbus Convention Center. It opened in 2014 in what had been a furniture showroom, and is built around a no-television, no-distraction room and a from-scratch bar programme: house bitters, house infusions, house syrups and shrubs. The current menu carries a small non-alcoholic section rather than a token line, with two built drinks — Not A Dream, a tropical construction of non-alcoholic gin, fruit purée, coconut cream and lime, pineapple and orange juice, and the Cucumber No-Jito of lime juice, mint syrup and cucumber soda. The bar also runs small-group cocktail classes and opens Wednesday to Saturday evenings only.

name: Denver Café & Kava
description: Denver Café & Kava opened on East Colfax in Park Hill in early 2026 as a deliberate zero-proof hangout — a room designed so that there is no pressure to drink, rather than a bar with a good alternatives list. It runs 7am to 2am every day of the week, which is the longest trading day of any alcohol-free venue in the city. The menu covers kava, mocktails, coffee and a range of Chinese and Vietnamese teas, plus small bites, and the calendar is community-led: open-mic nights, local vendor markets and themed parties. The founding team — Kevin Bloom, Elizabeth Leung, Cam Webbe, Jayden MacDonald and Jack Kestian — met as customers at Golden Kava Lounge, west of the city, and built this one together.

name: Departure Restaurant + Lounge
description: Departure is a pan-Asian rooftop restaurant and lounge on the 15th floor of The Nines hotel downtown, with two patios and city, river, and mountain views. Its beverage menu includes a dedicated "Zero Proof" section of named non-alcoholic cocktails — such as the Sunburst and Mood Ring — alongside non-alcoholic beers.

Dark beer is the hardest style to render without alcohol, which makes this one of the more technically impressive NA pours in Oregon. Open daily from 11am.

name: Deviant Kava
description: Deviant Kava is an entirely booze-free, two-floor "third space" that opened in Parkville, Missouri in 2024, founded by three friends (including owner Wesley Straight) who wanted to bring the community feel of the kava scene to greater Kansas City. Set in a refurbished home about 15 minutes north of downtown KC near Park University, it pairs traditionally brewed kava and kratom tea with a full alcohol-free cocktail bar, specialty coffee (Café Corazón espresso), Hugo Tea, kombucha, yerba mate, and nootropic wellness drinks. The zero-proof menu includes named mocktails like the Captain's Daiquiri and Ashes to Ashes, plus made-to-order alcohol-free Negronis and margaritas. The space spans a bar and lobby, a fireplace room with plants and a library, and upstairs study nooks and a piano, with a deck overlooking the Park University campus. It is positioned as a sober-friendly community hub.

name: Devil Takes A Holiday
description: Devil Takes a Holiday is a dark, demon-themed cocktail lounge on St Paul Street in downtown Burlington, run by Taylor Watts, who styles himself Head Devil. Its alcohol-free drinks are printed as atonements — a standing section of the rotating menu rather than an off-list favour — and they are built the way the alcoholic cocktails are, from bases, shrubs and syrups the bar makes itself. Watts has demonstrated the approach publicly on Vermont Public, showing a spiced cranberry shrub finished with non-alcoholic sparkling wine and a hot buttered drink built on a cocoa-and-brown-sugar scrub. Open from 5pm most nights, 4pm on Friday and Saturday, with a Sunday afternoon service.

name: Dew Drop Inn
description: Dew Drop Inn is a women-owned gastropub at 17th and Downing in Denver's Uptown neighborhood, opened in 2021 by the team behind two of Denver's classic dive bars — the Horseshoe Lounge and the Embassy Tavern. Named Westword's Best New Bar in 2022, the venue blends a neighborhood-bar warmth (all-day $8 beer-and-shot specials, two daily happy hours running open–6pm and 10pm–close) with a serious gastropub program: Bangkok-style mussels, charcuterie, muffuletta, fried chicken, with 85% of the menu prepared gluten-free. The bar runs a named non-alcoholic program called 'clear-headed cocktails' — six rotating NA cocktails alongside two NA beers and a non-alcoholic prosecco, called out by 303 Magazine in their 2025 Sober Summer mocktail roundup. Named NA selections include the Be Nice (NA gin, lavender bitters) and the Cosmonaught (orange liqueur, cranberry, citrus). The space — tiger-print wallpaper, exposed brick, long wooden bar — is consciously designed to 'make regulars,' a philosophy the founding team has carried through 20 years of Denver hospitality.

description: Diego's on Wayland Square is the East Side outpost of a Rhode Island Mexican group, and its bar builds non-alcoholic drinks with the same fresh-produce approach as its margaritas. Two standing builds are documented — one on apple cider reduction with cranberry, ginger and cinnamon, the other a cucumber, mango and lime build lengthened with ginger beer. A sibling room trades in Newport.

name: Dishoom King's Cross
description: Dishoom's King's Cross branch is the largest and most theatrical of the group, opened in 2014 inside a former Victorian railway transit shed — a godown, in Bombay parlance — on Stable Street behind Granary Square. Dishoom was founded by cousins Shamil and Kavi Thakrar, who opened their first site in Covent Garden in 2010 as a tribute to the old Irani cafés of Bombay, the all-day institutions built by Zoroastrian Persian immigrants; the main hall here recalls a 1920s Irani café, crowned by an art deco clock modelled on the one at Bombay's Victoria Terminus. It is regularly called the best mocktail bar in London, and the non-alcoholic list is a proper menu section rather than an afterthought: a Teetotal Espresso Martini, a Sober Negroni and a rotating range of 0% beers, served all day alongside the Bombay food.

description: Dishoom Manchester occupies a grand former Freemasons' Hall on Bridge Street, recreating the all-day romance of an old Bombay Irani café beneath enormous stained-glass windows. The group was founded by cousins Shamil and Kavi Thakrar as a tribute to the Irani cafés built by Zoroastrian Persian immigrants in Bombay; this branch opened in 2018 and leans into its building's past, with marble café tables, portraits on the walls and design nods to the Lodge Rising Star of Western India. Waiting guests are handed complimentary cups of chai, and a basement Permit Room bar sits below the main hall, named for the licences once required to drink under the Bombay Prohibition Act of 1949. Alcohol-free drinking is a proper menu section here — a full run of "Teetotal Tipples" served all day, including a Sober Summer Negroni, a Crossip-based Marine Drive Spritz and a Teetotal Espresso Martini, alongside lassis, chai, sharbats, 0% beers and alcohol-free sparkling wine.

The spectacle is the reason to include it: a bar where the entertainment is overhead rather than in the glass gives a non-drinker something to actually be there for. It also runs 3pm to 2am every single day, which makes it the most consistently available option in this guide by a wide margin. No closed days at all, which no other Sacramento venue here can claim.

description: Doberman Drawing Room is a cocktail-forward lounge and social club in Las Vegas' 18b Arts District, opened April 30, 2025 by Corner Bar Management in a 3,400-square-foot space styled after a moody 19th-century drawing room with private booths and an indoor atrium garden. The bar program is led by mixologist and partner Juyoung Kang (formerly of Fontainebleau's Collins bar), whose globally inspired, story-driven cocktails extend to a genuine spirit-free offering. The standing menu includes alcohol-free numbers such as the Coffee Cheesecake (a booze-free espresso martini with malt, coffee, honey, parmesan and nutmeg) and Good Vibrations (tomato, lychee, lemongrass, strawberry, white pepper and sumac). For Dry January 2026 the bar introduced "Zero-100," a two-menu tasting that pairs a sober-curious lineup with the regular drinking menu, featuring zero-proof cocktails like the Faux Fashioned (Lyre's Traditional Reserve with Lucano N/A Amaro), the Confetti (Lyre's Amaretto, zero-proof herbal liqueur, lemon and egg whites) and the Blush 75 (sparkling watermelon with Lyre's Pink Gin). Reservations (via SevenRooms) and walk-ins are both welcome; guests must be 21+ with a dressy-casual dress code.

description: Dobrá Tea is a Bohemian-style tea house at 1937 Murray Avenue in Squirrel Hill, established in 2012 by the Society of Tea Devotees, the Czech tea collective, and owned by Nathaniel Pantalone. It serves over 100 loose-leaf teas from around the world alongside light vegetarian fare, and describes what it is aiming for as a space somewhere between a bar and a church — a place for relaxation and community. That is the practical appeal for a non-drinker: low light, cushions, low tables and no pressure to turn the table, in a room that stays open until 10pm on weeknights and 11pm on Friday and Saturday, which is exactly when other alcohol-free options in Pittsburgh run out. The list is organised by category the way a wine list is by region — white, green, oolong, black and pu'er teas, the house chai blends it calls Specialteas, tisanes and herbal infusions, and an iced range. Food is mezze-leaning: hummus and baba ganoush plates, several pita preparations, dolmades, miso soup, and a long list of sweet bites including halva and baklava. Prices are not published online.

Its beverage programme was developed with Derek Brown, the nationally known bartender behind Positive Damage and a leading advocate for mindful drinking, and centres on a dedicated Low & No menu so that every dish can be paired with either a full cocktail or a spirit-free one. Named non-alcoholic drinks include Get Your Flowers, built on Fluere Spiced Cane with spiced pineapple syrup and grenadine, the botanical R_(n/a)_G&T on Fluere Botanical with Giffard Pamplemousse and elderflower, plus Astronomy Club and the Sigi Tolo Rickey. It keeps beer, wine and zero-proof drinks on hand at all times and runs a large non-alcoholic menu rather than a token pair of options — a policy choice that follows directly from the room's premise, since a bar built around belonging cannot make a third of its guests order soda. Open Tuesday to Saturday from 5pm, to midnight at weekends, closed Sunday and Monday.

All four are house builds on fresh juice and sparkling mineral water rather than non-alcoholic spirits: Fresca works cucumber, orange, lime, agave and jalapeño; El Jarrito leans savoury with grapefruit, lime, tamarind chipotle and guajillo; La Chica Fresa pairs strawberry with jamaica; and La Cariñosa keeps it to lemon and honey. name: Doshi House
description: Doshi House is a fully alcohol-free vegetarian cafe in Houston's Third Ward, so its coffee, tea, and tonic menu is non-alcoholic by default rather than a side program bolted onto a bar. The espresso bar runs on beans from Houston roaster Greenway Coffee, and the tea list spans a 36-hour brewed chai latte, Japanese matcha, and traditional karak cha masala chai. A separate 'Tonics & Infusions' section builds composed non-alcoholic drinks from real ingredients, like a tamarind-dates-jalapeño elixir and a hibiscus-lavender-rose blend, giving the drink list the same intentionality most bars reserve for cocktails.

Its documented alcohol-free build is the Blood Knot, which blends pineapple with a blueberry simple syrup and citrus soda — expressive without being heavy, in RESIDENT's December 2025 description. Dinner is the only service, from 5pm nightly, running to midnight on Friday and Saturday, with a daily happy hour from 5pm to 7pm. For anyone eating their way through Wynwood without drinking, it sits within a few blocks of Uchi, R House and Rosemary's, all of which run their own zero-proof lists.

Smoke & Mirrors is made with Tenneyson Black Ginger, the non-alcoholic bitter aperitif, and Dreaming of You is a passionfruit build that runs sweeter for anyone who wants it. The name is a small joke that lands well here — a bar called Double Standard applying a single standard to both halves of its menu — and the late hours help, running to midnight midweek and 2am on Friday and Saturday in the middle of the downtown hotel district.

The kitchen centers on traditional Neapolitan-style wood-fired pizza — built on a heirloom-yeast-starter dough and "double zero" (00) flour that gives the restaurant its name — alongside handmade pasta and shareable Southern Italian dishes. Beyond its Italian wine list and cocktails, Double Zero keeps a dedicated "zero proof cocktails" section on its beverage menu, with three named non-alcoholic drinks: the Bermuda Triangle (rosemary, orange, lime, brine, soda), So Fresh So Clean (turmeric, lime, pomegranate, soda), and Orange is the New Black (orange and lemon juice, fresh ginger, club soda). Four distinct named drinks is a genuine menu section, and the range matters: there is something tart, something herbal, something spicy and something creamy, which means a non-drinker can order differently across an evening instead of repeating one sweet glass. The Töst rosé is also sold by the bottle. It is styled like a high-end wine and spirits merchant, with the same catalogue behind it: roughly 138 non-alcoholic beers, 83 non-alcoholic wines, 63 zero-proof spirits, 45 ready-to-drink cocktails and 19 mixers and accessories, covering Seedlip, Lyre's, Ghia, Three Spirit, Kin Euphorics, Dr. Zero Zero and Martini among others. Nothing on the shelves contains meaningful alcohol. Staff advise by flavour and occasion rather than by brand, and the shop trades Tuesday to Sunday from noon to 8pm, closed Mondays.

name: Dray
description: Dray is a 100% non-alcoholic bottle shop at 18 Union Park Street in Boston's South End, opened in late 2023 by founder Pat Dooling and reported at the time as the city's first dedicated alcohol-free retail store. Nothing in the shop contains meaningful alcohol: the range is built to mirror a conventional wine and spirits merchant, and Dray's own catalogue currently lists roughly 138 non-alcoholic beers, 83 non-alcoholic wines, 63 zero-proof spirits, 45 ready-to-drink cocktails and a further 19 mixers and accessories. Staff work as advisers rather than clerks, steering customers between categories, and the shop runs tastings and community events. It trades Tuesday to Sunday from noon to 8pm and is closed Mondays. A second Dray opened in Central Square, Cambridge.

name: Drink Me! Tea Room
description: A reservation-only afternoon tea room on Warner Road in south Tempe, open four days a week and closing at 5pm. The draw for non-drinkers is a tea service built around loose-leaf blends plus a small list of named mocktails — the Two Days Slow and the Jack of Hearts — which DiningOut Phoenix highlighted in its May 2026 round-up of metro bars worth visiting for a mocktail. Worth being clear about: despite the tea-room format it is not alcohol-free, and its own materials advertise "special-tea cocktails" alongside the tea. Reservations are required and the short opening hours make walk-ins impractical.

That house-made base is what gives its non-alcoholic drinks something to be built from, and the bar keeps named zero-proof options rather than improvising: the Flint Tropics, the French Connection and the Blood Moon were all listed among downtown Grand Rapids' best non-alcoholic drinks in October 2025.

name: Dutch Courage
description: Dutch Courage is Baltimore's first gin-centric cocktail bar, opened in December 2019 by Brendan Dorr and Eric Fooy in a 1,500-square-foot rowhouse at 2229 N Charles Street in Old Goucher. Dorr set out to make somewhere deliberately bright: so many cocktail bars are dark and moody, he said before opening, but they wanted a place where you can have a cocktail at night and actually read the menu. The Baltimore Banner has written that the bar is redefining the non-alcoholic scene with its creative mocktails. Its zero-proof drinks include the N.A. Groni (a botanical gin syrup with orange oil, orange bitters and jasmine Tortuga kombucha), the First Lady (Seedlip Grove 42, grapefruit, rose water, sparkling non-alcoholic chardonnay and rosebuds) and the Emerald Mage (lemon, rosemary, spiced grenadine). The list rotates and the bar publishes its menus as PDFs that cannot be read online, so confirm the current roster on arrival. Snacks run to pickled vegetables with a herbed buttermilk dip. Open from 4pm daily, with happy hour weekdays 4–6pm. The same owners run the rum bar Pink Flamingo in Remington.

name: Eagle Park Brewing Company
description: Eagle Park Brewing Company is a Milwaukee brewery and taproom on the Lower East Side whose Hamilton Street location is the home of Solid State, its dedicated non-alcoholic beer line launched in January 2026. Rather than dealcoholizing a finished product, Eagle Park brews Solid State with a specially engineered yeast so it ferments to under 0.5% ABV while still tasting like full-strength beer. The four-beer N/A lineup — a Hazy IPA, a Pale Ale, a Mexican Lager with Lime, and a Cran-Orange Sour — is sold by the can for drinking in the taproom and in six-packs to go. As a working brewery it also pours a full slate of alcoholic beer, so the zero-proof cans sit alongside the regular tap list rather than replacing it.

Food is a rotating weekly Pizza of the Week with dips, salads, pretzels, breadsticks and soups; the menu is published only as an image. Its documented alcohol-free drink is a Virgin Pimm's of pomegranate, mint, cucumber and lemon, which is a genuinely sensible piece of thinking: a Pimm's Cup is already a long, herbaceous, fruit-heavy drink where the spirit is the least assertive component, so removing it costs less than it would almost anywhere else on a cocktail list.

name: Ebreeq Coffee House
description: Ebreeq Coffee House is a Yemeni coffeehouse on the Euclid Avenue side of the 200 Public Square tower in downtown Cleveland, opened in May 2025. It serves no alcohol. The 2,200-square-foot room was built around Yemeni coffee made the traditional way, with traditional Yemeni pastries alongside, and its co-owners include Ali Alwasim, Abdulhamed Alduais and Dia al-Baadani. The drinks the local press picked out are mufawar, Yemeni coffee with cream and cardamom; qishr, coffee husks brewed with ginger and cinnamon; and Adeni chai, a sweet spiced milk tea. Sabayah, a layered bread with butter and honey, is the food to order. It opens 7am to 8pm on weekdays and 8am to 9pm at weekends, so it is a daytime and early-evening room, not a late one.

Set in a mid-century-modern room of warm wood, acoustic panels, plants and vintage furnishings spun on a McIntosh sound system, it pairs elevated small plates with curated vinyl. As a sober owner, Young made an inclusive beverage program a priority from the start, with bar talent drawn from the storied (now-closed) Downtown Cocktail Room. The menu carries a dedicated "Non-Alcoholic Cocktails" section that mirrors classic spirited drinks using zero-proof substitutes -- including an N/A Old Fashioned (n/a bourbon, n/a amaro, simple syrup), Caught in the Rain (n/a rum, pineapple, mango, orange, coconut), Ring of Fire (n/a tequila, mango, orange, firewater bitters) and Take 5 (non-alcoholic amaro, cold brew, seasonal syrup) -- plus a separate "Mocktails" section of original non-spirited creations such as Cool Cat, Chef's Jam and Bright Size Life (ube syrup, lemon, soda).

The lady marmalade combines espresso with chocolate syrup and crushed Oreos; never promised you a rose garden pairs rose tonic with hibiscus and lychee; dolce vita layers tamarind and melon syrups under mandarin and bergamot soda with heavy cream; and the tropical tango runs pineapple, lime and coconut into ginger beer. name: Eem
description: Eem is a Thai barbecue restaurant and cocktail bar in N Portland's Boise neighborhood, opened in February 2019 by chef Earl Ninsom (Langbaan), pitmaster Matt Vicedomini (Matt's BBQ), and bartender Eric Nelson. It was named Restaurant of the Year by both The Oregonian and Portland Monthly in 2019 and repeatedly wins Willamette Week's "Best Thai" reader poll, pairing Texas-style smoked meats with bold Thai flavors. The non-alcoholic program, inspired by co-owner Nelson's own sobriety, lives in a dedicated "Clear Headed" menu section of four named zero-proof drinks at $8 each — about half the price of the full cocktails — built with the same house shrubs, cordials, and NA spirits. Named pours include the cucumber-yuzu Approved by Chef, the hojicha and strawberry-guava Secret Serendipity, and the coconut-pineapple That's It, That's All. Heck N/A beer rounds out the list.

It is also the late option in Norfolk's alcohol-free landscape, running to midnight midweek and 2am on Friday and Saturday. For anyone who wants a burger and a cold beer that happens to have no alcohol in it, rather than a project, this is the straightforward answer. CraveDFW singled out the Limonada Stand as 'a pear and hibiscus dream that doesn't skimp on complexity,' and the restaurant features the list for Dry January. It's a genuine named NA menu at an otherwise mezcal- and agave-forward restaurant.

The dining room and open-air patio look across the downtown Denver skyline, and the menu draws on Spain, North Africa and the Middle East: paella, mezze, spreads, kebabs and croquettas. The current dinner menu carries a dedicated Zero-Proof Cocktails section rather than a token option. Executive chef is Corey Ferguson. Dinner reservations are recommended, especially for the patio.

The house drinks are named and built rather than generic: Mango Sunrise, Clear Skies, Passion and Berry Energetic. No alcohol is served. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: the menu splits into kava for unwinding and what Elevate calls Mitra teas for daytime energy, and Mitra is Mitragyna speciosa — kratom. The naming is common across Florida and genuinely easy to miss. name: Elevated Kava Lounge Downtown
description: Elevated Kava Lounge's downtown room sits on College Street in the middle of Asheville's bar district and serves no alcohol at all, which is the point — it aims to provide the best kava and other alcohol alternatives in a cosy, artistic setting. The list runs kava, exotic and herbal teas, probiotic Buchi kombucha on tap, single-origin coffee and espresso from Brazilian-sourced beans roasted locally by Pisgah Coffee Roasters, tonics built from house mushroom tinctures, and Italian-style soda pops made from a large syrup selection. Free kava samples are offered to anyone curious. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: this lounge serves kratom alongside kava. Kratom acts on opioid receptors, carries dependence risk, and concentrated 7-OH kratom products face federal scheduling — a materially different proposition from kava, and worth knowing before you walk in. A second Elevated room operates in West Asheville, and both host open-mic nights.

name: ELEVEN Contemporary Kitchen
description: ELEVEN is big Burrito Restaurant Group's flagship fine-dining restaurant, opened in 2004 as the group's eleventh — hence the name — in a rehabilitated warehouse on Smallman Street beside the old rail lines in the Strip District. Eli Wahl has been executive chef since 2016, only the third in its history, and Pittsburgh Magazine named it one of the city's 25 best restaurants for 2026. Wine and beverage director Rob Hirst builds the zero-proof list by taking a popular cocktail and re-creating it without alcohol, and it is printed as its own section headed "Zero Proof / NA Cocktails": the Cosmo-not ($12) on Seedlip Grove 42 and Dhos Orange with cranberry and lime; the Pink Flamingo ($12) on Dhos gin-free with strawberry-honey, lemon, cucumber and mint; Pimm's Pathfinder ($12), a faithful Pimm's Cup on Pathfinder amaro with cucumber and Fever-Tree ginger beer; and Sunrise Over Smallman ($14) on Ritual non-alcoholic tequila. Heineken 0.0 and Sam Adams Just the Haze cover the beer. The list rotates.

name: Eli Tea Bar
description: Eli Tea Bar is an explicitly alcohol-free "sober bar" in Andersonville, opened in November 2021 by founder Elias "Eli" Majid, who launched the original Eli Tea in Birmingham, Michigan in 2012 and attended Loyola University in Chicago. Occupying the former True North cafe space at 5507 N Clark St, it pours more than 100 loose-leaf teas, kombucha on tap, house bubble/boba tea (made with fresh milk, boiled tea, and tapioca pearls), chai, tea lattes, and tea-based mocktails such as the kombucha-nada. Majid describes the concept as sitting "between a wine bar and coffee shop," built to give LGBTQ+ and sober-curious Chicagoans a late-night place to gather without alcohol. Evenings bring open mics, book clubs, craft nights, trivia, drag bingo, and DJ sets. By late 2024 the shop was outpacing its sales goals and planning a line of canned non-alcoholic tonics.

As of August 2026 Fable is running what it calls a soft relaunch after a period of reduced service, and says on its own site that it is currently offering a limited menu and shortened hours, from 7am to 4pm, with expanded hours and menu to come. Its published menu page is currently empty, so nothing about the current food or drink offering can be verified from it, and its own social account gives closing time as 5pm rather than 4pm. We previously listed three St. Agrestis Phony Negroni variants, craft lattes and a toasted-sugar lemonade here. We can no longer confirm any of those are being served — the only trace of that description we could find leads back to our own earlier copy rather than to any independent source — so treat it as unconfirmed rather than current. The café is open daily; check before travelling.

name: Fable Melbourne

Alongside a mixologist-designed cocktail list, it runs three signature house mocktails built with the same care as its cocktails, including the Sancho Panza Vol 2 (watermelon syrup, lime, grapefruit, aquafaba, soda) and the Northstar (ginger, lime, mint, cucumber), plus an alcohol-free spiced-rum build. The zero-proof drinks pair with an entirely gluten-free Mediterranean share-plate menu. Time Out calls it Melbourne's highest rooftop bar and rates its three signature mocktails as original and painstakingly prepared, built on watermelon cordial, alcohol-free spiced rum, mint and fresh fruit.

It was founded by Anastasia Farber, a former bartender who used her mixology background to build a place where people could socialize and "not be forced to have a drink in their hand." The roughly 1,100-square-foot space is part Adaptogen Bar, part rotating art gallery (works for sale), part small NA bottleshop, and part event venue hosting poetry slams, movie nights, and art parties. Drinks lean on natural ingredients and adaptogenic blends: the Elderberry Healer (Hatchet Granny, elderberry, lemon, soda, honey, black pepper), house Dandelion Root Tea, build-your-own Adaptogen Spritzes, and slow-simmered Eastern-European kompots. name: Fanboy
description: Fanboy is an intimate, atmospheric cocktail bar on West Broad Street serving small plates alongside a rotating dinner menu, and local coverage consistently singles out the length of its non-alcoholic drink list rather than the existence of one. It is the late option among Richmond's alcohol-free-friendly venues: open until midnight midweek and 2am on Friday and Saturday, which puts it in a very small group in this city where someone not drinking can still be out at one in the morning with a properly made drink in front of them. With Point 5 closing at 6pm and SoBar running only two nights a week, that late licence is genuinely scarce here. Closed Mondays, and the room is small enough to fill early at weekends.

name: Federal Cafe & Bar
description: Federal Cafe & Bar is a Kiwi- and Aussie-inspired brunch cafe that has anchored the Northern Quarter since 2014, now one of Manchester's most-followed coffee spots and a TripAdvisor Travelers' Choice 2025 winner. Its non-alcoholic drinking is genuinely developed rather than an afterthought, built around a proper matcha program — an iced matcha you can flavour with strawberry, blueberry or mango (£4.50), an oat-milk matcha latte and a Banana Bread Iced Matcha topped with banana bread cold foam (£5). Around it sit spiced chai and a 'dirty' chai spiked with an espresso shot, house batch and cold brew, hand-brewed single-origin filter coffee and fresh-pressed 'Fed' juices, so a non-drinker has a full all-day menu rather than a token soft drink.

The same seasonal craft extends to a small zero-proof list, including the Citron-Fraise (strawberry coulis, lemon, simple syrup), La Tahitienne (pineapple, lemon, hibiscus syrup, tonic), and La Fleur du Désert (Seedlip Notas de Agave, grapefruit, lime, jalapeño syrup). The bar is also known for building custom mocktails to taste on request.

name: Felix Trattoria
description: Felix Trattoria is chef Evan Funke's acclaimed regional-Italian restaurant on Abbot Kinney Boulevard in Venice, opened in 2017 with restaurateur Janet Zuccarini. Known for handmade pasta produced daily in a glass-enclosed "pasta laboratorio," Felix is a Michelin Guide restaurant and a fixture of LA's dining scene. Its bar runs a genuine named non-alcoholic cocktail program built around imported and craft zero-proof bases — England's Pentire botanical aperitivo and Seattle's Pathfinder hemp-and-botanical amaro — plus house-made ginger beer. Lead bartender Henry Terhune frames the list around Italian aperitivo culture: drinks meant "to pique your appetite" before a carb-rich meal. Named zero-proof options include the Monte Rosa, Mare Nostrum, Zenzero, and the Coca-Felix, a Chinotto-style "bitter Coca-Cola" riff — composed, restaurant-quality options rather than an afterthought.

It is celebrated for a deep collection of roughly forty amari and bitter liqueurs, but it also runs one of the inner metro's most developed zero-proof programs: a dedicated Zero Proof cocktail list alongside non-alcoholic beer and wine. Named alcohol-free pours include Nectar of the Gods (grapefruit, lemon, pickle brine, simple and soda), Billows & Thieves (grapefruit, lemon, cold brew, cardamom-cinnamon syrup), the N/agroni (Sanbitter, tart cherry, juniper syrup) and the N/alort, the house zero-proof answer to Malort, plus a Rosemary Peach Bellini, an Agua de Jamaica and a tart cherry, lemon and ginger health shot. 5280 flagged its "great nonalcoholic cocktail choices," and Westword named it Best You'd-Never-Know-It's-Vegan Restaurant in 2025.

description: Fermenteria on East Commerce Street builds its drinks around fermentation, which is the single most useful technique available to anyone making a serious alcohol-free drink — it produces acidity, funk and depth that no amount of fruit juice can imitate. The named zero-proof options are Butterfly Blossom, a pineapple coconut, and a strawberry lime tulsi built on holy basil. A venue whose whole identity is fermentation is naturally equipped for this category, since the process that makes kombucha interesting is the same one that makes wine interesting, minus the alcohol. Note the narrow window: it opens Thursday through Saturday only, from 4pm, and is closed the rest of the week.

name: The Fiction Kitchen
description: The Fiction Kitchen is Raleigh's long-running vegetarian and vegan restaurant, now in Gateway Plaza on Crabtree Boulevard after leaving downtown. Its dinner menu carries a full "Zero Proof Cocktails" section — six named builds between $8 and $10 built around acid, bitterness and texture rather than sugar: verjus in the Sorta Sangria, a beet syrup against tonic in Let the Beet Build, a drinking vinegar in the Seasonal Shrub, cold brew and hickory syrup in Wake 'n Shake, and a house-made falernum in Spring Fling. Athletic's golden ale and Sierra Nevada's non-alcoholic IPA are on too. For a restaurant rather than a bar, it is one of the most developed non-alcoholic lists in the metro. Check the hours first: closed Monday and Tuesday, split lunch and dinner service on Friday and Saturday, lunch only on Sunday.

name: Fifty West Brewing Company
description: Fifty West Brewing Company is a destination brewery and burger bar strung along US Route 50 (Wooster Pike) on Cincinnati's east side, founded in 2012 in a former Prohibition-era roadhouse. For non-drinkers it is more than an afterthought: the house lineup includes a 0.0% ABV sparkling Hop Water brewed with pineapple and Citra hops (zero calories, gluten-free), a made-in-house root beer, hand-spun milkshakes and root beer floats, plus fountain drinks and rotating non-alcoholic options. It is a working brewery, so beer flows freely, but the zero-proof choices are genuinely house-produced rather than a token can in the cooler. The Wooster Pike taproom anchors a sprawling Route 50 campus with patios and sand volleyball, making it an easy stop whether or not you are drinking beer.

Pittsburgh Magazine put it among the city's 25 best restaurants for 2026, describing it as serving comfort food with a thoughtful, elevated touch, and a reviewer characterised the room as comfortable and professionally done but not overly designed, full of houseplants and quirky art. It won the 2018 James Beard Award for Outstanding Wine Program, and that bar rigor extends to a small seasonal zero-proof section that changes with the menu. The bar pours Seedlip-based non-alcoholic drinks and a turmeric tonic, and will build NA cocktails to order. At the salon's tea bar, every pour stays at 0% alcohol: Copenhagen Sparkling Tea, tea elixirs, tea flights and botanical mocktails built on Abstinence zero-proof spirits, like the Tea Posy with Water Garden tea, Abstinence Cape Floral and grenadine. For non-drinkers, Forsythia keeps a small but real zero-proof offering at its full bar: the headliner is the "75 Year Old Virgin," a spirit-free riff on the classic French 75 built on juniper, cara cara orange, and lemon for a citrusy, botanical, gin-like character — a drink Philadelphia Magazine singled out among the city's best non-alcoholic cocktails. name: Fort Point Valencia
description: Fort Point Valencia is the Mission District beer hall of Fort Point Beer Company, the San Francisco brewery founded in 2014 by cousins Tyler and Justin Catalana. The 22-tap flagship reopened at 742 Valencia St in February 2022 with color-saturated plaster walls, oak woodwork, neon art, and a casual SF-style seafood menu. What earns it a spot here: Fort Point is one of the few breweries pouring its own non-alcoholic line. In January 2025, after roughly three years of R&D, it launched NA versions of its two best-known beers — NA KSA, a light, crisp Kölsch-style ale, and NA Villager, a balanced San Francisco-style IPA — both under 0.5% ABV and brewed (not dealcoholized) with a Berkeley Yeast strain that minimizes alcohol conversion. The NA beers are sold at Fort Point's San Francisco locations, including this Valencia beer hall.
signatureDrinks: NA KSA (Kölsch-style)|NA Villager (IPA)

name: Fount Board & Table
description: Fount Board & Table is an Uptown all-day cafe and grazing-board shop that keeps a dedicated "NA Wines, Spirits & Euphorics" section stocked with 20-plus non-alcoholic bottles to drink in or take home. Alongside the espresso and charcuterie, the retail wall curates alcohol-free wines, zero-proof spirits, NA beers, and functional "euphorics," making it one of the few Dallas coffee houses that doubles as a spirit-free bottle selection. The lineup is actively maintained — the venue's zero-proof menu category was refreshed in March 2026 — and the shop is run by husband-and-wife founders Olivia and Ryan Genthe.

name: The Fountain Room
description: The Fountain Room is a Wisconsin-style supper club in the Bottleworks District, opened in the summer of 2022 by the father-and-son restaurant team Perry and Blake Fogelsong after a pandemic-era trip north. The room is Art Deco jazz-age — velvet banquettes, chandeliers, a reel-to-reel machine — and OpenTable and People named it one of America's fifty most beautiful restaurants. The food is supper-club canon: pickled relish trays, prime rib, house desserts. Non-alcoholic drinks get their own printed "No ABV" section rather than a line at the bottom of the cocktail list, running to the Crouching Tiger, Circle City Sober, a Cherry Burlesque built on cherry, lime, honey syrup, ginger beer and mint, and an alcohol-removed Sauvignon Blanc by the glass.

name: Four Walls
description: Four Walls is a cocktail bar hidden inside The Joseph hotel at 405 4th Avenue South in downtown Nashville — hard to find but not quite a speakeasy, and, as Nashville Scene put it, the sort of place where grabbing a drink is an event, with proper lighting and volume levels appropriate for easy conversation. Its menu runs in numbered volumes and is currently on Volume 5. Lead bartender Lawson Ballinger approaches each drink like a scene, layered with unexpected ingredients and tactile presentation. Its alcohol-free offering is structured unusually and rather well: rather than a fixed list, the section headed "Mocktails | Alcohol-Free Experiences" asks you to choose one of ten flavour profiles — bright and zesty, rich and indulgent, herbaceous and fresh, spiced and warm, tropical and fruity, floral and aromatic, savoury and umami, sweet and silky, playful and effervescent, or complex and robust — and then leave the rest to the bartender. It is presented identically to the bar's Elevated Highballs section, not as an afterthought. No price is printed for the mocktails. Non-alcoholic beer is listed: Untitled Art Italian-style pilsner at $8 and Athletic Run Wild IPA at $9.

name: Française
description: Française is a French neighbourhood bistro on South Perry Street from Adam Hegsted, one of the Inland Northwest's most prolific restaurateurs, applying classic French technique to local produce in a room that is elegant without being formal. Its drinks list carries a named mocktail — the Lemon Sage Delight — alongside a proper loose-leaf tea selection running to earl grey, citrus chamomile, peppermint, orange spice, wild berry hibiscus, English breakfast and green. It opens at 3pm on weekdays and at 9am at weekends, which makes it one of the few rooms in this guide serving a considered non-alcoholic drink in the morning.

name: Franklin Ave Cocktails & Kitchen
address: 231 S Edison St, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
description: Salt Lake magazine's 2025 Best Restaurant, a buzzy New American spot tucked into the historic Franklin Avenue Variety Theatre building on Edison Street downtown — the fourth Salt Lake concept from the Bourbon Group, with chef Matt Crandall's menu mixing elevated plates with sharp bar food. For non-drinkers, the kitchen runs a rotating seasonal mocktail menu alongside its whiskey- and amaro-leaning cocktail list; City Cast Salt Lake singled out a comforting hibiscus-and-cinnamon hot-toddy-style mocktail as a standout. The art-covered, leather-and-exposed-brick basement room is a frequent recommendation for the downtown Edison Street cluster (note it is 21+).

name: Frannie & The Fox
description: Wood-fired Italian restaurant inside the boutique Hotel Emeline in Ansonborough, downtown Charleston, serving shareable, locally sourced plates and thin-crust pizzas. The beverage team keeps a small lineup of named non-alcoholic cocktails alongside the full bar, including the No'Groni, built to taste like a gin negroni from Gnista wormwood, gin-flavored syrup and orange bitters, and a blueberry mocktail made on Amethyst's South Carolina blueberry-ginger-mint NA spirit. Mocktails are described by the beverage team as curated with the same approach as the alcoholic cocktail program.

name: Free Spirit @ Riverdale Hub

description: Free Spirit is a fully alcohol-free cocktail bar and restaurant operated by Riverdale Hub, a not-for-profit social enterprise inside a converted century-old building in Toronto's Leslieville / Gerrard India Bazaar neighbourhood. It opened April 23, 2024 and runs on a no-tipping, living-wage model, with restaurant proceeds going toward addressing barriers for equity-deserving groups in the community. The ten-drink zero-proof menu spans a Bloody Caesar, a Cosmo built on Seedlip Garden 108, and an Espresso Martini made with Seedlip Spice 94, backed by a zero-proof beer list that includes Guinness 0.0 and Heineken 0.0.

name: Free Spirited
description: Free Spirited is a fully alcohol-free craft cocktail lounge and scratch kitchen in Alhambra, run by husband-and-wife Amber Pennington and Arleo De Guzman, and one of Southern California's first dedicated non-alcoholic bars. It opened in 2023 in a former Mexican restaurant. The current menu runs 26 cocktails across four sections — Health Conscious, Funky Flavors, Sweet Stuff and Caffeinated — and everything is $9, with tax and tip already included in the price, which is close to unheard of. A flight of up to four tasters is $5 each, and happy hour from 5 to 6 takes 20% off. The kitchen is entirely gluten-free and largely vegan. CORRECTION: we previously said the bar makes its own non-alcoholic spirits in-house. We could not source that anywhere and have removed it — what is true is that the drinks are built on unbranded house spirits named by character rather than brand (aloe herb, citrus rind, roasted grain, spiced molasses) plus its own FS bitters and vermouth. name: Free Spirits Beverage Company
description: Free Spirits is Idaho's first alcohol-free bottle shop, and unusually it is also a manufacturer — the business began in 2018 as the bitters maker iOnE and became a full non-alcoholic beverage company in 2020, producing its own products in-house with no preservatives. The shelves carry its own shrub cocktail mixes, including the smoky Luke Peary and the sweet Cherry Chill, alongside national ranges like Ritual Zero Proof. It also runs the Temperance Trail, a Dry January passport of eight alcohol-free stops across Boise now in its third year, which makes this shop the organising centre of the city's sober scene rather than only its supplier.

name: Freemason Abbey Restaurant
description: Freemason Abbey occupies a converted 1873 church in Norfolk's historic Freemason district — soaring ceilings, original woodwork, and a dining room that draws visitors as much for the building as the food. Its named alcohol-free drink is the Sparkly Blue Pearl, listed by Visit Norfolk among the city's mocktails worth ordering. The value here is situational: this is the room people book for an anniversary or a visiting family, exactly the kind of occasion where somebody at the table is pregnant, driving or simply not drinking, and having a proper named drink on the list keeps them part of the evening.
signatureDrinks: Sparkly Blue Pearl

name: Fremont Brewing
description: Fremont Brewing's Urban Beer Garden at 1050 N 34th Street is one of Seattle's best-known taprooms and pours the deepest line of house-brewed non-alcoholic beer in the city. The brewery was founded in 2009 by Matt Lincecum and Sara Nelson (now Seattle City Council President); note that although its own site still describes it as family-owned, Seattle Hospitality Group — owner of Pike Brewing — acquired a controlling interest in April 2024. Five non-alcoholic beers are on the taplist, all printed at under 0.5% ABV: Non-Alcoholic IPA (Citra and Citra Cryo hops), Hazy IPA (Mosaic and Krush), Dark (chocolate and black malts, Chinook and Hallertau), Lite (Bohemian pilsner malt and Czech Saaz) and the alcohol-free Hoppy Spritz hop water. A Non-Alcoholic Orange Wit exists but is not currently pouring here. An NA flight of five is $15. The line is decorated: silvers at the 2026 North American Non-Alcoholic Cup for the IPA and the Lite, a 2026 World Beer Cup bronze and a 2025 Great American Beer Festival silver for the Dark. The beer garden is explicitly family- and dog-friendly, with covered heated seating and board games.

name: Fresko
description: Fresko is a Mediterranean restaurant on Ingersoll Avenue with two documented alcohol-free drinks that sit at opposite ends of the register: a Blackberry Mocktail built on a spiced blackberry and rose simple syrup with lime juice and Fever Tree sparkling pink grapefruit, and a Chai Mocktail of chai tea, cola syrup and vanilla ice cream. The second is effectively a spiced float, and it is the rare alcohol-free drink designed to be a dessert rather than an aperitif — a category almost nobody caters for. Open 11am to 9pm through the week, later at weekends, and from 10am on Saturday and Sunday.

name: Freya
description: Freya is chef Doug Hewitt's tasting-menu restaurant in Detroit's New Center, where every menu comes with a choice of wine, cocktail, or non-alcoholic cocktail pairing built by beverage director Catherine Kurth. The non-alcoholic track is course-matched, not an afterthought — past pairings have included Rayula, a blend of castor and mango juices, turmeric honey, and lemon juice served alongside a roasted squab course, closing with a Black Raspberry Krydda Snaps made exclusively for the restaurant by Michigan's Norden Aquavit. Hewitt was a 2024 James Beard semifinalist for Best Chef: Great Lakes, and the kitchen treats the NA pairing with the same course-by-course intent as its alcohol counterparts.

name: The Friesian Gastro Pub

description: The Friesian Gastro Pub is a neighbourhood restaurant and bar on the Michigan Street corridor at 720 Michigan Street NE, trading since 2018. Its menu changes weekly with globally-inspired dishes, it carries a deep run of vegetarian and vegan options, and it smokes its own bacon and makes its own carrot cake. For non-drinkers the notable thing is structural: the online drink menu carries a dedicated Non-Alcoholic Beverages section listed alongside Cocktails, Drafts, Wine, Cans, Liquor and Sake, rather than burying zero-proof options at the foot of another page. The builds are properly composed and priced from about $5 to $8, including the Cherry Apple Tonic, Matcha Millions and a blueberry-honey lemonade.

name: Frisco Kava Bar
description: Frisco Kava Bar is a fully alcohol-free kava room on Preston Road serving what it calls 100% plant-based drinks. The menu runs to blended Kava-Ladas in mango, strawberry, piña colada, peach and mocha; a mocktail section including the Kava-Rita, Espresso Kavatini and The Frisco 75; plus flavoured kratom teas and raw kava. name: Front Street Cafe
description: Front Street Cafe in Fishtown runs an all-day operation under the Market-Frankford El, and its menu carries a printed "Zero Proof" section — four drinks, every one built on an alcohol-free spirit rather than juice. The Zero Proof Louie is the simplest, honey and lime with Ritual gin. The Refresher runs Ritual gin into a house ginger syrup with cranberry, ginger ale and strawberries. The Buffalo is the most interesting build in the city's zero-proof canon, combining Ritual whiskey with pomegranate syrup and Seedlip Spice 94 — two different alcohol-free spirits layered in one glass, which almost nobody does. The Mocha Espresso Martini uses Ritual tequila with espresso, house chocolate sauce and peppermint syrup. Dinner runs to ten on Friday and Saturday.

name: Fullsteam Brewery at Boxyard RTP
address: 900 Park Offices Dr, Research Triangle Park, Durham, NC 27709
description: Fullsteam's taproom at Boxyard RTP, the shipping-container development in Research Triangle Park, is the brewery's trading location, and it pours Blank Check — a 0.5% ABV "prohibition pilsner" the brewery makes itself as the alcohol-free counterpart to its Paycheck lager. It is Craft Malt Certified, brewed with locally malted Cumberland corn, Epiphany pilsner malt and North Carolina two-row barley alongside Wakatu, Saphir and Magnum hops, at 26 IBU — enough bitterness to keep it dry rather than sweet. An NA beer brewed in-house rather than bought in is rare anywhere and unique in this metro. Note the location: the original Rigsbee Avenue brewery is not trading and the downtown site is under construction, so Boxyard, Tuesday to Saturday eleven to eight, is the one that will get you a beer. Cans go to go; call ahead for draught.

name: Fura
description: Fura is a future-food, low-carbon cocktail bar on Amoy Street whose printed 'Ugly Delicious' menu section runs five dedicated non-alcoholic drinks alongside five house-fermented low-alcohol 'wines'. The zero- and low-proof work is central to the concept: imperfect surplus fruit and vegetables (in partnership with local vendor Fresh Veggies) are fermented in-house into fruit wines and kombucha rather than thrown away. Run by ex-Noma head forager Christina Rasmussen and ex-Operation Dagger bartender Sasha Wijidessa, it won the Ketel One Sustainable Bar Award at Asia's 50 Best Bars 2024.

name: Gai Noi
description: Gai Noi is chef Ann Ahmed's acclaimed Lao restaurant, opened in May 2023 in the former 4 Bells space on Harmon Place, overlooking Loring Park in downtown Minneapolis. Ahmed — also behind Lat 14 and Khâluna, and a James Beard Best Chef: Midwest nominee — draws on the Xieng Khouang region of Laos her family is from; the name references khao gai noi, a short-grain sticky rice. In 2023 Gai Noi became the only Minnesota restaurant named to the New York Times' list of the 50 best restaurants in America. Its drinks menu includes a dedicated "Zero-Proof Cocktails" section of five named, fruit-forward house creations: the Guava Mule, Star Boi (star fruit elixir, citrus oil), Dole Whip (pineapple and coconut cream), Pineapple Butterfly, and Lemongrass Palmer. The restaurant spans a ground-floor bar, upper dining rooms, and a rooftop patio.
signatureDrinks: Guava Mule|Star Boi|Dole Whip|Pineapple Butterfly|Lemongrass Palmer

name: Gaia's Kava Root
description: Gaia's Kava Root is a family-owned, 100% alcohol-free kava bar that opened in October 2024 on Central Avenue near the University of New Mexico, and describes itself as a sanctuary — "a living room for the curious, the creative, the healers, and the ones who needed something different." Kava shells run from $6 to $20 alongside kava shots, and the bar also serves kanna, the mood-lifting South African botanical, which is an unusual thing to find on a menu in the United States. A long herbal tea list covers strawberry, pineapple, cherry, watermelon, lavender, mango and lemon-lime, and the specialty mocktails contain no alcohol at all. It keeps late hours, running past midnight most nights and to 4am on Friday and Saturday. Both kava and kanna are psychoactive botanicals rather than inert soft drinks, and the bar restricts kava to adults 18 and over.

name: Garden Party
description: Garden Party is a combined plant shop and bar on South Madison Street in downtown Spokane, a room full of greenery where the drinks list runs to wine, wine cocktails, champagne cocktails, a couple of local taps from YaYa and Lumberbeard — and an entire mocktail menu of its own. Its most useful feature for a non-drinker is structural rather than liquid: the door is not carded, only the order is, so under-21s and anyone who would rather not be assessed on the way in can sit in the room like everybody else. Small bites rotate, with a grilled cheese made on bread from the bakery next door. Thursday to Saturday, 4pm to 11pm.

name: Gates & Brovi
description: Gates & Brovi is a neighbourhood American restaurant and bar on Monroe Street in Dudgeon-Monroe, the walkable stretch of shops and kitchens west of the UW campus, and it keeps a straightforward non-alcoholic list that covers what people actually order: an NA paloma, an NA margarita, an NA gin and tonic and a virgin bloody mary — the last of which is close to a civic requirement in Wisconsin. There is nothing avant-garde here, and that is the appeal; it is a well-run neighbourhood room where asking for a drink without alcohol produces a properly made one rather than a conversation. Weekend service starts at 9am.
