name: Gather Coffee & Kava Bar
description: Gather Coffee & Kava Bar is a fully alcohol-free kava bar and third-wave coffee house on Ray Street in North Park, San Diego, open from 2pm until late every night of the week. It runs two programs side by side: espresso and cold brew pulled from locally roasted Mostra Coffee beans, and noble kava sourced from sustainably grown crops in Vanuatu, the Solomon Islands, Fiji and Hawaii. Kava is a psychoactive root drink from the South Pacific, prepared as a water infusion and drunk socially in place of alcohol — it contains no alcohol, but it is mildly sedative in its own right, which matters if your recovery rules out intoxicants generally rather than alcohol specifically. Gather serves kava only, with no kratom on the menu, which is a meaningful distinction in a category where the two are often poured side by side. Newcomers are directed to the kava flight, which samples across preparations, and staff are widely described as walking first-timers through the whole experience. The room is dog-friendly, stocked with board games, and drinks can be taken to go.

Alongside its full-strength inventory it stocks roughly two dozen rotating NA beers from Athletic Brewing, Best Day Brewing, Gruvi, and others - both to-go and on the tasting bar.

name: Gemini Room
description: Gemini Room is a women- and LGBTQIA+-owned, 1970s-inspired all-day café and bar at 1101 East Pike Street in Capitol Hill's Chophouse Row, opened in mid-December 2022 as the debut project of Tanner Mclaughlin and Jackie Proctor in partnership with Burgess/Hall. By day it does locally roasted espresso, coffee and tea lattes, breakfast staples and seasonal bowls and sandwiches; after dark it becomes, in the Infatuation's words, a party that can only really be described as groovy, with mod lounge furniture and 1970s glassware. Its mocktail list is one of the longest in Seattle — nine drinks under a "Mocktails" heading — and most are $8. The full list: a bottled St. Agrestis Phony Negroni ($12), Clear Sky Sour ($13, Pathfinder Hemp and Root, lemon, simple syrup, soda), Sparkling Citrus Soda, Ginger Basil Grapefruit Soda, Fancy Shirley (Toschi cherry syrup, lemon-lime soda), Ube Orange Cream Soda, Everyone Loves a Rickey (coconut cream, lime, soda), a Crodino Spritz and a Pathfinder Espresso Tonic. A separate non-alcoholic section adds Athletic Brewing, kombucha and Casamara Club botanical sodas. Open from 9am; closed Mondays.

name: Gershwin's
description: Gershwin's is a Granby Street cocktail bar in downtown Norfolk whose alcohol-free drinks are built on non-alcoholic spirits and finished with the same techniques as its full menu. The Bohemian combines alcohol-free gin with elderflower syrup, grapefruit juice, egg white and bitters — a proper sour, foam and all — while the Grand Illumination pours non-alcoholic whiskey smoked over cherry wood with orange peel and bitters. Smoking a zero-proof drink tableside is the clearest possible signal that a bar considers the alcohol-free order worth its time, since the theatre is the point and none of it depends on the alcohol.

name: Gibson
description: Gibson is a second-floor speakeasy on Bukit Pasoh Road from the Jigger & Pony Group, a longtime fixture of Asia's 50 Best Bars, whose menu carries a genuinely considered non-alcoholic section illustrated with watercolour sketches of its key ingredients. The anchor is the Urban Farmer No.4 (S$18), a zero-proof build around locally grown cranberry hibiscus from urban-farming collective Edible Garden City, with tangy, citrusy notes. Gibson also pours a non-alcoholic Bloody Mary (S$18) and alcohol-free variations of its signature cocktails, so a non-drinker is treated to the same care as the spirit-forward list.

name: Gift Horse
description: Gift Horse is a raw bar on Westminster Street from chef Benjamin Sukle, built entirely on Rhode Island shellfish — its oyster programme runs through every growing region in the state. The bar makes non-alcoholic drinks with a local streak, including one built on Del's, the frozen lemonade that is a Rhode Island institution, and an orange shrub. Playful room, seriously sourced.

name: Gigantic
description: Gigantic is a jewel-box cocktail bar on Easthampton's Cottage Street, opened in 2018 by Ned King in a small room with a pressed-tin ceiling, painted portraits and stained-glass lamps. The cocktail list is organised by year of origin, from 1937 to the present, and the house mocktails get the same treatment as the spirited drinks — the Dream Defender is a zero-proof rebuild of the Zombie on lemon, lime, passionfruit, pineapple, pineapple syrup and mint. It is a full bar serving alcohol, so this is a good zero-proof list inside an ordinary bar rather than an alcohol-free room. No kitchen — eat first.
signatureDrinks: Dream Defender (zero-proof Zombie — lemon, lime, passionfruit, pineapple, pineapple syrup, mint)

name: Gigglewaters
description: Gigglewaters is a 1920s speakeasy-styled restaurant and bar in downtown Safety Harbor with a single-screen classic-movie theater in back — order a drink and catch an old film. Its award-winning bar treats mocktails with the same care as its cocktails; the Fyre Fest (blood orange, grapefruit, pineapple, honey, fresh basil, sugar rim) leads a spirit-free list that locals rank among the area's best. Opened in 2018 by Richie and Rachel Fine Wilson.  The screening room is the real differentiator for a non-drinker: an evening with a structure other than drinking is a far easier three hours to spend without a glass.

name: Gilt Bar
description: Gilt Bar is the River North restaurant and bar that launched Brendan Sodikoff's Hogsalt group in 2010, a dark, brass-and-leather room that describes itself as dedicated to the pleasures of drinking in restaurants and eating in bars, with a concealed speakeasy called The Library beneath it. Its cocktail menu carries a Spirit-Free heading whose drinks are priced at $14.95, within three dollars of the full-proof list. The Citrus Ritual is built on Ritual's tequila alternative with blood orange, lime, mint and club soda; the Seedlip Sour pairs Seedlip Grove 42 with cranberry; and a St. Agrestis Phony Negroni is poured from the bottle. Resy singled the program out in its guide to Chicago's non-alcoholic cocktails.

The Traditional column carries the Yemeni preparations the brand is built on — Harazi Mufawar, Maleki, Sana'ani, Jubani and Qishr — alongside the Adeni Chai that fuses Yemeni tea leaves with Indian masala spicing, cardamom and cinnamon. The New York Times featured Haraz in a June 2025 business story on the wave of Yemeni cafes meeting demand for late-night, alcohol-free social spaces. What started as one storefront in a converted insurance office has since scaled into a national franchise, with this East Dearborn location as the flagship.

description: Harold's Haunt is a queer-owned, witch-themed "they bar" on Grant Avenue in Millvale, opened in October 2022 by the people behind the attached Maude's Paperwing Gallery, and it is intentional about sober inclusion — its own site says there are always mocktails on the menu for its sober friends, served as house-made "Fauxtions" alongside the full bar. Food is vegan-friendly, supplied by Lemon Tree PGH, and orders are marked at the table with tarot cards; past dishes have included the Hobbit Pizza and Calcifer's Coals. There is a patio out back for when the front gets loud. Note that the bar does not publish a current drinks list online, so the Fauxtions rotate and are best asked about in person; the ones documented in press have been fruit-and-soda builds rather than non-alcoholic-spirit cocktails. The venue is candid that it is not fully accessible: there is a step at both the front and back doors, a steep slope in the back hallway, and small bathrooms without handles.

It roasts daily rather than in batches held in storage, and sells only as much as it needs so that what reaches the cup is fresh. The range is almost entirely Ethiopian single-origin, named by region and roast: Ethiopia Harrar in medium and dark, Yirgacheffe in medium and dark, Sidama in medium and dark, Limu in medium and dark, plus named lots including Sidama Sibune, Yirgacheffe Yirhama and Harrar Haruva, and decaf Sidama and Limu. Zero-proof builds run from Steady Pete's Ginger Brew (Tanqueray 0.0 and Lucky Saint IPA) and a Non-Alc Cherry Negroni with Lyre's Amaretti to the Afterburner, made with Botivo and Almave non-alcoholic agave spirit. For two years it was a 100% alcohol-free Cuban-coffee cafe and art space, founded by Eva Rodriguez-Cué to offer a "sober nightlife" alternative — a comfortable place for alcohol-free evening socializing when other cafes had closed. It pulled Cuban coffee drinks (Cubano, cafecito, café con leche, cortadito, and the shareable colada) with Cuban pastries, and doubled as a community hub for art and music.

Drinks arrive via a leather-bound book of spells, each cocktail tied to a piece of folklore, and the alcohol-free builds sit within that same framework under a dedicated Zero Proof list. They are not simplified: the spirit-free drinks use clarified milk, aquafaba, saline, bittering roots and house cordials, and are constructed with the same number of steps as the full-proof menu.

Several mocktails sit on the standing printed menu rather than being made on request, led by a pomegranate-ginger spritz at $10 built on non-alcoholic sparkling wine and a Passion Fruit Picante. The no-proof builds are not the alcoholic drink minus the alcohol; they are separate recipes engineered to land on the same flavour, so the earthy no-proof reaches for sparkling green and lapsang teas where the full-proof uses mezcal.

Drinks are the only thing served, and the mixology program takes Prohibition-era construction and runs it through a Singaporean lens, which extends to the zero-proof options listed alongside the cocktails rather than hidden behind a request. name: Here Nor There
description: Here Nor There is a reservation-only speakeasy in downtown Austin, located at 612 Brazos Street near the historic Driskill Hotel. Opened in June 2018, the bar seats only 55 guests in an intimate basement space accessed by a code-locked alley gate, with reservations made through a dedicated mobile app. The cocktail program is led by experienced mixologists with a globally-influenced, theatrical approach — guests are greeted with complimentary prosecco by a taxidermy bear before being escorted to their table. Cocktails are spirits-forward and priced between $30–50; upscale mocktails are available for guests who prefer alcohol-free options, though the bar's primary focus is craft cocktails.

name: Herman's Coffee
description: Herman's Coffee is a coffee roastery, café, and specialty market in Philadelphia's Pennsport neighborhood, opened by owner Mat Falco in 2017 inside a former auto-mechanic's shop. Beginning in 2020 — after discovering the non-alcoholic aperitif Ghia — Falco built what the Philadelphia Inquirer calls one of the region's largest zero-proof selections: over 200 non-alcoholic wines, spirits, and beers, plus 50–75 mixers and syrups and more than 100 bitters, much of it sold to take home. By day, the café pours house-made non-alcoholic creations such as the Blood Orange Espresso Tonic, Lavender Lemonade Spritz, and the "Don't Call Me Shirley Temple." On Friday and Saturday nights, Herman's After Dark switches to candlelit table service with a menu of cocktails and wines "with and without alcohol," plus light bites and rotating food pop-ups.

description: HEX Superette is the market, cafe, and bar from Shane and Meaghan Carpenter, whose HEX Ferments has been making kraut, kimchi, and kombucha since 2013 — production still runs out of the back of the same Govans building. The Kitchen & Bar menu keeps a dedicated NA Cocktails section: the Teetotally Tiki builds Ghia apéritif over HEX's own smoky pineapple kombucha with warm spices and lime, the Dandy Tonic pours house tonic with dandelion, chicory root, and lemon, and the Spicy Melissa mixes umami ginger syrup, lime, ginger, and tonic. Six house kombuchas — butterfly lime, ginger, lazy days, smoky pineapple, turmeric tonic, and a rotating seasonal — pour by the glass, and the farm sodas are built from house seasonal fruit concentrates and shrubs. It keeps a dedicated non-alcoholic menu section with a title worth the walk on its own — "Clear Eyes, Full Hearts, No Proof" — carrying named zero-proof cocktails built on real non-alcoholic spirits such as Pathfinder, St. Agrestis and Giffard's non-alcoholic aperitif.

It keeps the longest hours of any Yemeni room in the city, running 7am to 11:30pm most nights and to midnight on Friday and Saturday, and describes itself simply as open early and staying late. The drinks are traditional and spice-driven: the Heyma Latte built with cardamom and cinnamon, Aden tea cooked with cardamom, ginger and cream, and Mufawaar, the cream-topped spiced coffee that anchors most Yemeni menus. The #BeetBetter is the standout, combining beet, strawberry, lime, turbinado and Topo Chico into something genuinely complex; the Pina Colorita — coconut water, orange juice, pineapple and lime — is the lighter option; and the HG Mule swaps spirits for agave, lime and Buddha's Brew ginger kombucha, giving it a fermented bite most virgin mules lack. The 9,000-square-foot rooftop is partly covered and fitted with misters and firepits, so it works across seasons.

The printed menu marks every drink with a strength rating, and two are marked NO% instead: The Lemongrass Fizz, built on non-alcoholic spirits with lemongrass syrup, lime and soda, and The Berry Basil Smash, with non-alcoholic spirits, strawberry, raspberry, lemon and basil. Guajiro Cuban Comfort Food is permanently parked on site, and outside food is welcome. The taproom is pet- and family-friendly, open from 11am at weekends and 3pm on Mondays. IMPORTANT for anyone avoiding intoxicants: the taproom lists its non-alcoholic and THC options together, and alongside N/A beer, local High Noon nitro cold brew and local soda it sells Hi-Wire's own Hi-Jinks THC-infused sparkling water, produced in 2mg and 5mg doses in Original and Clementine. The name is a play on its concept: the caffeine drinks get you "high," and the no-alcohol policy keeps it "dry." Open daily from noon to midnight, it pitches itself as a "third space" for creatives, remote workers, and night owls who want bar-style socializing without booze. description: Higher Ground is a farm-driven modern British bistro on the fringe of Manchester's Chinatown, run by three friends — chef Joseph Otway, wine and drinks lead Daniel Craig Martin and general manager Richard Cossins — who met working at Dan Barber's Blue Hill at Stone Barns in New York. Alongside a natural-wine list of small low-intervention European growers, the team pours a no- and low-alcohol selection reviewers have singled out as exceptional.

His brief was a brewpub with a comfortable environment and a cool vibe, and the beer has backed the ambition up with Great American Beer Festival medals in three consecutive years within the brewery's first three. The taproom keeps the non-drinker in mind: Athletic Brewing non-alcoholic beer on hand, plus locally made Devil's Foot craft sodas — an Asheville mocktail-base staple — kombucha and soda. A relaxed, food-forward brewery where the alcohol-free options are genuine craft rather than the usual cola-or-water default.

name: Hillside Farmacy

The restaurant honors the building's history with a 'Soda Fountain' menu of house-made syrups and herbal blends — Visit Austin describes them as 'craft elixirs' rather than standard soft drinks, and the venue's own framing invites guests to order any of them 'with or without a splash of booze.' Beyond the soda fountain, the menu is farm-to-table New American: proteins from Texas ranchers and the Gulf Coast, Texas wildflower honey, microgreens from Joe's, mushrooms from Hi-Fi, locally roasted Proud Mary and Fara coffee, and Evergreen Chai brewed in East Austin. The space is family-friendly with three dining rooms and dog-friendly heated and cooled outdoor patios. The cocktail and wine programs lean into Texas distilleries (Still Austin Whiskey appears in their signature Old Fashioned) and approachable wines.

It is a World's 50 Best Discovery bar and a fixture on the Top 50 Cocktail Bars list, with a second room in Battersea. The space is a retro velvet-forward lounge that doubles as a rotating gallery for Denver artists, with a retail section for local makers. Music event nights run every other Friday; regular service is 18+, music nights are 21+. Featured in Westword's January 2026 NA roundup and 5280 Magazine's restaurant guide.

For non-drinkers, the appeal is two-fold: the shop keeps a deep, dedicated non-alcoholic section, and the bar runs a dedicated N/A draft line that rotates between Untitled Art and Athletic Brewing. The retail NA shelf is one of the broadest in the city, spanning Athletic Brewing (Free Wave, Run Wild, Upside Dawn), Untitled Art, Guinness 0.0, Lagunitas Hoppy Refresher, Brooklyn Special Effects, Best Day, Ghia, and St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, with Sober Carpenter sold by the single. name: Hosmer Bar
description: Hosmer Bar, in Bend's Waypoint Hotel on 3rd Street, puts zero-proof drinks at the front of the offer rather than the back. It makes non-alcoholic versions of the classics — negroni, bloody mary, sours — pours Crux's NØ MØ non-alcoholic beer and Fre alcohol-removed wines, and will substitute non-alcoholic spirits into other drinks on request. Closed Tuesdays; Sunday opens at 10am.

name: Hotel Neptune Bar
description: The European-style cocktail bar inside Hotel Neptune — the downtown boutique hotel that traded as The Dean until its June 2026 rebrand — sits behind a curtain off the lobby. It is a weekend room now: the hotel publishes the bar as open Friday and Saturday from 5pm, and some listings add a Thursday, so check before a midweek trip. Its non-alcoholic builds include a Paloma made with an agave alternative and a zero-proof Cosmopolitan. The same building holds a karaoke den and a lobby coffee shop, both keeping longer hours than the bar.

name: House of Found Objects
description: House of Found Objects is a downtown Birmingham cocktail bar on 2nd Avenue North whose zero-proof drinks are treated as creations in their own right rather than as subtractions — built from fresh fruit and botanicals, with the complexity and structure the bar puts into its alcoholic list. Bham Now's January 2026 guide to non-alcoholic drinking in the city leads with it. The room keeps late hours, opening at 4pm Tuesday through Saturday and running to midnight midweek and 2am on Friday and Saturday, which makes it one of the few places in the city where a non-drinker can genuinely stay out.

Guests order kava shells, botanical teas, boba, cold brew, and CBD drinks instead of cocktails. (Alcohol-free, though its kava and CBD drinks aren't substance-free.)

The format is the argument for including it: a piano bar is an entertainment venue where the show is the reason you are there, so the evening does not depend on what is in your glass. That, plus a 2am licence seven nights a week, makes it a viable late option in the most tourist-heavy part of the city. It opens at 7pm most nights and 6pm at weekends, running to 2am every single night of the week.

name: Hula's Modern Tiki
description: A hip, retro tiki restaurant and bar in Old Town Scottsdale, Hula's serves playful tropical mocktails in vintage tiki mugs, complete with umbrellas and fruity garnishes. Named zero-proof builds include the Captain's Colada (coconut cream, allspice falernum syrup, pineapple juice), the Castaway Cooler (a fruity ginger beer build) and the Hula Juice, which layers passion fruit syrup with pineapple, orange and cranberry. Tiki is a format that works unusually well without alcohol — the sweetness, spice and presentation carry the drink rather than the rum — and Hula's leans into that rather than treating the non-alcoholic list as an obligation. Multiple Valley locations, with the Old Town room the most central.

The drinks programme follows the Powell original, which means the alcohol-free side is unusually deep for a new opening: house cocktails including the Honolulu Mule, the Blue Hawaiian and the Baby Aspirin are all served in alcohol-free versions built to order rather than swapped for a soft drink. A wine bar is the hardest format in which to drink well without alcohol, which is what makes its standing commitment to keeping several non-alcoholic options worth noting. The house benchmark is the Phony Negroni at $10 — Seedlip Spice for the botanical backbone, DHOS Bittersweet for the amaro bitterness, aperitivo rosso for the vermouth weight — stirred and served in the same glass as the original.

The Paper King is the one to order: Thai tea syrup, pineapple and lemon lengthened with Stappi, the Italian red bitter soda. That last ingredient is the tell — Stappi exists to supply genuine bitterness, and reaching for it rather than another fruit juice is what separates a bar thinking about balance from one thinking about sweetness. The bar opens from 3pm midweek and 2pm at weekends, and is closed Mondays; it is a couple of minutes from Via Vecchia and Andy's.

name: Husk
description: Husk Nashville is an acclaimed Southern restaurant that opened on 23 May 2013 in a restored 1880s home in the Rutledge Hill section of downtown's SoBro, following chef Sean Brock's Charleston original of 2010. Brock's involvement is now historical rather than current — he is not listed on the restaurant's own site, and the kitchen has passed through seven executive chefs, most recently in August 2026 when Bryan O'Kelly was promoted after Ben Norton left for Los Angeles. The cooking remains hyper-regional and ingredient-driven Southern. Its bar keeps a dedicated "Spirit-Free" section that is deeper than most restaurants of its standing manage: the Faux-Spresso ($14, Pathfinder, Crema Coffee, cardamom, salted whip), Free Spirit ($10, Lyre's Apéritif, pomegranate-rosemary shrub, soda), and two house-made drinks at $7 — a Husk Lemonade cut with shiso, jalapeño and sea salt, and the T & T, a thyme-honey shrub with tonic and lemon. Southern sodas, Sierra Nevada's Trail Pass NA IPA and a Leitz non-alcoholic sparkling rosé complete it.

More than thirty matcha and hojicha items run across drinks, desserts and food, including a matcha kaya toast served with soft-boiled eggs. It is a daytime room rather than an evening one.

name: Hyacinth
description: Hyacinth is a 40-seat Italian and Mediterranean kitchen on Grand Avenue in St. Paul's Summit Hill, opened in August 2018 by chef Rikki Giambruno (formerly of Brooklyn's Franny's) and named for the street he grew up on in Victoria, Minnesota. Since 2023 it has been led by chef-owner Abraham Gessesse, a founding member of the team. The intimate room is known for house-made pasta and a frequently changing, ingredient-driven menu, and it ranks among the Twin Cities' most acclaimed restaurants, drawing top Star Tribune reviews and James Beard recognition. Its beverage list carries a dedicated non-alcoholic section that treats zero-proof drinking seriously: spirit-free cocktails alongside a house-made lychee soda, NA beer, and an NA sparkling wine. Recent named pours include the Spiritless Spritz, Final Say, and the seasonal Flightless Paper Plane. The NA list rotates with the kitchen, so specific drinks vary by visit.

A brewery bothering to build proper cocktails for people who are not drinking beer is genuinely unusual, and the choices are telling: a Southside and a Spanish G&T are both dry, herbal, bitter-leaning drinks rather than sweet ones. It also runs late, to midnight midweek and 2am on Friday and Saturday, which makes it a workable end to an evening. It sits on Brooklyn Avenue near the Pearl, next door to Tony's Siesta, which keeps similarly late hours.

name: In Confidence
description: In Confidence is the speakeasy inside the Hotel Fort Des Moines, and it stocks the Lyre's range properly — a Zero Proof Mint Julep built on Lyre's bourbon alternative with simple syrup and mint, and a gin and tonic on Lyre's London dry with Fever Tree tonic. Both are straight substitutions into classics, which is exactly what a lot of non-drinkers actually want: not an invented fruit drink, but the thing they used to order, made properly. A julep in particular is almost all spirit, so making a convincing one without alcohol requires the bar to have bought a real product rather than improvised.

name: In Good Spirits
description: In Good Spirits is a dedicated non-alcoholic bottle shop and community space in Chicago's West Town, opened on July 15, 2023 by couple Adriana Gaspar and Hector Diaz. The two ran sober pop-ups around the city before securing a permanent storefront; both came to the alcohol-free life through personal experience — Gaspar stopped drinking after losing her father to COVID-19, and Diaz cut back following a kidney cancer diagnosis. The shelves carry zero-proof beer, wine, spirits, aperitifs, functional and hemp drinks, and RTDs to take away, with local delivery and online pick-up ordering. This is a shop rather than a bar — drinks are sold to go, not poured to sit with. Beyond retail it works as a third space, and the events calendar is the reason to plan a visit: sober supper clubs with local restaurants, zero-proof cocktail workshops, 'POUring' brand tastings with producers such as Copenhagen Sparkling Tea Co. and Kolonne Null, book swaps, artist showcases, sound meditations, and Lotería nights. It is Chicago's longest-running non-alcoholic shop.

name: Incloud
description: Incloud is a fully alcohol-free Chinese teahouse on Prinsep Street, and the only venue of its kind in Singapore built around a floating stream: a channel of running water set into the communal table that carries cups of tea to guests. It trades as an elegant tea-set room by day, with pastries and full gongfu service, and shifts into something much closer to a bar at night. The hours are what make it genuinely useful to a non-drinker — it runs until 3am from Sunday to Friday and until 4am on Saturdays, which is later than most licensed bars in the city, making it one of the very few late-night social venues in Singapore where alcohol is not part of the equation.

name: Indígena by Owamni
description: Indígena by Owamni is the new Guthrie Theater home of chef Sean Sherman's James Beard Award-winning Indigenous restaurant, which closed its original Water Works space in May 2026 and reopened along the Mississippi riverfront in spring 2026. Operated through Sherman's nonprofit NĀTIFS (North American Traditional Indigenous Food Systems), it serves decolonized, pre-colonial cuisine that excludes wheat, dairy, cane sugar, and other colonial imports. The bar is a defining feature: built originally by Anishinaabe/Ojibwe bar manager Kareen Teague, it pioneered an entirely spirit-free Indigenous cocktail menu using foraged Minnesota ingredients — wild rice, corn, currants, teas, and birch, maple, or honey in place of cane sugar. The expanded Guthrie program keeps cocktails and mocktails sourced from BIPOC producers, plus Indigenous teas and Indigenous-owned Copper Cup coffee. Documented zero-proof pours include the Amikomin (black currant, juniper, sumac, birch) and Oginii-Waabigwan (rosehip, strawberry, lavender, agave, rosewater).

name: Inside Passage
description: Inside Passage is an immersive undersea-themed cocktail bar on Pike Street on Capitol Hill, entered through a passage inside Rumba, opened on 25 June 2021 by Travis Rosenthal's Pike Street Hospitality Group. The room is the point: aged ship-hull walls, float and pufferfish lights, and Kiki, an octopus with tentacles up to eighteen feet wrapped across the ceiling in a perpetual state of mid-slither — bar staff spent a spring at home crafting the fake suckers. Drinks arrive with enough theatre that Seattle Met named the phenomenon "the fajita effect": a bartender walks a drink carefully through the tight room and every table pauses to watch. It maintains a dedicated non-alcoholic menu headed "Spirit Free Libations". IMPORTANT: that menu is published through a system we cannot read — the site renders its drink lists entirely in the browser with no readable version underneath — so we cannot list the current spirit-free drinks, their ingredients or their prices, and we could not complete our usual check for infused ingredients. Ask at the bar. It is 21+, seats parties of six or fewer, takes reservations up to six weeks ahead, and adds a 20% service charge.

name: Insomnia ISG Kava Bar and Lounge
description: Insomnia ISG is a Temple Terrace kava lounge that describes itself plainly as a sober bar, open from noon to midnight through the week and to 11pm on Sunday, in a family-friendly room rather than a nightlife one. It serves no alcohol. The list runs kava, botanical teas, loose-leaf tea and coffee, and the venue sits close enough to the University of South Florida to function as a late study room as well as a social one. Two things to know before going: hookah is served, so the room is not smoke-free, and the hours posted on its own site differ slightly from other listings, so call ahead on (813) 570-8137 if you are arriving near closing.

name: Ishizuka
address: Basement B01/139 Bourke Street, Melbourne VIC 3000
description: Ishizuka is a two-hatted, 16-seat basement kaiseki counter down a Bourke Street laneway, where a Kaga-style seasonal degustation is matched course-by-course to drinks. Alongside its award-winning wine list, the kitchen runs a genuine non-alcoholic beverage pairing (from A$90 per person) built from house juices, teas and infusions timed to each of the courses. It's a real zero-proof pairing at a fine-dining level rather than a token soft-drink option, which makes the A$315 tasting menu fully drinkable without alcohol. The kaiseki menu offers non-alcoholic matches from $90 per person, printed on the same menu as the $250 wine matches rather than arranged on request.

name: Isidore
description: Isidore is the fine-dining anchor of the Pullman Market development, and its zero-proof drinks are built on the two non-alcoholic spirits that actually work rather than on syrup. The Maravilla Margarita is modified with Almave blanco, the agave-based non-alcoholic distillate developed with Lewis Hamilton, and the Labrador Spritz uses Tenneyson Black Ginger, a bitter non-alcoholic aperitif that supplies the quality most zero-proof drinks lack. Choosing those two products over a house cordial is the whole signal: they are expensive, they exist only to serve non-drinkers, and stocking them is a deliberate decision. Dinner only, Tuesday to Sunday from 5pm, inside the Pullman Market development just north of downtown.

name: Jackworth Ginger Beer
description: Jackworth is Pennsylvania's first modern ginger beer brewery, at 6615 Hamilton Avenue on the edge of Larimer, opened to the public in May 2024 by Jackworth Smith — that is his real name — who grew up in his father's East End restaurant, was tending bar at seventeen, and first brewed these recipes at home on a half-barrel system in 2013. It brews naturally fermented ginger beer in both alcoholic versions (a 5% ABV Original and a Sorrel) and a canned zero-proof line printed at 0.0%: Classic (organic Peruvian ginger, lime, water, cane sugar), Spicy (the same with habanero), Honey Lavender and Dry. Because the base is genuinely brewed rather than mixed from syrup, the alcohol-free version keeps the bite and body most zero-proof substitutes lack. The bar builds zero-proof cocktails on it too — a Texas Remedy, a Blood in the River and a Peaches for CJ have all featured — though the bar menu cannot be read online, so treat those names as indicative. The room is salvage-built: a bar of old fencing, bank marble and gold-leaf mansion windows.

The room is styled on Studio 54 — mirrored surfaces, a twelve-foot disco unicorn, sightlines to Mercedes-Benz Stadium — and it trades until 2am, which makes it one of the later options downtown. The non-alcoholic drinks are grouped under a menu heading of their own, Free-Spirited, rather than buried in the list. Rooftop Retreat pairs Ritual's tequila alternative with pineapple, basil and coconut water; Flashback uses a whiskey alternative with ginger and lemon; and Off the Record is built on zero-proof gin with vanilla, pomegranate and citrus. description: Jalsah is a fully alcohol-free Yemeni coffeehouse on South Broadway in Downtown Los Angeles, open until 9pm on Friday, Saturday and Sunday. It serves eleven Yemeni signature drinks alongside a full espresso bar: hot Adeni, black tea with milk, cardamom and warm spices; Mufawaar, a rich spiced coffee; Qishr, the cascara-style brew made from coffee husk; Baydani, a Yemeni white drink with toasted sesame and ginger; and Jebani. Beans are single-origin from terraced farms in the Yemeni highlands, sourced direct and roasted in small batches. The room is built for staying - free Wi-Fi, plenty of seating, no rush - and the shop's own line for it is to come in for one cup and stay for three. No alcohol is served at any hour.

name: Japp's Since 1879
description: Japp's Since 1879 is a historical-cocktail bar in Over-the-Rhine, opened in 2010 by celebrated Cincinnati bartender Molly Wellmann inside a 19th-century building that started as John G. Japp's hair-and-wig shop. Its specialty is drinks from the 1700s through the 1950s, made with housemade simple syrups, fresh herbs, berries, juices and floral waters, and that same craft carries over to what Wellmann calls "nonnys." The tepache is the detail that matters: a bar fermenting its own base gets acidity and funk that no juice can supply, and adding serrano heat pushes the drink further from sweetness in the direction of an actual cocktail. It runs a dedicated zero-proof cocktail programme built on Caribbean fruits, spices and house-made cordials, complemented by its basement bar Sousòl, which gives non-alcoholic drinks the same attention as the alcoholic list. The main dining room tasting menu is $325 and an abbreviated bar tasting is $185. Its non-alcoholic offering is one of the most ambitious in America: a dedicated Alcohol-Free Flight at $120, described as a progression of alcohol-free beverages created by the bar team, and priced as a genuine peer to the $145 traditional wine flight rather than a discount alternative. Bar director Austin Hennelly, who built it, believes it is the largest alcohol-free wine, beer and ready-to-drink list of any bar in the country. The drink is hand-brewed kava, customisable with botanical infusions. The group serves no alcohol anywhere, and its drink is hand-brewed kava customised with botanical infusions. Drinks are ordered in two steps, a kava grade followed by a mixer, and served in a shell with a spoon. The bar also pours teas and coffee and runs a pizza menu, and it keeps genuinely late hours for a venue with nothing alcoholic behind the bar.

name: Kava Kavern

Its stated focus is the blending rather than the pour: the bar builds kava tea blends from fresh and organic ingredients, with the flavour combinations composed by its own team rather than bought in. Fifteen hours of daily service in a single room is unusual in this category and makes it one of the more flexible options in a city with a deep kava scene — it works as a mid-morning stop, an afternoon working session and a late-night sit equally well. Kava is a psychoactive South Pacific root drink: alcohol-free, but genuinely relaxing and mildly intoxicating on its own terms.

Happy hour runs 3pm to 6:30pm, and the space doubles as a neighbourhood social hub with open mics for comedy, music and poetry, chess tournaments and tabletop card-gaming meetups. Everyone is welcome in the room and the coffee and tea are served to all ages, but kava itself goes only to guests 18 and over: it is a psychoactive South Pacific root drink, alcohol-free but genuinely sedating. The menu is built entirely around botanicals rather than alcohol: traditionally prepared kava served by the shell, kratom teas, extracts and shots, in-house-brewed blue lotus tea, botanical wellness elixirs blended for energy, focus or mood, handcrafted mocktails, and espresso drinks. An on-site deli, "The Market," serves sandwiches, bowls, and snacks, alongside retail kava powder and capsules. The lounge hosts weekly community nights and events and holds a Tripadvisor Travelers' Choice award. It serves the Wynwood and Upper Buena Vista neighborhoods.

A second room opened in Hollywood in 2026. It pours its own house-made kava nectar rather than third-party products: The O.G. is kava nectar and alkaline water at $9 for a single up to $19 for a quad, and the specialty nectars are $14 — Paradise (mango, pineapple, lime), Ube Coconut, Mexican Chocolate, Mango Lassi, Golden (turmeric, ginger, lemon), Cherry Drop, and Zenergy with Kona coffee and matcha, served until 6pm. Kava lattes run $12–$14 and there is a food menu of ramen, steamed buns and shave ice. IMPORTANT: it serves kava only — we found no kratom, kanna, THC or CBD anywhere, which is unsurprising since California made kratom illegal to sell at any age in October 2025. But note it publishes no dosage figures and no age policy. Open to 1am Friday and Saturday; free parking, dog-friendly patio.

IMPORTANT for readers in recovery, and this is not a detail the chain hides: Kavasutra markets itself as America's premier kava AND kratom bar. Kratom is a co-equal half of the business here, not a side listing. Its alkaloids act on opioid receptors, it produces tolerance and withdrawal in regular users, and several states ban it outright. Kava carries no comparable profile. Order specifically.

The hours are the practical draw: open from 9am on weekdays and to 2am on Friday and Saturday, it covers both ends of the day rather than only the evening, which makes it usable as a morning workspace and as a late-night alternative to a bar. After starting as a Wedgewood-Houston pop-up and opening a retail store in East Nashville, Styll expanded to Berry Hill — the neighborhood where the idea began — opening this roughly 1,000-square-foot shop in October 2025. Like the East Nashville store, it sells exclusively non-alcoholic beer, wine, spirits, and functional beverages (including adaptogenic, THC/CBD, and herbal drinks), and offers on-site sampling so customers can taste before buying. Killjoy bills itself as Nashville's first booze-free beverage shop and, per Styll, the only alcohol-free retail business of its kind in the city. The shop's stated mission is to help change the culture around drinking in Nashville.

The shelves are entirely alcohol-free: NA beer, still and sparkling wine, zero-proof spirits, ready-to-drink cocktails, plus kava, adaptogens, and THC/CBD drinks, with a knowledgeable team to guide customers through the selection. Confirmed brands on its own store include Athletic Brewing, Best Day Brewing, Go Brewing, Untitled Art, Dromme, and Prima Pavé. Killjoy was named among the country's top nonalcoholic bottle shops by Wine Enthusiast, and Styll won a NEXT Award from the Nashville Entrepreneur Center in 2024. Set in a converted Fell Street garage with 30-foot ceilings and a Sonoma olive tree at its center, the roughly 20-course menu leans Nordic, built on curing, drying, and fermentation. For non-drinkers, beverage director Vincent Balao — formerly of three-Michelin-star Atelier Crenn — created a dedicated spirit-free pairing ($135), offered alongside the wine and reserve pairings rather than as a substitute. It draws on housemade kombucha, seasonal shrubs, and amazake, plus Seedlip, Lyre's, and Proxies non-alcoholic wine. name: Kimball House
description: Kimball House is a bar and oyster restaurant in a converted 1890s rail depot beside the tracks in downtown Decatur, open since 2013. It is recommended in the Michelin Guide, holds the Guide's 2024 Exceptional Cocktails award for Georgia, and runs what is widely regarded as the deepest oyster programme in the metro. The zero-proof list is treated with the same seriousness as the absinthe and cocktail lists it is famous for. Tokyo Zero is the standout — ginger, yuzu, lime, pineapple and white shoyu, drawing on the same Japanese flavour vocabulary as the alcoholic menu — alongside a St. Agrestis Phony Negroni and a non-alcoholic Grapefruit Royale topped with Oddbird sparkling. The kitchen runs a full menu of pulled barbecue jackfruit sandwiches, yucca fries, big salads, and chicken sandwiches alongside espresso and oat milk lattes on tap and Figure 8 coffee. The bar offers a wide cocktail program, and Visit Austin's official tourism blog calls out Kinda Tropical for having one of the deepest non-alcoholic drink lists in town, naming a jalapeño pineapple margarita and the Rosemary Lane as standouts. The vibe is eclectic and relaxed — vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options run throughout the menu, and the patio is set back from the street with vines and plants creating a quiet, plant-shaded environment that doesn't feel like a bar in the conventional sense.

It pairs kava with a coffee programme and runs long days for the neighbourhood — 8am to 9pm early in the week, to 11pm on Friday and Saturday, with a short Sunday and a Tuesday closure. The room also hosts wellness programming, including breathwork and sound sessions. As the newest addition to a Northeast Ohio kava scene that had been entirely suburban — Sacred Waters in Lakewood, and Kava Sol in Willoughby until it closed its room in 2026 — it is the first to sit inside Cleveland's own city limits.

From April to September the bar also runs Roadrunner, a retro camper bar parked in its patio garden on Thursday to Saturday evenings, whose published menu carries two named mocktails at $9 — the Meteor Smash on mango and orange, the Milky Way on dark chocolate milk with nutmeg and caramel — plus Heineken 0.0. The zero-proof drinks change with the seasonal list and the bartenders build off-menu from the same syrups, so what is published understates what the bar can make. The kitchen serves modern Vietnamese cuisine with French and East Asian influences alongside an ambitious craft-cocktail program, and the bar runs a genuine zero-proof option: general manager David Tye uses Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits to rebuild several cocktails alcohol-free while keeping the original recipe intact, including a Papaya Margarita made with NA tequila, papaya, lime, agave, and black lava sea salt. Kingfisher is listed in the Michelin Guide and on national and statewide best-of lists, making it one of Golden Hill's most acclaimed dining-and-drinking destinations.

name: Kismet Modern Indian
description: Kismet Modern Indian on West Broad Street builds its non-alcoholic drinks with the same spice-forward logic as its cooking, and keeps two named mocktails on the printed list: Tiger's Tail and Familiar Faces. Indian food is a natural fit for alcohol-free drinking — the cuisine's own drinking tradition runs to lassi, nimbu pani and spiced coolers rather than wine, and chilli heat is generally better served by something cold and acidic than by alcohol. That makes ordering a zero-proof drink here feel like a considered pairing rather than a substitution, which is a rarer experience than it should be. It sits on the Scott's Addition edge of West Broad Street, so it slots easily into an evening built around the brewery district without requiring anyone at the table to drink.

name: Kitty Dare
description: Kitty Dare is a Mediterranean-inspired restaurant in Atlanta's Inman Park, in the storied 1029 Edgewood Ave space. The restaurant is named for Zarnegar's late friend, Kitty Dare Etheridge. The menu spans pan-Mediterranean plates such as berbere chicken with saffron rice cakes and bucatini with shrimp. Alongside its wine-forward bar, Kitty Dare runs a small named zero-proof cocktail list built on Amethyst 0.0% spirits. Named alcohol-free drinks include the Kian (Amethyst Blueberry Ginger Mint, lime, simple syrup, ginger beer) and the Farhad (Amethyst Lemon Cucumber Serrano, lemon, simple syrup, mint). It opens at 5pm on weeknights and runs to 11pm, and on Friday and Saturday it stays open until 2am. Guests pay a fee to take a table and play from a large game library, and the espresso counter runs the whole time. The menu carries no alcohol: espresso drinks, chai, matcha and London Fog tea lattes, hot chocolate, sodas, soda floats and milkshakes in vanilla, chocolate, Nutella, strawberry, espresso and banana, plus a rotating seasonal list of turmeric lattes, peaflower lemonade, blackberry mocha and strawberry matcha. Opened in August 2022 as the third room of a company founded in Carrboro in 2015 by UNC Chapel Hill alumna Elizabeth Gardner, it is an explicit alternative to the traditional bar scene rather than a cafe that happens to close late, and since Umbrella Dry Bar closed for good it is the only dedicated alcohol-free room left in Raleigh proper. The room is built as a crashed-plane-in-the-jungle: a real airplane fuselage forms the bar, surrounded by banyan roots, stone booths, fire-breathing skull idols, fog, and storm effects. The cocktail program leans grown-up and rum-deep (150+ rums), skipping the blue-curaçao tiki clichés. Notably for a serious cocktail bar, it prints five named zero-proof drinks on the main menu at about $14 each — built on house-made "LR N/A Cask Spirit" and "N/A Cane Spirit" plus Pathfinder no-ABV spirit — so the alcohol-free cocktails get the same theatrical treatment as the full-proof ones. Named NA pours include the Golden Idol, Glass Ruby, Mocking Bird, Wrong Island, and El Peligosto. Wednesday bingo nights are a local draw.

It was named one of Esquire's Best New Restaurants of 2024. Two drinks is a short list, but the construction is the point — using an alcohol-free spirit as the base means the drink is built the way a cocktail is, with the same bitterness and length. The menu runs to kava served in the traditional way, kratom, herbal teas and house blends, in a lounge built for sitting and talking rather than for a quick drink. In a city whose reputation rests almost entirely on its bars and its beer, having somewhere that keeps bar hours without serving alcohol changes what an evening out can look like. Note that kava is mildly psychoactive and kratom is also served, so this is a night out without alcohol rather than a substance-free room.

Columbus Underground readers voted it the city's best non-alcoholic drink menu in the 2025 Best of Columbus poll. Roughly three new cocktail menus are released a year, each carrying named N/A cocktails alongside the full-proof list, and most specialty cocktails can be built without alcohol at a reduced price. Non-alcoholic beer comes from Athletic Brewing and Best Day.

name: Lawrence Hall
description: Lawrence Hall is a food hall at 4609 Butler Street in Lawrenceville, in an 1890s building that has been a theatre and a car dealership, opened in April 2024 by Brett Minarik, Phoebe Fraser and Adam Harvey after five years of renovation. It holds four independent restaurants, a Leona's ice cream shop, seating for 225 and a mezzanine, anchored by its bar Dear James — named for Captain James Lawrence, whose dying order gave the neighbourhood its name. The bar did something almost no venue does: it hired a dedicated non-alcoholic beverage consultant, Katrina Tomacchio, who advised Boston-area bars on zero-proof drinks before moving here, gave up alcohol herself, and co-owns two of the hall's own tenant restaurants. The programme uses hyper-local sourcing, house-made syrups and original recipes rather than bought-in mixers. One documented example is the Capture of The Chesapeake, a campfire espresso martini of cold brew, Lyre's coffee and white cane spirits, graham cracker syrup and non-alcoholic aromatic bitters with a torched marshmallow. The list rotates by season and is published only through the bar's ordering system.

Alongside kava it pours exotic and botanical teas, kratom and coffee. The evening half is a genuine social room rather than a cafe with the lights down: there is a free pool table and games, and it hosts live music and a recurring KOOP 91.7 FM DJ residency, which the community station bills as taking place "in a sober-forward setting." (Kava is non-alcoholic but psychoactive — alcohol-free, not substance-free.)

name: LBM
description: LBM is a small, deliberately eccentric cocktail bar at 12301 Madison Avenue in Lakewood's Birdtown, and Cleveland Scene's description has held up for years: best described as weird but good, not for everyone, but earning a deep well of respect for having a personality, a point of view, and the nerve to carve out an eccentric niche. Co-owner and bartender Eric Ho co-founded the Cleveland chapter of the US Bartenders Guild and works with real technique — measuring out acids to the hundredth of a gram, milk-washing tea infusions to cut the astringency. The menu runs in themed volumes, and its non-alcoholic cocktails get their own printed heading rather than a footnote: three at $10 each. Sacred Ashes builds tamarind, cardamom and chipotle against wildflower honey and rosewater; Amethyst runs chicha morada — Peruvian purple corn — with pineapple, clove, cinnamon, apple and lime; and Sigil is the autumnal one, with cider, maple, chicory, chocolate, hazelnut and orange peel. Non-alcoholic beer runs $6–$7. Open from 4pm, to 2.30am on Friday and Saturday.

description: Le Lounge is the intimate cocktail bar inside No Vacancy, an eight-room boutique guesthouse on the corner of 18th and Wyandotte in Kansas City's Crossroads Arts District. Alongside an ambitious craft-cocktail program — lead bartenders have used liquid nitrogen to keep martini glasses cold — Le Lounge maintains a small but genuine non-alcoholic offering, including the Sober Lush (a grapefruit, citrus, and jalapeño mocktail) and a non-alcoholic golden ale from Athletic Brewing. It opens at 10am six days a week and stays open until midnight every night, which is an almost unheard-of span. The non-alcoholic drinks are named and built: the Leopold's Scarlet Mule runs hibiscus and sage against ginger beer and orange bitters, and a pomegranate sage spritz sits alongside it. Both turn up in Madison's zero-proof coverage.

name: Life on Mars
description: Life on Mars is a plant-based cocktail bar at Pike and Harvard on Capitol Hill, opened in June 2019 by KEXP DJ John Richards, Amy Lindsey Richards, Leigh Sims and Neumos co-owner Steven Severin. It has a 6,000-record vinyl wall, a covered patio, an all-vegan kitchen and one of the most developed non-alcoholic menus in Seattle — a programme that dates to January 2022, when the bar reopened with nine zero-proof cocktails for Dry January. The section is headed "N/A and Low ABV Cocktails", and the naming matters: these are not all 0%. Pathfinder Spritz (0.03%, $14) has been on the list since 2019; High Violet (0.03%, $15) uses Pathfinder with Almave Ambar and blueberry coffee syrup; Mesmerize (0.1%, $13) is black-pepper-infused Pathfinder with lemon lapsang oleo; the canned Pathfinder Negroni is 0.5% at $14; and Two of Hearts is printed at 0.12–2.98% ABV, so it is genuinely low-alcohol rather than alcohol-free. The menu's own disclaimer notes all N/A spirits may contain trace alcohol. Every drink credits its creator and year. 21+ inside and out.

description: Lioness is a small, loud Italian wine bar and restaurant at 7009 Greenwood Ave N in Phinney Ridge, opened at the turn of 2024 by chef Renée Erickson's Sea Creatures group. It has eight indoor tables and a bar too tight to seat anyone — customers stand at it, as drinkers do in Rome or Barcelona — with candles flickering in Chianti bottles and custom-painted plates Erickson chose herself. The food is small-plate Italian: burrata, smoked black cod mousse, brothy clams, bouncy cavatelli and a much-discussed $18 meatball. Its non-alcoholic programme is well regarded locally — the Infatuation describes people mingling over bergamot-infused spritzes and frothy zero-proof garibaldis, and Seattle's own alcohol-free bottle shop rates the bar's spirit-free work as top shelf, crediting bartender Hudson with about three seasonal non-alcoholic cocktails at a time. PLEASE NOTE: Lioness's website sits behind a security check we cannot get past, so we could not read the current drinks list — the named zero-proof cocktails and their prices need confirming in person. A clarification on awards: Erickson won a James Beard Award in 2016, but for an earlier restaurant, not for Lioness.

name: Lions Den
description: Lions Den is the bar at Le Méridien Dallas in the historic Stoneleigh, opened in 2026 under chef Michael White, and its menu carries a printed Zero Proof section that treats non-alcoholic drinking as an aperitivo tradition rather than a lemonade problem. Giusto E Sbagliato is the ambitious one — Lyre's American Malt with Roots Rosso, a cocoa-infused Giffard aperitif syrup and Crodino, the Italian bitter aperitivo. The Prickly Hibiscus Spritz is built on Ghia with hibiscus, prickly pear, lemon and club soda, alongside a third build called La Bombola. The bar runs breakfast, lunch and dinner services daily, so the list is available from 6:30am.

name: Listen Bar
description: IMPORTANT — LISTEN BAR APPEARS TO BE DORMANT. It is a pioneering alcohol-free bar that has always run as a roving pop-up rather than a fixed venue, founded by Lorelei Bandrovschi after a friend dared her to spend a month without drinking, and first opened in October 2018 as a five-day proof-of-concept in an empty South Williamsburg bar space. Staffed by musician bartenders, it became one of the original templates for the modern non-alcoholic bar and drew national press. As of August 2026, however, we can find no confirmed activity dated later than January 2025: the newest entry on its own events page is the Good AF Awards 2025, and no 2026 edition or event appears anywhere. Its website and Instagram both remain live and are written in the present tense, which is not the same as being open. Documented signature drinks have included Actual Sunshine, created by Eamon Rockey, and Dollar Slice, by Aaron Polsky, alongside Athletic Brewing beer and Pilot Kombucha on tap. Check before planning around it.

name: Little Coyote
description: Little Coyote is a smoked-barbecue restaurant in St. Elmo, at the foot of Lookout Mountain, from the team behind Main Street Meats and Easy Bistro — a MICHELIN Guide listing and one of the more serious kitchens in Chattanooga. Its bar offers zero-proof versions of the two drinks a barbecue room actually needs, a margarita and a paloma, both built rather than poured from a mix. In a format where the default alternative is sweet tea, having a proper sour and a proper citrus highball available without alcohol is more useful than a long mocktail list would be. Dinner from 4pm daily, with weekend lunch from 11:30am.

name: Little Jumbo
description: Little Jumbo is a craft cocktail bar at 241 Broadway Street in Asheville's Five Points, opened on 7 November 2017 in the old Jenkins grocery by co-owners Chall Gray and Jay Sanders, with Leisa Payne in the kitchen. The room keeps the building's bones — tin ceilings, green leather — and USA Today named it Bar of the Year in 2025, with Garden & Gun placing it among the best of the South. Its non-alcoholic list is one of the longest in the city: a printed "Spirit-Free Sippers" section of seven drinks at $9–$10, roughly half the price of the full cocktails, and built across three different non-alcoholic spirit houses rather than one. Rita's Day Off ($10) uses Ritual NA tequila with basil, lime, orange, lemon and agave; Mint to Refresh You ($9) uses Ritual NA rum; the Cos-No-Politan ($9) and Drømme Roll Please ($10) are built on Drømme; Shoots Then Leaves ($9) pairs Seedlip Garden 108 with spicy ginger ale and celery bitters; and the Berry-Nice Gimlet ($10) layers an Amethyst blueberry-ginger-mint with two bitters and orange flower water. The list rotates seasonally.

description: Little Mercies is a small, multi-award-winning neighbourhood cocktail bar on Broadway Parade in Crouch End, open since 2018. It was founded by Alan Sherwood with brothers Max and Noel Venning — the team behind the acclaimed Three Sheets in Dalston and Soho — and carries the same low-waste, precision-led ethos, having been named Sustainable Bar of the Year by the UK's Top 50 Cocktail Bars three times, in 2022, 2023 and 2025. The space is compact and unshowy, with bare brick walls, accents of midnight blue, banquettes and a handful of bar stools, and it fills with a bustling neighbourhood crowd; a kitchen turns out playful seasonal small plates, so it works equally as a date-night spot and a drop-in local. Alongside its cocktail program it pours tropical mocktails built on fresh fruit and juices, including "The Shallow End" (strawberries, lime, and seltzer) and "The School Night," which pairs a non-alcoholic dry riesling with citrus cordial and mulled hibiscus.

Syrups, infusions and foams are all made in house, which is what separates these from sweetened juice. Named non-alcoholic builds include the N/A Paloma (spirit-free blanco tequila, seasonal grapefruit soda, key lime, sea salt), an N/A White Grapefruit and Koji Paloma, and the blackberry-lemon Big City Nights.

name: Little Sparrow
description: Little Sparrow is Ford Fry's French bistro in the Westside Provisions District, opened in October 2023 in the former JCT Kitchen & Bar space and named for Edith Piaf. It is recommended in the Michelin Guide and was named one of Esquire's best new restaurants in America in 2024. The bar keeps three non-alcoholic cocktails on the standing menu rather than improvising them on request. No Regrets is the most ambitious of the three, described on the menu itself as peaty and complex, reminiscent of a fine Speyside malt; Triple Crown builds Wilfred's bitter orange aperitif into a ginger-forward highball; and Rose-Colored Glasses is a blood orange fizz. Steak frites, oysters and classic bistro cooking fill the plates.

The kitchen emphasizes scratch cooking and regional sourcing — house-made sourdough rye, pierogi ruskie, kielbasa, and rotisserie pork over bigos. In 2024 it was the only Philadelphia restaurant named to The New York Times' "Restaurant List: 50 Favorite Places in America Right Now," and it won a Philadelphia Magazine Best of Philly award. The bar runs a dedicated zero-proof section on its menu titled "bezalkoholowe" (Polish for "non-alcoholic"), priced at $7, alongside the cocktail, wine, and beer lists. Named NA drinks include the Mleczarz (whey, apple shrub, dill), Sadownik (tart cherry, orange, cardamom), Zielarz (rosemary honey, herbal tea, bitters), and Feniks, plus a non-alcoholic beer.

It was shortlisted at the inaugural NYC's Best Bars for NA Awards. Its practical advantage over almost everything else in this guide is time: 11am to 2am, every single day, so it works for a mid-afternoon meeting and a late night from the same room. Alcohol is served. Spirited Away, New York's deepest non-alcoholic bottle shop, is a five-minute walk away on Eighth Avenue, which makes this a natural pairing for an afternoon.

name: L'Oca d'Oro
description: L'Oca d'Oro is an Italian-inspired neighborhood restaurant in Austin's Mueller district, opened in 2016 by chef/owner Fiore Tedesco and co-owner Adam Orman after a pop-up series that began in 2013. Tedesco, a 2017 StarChefs Austin–San Antonio Rising Star, builds a seasonal, locally sourced menu of housemade pasta and Italian fare, with a stated emphasis on sourcing and staff compensation. The bar program carries a genuine, menu-listed "No / Very Low ABV" section rather than an afterthought. Zero-proof options include the School Night Spritz (strawberry cordial, fresh basil and mint, lime, bubbles) and the Dry County O.F. A Ritual Zero Proof gin alternative can be paired with housemade Italian sodas (limonata, orange cream, basil-lime, tangerine-rosemary). name: Local Jones
description: Local Jones is the all-American bistro and neighbourhood bar inside Halcyon, a hotel in Cherry Creek, serving breakfast, lunch and dinner from 7:30am daily. Its zero-proof drinks are treated as part of the cocktail list rather than as a soft-drink afterthought: Visit Denver names the Snowcap, built from vanilla mint chai tea with lemon, honey, pomegranate and egg white, and the spicier Prickle My Fancy, describing both as the perfect people-watching sippers. The egg-white build on the Snowcap is the tell — it is shaken and finished like a sour rather than poured. The room's Cherry Creek North setting, all-day hours and hotel setting make it one of the more practical options in the neighbourhood for a mixed group meeting early or late.

There are five mocktail flavours on the standing list, including mango, hibiscus and corazón, alongside buzz-free margaritas and a range of aguas frescas — the traditional Mexican fruit waters that were alcohol-free long before anyone marketed them as such. That combination matters in practice: the aguas frescas mean a non-drinker can order something that belongs on the table rather than something invented to fill a gap, and the zero-proof margaritas cover the social ritual everyone else is participating in.

IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: alongside kava, the bar sells kratom and stocks hemp products including vapes. Kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries dependence and withdrawal risk that kava does not, so if the reason you are looking for a kava bar is that you are avoiding substances with a hold, this room requires you to order specifically.

It serves kava and kratom tea along with kombucha on tap and soft drinks, drawing a regular neighborhood crowd with live music and trivia from morning into the early-morning hours. (It serves kratom alongside kava.)  It shares Gulfport's short main street with Sober Bar, the fully zero-proof room that opened in 2026 — two alcohol-free venues within a few hundred metres, which makes this small waterfront town the densest pocket of sober nightlife anywhere in Tampa Bay.

Its zero-proof builds are seasonal and properly constructed rather than sweetened — the Honeycrisp and Tart Cherry Mule leans on apple and sour cherry against ginger, and the Pineapple Mint No-Jito is the house mojito without the rum. name: Matcha Mate
description: Matcha Mate is a fully alcohol-free matcha cafe and tasting room at 100 Langridge Street, Collingwood, opened as a standalone shop at the end of 2025 by Belle Vy and Chian Ting — who first ran it as a pop-up inside their CBD dessert shop Nimbo in 2023. Guests are walked through seven first-harvest Japanese matcha blends and two roasted hojicha varieties the way a wine bar guides you through bottles, from the creamy, malty house blend Hikari to the bright, floral single-cultivar Osu, all hand-whisked to order. Zero alcohol by design, it's a genuine daytime social spot built entirely around tea.

name: Matilda Midnight
description: Matilda Midnight is a downtown Chattanooga cocktail lounge on East 10th Street whose drinks are named after tarot cards, a conceit that runs through the alcohol-free options as well as the spirited ones. The house mocktail is the Abundance — coconut water, house cream, pineapple, lime, lavender syrup and soda — a rich, layered build that uses a made-in-house cream rather than a bought mixer, which is the difference between a drink and a soft drink. The room is dark, late and deliberately atmospheric, opening at 5pm Wednesday through Sunday and running to midnight, and closed Monday and Tuesday.

name: Mattie's at Green Pastures
address: 811 W Live Oak St, Austin, TX 78704
description: Mattie's at Green Pastures is a historic American restaurant set in an 1895 Victorian home in Austin's Bouldin Creek neighborhood. The property is a Texas Recorded Historic Landmark on the National Register of Historic Places — originally opened as a restaurant in 1946, it was notable for serving customers of all races 18 years before Austin restaurants were desegregated by law. Renovated and reopened in 2017 as Mattie's, named after the property's matriarch, the menu features pan-Southern farm-fresh fare under sprawling live oaks with resident peacocks roaming the grounds. The cocktail program leans Southern (John Henry's Julep with Still Austin bourbon is a signature), and the Back Porch Tea — a blend of spearmint and eucalyptus tea with wildflower honey, lemon, and fresh mint — is explicitly available in a non-alcoholic preparation.
signatureDrinks: The Back Porch Tea (available NA: spearmint and eucalyptus tea with wildflower honey, lemon, fresh mint)

name: Maui Brewing Co. Waikīkī
description: Maui Brewing Co.'s Waikīkī brewpub sits inside the Outrigger Waikiki Beachcomber Hotel on Kalākaua Avenue and bills itself as the largest bar in Waikīkī, with thirty-six taps running Maui Brewing year-round beers, limited releases and guest pours from other independent brewers. Its documented non-alcoholic build is the Orange Crush — orange juice, mint, lemon-lime soda and simple syrup. Happy hour runs Monday to Friday from 3.30pm and there is a late-night happy hour from 9.30pm most nights, which along with the 11pm close makes it one of the more flexible rooms on the strip for a group that is only partly drinking.
signatureDrinks: Orange Crush (orange juice, mint, lemon-lime soda, simple syrup)

name: Mauro Colagreco at Raffles London at The OWO
address: Raffles London at The OWO, Whitehall, London SW1A 2BX
hours: Lunch: Thu–Sat 12pm–2pm; Dinner: Tue–Sat 6pm–10pm; closed Sun–Mon
description: Mauro Colagreco at Raffles London at The OWO is the one-Michelin-star (2025) flagship of three-Michelin-star chef Mauro Colagreco, set inside the restored Old War Office on Whitehall. Its non-alcoholic offering is a genuine, kitchen-led programme rather than an afterthought: a dedicated multi-course Temperance Pairing (about £80 for five courses, £105 for seven) of sparkling teas, water kefirs and from-scratch mocktails built to mirror the tasting menu's 70-plus British fruits and vegetables. Serves include The Smokey Carrot, the English Garden No-Tini with Seedlip Garden 108 and Everleaf Marine, and the 'Dandy Smoke' zero-alcohol homage to Islay whisky.

name: Max's South Seas Hideaway
address: 58 Ionia Ave SW, Grand Rapids, MI 49503
description: Max's South Seas Hideaway is a two-storey tiki bar and restaurant at 58 Ionia Avenue SW, and the most ambitious tiki project built in the Midwest in decades. It is a joint venture between Mark Sellers, who founded HopCat; Martin Cate, the James Beard award-winning author and owner of San Francisco's Smuggler's Cove, who designed the cocktail program; and Gecko, a Hawaii-based tiki and Polynesian artist. The two floors hold one of the largest collections of new and vintage tiki art and memorabilia anywhere. The bar keeps a standing Zero Proof menu of eight island-style mocktails — among them the Ginger Zing, Coconut Mojito, Island Passion, Pomegranate Punch, Orange Creamsicle and both a Pom and a standard Virgin Pina Colada — and also pours locally made Brix Sodas.

name: Maya Moon Cacao Lounge
description: Maya Moon Cacao Lounge is an alcohol-free ceremonial-cacao concept that opened in May 2025 inside GOODONYA, the long-running organic eatery on South Coast Highway 101 in Encinitas. A North County outpost of Maya Moon Collective — founded by Kathryn Rogers, whose Normal Heights café bills itself as Southern California's first ceremonial-cacao café — its draw is a rotating set of signature herbal cacao blends, drinking-cacao tasting flights, adaptogenic drinks, handcrafted truffles, and house honey marshmallows, a genuine zero-proof, ritual-forward experience. Note that the host GOODONYA also serves natural wine, prosecco, and local beer alongside an alcohol-free "social tonic" menu, so the dry experience here is the cacao program rather than the whole building.

name: Mayawell
description: Mayawell is a bar in the Pepper Place district of Birmingham, east of downtown near the Saturday market, and its contribution to this guide is the Chef's Kiss — a mocktail Bham Now picked out by name in its January 2026 round-up of the city's non-alcoholic drinking, on the strength of how it looks as much as how it tastes. Presentation is not a trivial consideration in this category: a drink that arrives looking like everyone else's is the difference between being included in a round and being visibly opted out of one. Open Tuesday to Saturday from 4pm, with a 2pm Saturday start, closed Sunday and Monday.
signatureDrinks: Chef's Kiss

name: Mazajj Organic Coffee
description: Mazajj Organic Coffee is a Yemeni coffeehouse on Richmond Avenue in Greater Uptown, and it keeps later hours than almost any bar in Houston: midnight Sunday through Thursday and one in the morning on Friday and Saturday. The drinks are the traditional Yemeni repertoire rather than a Western cafe list — Adeni chai, black tea brewed with cardamom, cinnamon and milk; qishr, made from spiced coffee husks rather than the bean; and a spiced sweet latte built on double espresso with cardamom and cinnamon. Texas Monthly covered the venue as part of the Yemeni coffeehouse wave that has spread across Texas since 2024. No alcohol is served or licensed at the address, and the room is built for sitting rather than for takeaway, which is the entire point of the format.

It holds a AAA Four Diamond rating and serves expressive entrees, shareables and desserts in the Madrid idiom the name points at. For non-drinkers the relevant point is that the mixing team builds a mocktail list alongside the cocktails rather than treating zero-proof as a request to be handled — Experience Grand Rapids describes the non-alcoholic selection as every bit as impressive as the rest of the menu. The named build most often cited is the Elote, a fruity, iced and bright drink finished with a mint garnish. Non-alcoholic beers are also stocked.

name: Mean Mule Distilling Co.

description: Mean Mule Distilling Co. is a woman-owned agave-spirits distillery and tasting room in Kansas City's Crossroads Arts District, founded by Jeff Evans (CEO) and Meg Evans (COO) with master distiller Tyler Gloe. The company began distilling in 2016 from 100% organic blue Weber agave and opened its Crossroads distillery and tasting room at 1733 Locust St in April 2019. Its core lineup is American Agave Spirit in Silver, Gold, and Heritage expressions; the flagship Silver earned a gold medal at the San Francisco World Spirits Competition. Beyond spirit flights and craft cocktails, the tasting room keeps a small dedicated mocktail list of roughly five house-built zero-proof drinks. Named examples include Pickle's Punch (house red-pepper syrup, cactus brine, ginger beer, lime) and the Kleopatra, built on Ghia's non-alcoholic aperitif with an almond-and-ube syrup.

name: Mélange by Cali Sober
description: Mélange by Cali Sober opened on 14 November 2025 above Bamboula's at 516 Frenchmen Street in the Marigny, from Monica Olano — known online as Cali Sober Mom and founder of the Cali Sober Market in Metairie — and it bills itself as the first non-alcoholic, functional and THC beverage bar on Frenchmen Street. READ THIS BEFORE VISITING: the venue is alcohol-free but explicitly not substance-free. Alongside house-crafted non-alcoholic cocktails it serves kava, functional-mushroom drinks and hemp-derived THC beverages that it describes as legal under the 2018 Hemp Bill and Louisiana regulations. The important mechanic is that THC is served in individual vials so guests add their own dose to a drink rather than being served a fixed-strength cocktail — so the same named drink can be entirely inert or not, depending on what you add. Named drinks include the Mélange Old Fashioned, a Vesper Martini and the Cali Sober Love Potion, and the menu explains for each whether it is built to give an energy buzz, a calming effect, or a THC buzz. It has a balcony over the live music room. Open Thursday to Sunday evenings.
signatureDrinks: Cali Sober Love Potion|Cali Sober Night Kiss

name: Melrose Umbrella Co.
description: Melrose Umbrella Co. is a post-Prohibition-themed craft cocktail bar at 7465 Melrose Avenue in the Fairfax District, open since 2013 from owners Zach Patterson and Austin Melrose. The room is built from salvage: an 1890s fireplace facing an arched ceiling covered in New York City subway tile, and a massive 1920s wooden apothecary cabinet shipped from the East Coast and retrofitted as the back bar, with a string-lit heated patio behind. Its non-alcoholic offering is a genuine nine-item menu across two printed sections. Under "Non-Alcoholic Cocktails" sit five at $15: Not Even Smashed (Ritual zero-proof whiskey, blackberry, mint, lemon, elderflower tonic), the Pa-No-Ma (Ritual zero-proof tequila, prickly pear, green apple, ruby red grapefruit), the Keto Pepino (Ritual zero-proof gin, cucumber, lime, monkfruit, celery salt), The Valet (Pathfinder, Pentire Coastal Spritz, Seedlip Garden 108, orange), and a canned Piña Margarita or Negroni. Under "Non-Alcoholic Beers, Bubbles & Beyond" sit four cans at $7, including Athletic's Run Wild IPA and Deschutes' organic Kernza Golden. Open from noon, closed Mondays; reservations via Resy.

name: Merchant & Trade
description: Merchant & Trade is a 19th-floor rooftop bar and lounge atop the Kimpton Tryon Park Hotel in Uptown Charlotte, offering panoramic skyline views across four distinct zones — indoor bar, outdoor terrace, private terrace, and the lawn. The venue maintains a serious zero-proof cocktail program with rotating seasonal mocktails crafted with the same care as their alcoholic offerings, using ingredients like Seedlip Spice 94, Ritual Zero Proof spirits, and locally brewed Lenny Boy Ginger Kombucha. Named drinks include the Endless Vacation, Bobcat Territory, The Gold Line, and the Faux & Falcon, reflecting both local Charlotte culture and a genuine commitment to spirit-free options.

description: Merchant has been the reference craft cocktail bar on Madison's Capitol Square for years, and is one of the handful of downtown rooms local coverage consistently names when the question is where to drink well without alcohol. Its zero-proof menu is built rather than substituted — the No Regrets works a non-alcoholic "gin-ish" spirit against rosemary and lime, which is a dry, herbaceous drink rather than a sweet one. The bar sits on South Pinckney Street a few doors from Settle Down Tavern and around the corner from Lucille and Eno Vino, which makes it the natural anchor of an alcohol-free evening on the Square. Closed Mondays; weekend brunch from 9am.

name: Mercury
description: Mercury is a downtown Omaha cocktail bar on South 16th Street, and local drinks coverage credits it with the most extensive dedicated mocktail list in the city — dedicated being the operative word, meaning a standing section written as its own thing rather than a couple of substitutions offered on request. It is open 4pm to midnight seven days a week with no closed night, which combined with the depth of the list makes it the single most reliable place in Omaha to turn up without a plan and order well without alcohol. The room is a stylish mid-century lounge, intimate rather than loud.

The kitchen sources accordingly. Its documented zero-proof drink is the Maikaʻi Zero Proof Mai Tai, finished with a honey liliko\'i foam, which is a more considered piece of construction than the name suggests: the foam supplies the weight and texture that a mai tai normally gets from rum, and the passionfruit brings acidity. It sits in the same group as Monkeypod Kitchen in Waikīkī.

name: The Merryweather
description: The Merryweather is a neighbourhood bar on the corner of Lydia Street in Schnitzelburg, one of Louisville's older working-class German neighbourhoods on the south side. Its non-alcoholic programme is unusually committed for a corner bar: the standing Sober Ghia Spritz is built on Ghia, the gentian-and-yuzu Mediterranean aperitif, and each January the bar prints a full alcohol-free menu of its own — the Dry Tai, the Nada Colada, the Mock-Scow Mule and the Not Toddy, which cover the tiki, tropical, ginger and hot-drink positions between them. That is a bar treating Dry January as a menu-writing exercise rather than a marketing line, and it is why the venue keeps appearing in Louisville's zero-proof coverage.
