description: Mesmer Kava is Vermont's first kava bar, opened in May 2025 by Gwen and Roderick Russell in Suite 109 of the Karma Bird House on Maple Street, a block from the Burlington waterfront. It serves traditionally prepared kava from the ground root of the South Pacific plant, plus kava drinks built with pineapple and ginger, herbal teas and kava-infused hot chocolate. Nothing on the menu contains alcohol, and it keeps genuine evening hours — 3pm to 8pm Wednesday through Saturday, from 4:30pm on Tuesday — which makes it the only room in the state offering a sit-down evening out with no alcohol in the building. Kava is mildly psychoactive, which the owners state plainly.

name: Meta
description: Meta is chef Sun Kim's two-Michelin-starred contemporary Korean restaurant on Mohamed Sultan Road, near Robertson Quay. Its tasting menus are offered with a full non-alcoholic pairing at S$120++, a house-made zero-proof flight built to run course-by-course alongside the S$280++ wine pairing rather than as an afterthought. The NA program mirrors the kitchen's Korean-rooted, seasonally driven cooking, giving diners a genuine no-alcohol route through the full degustation. Chef Sun Kim told The Korea Times he does not believe in perfection so much as the process of getting closer to it, and the drinks flight is treated with that same seriousness.

name: Meteor
hours: Mon 4pm-12am; Tue closed; Wed-Fri 4pm-2am; Sat 12pm-2am; Sun 12pm-12am
description: Meteor is a cocktail bar in the Hawthorne neighbourhood of North Minneapolis, opened by Elliot Manthey and Robb Jones in a former dive on North 2nd Street and since recognised well beyond the city — a 2024 James Beard Award semifinalist for Outstanding Bar, and listed by the World's 50 Best Discovery guide. Its reputation rests on a seasonal cocktail programme built across mezcal, aquavit and other less-obvious spirits, and the same bar team applies that thinking to drinks with nothing in them: the standing non-alcoholic reference point is a wild rice horchata, a Minnesota reworking of the drink, alongside rotating seasonal zero-proof builds. Hot dogs are the food.
signatureDrinks: Wild rice horchata

name: metrobar
address: 640 Rhode Island Ave NE, Washington, DC 20002
hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed 5pm-11pm; Thu 5pm-12am; Fri 4pm-1am; Sat 12pm-1am; Sun 12pm-11pm
description: metrobar is an 11,000-square-foot indoor-outdoor bar built around a redesigned WMATA Metro railcar, which serves as the central bar structure, with a platform-style lounge and a cocktail garden beside the Rhode Island Ave-Brentwood station in Edgewood. The concept is to connect the District's eight wards through craft cocktails spotlighting local DMV spirits, breweries and wineries, with food from rotating truck partners. It was voted Best Bar in DC by Washington City Paper readers in 2024 and was a 2025 Rammys Best Bar finalist. Non-alcoholic drinks are on the everyday menu alongside the cocktails, beer, cider and wine, and each January the bar runs a full Dry January menu of hot and cold spirit-free libations billed as District-made cocktails without the hangover. Ordering is by QR-code Toast tab at the table.

name: Miami Kava & Coffee
description: Miami Kava & Coffee is a fully alcohol-free kava lounge in Little River, billed as the City of Miami's first kava bar. The business started in 2015 in a small Wynwood house under the names House of Roots and later Roots Miami Kava, before expanding across Miami and settling its flagship room at 393 NE 59th St; in 2025 it marked its tenth anniversary. Everything served is plant-based and zero-proof: fresh-brewed traditional kava, herbal teas, house-brewed yerba mate, specialty coffee, and pressed ginger shots. The drink menu carries playful named pours such as the Cheech, Mr. T, Icey Tea, and the Fruity Rooty kava shot. Long a hub for Miami's creative community, the venue hosts open mics, live music, and local art showcases, functioning as a gathering space for artists and the sober-curious alike.

name: Michael’s Genuine Food & Drink
description: Michael's Genuine Food & Drink is chef Michael Schwartz's flagship neighborhood restaurant in Miami's Design District, open since 2007. A James Beard Award winner (Best Chef: South, 2010), Schwartz built the room around fresh, local, wood-fired cooking, and it carries a 2026 MICHELIN Guide Bib Gourmand. Its bar runs one of Miami's more developed zero-proof offerings: the Greater Miami CVB describes it as "one of the city's most robust zero-proof programs," built on house-made sodas, seasonal juice blends, and named non-alcoholic cocktails. Two confirmed spirit-free pours are the No-Proof Bulletproof, made with Lyre's American Malt, cherry-rosemary syrup and lemon, and Find Your Path, with Pathfinder hemp-derived non-alcoholic spirit, mint, citrus, and soda. The NA list sits inside a full-service bar rather than a dedicated alcohol-free venue, making it a comfortable fit for non-drinkers.
signatureDrinks: No-Proof Bulletproof|Find Your Path

name: Middle Park Hotel
description: This heritage bayside gastropub near Albert Park keeps a genuine booze-free option going behind the bar. Alongside alcohol-free beer and wine, Middle Park Hotel pours a zero-proof Espresso Martini built on cold-drip coffee, vanilla and Lyre's organic cane and coffee spirits, earning it a spot on Broadsheet's roundup of Melbourne's best non-alcoholic bars.
signatureDrinks: Espresso Martini - cold-drip coffee, vanilla and Lyre's organic cane and coffee spirits

name: Midnight Cowboy
description: Midnight Cowboy is one of Austin's oldest and most well-known speakeasies, opened in 2012 in a 313 E 6th Street building that previously housed a brothel masquerading as a massage parlor — Midnight Cowboy Modeling Oriental Massage — and the venue embraces that history rather than hiding it. Entry is by reservation only: guests receive a code name from a Prohibition-era bartender (e.g. Harry Craddock), then push the corresponding button at the unmarked door, ring the bell, and are escorted to one of nine intimate booths for a one-to-two-hour cocktail experience. Drinks are crafted tableside via a bar cart with theatrical presentation, and recent menus have followed themed concepts (a tarot-inspired menu, for example) that span stirred classics, martinis, sours, tiki variations, and zero-proof creations. ATX Today's January 2026 Austin mocktails roundup specifically highlights Midnight Cowboy's zero-proof program, which uses alcohol-free gin and whiskey to build full cocktail experiences rather than juice-based mocktails. Cocktails are $14–$16, with discounts for ordering multiples of the same drink. Located in the heart of 6th Street nightlife, Midnight Cowboy is the quiet, intentional exception on an otherwise raucous block.

name: Midnight Morning
description: Midnight Morning is an all-day cafe, bar and restaurant at 14 Birch Street in Roslindale Village, opened in 2023 by owner Virginia Schubert in the space that had long housed Birch Street Bistro. Schubert worked in design before moving into hospitality, and the business is certified with the City of Boston as a Minority Business Enterprise, Woman Business Enterprise and Small Local Business Enterprise. The kitchen, led by executive chef Rory Lee, runs a made-from-scratch seasonal menu across breakfast, lunch, dinner and weekend brunch. The bar keeps a standing Zero Proof section of four cocktails at $10, all built on non-alcoholic spirits rather than juice: Remember Me with AMASS Riverine, Bad Decisions with Everleaf Forest, Threat Level Midnight with Zero Zero Amaro and cold brew, and the Arbore'rum with Ritual Proof Rum. Two non-alcoholic beers are poured alongside them.

While the bar is known for an extensive tequila and mezcal program, its cocktail menu carries a dedicated "Zero Proof" section of crafted mocktails priced at $13. The standout is the Watermelon Cooler, which uses Almave Blanco non-alcoholic tequila with watermelon, lime, and soda, alongside options like Pinky's Up (hibiscus, passion fruit, pineapple, soda) and Nice Mangos (mango, lime, agave, ginger beer). The restaurant was highlighted in Las Vegas Weekly's January 2026 Dry January guide for these alcohol-free offerings. Weekend brunch runs Saturday and Sunday from 10am to 3pm.

name: Mikkeller Brewpub London
description: Mikkeller Brewpub London is the Danish cult brewery's two-floor Exmouth Market brewpub, opened in 2019 in collaboration with pop singer Rick Astley and built around an on-site 7.5-hectolitre brewery that feeds 20 ever-changing taps. Roughly half the taps pour beer brewed on the premises, and the line-up always keeps at least one non-alcoholic beer on draught, including Mikkeller's own alcohol-free IPA that reviewers say drinks like the full-strength original rather than a compromise. Because Mikkeller is one of the most respected names in low- and no-alcohol brewing, the NA pour here is a genuine draught option beside the food, not a token soft drink.

name: Miku Toronto
address: 10 Bay St #105, Toronto, ON M5J 2R8, Canada (WaterPark Place)
description: Miku Toronto is an Aburi-style Japanese sushi restaurant on the Harbourfront, occupying more than 7,000 square feet inside WaterPark Place on Bay Street with a raw bar, sushi bar, and large patio. It opened in 2015 as ABURI Restaurants' first East Coast location, following the group's expansion from Japan to Vancouver. Alongside its wine and sake program, Miku carries what Foodism.ca calls "a substantial section of zero-proof drinks," including non-alcoholic wine, non-alcoholic beer, and named mocktails such as the yuzu-elderflower-lavender Tōji Fizz.
signatureDrinks: Tōji Fizz — yuzu, elderflower, and lavender (described by Foodism as "a floral lemonade")

name: Mint Coffeehouse
description: Mint Coffeehouse is a Middle Eastern-influenced cafe on Lawrenceville Highway in Tucker, opened on 15 August 2024 by the husband-and-wife team Ahmad and Marianna Alzoukani as the bricks-and-mortar home of their existing catering and mobile espresso business. Ahmad is Syrian, and the decor and part of the menu reflect that: Syrian-inspired fittings, and manaeesh flatbread with cheese and vegetables sold next to the toasts and pastries. Coffee is a Colombian blend used for both espresso and drip. The house drinks are the Mint Mocha Latte and an in-house chai latte, with matcha, cold brew and fruit smoothies alongside. No alcohol is served. Hours are daytime only, which is why this is a strong daytime alternative rather than a going-out room.

name: Mint Mark
description: Mint Mark is a near-east-side restaurant and bar that moved from its small Winnebago Street room to a larger space on East Washington Avenue, and it runs one of the zero-proof menus Madison's food press names first. The drinks carry the same off-kilter humour as the rest of the operation — "What Is This, A Titleist?" and "Narrow Straits" are both standing alcohol-free builds. The venue runs three distinct services under one roof: coffee on weekday mornings from 7am, dinner from 5pm, and a bar that stays open to 2am Monday through Saturday, which makes it usable at almost any hour a non-drinker might want a room to be in.
signatureDrinks: What Is This, A Titleist?|Narrow Straits

name: Minus Moonshine
description: The second Minus Moonshine bottle shop, on the corner of Driggs Avenue and Eckford Street in Greenpoint, Brooklyn. Like the original Prospect Heights store it is entirely alcohol-free: NA beer, wine, spirits, aperitifs, ready-to-drink cocktails, mixers and bitters, from a stock list the shop has been building since 2021 that includes Ghia, Seedlip, Kin Euphorics and Curious Elixirs. Minus Moonshine is Queer, Trans-Nonbinary, Indigenous and Autistic owned, and founder Aqxyl Storms has run both shops on a "drink what you love" premise — zero-proof versions of the drinks people actually miss, rather than substitutes framed as compromises. Open seven days a week, with same-day local delivery on orders placed online before 5pm.

name: Minus Moonshine
description: Minus Moonshine is a fully alcohol-free bottle shop in Prospect Heights, Brooklyn, opened in 2021 by founder Aqxyl Storms — making it one of New York City's earliest dedicated zero-proof package shops. From the street it reads like a neighborhood liquor store, but every bottle is non-alcoholic: NA beer, wine, spirits, aperitifs, mixers, bitters, and adaptogenic "potions." Inventory spans well-known zero-proof names including Ghia, Seedlip, Kin Euphorics, and Curious Elixirs, alongside NA wines and CBD/adaptogen spritzers. The shop is Queer, Trans-Nonbinary, Indigenous and Autistic owned, and is built around the idea of "drink what you love" — non-alcoholic whiskey, wine and aperitivo for sober and sober-curious customers, rather than substitutes framed as compromises. A second Brooklyn shop is open in Greenpoint, at 257 Driggs Ave.

name: Mirador
hours: Mon closed; Tue-Fri 11am-3pm; Sat 10:30am-2:30pm; Sun closed
description: Mirador, the penthouse restaurant atop the former Forty Five Ten department store in Downtown Dallas, refreshed its menu for 2026 with a wellness-minded direction that includes three spirit-free mocktails built like the kitchen's cocktails. The lineup leads with the Main Squeeze (passion fruit, coconut, orgeat and citrus finished with a splash of Topo Chico), the Citrus Sparkler (berry cordial, citrus and mint over mineral water), and the Smoked Milk Tea, which layers Fujian Province smoked lapsang souchong with creamy coconut milk, rosemary honey, strawberry and lime. These are composed, ingredient-driven builds served alongside the lunch and afternoon-tea service, not afterthought sodas.

name: Mírate
address: 1712 N Vermont Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90027
description: IMPORTANT CORRECTION — WE HAVE REMOVED THIS VENUE'S LISTED DRINKS. Mírate is an award-winning multi-level Oaxaca-inspired restaurant and mezcalería in Los Feliz from co-owner Matthew Egan and chef Joshua Gil, opened in late November 2022, ranked No.12 in North America's 50 Best Bars in 2025 and No.28 in 2026. We previously listed its Tepache and Nitro Pulque as non-alcoholic drinks. That was wrong. They sit in a section called "Bebidas Ancestral" — ancestral beverages — which appears between the cocktail list and the Mexican wine list as another alcoholic category, alongside Pasita, a Mexican rum-raisin liqueur. Nothing on the menu describes them as non-alcoholic or prints an ABV. Pulque is traditionally 4–7% ABV, roughly beer strength; tepache varies with ferment length. Beverage director Max Reis says he takes pride in offering them "in their authentic format" so guests can taste "the ingredient in its pure form", and the same tepache and pulque are used inside the bar's alcoholic cocktails. We found no dedicated alcohol-free section here. Ask the bar directly rather than ordering from Bebidas Ancestral expecting zero proof.

name: Miru
description: Miru is the Japanese restaurant on the eleventh floor of the St. Regis Chicago in Lakeshore East, looking out over the mouth of the Chicago River toward Navy Pier and Lake Michigan, and it runs one of the deepest hotel-restaurant zero-proof lists in the city. A Spirit Free heading on the cocktail menu holds six drinks at $14-$16: Setting Sun with fresh yuzu, Valencia orange, lychee and soda; Sunny Day with lemon, passionfruit, rice cordial and ginger beer; an N/A Rita of agave, fresh lime and sea salt; a Phony Negroni Bianco; an N/Aperol Spritz built on Lyre's Italian Orange and Lyre's sparkling; and a Coffee Cloud of Metropolis cold brew, demerara and vanilla. A separate zero-proof wine list carries Prima Pave and Oddbird by the glass and bottle.

name: Miss Angeline's
description: Miss Angeline's on Denton's downtown square runs the deepest non-alcoholic cocktail list in the metroplex: a printed Non-Alcoholic Drinks section with eight named mocktails, nearly all built on Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits. The range covers a MockaRita, a French 86, a PiNO Colada, an EspressotiNO and a NOgroni — meaning a non-drinker can order across the whole cocktail canon rather than picking from two. Six taps and cans back it up, including Guinness Zero and four Athletic Brewing beers. Open daily until 2am.

name: Mita's
description: Mita's is James Beard-nominated chef Jose Salazar's Spanish and Latin American tapas restaurant in downtown Cincinnati's 84.51° building at Fifth and Race. Its drinks list carries a dedicated "No Alcoholicas" section built on Ritual's zero-proof tequila alternative: the Sacrificio pairs it with guava, hibiscus, and lime, while the Paloma Picante adds grapefruit, jalapeño, ginger, agave, lime, and soda for a spicy, citrus-forward pour (both $12.50). Beyond the house mocktails, the kitchen stocks Best Day Brewing non-alcoholic beer in lime cerveza or West Coast IPA, plus Leitz Eins-Zwei-Zero non-alcoholic sparkling wine, alongside Jarritos and Mexican fountain sodas. It's a genuine sit-down alcohol-free option inside one of the city's most ambitious tapas rooms, named for Salazar's Colombian grandmother.

name: Mitch e Amaro
address: 306 Armour Rd, North Kansas City, MO 64116
description: Mitch e Amaro is a cocktail-supply shop, specialty bottle store and bar opened in February 2019 by brothers Josh and Ben Edwards on Armour Road in North Kansas City, in the former Le Monde Bakery space. The centrepiece bar is an integral part of the store, separating the retail at the front from the lounge at the back, so it functions equally as a shop and as a place to sit and drink. Its printed "Non-Alcoholic" menu is priced flat at $10 — the same as many of its alcoholic cocktails — and is built almost entirely on Seedlip: Garden 108, Spice 94 and Grove 42 are each available with soda, tonic or Fever-Tree ginger beer, alongside built drinks including the Pen-No-Cillin (Spice 94, lemon, honey ginger syrup), the Garden Sour, the Rabarbar-Oh-No! Highball and Unbuzzed, made with cold brew from local roaster Colony. One item, Smoke & Spice, carries the bar's own printed note that its Bittermens habanero shrub contains a trace amount of alcohol. Retail shelves stock Bare Zero-Proof, Kin Euphorics and Ritual Zero-Proof.

name: Mitsi
description: Mitsi is a cocktail bar and sushi counter on Naud Street, in the pocket between Chinatown and Mission Junction, opened in April 2026 by Ben Lovett of Mumford and Sons through his hospitality company TVG and sitting next door to the Pacific Electric concert venue. It seats about 110 across indoor and outdoor space, with a working sushi counter built into one end of a long bar, and a food menu by chef Jon Kim. It is licensed, and the drink menu carries a named Spirit Free section: the Phony Negroni from St. Agrestis in New York, a Longan Osmanthus Flower sparkling tea from S.C Lab in Taiwan, and a Tieguanyin Apple sparkling tea from the same producer. Open Thursday to Saturday only, 6pm to 1am, with the kitchen running to 11pm.

name: Mixtli
address: 812 S Alamo St Ste 103, San Antonio, TX 78210
description: Mixtli is San Antonio's most ambitious restaurant — a tasting-menu room in Southtown exploring regional Mexican cooking with real scholarship, and one of the most decorated kitchens in Texas. It offers multiple zero-proof options alongside its pairings, which matters disproportionately at this kind of venue: a long tasting menu is precisely the format where a non-drinker is most exposed, sitting through fifteen courses while everyone else receives a matched pour. The individual drinks are not publicly documented, so ask when booking rather than on the night. Dinner only, Tuesday to Saturday from 5:30pm; the room is small and reservations are essential.

name: Mnemonic Coffee
description: Mnemonic Coffee is a queer, women-owned café in Bankers Hill, opened in July 2023 by longtime specialty-coffee pros Gia Giambalvo and Sarah Girdzius and built intentionally as both a coffee and zero-proof drink space. Alongside oat-milk lattes, cold brew, and pour-overs, the team builds creative coffee sodas and mocktails for people who want the communal feel of a café without alcohol — or without downing multiple cups of caffeine. Named non-alcoholic drinks include the Maple St. (maple syrup, long pepper, cinnamon, apple foam, Topo Chico), the Soy Libre (Coke, simple syrup, soy sauce, lime, cinnamon), the cardamom-and-jasmine Ocean Eyes, and the orange-cream-soda-like Zephyr. The 1970s-inspired space keeps daytime hours, Tuesday through Sunday, with pastries from Relic Bageri.
signatureDrinks: Maple St.|Soy Libre|Ocean Eyes|Zephyr

name: MO Bar
address: 5 Raffles Avenue, Level 3, Mandarin Oriental, Singapore 039797
description: MO Bar, the flagship cocktail bar of Mandarin Oriental, Singapore, treats its non-alcoholic drinks as first-class pours rather than afterthoughts. The kitchen-driven bar team makes its own kombuchas and ferments, and the current Vol. 7 'Modern Localism' menu is built so drinks can be ordered either way: mocktails such as The Artis (fermented banana tibicos, pandan and coconut salt) are served alcohol-free by default with the choice to add vodka, while cocktails like B.T.B (Bean to Bar) come in a non-alcoholic variation. An earlier menu produced The Formosan (S$16), a coconut-cream Irish-coffee alternative served hot or cold.

name: Mockery Zero Proof
hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed 12pm-5pm; Thu-Sat 2pm-7pm; Sun closed
description: Mockery Zero Proof is Detroit's first dedicated zero-proof bottle shop, stocking non-alcoholic spirits, wines, and beers out of a storefront on the Livernois–McNichols corridor in Bagley. Founder Karlyta Williams — trained as a zero-proof bartender over three years and previously ran a mobile NA bar — also books Private Pours, one-hour closed-door sessions where guests choose a guided non-alcoholic wine flight or a custom zero-proof cocktail mixed to their own flavor and mood. It soft-opened in November 2024 with a grand opening timed to Dry January 2025, and keeps a running calendar of sober social events, including a February 2026 Galentine's zero-proof gathering.

name: Mockingbird
description: Mockingbird is Park Slope's first fully alcohol-free cocktail bar, serving thoughtfully crafted zero-proof cocktails alongside coffee, matcha, weekend brunch, and elevated bar bites at 213 7th Ave in Brooklyn.

name: Modern World
description: A fully non-alcoholic bottle shop on the Avenue in Hampden, opened by Laurie Hefner, a Minneapolis native who came up in hospitality and natural wine and was partly inspired by a friend's shop back home. Everything on the shelves is spirit-free at no more than 0.5 percent ABV, spanning canned NA cocktails, zero-proof spirits like Aplós, hop waters such as Hoplark Hopsour, and NA beers including La Trappe Nillis 0.0. The stock runs well past drinks into tinned fish and conservas from Espinaler, Gueyu Mar and Jose Gourmet, plus Torres chips, glassware and pantry goods, which makes it as much a dinner-party shop as a bottle shop. It is retail only, with no bar or on-site cocktail service, but Hefner has been explicit that she built it as a third space where not drinking isn't othered.

name: Moku Kitchen
address: 660 Ala Moana Blvd, Ste 145, Honolulu, HI 96813
description: Moku Kitchen is the anchor restaurant at SALT at Our Kakaʻako, the warehouse redevelopment that became the district's main food and drink block. It trades daily from 11am to 11pm, a longer day than most of Kakaʻako manages, and the kitchen works a farm-to-table brief with Hawaiian growers. Its current non-alcoholic build is the Mahana Sands, made with agave, lemon juice, pineapple juice, cucumber juice and soda water — mahana meaning warmth in Hawaiian, and the name taken from a green and a beach on Hawaiʻi Island. The cucumber juice is what makes it work, cutting the pineapple so the drink finishes dry rather than sweet. An earlier fixture, the So Figgin' Awesome, paired cinnamon, fig and vanilla in soda.

name: Monarch
description: Monarch is a wood-fired modern Italian restaurant on the 49th floor of The National building in downtown Dallas, created by two-Michelin-star chef Danny Grant, with a rotating seasonal zero-proof cocktail menu alongside its full bar.

name: Monday Morning
description: Monday Morning is a fully alcohol-free bottle shop and tasting bar in Ocean Beach, the second San Diego location from founder Zane Curtis, opened January 2, 2026 at 4967 Newport Ave inside the OB Business Center — on the one-year anniversary of the original Pacific Beach store. It stocks more than 500 zero-proof products: non-alcoholic beer, dealcoholized wine, spirit alternatives, ready-to-drink mocktails, and functional drinks across 50-plus brands including Athletic, Bravus, Partake, Seedlip, and Ritual. A tasting bar lets customers try anything before buying, and because the OB space is compact, the team opens the windows to serve the boardwalk. It's a genuine alcohol-free retail-and-tasting destination steps from the beach.

name: Monday Morning
description: Monday Morning is San Diego's first exclusively non-alcoholic bottle shop and tasting room, opened in Pacific Beach in late 2024 by founder Zane Curtis after he embraced a sober lifestyle. The shop stocks more than 500 zero-proof products — non-alcoholic beer (IPAs, lagers, stouts, sours, wheat), dealcoholized wine, spirit alternatives (gin, whiskey, tequila, rum), ready-to-drink mocktails, and functional drinks with adaptogens and nootropics — across 50-plus brands including Athletic, Bravus, Partake, Seedlip, and Ritual. A tasting bar lets customers sample anything before buying, with staff guiding selections. Curtis's business also handles NA distribution, custom recipes, staff training, and events, and in January 2026 it opened a second location in Ocean Beach.

name: Monkeypod Kitchen by Merriman
description: Monkeypod Kitchen by Merriman opened in 2024 inside the OUTRIGGER Reef Waikiki Beach Resort as the centrepiece of an $85 million rebuild of the property. It comes from chef Peter Merriman, one of the founders of Hawaii Regional Cuisine, through his Handcrafted Restaurants group. The mocktail list is a full menu section rather than an afterthought: the Virgin Monkeypod Mai Tai, the Blind Tiger built on hibiscus and lavender soda, and the Green Fevah. Opening daily from 7am to 11pm with happy hours at both 3.30pm and 9pm, it is the most reliably available option in Waikīkī for a table where not everybody is drinking.

name: Moon Flower
description: Moon Flower is a fully alcohol-free cocktail lounge that takes over Maya Moon Collective — a cacao café and organic chocolate shop on Adams Avenue in Normal Heights — Thursday through Sunday evenings. The zero-proof program is run by co-owner Grace Mestecky alongside Maya Moon founder Kathryn Rogers, who launched the collective's booze-free menu in 2023; the evening lounge format took shape in 2024. The rotating, seasonal menu leans on functional and adaptogenic ingredients, local produce, and herbs, building booze-free riffs on classic cocktails. Signature pours include Smoke and Mirrors (NA whiskey, black cardamom, orange bitters, burned honey, lapsang souchong), Spiritual Rest (Dromme, Everleaf, lemon, honey, ginger, turmeric), and Hi Barbie! (NA gin, NA bubbly, prickly pear, strawberry, yuzu, lime, kanna).

name: Moon Rabbit
description: Moon Rabbit is chef-owner Kevin Tien's modern Vietnamese restaurant at 927 F Street NW in Penn Quarter, reborn there in 2024 in the former Co.Co. Sala space after its original run inside the Wharf's InterContinental hotel closed in 2023. The intimate room of roughly 50 seats pairs Tien's cooking, threaded with his Louisiana roots, with a bar led by director Thi Nguyen, who won the 2024 Michelin Guide Washington DC Exceptional Cocktails Award. The Spirit Free list is given equal billing and equal pricing at $13: The Life of A Showgirl, with nectarine, verjus blanc and jasmine-lemongrass soda; Sai Gon Fruit Cart, on Lyre's white cane spirit with lacto-fermented pineapple and shrimp salt; Tho Ngoc | Jade, with soursop and osmanthus; and Ho Xuan Huong | The Poet. A zero-proof Beaujolais is poured by the glass.

name: Moona Moono
description: Moona Moono is a coffee, matcha and boba shop at Hennepin and 31st in Uptown that doubles as a retail space for Asian and Asian-American goods — K-beauty, stationery, ceramics, blind boxes. It is one of the few rooms in the neighbourhood that a sober restaurant critic has flagged as a place to spend an evening: it keeps cans of Ghia, the non-alcoholic aperitif, alongside a salted yuzu soda and a full matcha and espresso list, and it programmes the space with mahjong nights, silent book clubs, lo-fi craft nights and body-doubling sessions rather than relying on drinks alone to fill seats. A short list of Japanese beers is also stocked.

name: The Moon's Daughters
description: The Moon's Daughters is the rooftop bar at the Thompson Hotel, twenty floors above the River Walk with the best view in downtown San Antonio, and it keeps named zero-proof drinks on the list — Pluto's Revenge and Feeling Prickly, the latter built on the prickly pear that turns up across the city's better alcohol-free menus. Rooftop bars are usually the worst rooms for a non-drinker, because the whole proposition is a cocktail and a view at sunset. Having something properly made here means the person not drinking gets the view on the same terms as everyone else. It also serves from 7am daily and runs to 2am at weekends, an unusually long window for a hotel rooftop.

name: More or Less
address: 434 Leonard St NW, Grand Rapids, MI 49504
description: More or Less is a fully non-alcoholic bottle shop at 434 Leonard Street NW on the West Side of Grand Rapids, and Michigan's original dedicated non-alcoholic retail store. It was founded by Chad Clark and Neil DeMeester, who both stopped drinking in recent years and opened the shop at the turn of 2023 under the name Alt City NA Bottles and Beer before rebranding. The shelves carry more than 450 alcohol alternatives: canned craft mocktails, zero-proof spirits, botanical seltzers, gourmet sodas, adaptogenic drinks, CBD seltzers and non-alcoholic wines. Between six and ten bottles are kept open on a rotating basis so customers can taste before committing to a full bottle, which is the shop's main answer to a category where a bad guess is expensive.

name: Mother Cocktail Bar
address: 874 Queen St W, Toronto, ON M6J 1G3, Canada
description: Mother Cocktail Bar is a full-service cocktail bar and restaurant on Queen Street West in Toronto's West Queen West neighborhood, built around rotating, thematically-driven menus and fermentation-forward technique. Its current menu, "The 5th Horizon," carries a dedicated Signature Non-Alcoholic section with three named, house-made zero-proof cocktails — Tomato Soup, Fading Silhouette and Tonka Brew — each priced at $17. The bar was ranked No. 48 on Canada's 100 Best Bars 2026 list and No. 22 on North America's 50 Best Bars 2026.

name: Mother's House
description: Mother's House is a woman-owned tattoo studio, coffee lounge, and mocktail bar tucked into Oak Lawn in Dallas, founded by tattoo artist Brieana Jones, who spent years sketching in coffee shops before building a space that married her two loves. The result is a fully alcohol-free venue: every guest is met by a non-alcoholic beverage and coffee lounge serving espresso-based drinks, teas, and mocktails, with seating in a whimsical striped-ceiling lounge or a green checkered patio. The studio runs six artists and is widely noted as a safe, judgment-free, LGBTQ+-welcoming space. Walk-ins are welcome Wednesday through Saturday. Because the venue pours zero alcohol by design, the coffee-and-mocktail bar is genuinely sober-first rather than a token NA list bolted onto an alcohol program.

name: Mothership
description: Mothership is a sci-fi tiki cocktail bar and fully plant-based restaurant in South Park, opened in August 2022 by the team behind the vegan restaurant Kindred. The immersive, crash-landed-spaceship interior won an Orchid Award, and while the rum-forward tiki list is the headline, the bar also runs a genuine, fully built-out zero-proof program: its menu carries a dedicated "Beverages" section where every drink is labeled zero-proof. Named alcohol-free options include the X-Ray (white cane NA spirit, lime, Szechuan peppercorn, spearmint, peppermint oil), Tracking Device (coconut water, coconut cream, lime, hibiscus), Baby Bird (Italian bitter NA spirit, blood orange, caramelized pineapple, lime, soda), and Mindchiller. Mothership ranked among Yelp's 2023 Top 25 mocktail spots in the U.S.
signatureDrinks: X-Ray|Tracking Device|Baby Bird|Mindchiller

name: MOTW Coffee and Pastries
description: MOTW Coffee and Pastries is the Georgia branch of a specialty coffee and Arabic pastry chain that grew out of Muslims of the World, the storytelling platform Sajjad Shah started on Instagram. The Alpharetta shop sits on McGinnis Ferry Road and is fully alcohol-free, trading to 11pm Sunday through Thursday and to 1am on Friday and Saturday. That late close is what makes it useful as a going-out room rather than a morning stop, and it is one of the few in the far north metro. The counter pairs an espresso programme with Arabic pastries and desserts, and the company frames the cafe as an extension of its community and philanthropic work rather than as a straight retail concept. The Atlanta-area franchise is run by local owner Mudassir.

name: MOTW Coffee & Pastries
description: MOTW Coffee & Pastries is an alcohol-free cafe on Willard Street in Quincy, the Boston-area location of a chain that grew out of Muslims of the World, the Instagram storytelling project Sajjad Shah founded in 2014. The Quincy store runs to 9pm on weeknights and to midnight on Fridays and Saturdays, and its roughly 1,700 square feet are split between table seating and a lounge area of sofas meant for long stays. The menu is globally sourced rather than American-cafe generic: Yemeni chai and Egyptian teas sit beside date cardamom, Spanish and pistachio lattes, matcha drinks and fruit refreshers. Food is Arabic pastry and light bites, including baklava, milk cakes, date cookies, muffins and halal savory empanadas. It is Muslim-owned and halal; no alcohol is sold or served.
signatureDrinks: Yemeni chai|Date cardamom latte|Spanish latte|Pistachio latte|Egyptian tea

name: Mountain Madre
description: Mountain Madre is a Mexican kitchen and agave bar at 13 W Walnut Street in downtown Asheville, from owners Danny and Paige Scully, who built it to bring families and friends together. The kitchen runs empanadas at $14, chorizo-stuffed avocado at $18, downtown street tacos at $15, smoked brisket tacos at $17, enchiladas at $21 and carne asada at $34, with a proper kids' menu. It reopened with limited hours after Hurricane Helene. Its non-alcoholic drinks sit in a clearly separate section headed "0% ABV Cocktails", all built on Seedlip: the Prickly Pear ($13, Seedlip Notas de Agave, fresh lime, agave), Spicy Fuego ($15, Seedlip Garden 108, habanero pineapple syrup, lime) and Spiced Violet ($16, Seedlip Spice 94, blackberry syrup, lime). IMPORTANT: the bar's Blackberry Smoke and Spice of Life are full-strength margaritas built on mezcal and tequila and appear only in the alcoholic Margaritas section — order from the 0% ABV list by name.

name: Mr West Bar & Bottle Shop
hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 1pm-11pm; Fri 1pm-1am; Sat 12pm-1am; Sun 12pm-10pm
description: A two-level Footscray institution that pairs a proper walk-in bottle shop downstairs with a bar upstairs, both taking non-alcoholic drinks seriously. The bottle shop stocks a genuine zero-proof range across beer, wine and spirits alongside the natural wine and wild-fermented beer it's known for, so you can walk in and buy alcohol-free by the bottle. Confirmed non-alcoholic stock has included Garage Project's Tiny non-alc Stout and IPA and Dr Lo non-alcoholic sparkling, plus house-made non-alcoholic options poured in the bar. NoLo Life rates its no/low range a 4 out of 5. A Footscray bar with a full bottle shop downstairs, run by two operators who track new alcohol-free releases closely enough to have supplied a national non-alcoholic guide with its first NA beer.

name: M'tucci's Bar Roma
description: M'tucci's Bar Roma is the Nob Hill room of a local Italian restaurant group, on Central Avenue, and its alcohol-free drinks are built on house shrubs — pineapple rosemary and blueberry raspberry among them. Shrubs are the most useful thing a restaurant can make for a non-drinker: fruit preserved in vinegar and sugar, they bring sharp acidity and a savoury edge that no juice can, and they hold up across a meal instead of cloying. Italian dining is also where the aperitivo ritual lives, so a bar making its own shrubs can give a non-drinker something to do at the start of dinner. Open 11am daily, to 10pm and 11pm at weekends.

name: Muchacho
description: Muchacho keeps a printed zero-proof cocktail section on its bar menu built with real non-alcoholic spirits, not a token juice pour. The Mock-a-Rita swaps hibiscus-infused Lyre's Agave into the house margarita, and the No-Fashioned is built on Lyre's American Malt with chicha morada and orange. Rounding out the list are the No-Groni Sbagliato (non-alcoholic gin, Italian rosso, rose water, non-alcoholic prosecco) and the herbal Serene-Tea (pear, green tea, grenadine, lemon). Dallas's DiningOut named the lineup among the city's best zero-proof cocktails for Dry January.

name: Muddy Water Kava
description: Muddy Water runs 8am to 2am every day of the week in north St. Petersburg, one of the longest trading days in a county that calls itself the unofficial kava capital of the United States. Kava is the primary focus, and the coffee and tea alongside it are locally roasted, organic and treated as a programme in their own right rather than as filler. The staff are the selling point: the venue's own framing is that they will walk you through a wide array of botanicals — damiana, rhodiola, yerba mate, kanna, matcha. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: kratom is among those botanicals. It acts on opioid receptors and carries dependence and withdrawal risk that kava does not, so say what you are avoiding and they will steer you.

name: Multnomah Whiskey Library
description: Multnomah Whiskey Library is a spirits library at 1124 SW Alder Street in downtown Portland, famous for one of the deepest whisky collections in the country — and, less famously, it keeps a real non-alcoholic list. CORRECTION TO OUR EARLIER LISTING: older versions of its beverage menu carried nothing alcohol-free; the current menu, updated in April 2026, has a printed "Mocktails" section of six drinks. Love at Midnight ($10) is coconut cream, pineapple, lime, orange and demerara; Jungle Flower ($12) pairs pineapple with Ghia apéritif, lime and house falernum; Out of the Woods ($15) is the ambitious one, built on Everleaf Forest apéritif with non-alcoholic sparkling wine and lemon; and three bottled St. Agrestis Phony Negronis — original, white and espresso — are $12 each. Best Day Electro Lime and Athletic Run Wild are $7. IMPORTANT ON ACCESS: the formal Library room is member-nominated and reservation-led, but the ground-floor Green Room takes walk-ins every day with no membership and no reservation — its general manager says plainly that they want walk-ins. All spaces are 21+.

name: Muni Muni Tea Shop
description: Muni Muni Tea Shop is a fully alcohol-free tea and matcha bar on Church Street in downtown Nashville, a few blocks north of the Broadway strip. Everything is brewed or whisked to order rather than poured from a batch, and the menu is unusually specific about it: ceremonial-grade matcha, first-flush roasted hojicha, assam and jasmine green teas brewed per cup. The signature builds include a Strawberry Matcha Latte with milk cap and strawberry inclusions, a Coconut Matcha Latte with house virgin coquito and toasted coconut, a Hojicha Cheese Einspanner, and Cafe Cha, which layers earl grey and blue mountain coffee over coffee jelly. Bubble tea and tapioca options run alongside. No alcohol is served, and it stays open to 7pm on Friday, Saturday and Sunday.

name: Muskellounge & Sporting Club
description: Muskellounge & Sporting Club is a cocktail bar on Monona Drive in the Lake Edge neighbourhood, themed around Wisconsin's fishing and sporting-club tradition, and its non-alcoholic list leans on ready-to-drink bitters rather than sugar. It pours St. Agrestis's Phony Negroni — the Brooklyn producer's non-alcoholic negroni in a bottle, which is genuinely bitter and carbonated — alongside the Amaro Falso, its zero-proof amaro. Serving two bittersweet Italian styles rather than two sweet ones is an unusual and welcome choice. The bar keeps late hours for the east side, to midnight midweek and 1am on Friday and Saturday.
signatureDrinks: St. Agrestis Phony Negroni (non-alcoholic negroni, bitter and carbonated)|St. Agrestis Amaro Falso (non-alcoholic amaro)

name: Myriel
address: 470 S Cleveland Ave, Saint Paul, MN 55105
description: Myriel is chef-owner Karyn Tomlinson's tasting-menu restaurant on South Cleveland Avenue in Macalester-Groveland; Tomlinson won the James Beard Award for Best Chef: Midwest in June 2025. The kitchen cooks a Midwestern menu from what the season gives it, and the beverage side runs a full non-alcoholic pairing against the tasting menu rather than offering a single spirit-free drink as an alternative. The pairing's anchor is a dry sparkling tea, deliberately oversteeped so that the tannin gives it the body and drying finish of a wine and resets the palate between courses. Two sweeter non-alcoholic options run alongside it. Bar seats are held for walk-ins.
signatureDrinks: Dry sparkling tea (oversteeped, served as a non-alcoholic tasting-menu pairing)

name: Naïve Kitchen + Bar
description: Naïve occupies a corner building on East Washington Street in Butchertown and has been one of Louisville's more health-conscious restaurants since it opened, winning LEO Weekly's Readers Choice for Best Butchertown Restaurant and building a reputation on vegetable-forward cooking and an eco-minded operation. Its earlier menu carried a genuinely developed alcohol-free list — a Grapefruit Thyme Spritz, a ginger turmeric mule using the Louisville-made Modica mixers, and an apricot tarragon shrub soda — and Louisville's visitor bureau listed it among the city's best mocktail stops on that basis. The kitchen has since relaunched with a Latin-leaning menu, so ask what the current alcohol-free builds are.

name: Nalu Kava Tea Lounge
description: Nalu is a fully alcohol-free tea lounge hidden on the second floor above Cherry Sprout Produce in Humboldt, reached by an alley behind the Red Fox. Owner Holland Mulder opened it after deciding she no longer wanted to spend evenings in bars, and the menu is built around hand-prepared kava, thick drinking chocolate, mushroom tonics such as chaga and lion's mane, superfood lattes, kombucha and fire cider. The indoor room is full of plants, books and oracle decks; above it sits a rooftop patio and greenhouse. Kava is alcohol-free but psychoactive and mildly sedating — worth knowing before a first visit.

name: Namak
description: Namak is an Eastern Mediterranean and Persian restaurant at 1813 Columbia Road NW in the heart of Adams Morgan, opened in 2024 by longtime friends and established restaurateurs John Cidre and Saied Azali. The kitchen turns out creative takes on Persian, Greek, Turkish and North African cooking - sesame-crusted feta, walnut-marinated tenderloin kebabs, braised lamb shoulder in a harissa-scented jus - inside a room of cosy alcoves and Moroccan tile work. Its non-alcoholic list is unusually serious for a restaurant, and Resy singled it out as a menu where the zero-proof drinks take centre stage. The Zero Proof section of its current menu runs from the N/Amaro Namakia, a house-made lapsang souchong amaro-style liqueur, and Sekahnjebin, built on mint, cucumber, rose, honey and vinegar, to Şalgam, the traditional spicy fermented black carrot juice, plus house-made sodas in ginger-lemongrass, spiced mango-passionfruit and blackberry-long hot pepper.
signatureDrinks: N/Amaro Namakia|Sekahnjebin|Şalgam|House Made Soda

name: Namaste & Midtown
description: Namaste & Midtown is a fully alcohol-free kava and healing lounge on Kansas City's 39th Street corridor, in the Volker/Midtown area. It reopened in August 2025 from the former Midtown Kava, reframed by owners Moon Brown (a community organizer and anti-violence advocate), Alan Wayne (a Kansas City rapper behind the "Namaste & Shit" brand), and Andrew Beck. Local press describes it as a Black- and queer-owned sober bar built as a sanctuary for Black, queer, trans, and sober communities. The drink program is entirely zero-proof: house "Sacred Sips" plus carried-over staples like kombucha, traditional kava, and THC- and CBD-infused herbal teas. Named pours include Blue Moon (kava, coconut, CBD, microdose THC), Glitch in the Matrix (kava, ube coconut cream, vanilla matcha), and Astral Grounds (cold brew, functional mushrooms, cacao, eucalyptus honey, kava). The space also hosts "Tiny Shell Sessions" spotlighting Black and queer artists.
signatureDrinks: Blue Moon|Glitch in the Matrix|Astral Grounds

name: Nari
description: Nari is a one-Michelin-star contemporary Thai restaurant inside Hotel Kabuki in San Francisco's Japantown, from chef/owner Pim Techamuanvivit of Kin Khao. The name "Nari," a Thai word for "women," honors generations of Thai women who shaped the country's cuisine, and the kitchen filters traditional Thai cooking through California ingredients. The bar runs a small, deliberately edited "zero-proof cocktails" list that sits alongside the full cocktail and wine programs — five spirit-free drinks at $16 each, built on non-alcoholic spirits like Seedlip Grove and Pentire. Current named pours include the Unakarn (Seedlip Grove, shiso, lemongrass, tonic), the Suwan (Seedlip Grove, pomegranate, lime), the Nohra (Pentire Adrift, mint, lime, shiso), the Illa (Pentire, passionfruit, lemon, orgeat), and the dairy-forward Kusuma (mango-lassi, pandan, pineapple). It's a fine-dining destination, so reservations are recommended well in advance.

name: Narrative
description: Narrative is the signature restaurant of The Jacquard, an Autograph Collection hotel in Cherry Creek North with a rooftop pool and bar. It runs a seasonal mocktail list alongside its cocktails, changed with the menu rather than held static: Visit Denver names Bitter Passion, built on passion fruit and ginger, and Herb Heaven, made with lemon, mint and cucumber. The restaurant opens at 6:30am on weekdays and 7am at weekends and serves through to 11pm, covering breakfast, lunch, dinner and late drinks in a neighbourhood where most kitchens close earlier. The rooftop gives the same drinks a second setting in summer. It is a modest but genuine zero-proof offering in a part of Denver that the city's existing non-alcoholic coverage has largely missed.

name: Native
description: Native, Vijay Mudaliar's pioneering sustainability-led cocktail bar on Amoy Street, runs a full non-alcoholic menu with as many drinks as its alcohol list, all built without refined sugar using hydrosols, edible oils and in-house ferments. Zero-proof anchors include the Sereh Telang (butterfly pea, lemongrass, calamansi) and a house Thai-style ginger beer (galangal, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaf, chili), each around S$12. The team leans on its fermentation lab -- kombuchas, misos, meads and a koji-aged 'pineapple shoyu' from fruit waste -- to give the no-alcohol builds real depth. Native ranked No. 45 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025 and No. 84 on The World's 50 Best Bars 2025.

description: Nativo is a modern Mexican cantina on York Boulevard in Highland Park, owned by Gabriel Paredes and Corrissa Hernandez, who also run Xelas in Boyle Heights. It is a licensed bar built around agave, rum and cerveza artesanal, and it carries one of the deepest standing zero-proof lists in Los Angeles: a titled Zero Proof Cocktails section with six named builds, all made with zero percent alcohol. The list runs a Margarita Mocktail on Ritual Zero tequila with orange cordial, lime, agave and housemade Tajin salt; a Zero Proof Pina Colada; a Paloma Mocktail; a Zero Proof Mojito; a Zero Proof Whiskey Sour with egg whites; and a Zero Proof Penicillin finished with a smoky botanical mist spray. Open to 2am on Friday and Saturday.

description: Nautilus Pier 4 is the Boston outpost of the Nantucket restaurant The Nautilus, on the water at Pier 4 Boulevard in the Seaport. It serves modern Asian-inflected seafood and small plates with a raw bar, dinner nightly and lunch at weekends. Its drinks list prints a non-alcoholic section under the heading Don't Mock It 'Til You Try It, subtitled N/A bevies for the sober curious, with three named drinks at $13 and cold brew on draft at $7. G+G is guava, grapefruit, citrus and soda; Pineapple Express is pineapple, a house-made ginger soda and lime; and Thai Herb Swing is watermelon, Thai herbs, lime and soda. The cold brew is roasted locally at Atomic Coffee. The builds are citrus- and fruit-forward and designed to sit next to seafood.

description: Navy Strength is a tropical cocktail bar at 2505 2nd Avenue in Belltown (entrance on Wall Street), opened on 30 March 2017 by Anu Apte and Chris Elford, whose Canoe Ventures group also runs Rob Roy and Vinnie's Wine Shop. It won Best New American Cocktail Bar at the 2018 Spirited Awards at Tales of the Cocktail. "Tiki bar" undersells it — the drinks list travels, taking on a new set of international flavours every six months, the first of which was India, in a nod to Apte's heritage. It keeps three named non-alcoholic drinks on the menu at all times under a heading that simply reads "Mocktails", each $12: the Sober Saturn (bright, zesty, passion fruit), the Mint Sour (light and easy-drinking) and the Pom Pom (fruity and bubbly). The bar prints tasting notes rather than ingredients for these, so ask what is in them if it matters. Food runs from a $19 nacho platter to $7 sliders and $4.50 Pacific Northwest oysters. The bar is 21+, open Wednesday to Saturday. During its October 2026 Halloween pop-up, Nightmare on Wall Street, the regular list is swapped for a horror-film cocktail menu on which three drinks — Lamia's Curse, Pearl's Swizzle and Mister Babadook — can be made as mocktails; the standing three come back with the regular menu.

name: neat.
address: 11780 W Pico Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90064
description: neat. is a whiskey and cocktail bar on Pico Boulevard in West Los Angeles, known for a deep rare-spirits list and guided whiskey tastings, and it keeps a standing non-alcoholic section on the same printed drink menu. That section runs five items: Wishful Sinful, built on Pathfinder non-alcoholic spirit with yuzu, lemon and ginger; Eyes Wide Shut, an espresso build with cucumber tonic and orange; Alter Ego, with elderflower, cucumber, mint and lemon; a non-alcoholic Negroni; and Weihenstephaner's alcohol-free lager. Prices run $8 to $12, in line with the rest of the room rather than marked down. The bar is open until 2am Thursday through Saturday, with happy hour every day from 5 to 7pm.

name: Neon Moon
description: Neon Moon is a late bar on 2nd Avenue North in downtown Birmingham, and it opens when most places are winding down — 8pm midweek, 6pm at weekends, running to 2am every night it trades. Its non-alcoholic list is genuinely deep rather than nominal, with enough drink creations that Bham Now described it as a room where you will not feel like you are missing out on anything, and its frozen Kentucky coffee is the one the paper singled out. A late bar that has done this work is unusually valuable, because midnight onwards is where alcohol-free options normally disappear.
signatureDrinks: Frozen Kentucky coffee (non-alcoholic)

name: Neon Pigeon
description: Neon Pigeon is a Tokyo-inspired 'third culture' izakaya on Carpenter Street whose drinks list is deliberately split into full-proof, half-proof and zero-proof cocktails built with the same craft — the alcohol-free builds are listed alongside the rest rather than buried at the back of the menu. The best-selling zero-proof No Kaze pours Lyre's London Dry (alcohol-free gin) with London Essence blood-orange-and-elderflower tonic, a house Thai-basil cordial and a dashi-and-seaweed saline, garnished with Japanese cucumber, shiso and celery. The floral Lady Hinata (S$14) layers zero-proof gin with lavender, cucumber and shishito peppers, and there's a non-alcoholic Amaretti Sour built on Lyre's Amaretti and zero-proof Prosecco.

name: Nest at Nurture
description: Nest is the cafe inside Nurture, a wellness campus on Federal Boulevard in West Highland that also houses fitness studios and care providers. It opened in May 2020 under co-founder Kelly Campbell with culinary director Elizabeth Woodard, and its beverage programme is built around cold-pressed juice, adaptogenic drinks and coffee rather than around a bar. Named juices include the Jasper, a watermelon-lime-jalapeño-cilantro blend, and the Onyx, made with lavender, raw honey, lemon and ginger with activated charcoal; the coffee menu extends to adaptogenic mushrooms and oils such as palo santo, and there is an iced mushroom coffee served with oat or A2 whole milk. Westword lists it among Denver's non-alcoholic options for its mocktails. It is a daytime venue, closing at 4pm.

name: Nevada Brew Works
address: 1327 S Main St Ste 160, Las Vegas, NV 89104
description: Nevada Brew Works is a family-friendly craft brewery and brewpub in the heart of the Las Vegas Arts District, with an industrial taproom where the brewing tanks are in full view and a spacious outdoor beer garden strung with lights. Beyond its house-brewed beers and brick-oven pizza, burgers and pub fare, the taproom markets itself as "accessible for any kind of drinker," keeping rotating non-alcoholic beers on hand along with mocktails, cider and wine, plus simple zero-proof staples like lemonade and Arnold Palmers. It draws a mixed crowd of locals, families and visitors for casual hangouts, date nights and weekend afternoons. The brewery has grown beyond its original Arts District home, adding a second location at Boca Park in Summerlin. Non-drinkers can comfortably join a group here, though the non-alcoholic program is accommodating rather than a dedicated, named zero-proof menu.

name: Never Say Dive
description: Never Say Dive sits on Broadview Road in Old Brooklyn, the largely residential south-west Cleveland neighbourhood that has slowly been gaining bars worth crossing town for, and the name is the joke: it looks like a dive and is emphatically not one. The kitchen runs rotating seasonal dishes and hands the room over to guest cooks regularly — a Cold Noodle Monday Vietnamese pop-up is the standing example — and the bar takes reservations through Resy, which tells you how the place actually operates behind the shopfront. Its non-alcoholic drink comes off the same station as the cocktails: a house strawberry tonic at $9 built from strawberry syrup with cinchona bark, fennel seed and basil, so it carries genuine quinine bitterness rather than sweetness with soda over it. Four non-alcoholic beers sit in the fridge alongside.
signatureDrinks: Strawberry tonic (strawberry syrup, cinchona bark, fennel seed, basil)

name: New Holland Brewing – The Knickerbocker
address: 417 Bridge St NW, Grand Rapids, MI 49504
description: The Knickerbocker is New Holland Brewing's Grand Rapids brewpub, on the Bridge Street strip at 417 Bridge Street NW. It is a large room by brewpub standards — three separate bars, a wood-fired oven, indoor and outdoor beer gardens and several private dining spaces. Its relevance to non-alcoholic drinking is that New Holland brews its own alcohol-free beer rather than stocking somebody else's: Zylch IPA is a 0.00% ABV IPA made with ingredients that let it carry real malt and hops. The brewery also produces Aquanut, a non-alcoholic sparkling water, and the bars mix a selection of zero-proof cocktails. In a city that has called itself Beer City USA since 2012, this is the brewery that answers the question of what a non-drinker orders.

name: New Mexico Ferments
description: New Mexico Ferments is a local kombucha producer in Albuquerque with kombucha on tap, and it is the second working ferment house in this city guide alongside UrbanMama505. For a non-drinker the value is takeaway rather than an evening out: growler fills and bottles mean the drink you would order in a bar is available at home, which is where most people who have stopped drinking need the alternatives most. Albuquerque having two independent kombucha brewers pouring on tap is a genuinely unusual local asset for a metro this size. Hours are not published reliably for a producer this small, so check before travelling.

name: Night Hawk
description: Night Hawk is a small, consistently full cocktail bar hidden behind Five Oars Coffee Roasters on Tanjong Pagar Road, named for Edward Hopper's 1942 painting Nighthawks and fitted out to match. It is run by veteran bartender Peter Chua and ranked 77th on Asia's 50 Best Bars in 2025. Its commitment to non-drinkers shows in the pricing rather than in marketing: non-alcoholic drinks are a standing line on the menu at S$22++ against S$25++ for the spirited ones, so a zero-proof order is a normal transaction at a normal price. Bartenders will also build non-alcoholic versions of menu drinks or work to a guest's palate. Walk-in only — the bar takes no reservations.

name: Nightjar
description: Nightjar opened in 2011 on City Road at the northern edge of Shoreditch and was among the bars that defined London's modern cocktail revival. It was founded by Edmund Weil and Rosie Stimpson, a jazz, swing and blues singer, who set out to build a room that would do justice to the music as much as the drinks — Weil has said the idea came from the style and the music angle before the drinks, rooted in a love of art deco design and the pre-Prohibition era. It took Difford's Guide's Best New Bar award in its opening year and went on to place third on The World's 50 Best Bars in 2012. There is live music nightly, and the menu carries an explicit non-alcoholic section rather than off-menu mocktails: the signature Adonis is built from Taronja de Gris orange wine, Aperitivo Professore, Fino sherry, barrel-aged tsipouro and Muyu Vetiver Gris for genuine bittersweet depth.

description: Nightshade is a nightlife venue at 32 Banks Ave #105 in Asheville's South Slope, open Thursday to Saturday evenings, with DJs, live shows and a BASSBOSS sound system, partnered with Plant Bar for plant-based food. It serves genuine zero-proof cocktails — a Matcha Blossom ($12) with matcha, pineapple, sakura and Roots Divino, a Lemon Pop Drop ($11), a Butterfly Gin & Tonic ($12), a zero-proof Old Fashioned ($11) and a Spring No-Jito ($9) — plus a Mertails line crafted by The Nohm. READ THIS BEFORE VISITING: Nightshade markets itself as "entirely alcohol-free", and that is true of alcohol only. It also runs a menu section headed "Catch a Buzz" of cannabinoid drinks on draft at $7, dosed from CBD-only up to Cosmic at 15mg THC ("potent"), Yerba Mate at 25mg THC, and Elevation at 50mg THC ("very potent"), with $3 add-on shots including HHC, delta-9, kanna, blue lotus and kava. The only warning printed on the menu concerns caffeine and pregnancy. Anyone avoiding intoxicants should order strictly from the signature or classic cocktail sections and say so clearly.

description: North Main is a woman-owned and LGBTQ+-owned kava bar in downtown Lowell, west of Charlotte in Gaston County, and by its own account the only kava bar for seventy-five miles. The biergarten seats around 250 at communal tables and runs year-round, heated in winter and shaded in summer.

The drinks lean on Somali and other global coffee and tea traditions and rotate seasonally; the baking is done in house by one of the owners, a self-taught baker, and covers chocolate pistachio scones, tahini banana bread, brown butter cinnamon rolls and an Egyptian croissant bread pudding served with cardamom creme anglaise.

Honey Badger is lemon, grapefruit, honey and ginger beer at $15; Super Fresh is white cranberry, lemon and soda at $14; and Raspberry Fields is built on Lyre's Italian Spritz with raspberry, basil, agave and lemon at $15. It began as a coffee shop and now describes itself as a haven for botanical wellness: micronized kava prepared in juice or milk, functional mushroom drinks built on Sporeganix powders from Winston-Salem, Rishi organic teas and Pure Intentions Peruvian coffee, with comfortable seating, workspaces and weekly drumming, stretching and monthly Kirtan music events. It also prepares kratom drinks and sells delta-THC and CBD products, all labelled, so read before you order. No alcohol is served. The two standing builds run citrus-forward and herbal respectively — a house citrus cordial and a garden julep. Small room, seasonal list.

It was opened by career bartender Joshua James, who bills it as San Francisco's first non-alcoholic bar, and it serves scratch-made food and Four Barrel coffee alongside craft zero-proof cocktails, chai and kava. The retail side stocks one of the largest selections of non-alcoholic beer, wine and spirits in the country. The cafe also runs Temperance Tastings, alcohol-free mixology classes, a private lounge called Temperance and a membership programme, Club AF. The San Francisco Standard has called it the granddaddy of the city's alcohol-free nightlife, and it is the anchor of non-alcoholic drinking in San Francisco.

Isaac Showaki founded Octopi and launched Untitled Art with Levi Funk of Funk Factory Geuzeria in December 2016; the non-alcoholic range is fully fermented and then stripped of ethanol by reverse osmosis, which preserves the hop oils and malt character that boiling-off destroys. The taproom pours the line on site, including the mango dragonfruit sour and the west coast IPA that Visit Madison singles out.

That breadth is the point — a brewery that carries five different categories of alcohol-free drink has thought about the fact that non-drinkers have preferences too, rather than assuming one NA lager covers everybody. Opened in November 2024 by Matt and Jess Longueville — the couple behind cocktail-catering company STL Barkeep and The Vandy — Off Elm is a walk-in-only, mid-century-modern room on Big Bend Boulevard. The printed menu carries a dedicated Non Alcoholic section: Blood For The Blood God layers zero-proof rum with blood orange, lime, orgeat, and bitters, while the Crimson Gimlet pairs zero-proof gin with red wine syrup and lime. Gruvi NA lager and Best Day NA kölsch anchor the beer list, and the menu promises most classic cocktails can be made non-alcoholic.

name: Offtrack
description: Offtrack is a music-centric bar and restaurant at 34 North Canal Road, near Boat Quay, that placed No.16 on Asia's 50 Best Bars in 2026. The room is built around listening: an acoustically treated space, a carefully assembled sound system and a wall of vinyl from Singapore and the wider region. The cocktail list is an equal split of classics and contemporary builds, and the bar states plainly that the menu also offers an inclusive non-alcoholic selection of mocktails and non-alcoholic beers. A visitor in 2025 recorded a Passionfruit Jamu Soda at S$16 from that list. The kitchen serves a pan-Asian menu, with a late-night snack menu on Fridays and Saturdays, and it trades until midnight on weekdays and 1am at weekends.

name: Old City Kava Company
description: Old City Kava Company is a fully alcohol-free kava and kratom lounge that opened in December 2025 at 40 S. 2nd Street in Philadelphia's historic Old City. Founded by Luca Kobza and Adam Lagner, the 1,900-square-foot space is built as a bar alternative for the sober-curious, with roughly 60 seats across a bar, two-tops, and jewel-toned couches, a small board-game collection, and rotating contemporary art for sale. The drink program centers on 16-plus kava-, kratom-, and botanical-tea-based mocktails, including the Lemongrass Paloma, the Old City Red Eye (kava, kratom, ReAnimator cold brew, oat milk, agave, vanilla), the Old Citywide, the Cucumber Basil Cooler, and Maple Masala. By day it doubles as a coworking cafe serving ReAnimator coffee, Random Tea Room teas, and Funky Fresh kombucha; it stays open until midnight on weekdays and 2 a.m. on weekends.

Its bartenders build named spirit-free cocktails to order — the Sober Mule (CleanCo Clean G, strawberry-watermelon agave, Giffard orgeat, lemon, ginger beer) and Not Another Spicy Margarita (habanero- and jalapeño-infused Seedlip Notas de Agave, agave, lime) — treating zero-proof drinks with the same care as the full cocktail list.  It is a neighbourhood restaurant rather than a sober venue, which is exactly why it works for the common case — a table of six where one person is not drinking and nobody wants to pick the venue around that.

Named Salt Lake magazine's Best Restaurant of 2025 and a repeat James Beard Award semifinalist for Best Chef: Mountain, it is one of the city's most decorated kitchens. Oquirrh was an early local restaurant to take non-alcoholic drinking seriously — it keeps a stock of NA spirits, including non-alcoholic whiskey, so the bar can build a zero-proof version of essentially any cocktail on its menu, with the same care given to the wine and whisky list.

It was the first shop of its kind in the Indianapolis metro and remains the anchor of the region's alcohol-free retail scene. The shelves run to alcohol-removed red, white, rosé and sparkling wine, non-alcoholic beer, zero-proof cocktail spirits, ready-to-drink mocktails, bitters, mixers, syrups and kava drinks, with most of the range low-sugar, gluten-free and vegan. There is a small bar and lounge area at the back, and the staff pour generous samples rather than sell blind. The business took the Orangily name in 2025.

description: Orangily's second shop opened in March 2025 on East 54th Street in the SoBro stretch of Meridian-Kessler, next door to United State of Indiana and across from Breadworks. It is the only dedicated non-alcoholic bottle shop inside Marion County — the original Orangily and every other alcohol-free retailer in the metro sits out in Hamilton County. Sisters Andrea Simpson and Kristin Patrick stock alcohol-removed wine, non-alcoholic beer, zero-proof spirits, ready-to-drink mocktails, kava drinks, mixers, bitters and syrups, and keep bottles open for tasting so nobody buys unseen. Afternoon and weekend hours are built around the neighbourhood rather than around a bar crowd, and personalised delivery is available by text.

name: Orapax Restaurant and Bar
description: Orapax is a long-running neighbourhood restaurant and bar in Ghent, the kind of unpretentious room that has fed a Norfolk neighbourhood for decades, and its named alcohol-free drink is the Sparkling Lavender Lemonade — Perrier, fresh lemon juice, lavender syrup, fresh rosemary and blackberries. What earns it a listing is the specification: fresh juice and fresh rosemary rather than a mix, in a venue whose reputation rests on Greek-inflected comfort food rather than its bar. It also keeps genuinely useful hours, open from 11am to 10pm most days, which makes it a rare all-day option. Most of the region's better alcohol-free drinking hides behind 5pm bar openings, so an all-day kitchen matters.

The current entry is the Maiden Manhattan: cold brew coffee, cranberry, lemon, demerara and Angostura bitters, a stirred, dark, genuinely bitter drink built to sit beside food rather than to refresh. Dinner runs Wednesday to Sunday from 5pm, with weekend brunch from 10am, and the kitchen is among the more ambitious in the metro.

The bar designs each drink around flavour and experience first, not alcohol level, so lighter builds like the Bubble Club - distilled guava lychee, umeshu, vitamin C cordial and water - sit alongside its full-strength cocktails as fully developed offerings. Bursik favours year-round moderation and 'discovery, not restriction' over strict abstinence.

It takes its name from a mid-century Nite Cap whose original signage was found during renovation. With roughly 14 bar seats plus tables, it hosts burlesque, drag, comedy, and live music alongside a craft cocktail and Italian wine program. Its zero-proof list is fully built out with named drinks rather than afterthoughts: the Corset Strings (Lyre's NA dark cane, chai cordial, lemon, soda, NA bitters), the Stage Kitten (NA gin, hibiscus cordial, lime, NA bubbles), the Show Stopper (cold brew, coffee demerara, NA gin, foam), and Dazzle 'Em (NA rum, lime, ginger syrup, ginger beer).

The restaurant lists three pairings against its $325 tasting menu - spirit free, standard and reserve - with wine director Emily Rosenfeld curating the wine flights and bar director Maddie Balintona building the spirit-free one from creative non-alcoholic beverages made to complement the menu course by course. Cocktails in the dining room are created by Balintona; the wine list, curated by Rosenfeld, is old-world in emphasis with a focus on white wines. Service runs Tuesday to Saturday evenings only.

Choose Chicago, the city's official tourism body, lists it among the Chicago bars with the best mocktails, describing a non-alcoholic list that leans on classic Mexican flavors and ingredients; Block Club Chicago has separately documented zero-proof drinks made with carrot juice, grapefruit juice, apricot cinnamon syrup and ginger beer. The anchor is All In, Other Half's own non-alcoholic hazy IPA at under 0.5% ABV — hopped with Citra, Simcoe and Centennial, giving notes of peach candy, ripe grapefruit and mango. That it is brewed in-house rather than bought in matters: this is a brewery known nationally for hop-forward beer applying that expertise to a beer with the alcohol taken out. Alongside it the taproom pours St. Agrestis Phony White Negroni and Phony Mezcal Negroni. The room runs to eleven on Friday and Saturday.

It is part bar, part shop: you can buy local vegetables and fruit, olive oil and fresh pasta, or order lunch, dinner, drinks and snacks from noon through the evening. description: Pig and Tiger is a Taiwanese night-market restaurant in Denver's Five Points, opened in August 2025 by co-chefs and co-owners Darren Chang, a Top Chef alum, and Travis Masar, who launched the concept in 2020 as a stall at Avanti in Boulder; the name comes from their Chinese zodiac signs. The current list marks two: the May Mei, a Taiwanese salted plum spritz inspired by Chang's mother's favourite flavour, and Curious Mr. Brown, a riff on the iconic Taiwanese canned coffee built with coffee and monkey bread tea. Both are made with the same house syrups and scrap-derived sugars as the full-proof list. Large-format drinks arrive in teapots, and the menu changes with the season.
signatureDrinks: May Mei (available zero proof: Taiwanese salted plum spritz)|Curious Mr. Brown (available zero proof: coffee and monkey bread tea, after the Taiwanese canned coffee)

name: Pig Latin
hours: Mon 4pm-9pm; Tue-Wed 11am-9pm; Thu 11am-10pm; Fri 11am-11pm; Sat 10am-11pm; Sun 10am-9pm
description: Pig Latin is a riverside restaurant in Eagle, the affluent suburb north-west of Boise, and it covers all three registers a non-drinker might want across a day: mocktails, proper coffee and matcha. That breadth is more useful than it sounds — most venues offer one of the three, so a place serving a decent matcha in the morning and a built mocktail in the evening covers a whole day's worth of alcohol-free drinking in a part of the metro that has very little else. Open from 10am at weekends and to 11pm on Friday. Eagle sits about fifteen minutes north-west of downtown Boise and has very little else documented, which makes a single all-day venue disproportionately useful there.
signatureDrinks: Mocktails|Coffee|Matcha

name: Pillion Tea
hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 10am-4pm; Fri 1:30pm-7pm; Sat 10am-4pm; Sun closed
description: Pillion Tea is a fully alcohol-free tea house on West Biddle Street in Mid-Town Belvedere, open since March 2019 and built around loose leaf sold by the ounce — Keemun Hao Ya, Iron Goddess of Mercy, Yunnan Gold, and compressed sheng pu-er cakes from Ai Lao Shan and Yi Wu. The drinks program runs well past steeped tea: the shop makes its own syrups and even a housemade non-alcoholic rum, which anchors a seasonal mocktail of sticky rice pu-er shaken with coconut milk and salted banana simple syrup. House sodas pair fresh seltzer with tea and fruit syrups — Rooibos Cream Soda, Blueberry Matcha, Hibiscus & Rose Spritzer, and the Lucky Piña built on Karigane green tea and yuzu-pineapple syrup. The caffeine-free Desert Rose Latte (honeybush, spice syrup, vanilla bean, rosewater) is an homage to the family farms in South Africa, Syria, Lebanon, Palestine, Sri Lanka, and Afghanistan whose ingredients are featured in the cup. It is a daytime room rather than a night spot: closed Sunday and Monday, with a late Friday close at 7pm.
signatureDrinks: Seasonal Mocktail|Desert Rose Latte|Rooibos Cream Soda|Hibiscus & Rose Spritzer|Lucky Piña|Ginger Mint Spritz|Blueberry Matcha

name: Pilot Project Brewing
description: Pilot Project Brewing, opened in August 2019 by co-founders Dan Abel and Jordan Radke, bills itself as the country's first dedicated brewery incubator — a Logan Square tasting room, café, and kitchen that gives startup and minority-owned breweries a launch pad for production and distribution. Its non-alcoholic credentials are unusually deep for a brewery: Pilot Project is the U.S. brewing and distribution partner for Mash Gang, the London NA-beer brand founded by Jordan Childs and James Loveday in 2020. Pilot Project brews Mash Gang's lineup stateside and pours it on tap here, including Journey Juice (a Tajín-spiked mango IPA at 0.5% ABV) and Stoop Lite (a light, chili-and-Szechuan-tinged lager). The rotating Mash Gang range also features Chug (hazy IPA), Glug (cerveza), and the seasonal Lesser Evil (chocolate-cherry stout). Local coffee and tea round out the zero-proof options.
signatureDrinks: Journey Juice|Stoop Lite|Chug|Glug

name: The Pine Room
description: The Pine Room is a neighbourhood restaurant in historic Harrods Creek, on River Road north-east of Louisville, and it keeps one of the better-stocked non-alcoholic back bars in the metro. Rather than a single token bottle it carries both of the Louisville-made Spiritless expressions — Kentucky 74, the non-alcoholic bourbon, and Jalisco 55, the non-alcoholic tequila — which means the two drinks most people actually want, an old fashioned and a paloma, can both be built properly here without alcohol. The paloma is the one the city's zero-proof coverage names. Dinner runs Tuesday to Sunday with weekend brunch from 9am, and the room sits close enough to the Ohio River to make the drive worthwhile.
signatureDrinks: Non-alcoholic Paloma (Spiritless Jalisco 55, grapefruit, lime)|Non-alcoholic Old Fashioned (Spiritless Kentucky 74)
