name: Pink Flamingo
description: Pink Flamingo is a rum-focused tropical tavern that Dutch Courage co-owners Brendan Dorr and Eric Fooy opened in April 2025 in the Remington building that ran as Dizzy Issie's from 1937, became The Dizz in 1997, and sat shuttered after closing in fall 2019. Its Spirit Free list is a standing section of the menu rather than an on-request favor: the Road Less Traveled builds Pathfinder N/A amaro into a mule with blood orange-Calabrian chile honey, lime and ginger beer, while The Shallows pours Lyre's N.A. cane spirit with fassionola and All The Bitter aromatic bitters. If The Shoe Fitz mixes Mionetto N/A prosecco with aperitif and soda water, and a Yuzu-Thai Basil-Limeade rounds out the zero-proof cocktails alongside NA cans from Athletic, Best Day and Lagunitas. Bar manager Nick Pikounis told PUNCH the Road Less Traveled is the bar's single most-ordered N/A drink. The bar was named a 2026 James Beard Award semifinalist for Best New Bar.
signatureDrinks: Road Less Traveled|The Shallows|If The Shoe Fitz|Yuzu-Thai Basil-Limeade

name: Pink Gorilla Kava
address: 340 W Flagler St, CU #102, Miami, FL 33130
description: Pink Gorilla Kava is a fully alcohol-free coffee-and-kava hybrid that opened in April 2026 at 340 W Flagler St in Downtown Miami, a short walk from the Miami River and Brickell. It comes from the team behind the Miami fashion label Pink Gorilla — founders Daniel Karan and Christian Ramos — with restaurateur Giancarlo Rodriguez involved in the venue. The concept runs as a specialty coffee bar by day and a kava lounge by night, pitched as a low-key, sober alternative to the neighborhood's club-heavy scene. Mornings bring organic coffee, lattes, and ceremonial matcha with scratch-made syrups and pastries from local bakeries; evenings shift to traditional kava and botanical "k-tea." The roughly 66-seat space includes a large outdoor terrace and doubles as a retail storefront for the Pink Gorilla brand. Early reviews praise the matcha and coffee.

name: Pink Lantern
description: Pink Lantern is downtown Birmingham's most talked-about recent opening and, for a non-drinker, its most useful: it runs from 7am to midnight on weekdays and to 2am on Friday and Saturday, which means coffee, lunch, an early drink and a late one all happen in the same room. The mocktails are built rather than poured — a Disco Paradise of club soda, lime, mint, dragon fruit and elderflower, and a Fool Me Twice where spicy ginger beer meets cantaloupe, pineapple and bright lemon. Birmingham's own Bham Now singled the bar out for them in its January 2026 guide to drinking without alcohol in the city.
signatureDrinks: Disco Paradise — club soda, lime, mint, dragon fruit, elderflower|Fool Me Twice — spicy ginger beer, cantaloupe, pineapple, lemon

name: Pinky's
description: Pinky's is a Scott's Addition bar and restaurant that does something quietly unusual with its non-alcoholic drinks: it prices them below the cocktails. That sounds minor and is not — plenty of bars charge full cocktail money for a drink with the expensive ingredient removed, and the resentment that causes is one of the most common complaints among people who do not drink. The list is named rather than improvised, with the Cyprus Cooler and The Afternoon in Monaco — strawberry, basil, lime and soda water — singled out by local guides, and non-alcoholic Heineken behind the bar for anyone who just wants a beer in hand.
signatureDrinks: The Afternoon in Monaco - strawberry, basil, lime, soda water|Cyprus Cooler|Non-alcoholic Heineken

name: Pins Mechanical Co.
description: Pins Mechanical Co. is a large South Congress games bar — duckpin bowling, pinball, patio — and its zero-proof list is specified with real ingredients rather than left as an afterthought, which is rare in the activity-bar category. Extra Credit is built on Lyre's Aperitif Rosso with Italian spritz, honey mango and rose water; Gym Class Zero pairs a non-alcoholic gin with desert pear and tonic. The venue matters for a specific reason: the whole proposition is the games rather than the drinking, so a group can spend a long evening here with no one's order standing out. Open late Friday and Saturday to 2am.
signatureDrinks: Extra Credit - Lyre's Aperitif Rosso, Italian spritz, honey mango, rose water|Gym Class Zero - non-alcoholic gin, desert pear, tonic

name: Pins Mechanical Co.
description: Pins Mechanical Co. is a South End entertainment bar anchoring duckpin bowling, 40+ pinball machines, and classic arcade games in a lively, all-ages-friendly setting. The drinks menu includes two dedicated zero-proof cocktails — the Carmen Sandiego and Johnny Tsunami — both crafted with Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits, plus three NA beers (Athletic Run Wild IPA, BrewDog Elvis Juice AF, Sam Adams Just the Haze NA). A separate kids' mocktail section (Juice Box Hero, Lisa Simpson, Optimus Prime, Shorty Baller) rounds out the NA lineup, making it a genuinely sober-friendly destination for entertainment-seekers who want more than soda.
signatureDrinks: Carmen Sandiego (Lyre's Aperitif Rosso, Lyre's Italian Spritz, honey mango, rose water — 0.0% ABV) $11|Johnny Tsunami (Lyre's Dry London, lavender, blue razz — 0.0% ABV) $11

name: Pizza Lupo
description: Pizza Lupo is a wood-fired Neapolitan pizzeria on Frankfort Avenue, opened in 2017 by the musicians Adam Turla and Sarah Balliet of Murder By Death with chef Max Balliet of Holy Molé. The drinks programme is natural wine, Italian amari and a full bar, and — unusually for a room that specific about its wine list — it prints a non-alcoholic menu described plainly as being for designated drivers. The Chinotto Dream is the build regulars name, running on chinotto, the bitter Italian citrus soda that is the closest thing in the soft-drink world to an aperitivo. Service is nightly from 5pm.
signatureDrinks: Chinotto Dream (chinotto bitter citrus soda build)

name: PKL Social
description: Pickleball-and-golf-sim sports bar and beer garden on Shepherd Drive in Houston's Washington Avenue/Heights corridor, merged with sister concept FM Kitchen & Bar in July 2025, pouring a modest but real non-alcoholic lineup that includes Athletic Brewing NA beer and a house cherry limeade.
signatureDrinks: PKL Cherry Limeade (non-alcoholic)|Frozen Strawberry Lemonade (non-alcoholic)|Athletic Brewing (non-alcoholic craft beer)

name: Planet of the Tapes
description: Planet of the Tapes is a comedy club, bar and video-store-themed hangout on Barret Avenue in Phoenix Hill, and it has the most non-drinker-friendly pricing policy in Louisville: any of its movie-inspired cocktails can be made as a mocktail for $5, a flat price well under the alcoholic version rather than the usual practice of charging cocktail money for juice. It also makes its own sodas in house — mango pineapple, raspberry pomegranate and lavender lemon — and names drinks with the same cheerful nonsense as the rest of the room, including the Shirley Temple of Doom and The Mangolorian. Shows and open mics run most nights until midnight, or 2am at weekends.

name: Plant Bar
address: 202 Manufacturers Rd Ste B, Chattanooga, TN 37405
description: Plant Bar is a specialty coffee, tea and zero-proof bar on Manufacturers Road on the North Shore, the Chattanooga half of a two-city operation that also runs in Asheville. It serves artisanal coffee, traditional Chinese and herbal teas, boba, cacao and a zero-proof cocktail list, with locally made pastries alongside, and it describes itself plainly as a non-alcoholic venue rather than a café that happens to lack a licence. Oat, almond, coconut, soy and whole milk are all included at no extra charge, and decaf espresso is offered on every drink. It is open from 8am to 10pm most days and to 11pm Thursday through Saturday.

The menu carries a dedicated Spirit Free Cocktails section — six $10 drinks built with the same rigor as the house classics, using Feragaia free spirit, Dhos zero-proof gin and tequila, Giffard NA Spritz and Nozeco alcohol-free sparkling rosé. Standouts include Not a Pickle, Bell Tolls, Mace of Spades and Under The Grapefruit Moon. St. Louis Magazine calls it a St. Louis institution that 'makes mocktails with equal skill and finesse.'

The chalkboard list of roughly five cocktails rotates constantly, and the NA builds get the same culinary treatment as the boozy ones: recent menus have featured the Flibbertygibbety, with zero-proof tequila, star anise, bitter lemon, and a coffee reduction, and the frozen Jelly of The Month Club made with Ritual rum alternative. Kombucha and NA seltzers round things out amid pinball, live music, karaoke, and comedy nights.

description: Pleasant House Pub is the Pilsen all-day pub built around British royal pies - steak and ale, kale and mushroom, chicken balti - in the former Nightwood space on South Halsted Street, open from 10am for coffee and pastry and switching to full-service dinner in the evening. Its drinks list carries a clearly marked NA block with four options: an NA Aperitif Spritz built from a Giffard non-alcoholic aperitif with soda, tonic water and an orange twist at $9; a Proxies Bubbly Red wine alternative with blackberry, raspberry and black tea notes at $11; a Saint Viviana sparkling chardonnay at $13; and a Cann blood orange cardamom at $12, which contains 2mg THC and 4mg CBD per 8oz can and should be avoided by anyone steering clear of cannabinoids.

The beverage program treats mocktails as a first-class option alongside cocktails: every drink is built from a shared base of eight house-made syrups — including ube coconut, brown sugar cardamom, chai, and Thai tea — and can be prepared as a coffee, cocktail, mocktail, or THC-infused drink. Guests who don't drink alcohol can experience the full flavor-forward menu without compromise.

name: Plume

The current menu carries three built mocktails using genuine zero-proof spirits — Seedlip, Giffard NA Apéritif, and Ritual Zero Proof Whiskey — and CultureMap Houston's Dry January coverage has separately profiled four more named $10 mocktails from the bar's rotating list. It's a full bar first, not an alcohol-free venue, but non-drinking guests get composed drinks rather than a soda-and-lime substitute.

name: Point 5
description: Point 5 is Richmond's dedicated non-alcoholic bottle shop, on West Cary Street in Carytown, and as of 2026 it is the last one standing in the city — the Fan's Ceremony has closed its Richmond location and moved to Norfolk. Owner Jody Sidle stocks more than 100 brands across zero-proof spirits, non-alcoholic beer and wine, functional drinks, ready-to-drink mocktails and botanical elixirs, which makes it the one place in Richmond where the whole category sits on a shelf to be compared. It is a shop rather than a bar, but it runs tastings, education classes and community events for alcohol-free living, so it functions as the scene's meeting point too.

name: Point Easy
description: Point Easy is a chef-driven New American restaurant in Denver's Whittier neighborhood, opened on June 29, 2022 in the former Whittier Pub space at the corner of East 28th Avenue and Williams Street. The owners are Andy Bruch and brothers Dan and Dennis "Denn" Phelps, alumni of the Kitchen Restaurant Group in Boulder who had developed the concept years before the pandemic delayed it; Denn Phelps, who wrote the opening menu, died unexpectedly on July 22, 2022, weeks after the doors opened, and the team has run the restaurant in his memory since. The kitchen is now led by executive chef Reuben Tomlins, with Richard Long as general manager. The menu is seasonal and farm-driven with a house-made pasta program, and the wine list favours biodynamic and small-producer bottles. The bar keeps a headed 0% ABV section of six drinks on its own published menu, from a fermented pineapple tepache and a Colorado-made non-alcoholic crabapple cider to cocktails built on Dr Zero Zero amaro, Citadel non-alcoholic gin and Giffard elderflower non-alcoholic liqueur, and the bar's Get Fed service will build a drink to a guest's stated preferences.

name: Poka Lola Social Club
description: Poka Lola Social Club is a cocktail bar inside The Maven Hotel at Dairy Block in Denver's LoDo (Lower Downtown) neighborhood, with a concept that blends art-deco elegance and Midwestern soda-shop nostalgia inspired by turn-of-the-century American soda fountain culture. Beverage manager Lexi Parker runs a seasonal cocktail program built around fresh produce — recent menus have featured ingredients like ube, lychee, snap peas, turmeric, and pink peppercorn-infused spirits. The bar maintains a dedicated non-alcoholic cocktail menu on its own website, which turns over with the seasons: the current list runs Water Your Garden (La Borosa non-alcoholic agave spirit, Giffard NA aperitif, herbes de Provence, lemon), Sandy Cheeks (house coconut cream, pineapple, lime), Walking on Sunshine (strawberry, honey, mint, lemon), and Rootin' Tootin' (sarsaparilla, molasses, wintergreen, star anise). The venue features live music, an alley bar that opens for warm-weather seating, and a 'Dealer's Choice' option where the bar crew creates a custom cocktail based on the guest's preferences.

name: Polite Provisions
description: Polite Provisions is a craft cocktail bar that opened in 2013 from San Diego hospitality group CH Projects, set in a 1920s apothecary-style room with a long marble bar near the North Park–Normal Heights border. After a closure tied to a liquor-license suspension, it reopened in early 2025 with a reworked menu organized into five sections — including a dedicated "Sans Alcohol" list — under beverage director Alicia Perry. The zero-proof options lean into the bar's housemade-soda and soda-fountain heritage: Daisy's Soda Pop (apple spice, pomegranate, lime, soda) and Gabe's Painless Killer (passionfruit, coconut, pineapple, lime), plus brand-built drinks like a Cinnamon Cherry Cola on Pentire and a Cacao Strawberry on Feragaia, some served as ice cream floats. It carries James Beard and Tales of the Cocktail recognition.

name: Polly Bar

description: Polly is one of Melbourne's oldest surviving cocktail bars, a plush, Art Deco-styled room on Brunswick Street in the heart of Fitzroy. Its non-alcoholic offering isn't an afterthought: the menu carries a dedicated printed mocktail section, built with the same attention to flavour that goes into its cocktails, spanning bright-and-fresh through creamy-and-indulgent. Named zero-proof drinks include Summer In Fitzroy, Teas Me, Sassy Lassie and Milk Bar. Polly keeps a dedicated mocktail menu printed below the cocktail list, built with the same attention to flavour the bar gives its cocktails, and running from bright and fresh through to creamy and indulgent.

name: Pomona Cafe & Wine Bar
description: Pomona Cafe & Wine Bar opened in July 2026 in East Boston's Maverick Square, an all-day room that pours single-origin Colombian drip and espresso in the morning and turns into a small wine bar at night. It is open 8am to midnight every day of the week, which is unusual for the neighborhood. The drinks list carries a named Mocktails section with three builds: Hugo Libre, a spritz of elderflower, fresh mint, lime juice, non-alcoholic sparkling wine and soda at $15; Corsa, made with non-alcoholic tequila, strawberry, grapefruit, lime, aperitivo and soda water at $14; and Roselle, a raspberry, hibiscus and lemon build at $13. Separate non-alcoholic wine and beer sections list a dealcoholised Loire rose, a German zero sparkling brut and Zero Gravity's Green State Lager Zero.

name: Pop's Blue Moon
description: Pop's Blue Moon calls itself "A Mindful Bar," and it has receipts: this century-old tavern on The Hill — built with lumber salvaged from the 1904 World's Fair — pours one of St. Louis' deepest non-alcoholic lineups alongside its regular bar. Owner Joshua Grigaitis launched booze-free New Moon N/A Saturdays back in November 2018, and by 2022 Feast Magazine reported that non-alcoholic options accounted for about 30 percent of sales, from Athletic Brewing and WellBeing beers to some ten varieties of Lyre's zero-proof spirits and his own Cheerz NA seltzers. One honest heads-up: alcohol-free here isn't always substance-free — the bar also serves CBD, CBG and delta-8 THC-infused drinks. Live music keeps the tiny room loud most nights.

name: Port Street Beer House
description: Port Street Beer House is the Northern Quarter's benchmark craft-beer bar, open since 2011 and a cornerstone of Manchester's independent beer scene. Alongside its 18 keg lines, seven cask pumps and hundreds of rotating cans, it keeps a genuinely deep alcohol-free bank rather than a token 0% option — modern, crafty zero-per-cent beers on tap and in the fridge from brewers such as Hawkshead, Jever and Schneider Weisse. It is widely cited as the best place in the city to actually drink a range of good AF beer rather than settle for whatever is left over. Run by the Common & Co group, it treats a well-poured 0.0% with the same seriousness as its cask and keg.

name: Porzana
description: Porzana is Daniel del Prado's Argentinian wood-fire steakhouse in the North Loop, occupying the former Bachelor Farmer space on North 1st Street. It keeps one of the deepest standing spirit-free lists in the city: six non-alcoholic drinks, five of them at $13, listed on the same cocktail menu as the full-strength ones rather than tucked away. The house builds are the Sanguino, with blood orange, white chocolate, rhubarb, elderflower, lime and sparkling tea, and the Serrata, with blackberry, hibiscus, beet, Greek yogurt and lemon. A tarragon and verde tea drink called T&T, two Copenhagen sparkling teas and a dealcoholised sparkling rose complete the section.

name: Post Haste
description: Post Haste is a farm-to-glass cocktail bar and restaurant that opened in June 2023 at 2519 Frankford Ave in Philadelphia's East Kensington neighborhood, led by beverage director Fred Beebe and director of operations Gabe Guerrero. Its defining conceit is hyper-regional sourcing: every spirit, beer, wine, herb, and mixer comes from east of the Mississippi River. That same craft extends to a dedicated "Free Spirit" zero-proof section, where the bar builds non-alcoholic cocktails with as much intent as the full-proof list. Current spirit-free pours include the Tea El See (Charleston black tea, condensed oat milk, allspice, cardamom, pandan, and Ritual non-alcoholic aperitivo), the Holy Negroni, and Peachy Keen. Post Haste was named to Esquire's Best Bars in America 2024, one of two Philadelphia bars on that year's list. NA cocktails run $12–$14.

description: Opened in June 2018 by Takashi and Tamara Gibo — the team behind the acclaimed Takashi sushi next door — Post Office Place is an intimate craft cocktail bar that shares an entrance with the restaurant on Market Street. Known for a deep Japanese whisky list and a James Beard Foundation Outstanding Bar Program semifinalist nod in 2023, it also keeps one of the most thorough printed non-alcoholic menus in Salt Lake City. The dedicated NA menu itemizes a bottled St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, Athletic NA beers, Gruvi Sparkling Rosé, and build-your-own zero-proof cocktails on Spiritless (Kentucky 74, Jalisco 55), Dhōs Gin, and Monday Zero whisky — plus a bespoke "Bartender Roulette" the team crafts to order. In 2026 the bar was named Salt Lake magazine's Best Restaurant alongside its Takashi omakase collaboration.

name: Postino WineCafe
address: 1301 S Lamar Blvd, Ste 102, Austin, TX 78704
description: Postino WineCafe is a regional wine-bar chain founded in Phoenix's Arcadia neighborhood in 2001 by Craig and Kris DeMarco (Upward Projects), known for its approachable wine list, bruschetta boards, and "Board + Bottle" deals. The South Lamar location — Postino's Austin South Lamar outpost — opened November 9, 2024, near the Saxon Pub. In January 2025, Postino introduced a five-drink zero-proof cocktail menu across all its locations, its first dedicated non-alcoholic cocktail program: the Glow-Up (cucumber, mint, lime, ginger beer), the Espresso Flirtini (spiced cane, hazelnut, espresso), the Mockingbird (pineapple, Italian orange, toasted almond bitters), the Unfashioned (honey, bitters, amaro), and the Naked Ranch Water (lime and soda). The full-service wine bar pairs these with its small-plates menu, 12-plus bruschetta varieties, and an extensive wine and beer list.

name: Posto
description: Posto is chef Joe Cassinelli's Neapolitan pizzeria and enoteca, which moved from Davis Square to a larger room at Assembly Row in Somerville in November 2024 after thirteen years on Elm Street. Wood-fired pizza, house pasta and grilled meats sit alongside a long wine list and, notably, a printed 'Zero Proof - Alcohol Free' section of eight drinks. Six are built on non-alcoholic spirits at $15, matching the cocktail price: an N/A-perol Spritz on non-alcoholic Mionetto aperitivo and N/A sparkling wine, an Espress-No Martini on Fluere spiced cane with dark roast espresso and cream, a No-Groni and a Faux Mule on non-alcoholic Amsterdam Damrak, a No-jito, and a Tilden Spritz. Two simpler spritzes are $8.

name: Potluck Teahouse

description: Potluck Teahouse is a fully alcohol-free teahouse and working pottery studio on Gallatin Pike in Inglewood, East Nashville, and it describes itself as the city's only pottery studio-teahouse. The tea list is a curated selection rather than a house blend: single-origin and blended leaf from High Garden, the original East Nashville teahouse whose signature blends Potluck deliberately carries on; from Tea for Tea, blended locally in Nashville; and from Spirit Tea in Chicago. Pours run to Rose Garden Grey, Sun Drenched, Bee's Knees, Garden Party Green, Kodama Sencha and Lapsang Souchong, all $4.50. The room doubles as a gallery for local pottery and goods, and the studio runs public workshops - wheel throwing, handbuilding, matcha-set classes with a tasting. No alcohol is served.

name: Prazbar
description: CHECK BEFORE YOU TRAVEL — this listing has changed. Prāzbar is a faith-based, fully non-alcoholic wine project founded by Quenjana Adams, which began as pop-ups in Bronzeville and West Town in late 2021 and opened a permanent shop, "2048", at 2048 W Chicago Ave in September 2023, named for its address. As of September 2026 we still cannot confirm that shop is still trading: every one of its own web properties is dead (2048chi.com no longer resolves, prazbar.org and both of its Square storefronts return 404), prazbar.com forwards to a ticket page for a one-off fashion event at a different venue, and no opening hours have been publishable since 2023. What is definitely active is the brand. Adams posts regularly, and in June 2026 announced that Prāzbar is building a permanent music venue for faith-genre live music in Chicago — writing that the team has spent several years producing live faith and music events in the city and that "today, we are building that home." Treat Prāzbar for now as an alcohol-free events producer with a venue in development. The wines it pours are all between 0% and 0.5% ABV.

name: Press 626 Wine Bar
hours: Mon closed; Tue-Wed 11am-10pm; Thu-Sat 11am-11pm; Sun closed
description: Press 626 is a wine bar and cafe in a converted Ghent house, and its non-alcoholic offering is a set of Garden Lemonade Spritzers built in three variations — lavender rosemary, chamomile orange, and pomegranate sage. Herb-and-flower pairings like those are a deliberate choice rather than a default: they give a soft drink aromatic complexity and a dry finish, which is exactly what is missing when you take wine off the table. In a venue where the entire proposition is wine, having a considered alternative on the printed list is the difference between a guest being catered for and being tolerated.

name: Prima Dopo
description: A Fells Point "cucina and cocktail house" on Thames Street serving contemporary Italian small plates, artisan pizza and house-made pasta until 2 a.m. on weekends. Its main menu boxes out a dedicated Mocktails section beside the cocktail list, built on real non-alcoholic spirits rather than juice: My Cousin Dill combines Seedlip Grove 42 with cucumber puree, lemon, agave, dill and soda, and Le Moxie mixes Seedlip Spice 94 with strawberry puree, lemon, agave, rosemary and ginger ale. The third pour, Cafe Kinda Dopo, is a cold brew with brown sugar simple syrup and oat milk — a zero-proof mirror of the bar's Casamigos-spiked Cafe Dopo. All three are $12, in line with the house cocktails.

Its bar carries four signature zero-proof mocktails priced around $10-$12, on par with many of the restaurant's alcoholic cocktails rather than as an afterthought; confirmed builds include the Strawberry Rose Refresher and the Kosnopolitan. It remains a full-bar restaurant first, so this is a solid named NA list, not an alcohol-free destination.

name: Proof on Main
description: Proof on Main is the restaurant and bar of the 21c Museum Hotel on West Main Street, open since 2006 and a fixture of Louisville dining, with a bar holding more than 75 Kentucky bourbons. Its non-alcoholic programme is among the deepest in the city and is built on stock rather than improvisation: the bar carries the full Lyre's range plus Spiritless Kentucky 74 and Jalisco 55, the Louisville-made non-alcoholic bourbon and tequila, and NKD LDY de-alcoholised gin, and it makes its own ginger ale and tonic water in house. Effectively anything on the cocktail list can be built alcohol-free, and the bar also understands half-measures for anyone reducing rather than stopping.

Alongside its beer, wine, and cocktail list, the bar has run a crafted non-alcoholic agave program built around Almave, the zero-proof blue-agave "tequila" co-created by Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton, including the Golden Hour Margarita (Almave Blanco, fresh lime, prickly pear syrup, agave nectar), the Blanco Paloma (Almave Blanco, fresh grapefruit and lime, Squirt), and the Ámbar Carajillo (Almave Ámbar, cold brew, agave nectar, aromatic bitters). These crafted zero-proof drinks were highlighted as a Dry January feature rather than a permanent year-round menu. Standing non-alcoholic choices at the bar include Fever-Tree sodas, fresh-pressed juices, Perrier, and Red Bull, and the surrounding food hall offers coffee, donuts, and other vendors for non-drinkers. The food hall is open daily from 7:00 AM, making the bar an accessible Strip option for an alcohol-free order.

description: Public Records is a plant-based restaurant, cocktail bar, and hi-fi music venue in Gowanus, Brooklyn, opened in April 2019 by musician Francis Harris, designer Shane Davis, and hospitality director Erik VanderWal. It occupies a 1910s building that served as the ASPCA's Brooklyn headquarters for decades, and the all-vegan kitchen nods to that history. The campus spans several spaces, including The Atrium restaurant-lounge, where the bar program runs alongside an extensive cocktail list. The Atrium menu carries a dedicated "Zero-Proof" section of fully built spirit-free cocktails rather than an afterthought mocktail or two. Current named options include the Palomar (NA mezcal, elderflower cordial, spiced grapefruit shrub, lemon balm, soda), Not For Rita (NA agave spirit, spiced grapefruit shrub, lime, agave, damiana), and Press For Time (coffee, cinnamon-lapsang-sorghum syrup, vanilla-coconut cream whip, reishi, orange), plus housemade sodas.

description: Pufferfish is a rooftop tiki bar perched on the sixth floor of Hotel Metro in downtown Milwaukee's East Town, pairing skyline views with a playful, island-inspired cocktail program. Its menu carries a dedicated "Spiritless Cocktails" section — a standing, named list of zero-proof tiki drinks built on Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits and served in full tiki style. Alongside an alcohol-free take on the signature PufferFish, the list includes spiritless versions of the Mai-Tai, Rum Collins, Snaquiri and Old Fashioned. Its 2025 'Recipe Book' menu — published as a genuine take-home recipe book — sets three no-booze punches alongside fifteen spirited ones, and the bar has highlighted its alcohol-free serves as strong sellers. All three zero-proof drinks are built on Everleaf, the British non-alcoholic aperitif, and are made sustainably from the same ingredients as the spirited cocktails earlier in the menu.

Its North Park taproom on El Cajon Boulevard pours 20 taps in a tucked-away courtyard with URBN Pizza handling food. In April 2026 the brewery expanded into non-alcoholic beer, brewing two house NA options now poured year-round at all five of its taprooms: Grounded, an NA IPA built on Citra and Mosaic hops with lemongrass, citrus, and resin notes; and Sunsip, an NA blonde ale with flavors of fresh-baked bread, jasmine, and lemon peel — both below 0.5% ABV. name: Pusadee's Garden
description: Pusadee's Garden is a family-owned Thai restaurant on Butler Street in Upper Lawrenceville, named for Pusadee Tongdee and run by her daughters Watcharee and Bootsaba Tongdee with Michael Johnson. It closed in 2017 and reopened in January 2021 after a four-year ground-up rebuild by mossArchitects that won a Design Pittsburgh Honor Award — two renovated buildings joined by an entry arcade, a glass-box bar and an open kitchen with traditional Thai tao charcoal stoves, around a courtyard garden visible from most of the dining rooms. Chef Bootsaba "Gik" Tongdee was named a James Beard semifinalist for Best Chef: Mid-Atlantic in 2024. Its bar menu has a section headed "Spirit-Free/Non-Alcoholic" holding Give it a Chai ($8, chai, ginger, lemon), the house seltzer ($6, Thai basil, pink peppercorn, strawberry) and AL's Classic Lager, a non-alcoholic lager under 0.5% ABV ($7). The Pathfinder non-alcoholic amaro ($10) is also poured but is filed with the amari rather than in the spirit-free block, so ask for it by name. Reservations are Resy-only, tables cap at six, and there are no highchairs or boosters.

It is a licensed cocktail bar built around margaritas, tequila and mezcal, and it carries a standing zero-proof section on its printed menu headed Nada Guey: the Paloma Refresco with ruby grapefruit, lava salt, fresh lime and fizzy water; La Playa with fluffy pineapple, toasted cinnamon, pomegranate and chia seeds; and the Fresa Loca with fresh strawberry, mandarin orange and citrus tonic, each $9. The room is a low-lit lounge with a hidden entrance across from Bridgestone Arena, floral wall murals and a daisy-tiled floor, and it stays open to 2am on Thursday, Friday and Saturday.

name: Qahwah House
description: Qahwah House is a fully alcohol-free Yemeni coffeehouse — there's no bar and never has been. The East Dearborn flagship at 6655 Schaefer Rd pours traditional preparations like Mofawar (cardamom-and-cream coffee), Rada'ey (ginger-cardamom light roast), Qishr (cascara with ginger and cinnamon), and Adeni Chai (black tea, cardamom, nutmeg, milk), made from beans sourced directly from founder Ibrahim Alhasbani's family farms in Yemen. It's the original location behind what's now a 30-plus-store chain, and the reason East Dearborn is a genuine destination for Yemeni coffee culture rather than just another espresso stop.

description: Qahwah House is a Yemeni coffeehouse on Central Avenue NE in Windom Park, the Minnesota outpost of a chain founded in Dearborn, Michigan in 2017. It serves no alcohol at all and stays open until midnight seven nights a week, which makes it an evening room rather than a morning coffee stop. Coffee is imported directly from Yemen and roasted on the premises. The menu keeps a full Yemeni Style Coffee and Tea section alongside the espresso bar: Sana'ani, Jubani, Mofawar, Rada'ey and Qishr are all listed by their regional names, and the Adeni Chai is built on Yemeni black tea with cardamom, nutmeg and milk. Sabayah and other Yemeni pastries are sold at the counter.

Qamaria's coffees are organised around how different Yemeni villages prepare them, so the menu lists Mufawaar, Juban and qishr — the spiced drink brewed from coffee husks — by name rather than by roast level, alongside Aden tea, a cardamom-and-cinnamon house latte, pistachio lattes, refreshers and smoothies.

description: Qamaria Yemeni Coffee Co. opened on Prairie Center Drive in Eden Prairie on 15 February 2025, the chain's third Minnesota shop and the only Yemeni coffeehouse in the southwest metro. The menu is the Qamaria standard: qishr brewed from coffee husks with ginger and cinnamon, Mufawaar with cardamom and cream, Juban, Aden tea, and a house latte spiced with cardamom and cinnamon, alongside pistachio lattes, an espresso list, refreshers and smoothies. Pistachio milk cake, honeycomb bread and Dubai chocolate anchor the pastry counter. The room is set up for long sittings rather than quick pickups, with large tables and no closing-time pressure until well after most Eden Prairie restaurants have shut for the night.

description: Qamaria Yemeni Coffee is a large, fully alcohol-free Yemeni coffeehouse on the stretch of North Kedzie Avenue in Albany Park that has become Chicago's densest cluster of Middle Eastern cafes. It is the Chicago outpost of Qamaria Yemeni Coffee Co., founded by Yemeni entrepreneurs Hatem and Munif with the stated mission of sharing Yemeni-sourced coffee with the world, and it keeps the late hours that define the category: open until midnight most nights and until 1am on Friday and Saturday. The room is built for sitting rather than grabbing and going, with a deep floor of tables a block north of the CTA Brown Line's Kedzie stop. The menu runs on light-roast Yemeni coffee, spiced milk drinks, signature lattes and a case of Middle Eastern pastries and cakes. No alcohol is served at any hour.

description: Qamaria Yemeni Coffee Co. is a fully alcohol-free Yemeni coffeehouse on East Hampden Avenue in Aurora, the first Colorado outpost of a chain founded by Yemeni entrepreneurs Hatem Al-Eidaroos and Munif, who source single-origin beans from the Haraz region of Yemen. It opened in April 2026 near the Colorado Muslim Community Center and stays open to 10pm on weeknights and 11pm on Fridays and Saturdays, which makes it a genuine late-evening alternative to a bar rather than a daytime cafe. The room is laid out for lingering, with traditional Yemeni floor seating and cushions alongside conventional tables. Alongside espresso drinks the menu runs to qishr, the tangy infusion brewed from dried coffee husks, and spiced drinks built on cardamom and cinnamon, served with baklava, milk cakes and honeycomb bread.

description: Qamaria Yemeni Coffee Co. is a 3,600-square-foot Yemeni coffeehouse in the International Village shopping centre on North Berkeley Lake Road in Duluth, north-east of Atlanta. It is the largest cafe the chain has built, seating roughly 140 people across booths, tables and two lounge areas, and it is fully alcohol-free. Opening hours are the point of it: noon to midnight Monday through Thursday and 10am to 1am on Friday and Saturday, which puts it among the few late-night rooms in the north-eastern suburbs that pour nothing stronger than coffee. The beans are 100% Yemeni and are served in both traditional Yemeni and espresso preparations. Qishr, Adeni chai, the house Qamaria Latte and pistachio lattes anchor the drinks list, with cakes and honeycomb bread from a prep kitchen on site.

The menu runs the traditional Yemeni preparations rather than a standard espresso list: iced mufawaar built on coffee with cardamom and cream, juban kettle coffee, qishr infused from cascara with cardamom, ginger and cinnamon, and Aden tea. Sweeter modern drinks sit alongside them, including an iced pistachio latte and the araysi, a mango drink finished with vanilla drizzle. description: Queen & Rook is a board game cafe on South Street with a printed menu section headed "Zero Proof Cocktails & Beer", eight drinks deep and flat-priced at $8 — one of the longest non-alcoholic lists in Philadelphia. Princess Rosalina builds butterfly pea tea with lychee, lime and soda; Galadriel runs pineapple and lychee against jalapeño, tajín and cilantro; Abraxos gets Iron Teeth uses a blackberry shrub with mint and lemon; and Smaug's Scales pairs a strawberry shrub with basil and lemon. It is the second location of a small operation that started in suburban Libertyville, and it is run as a late-night room: doors open at 5am and stay open until midnight on weeknights and 1am on Friday and Saturday. The name, logo and wall mural all reference the Queen of Sheba, ruler of Yemen and Ethiopia, and the beans are sourced from Yemen. The menu covers traditional milk and cardamom-spiced coffees at $5-$6, spiced signature lattes, teas, smoothies, breakfast plates and a dessert case. No alcohol is served.

name: Radio Bar
description: Radio Bar is a neighbourhood cocktail bar on Northwest Boulevard in Spokane's Audubon-Downriver district, a cosy room with a fireplace and a retro sound system, well outside the downtown bar cluster. Its drinks list balances classics with the bartenders' own creations, and carries a handful of non-alcoholic cocktails on a rotating seasonal basis alongside a range of alcohol-free beers — the seasonal rotation being the point, since the list changes with the produce rather than sitting static. Imported wine, bottled and canned beer, cider and seltzer fill out the rest. Open Tuesday to Saturday from 4pm, plus Sunday afternoons, closed Monday.

name: Ramadan's Egyptian Coffee House
description: Ramadan's Egyptian Coffee House is an alcohol-free late-night cafe in Marcy Holmes, a block from Dinkytown and the University of Minnesota campus. It soft-opened on 4 June 2026 under owner Ramadan Hussein, with his cousin Ali Mohammed helping run it, and it does not open until 1pm — the schedule of an evening room, running to midnight on weeknights and 1am on Friday and Saturday. The drinks list is genuinely Egyptian rather than Egyptian-themed: sahlab, sobia, carob, tamarind and hibiscus sit alongside Shaay Koshary, Shaay Fatla and Shaay Bilaban teas, Turkish coffee and a saffron or cardamom Arabic coffee served from a dallah.

name: Rare Bird Rooftop
description: Rare Bird is the rooftop bar and lounge atop the Noelle Hotel in downtown Nashville, perched on the building's 13th floor with views over the skyline and the Cumberland River. It opened to the public in March 2018, built around a "draft cocktails and uncaged spirits" concept in a colorful, design-forward setting. The bar is walk-in only and runs a daily "Golden Hour" happy-hour menu on weekdays. Alongside its full cocktail program, Rare Bird keeps a small headed zero-proof section it calls Hatchlings, both drinks at $13: The Perch, built on Seedlip Garden with orgeat and lime, and the Blushing Canary, with strawberry, passionfruit, lemon and Topo Chico. The list turns over — the Lemon Julip, N/Aperol Spritz and Daiquiri-Ish that anchored it in 2025 are gone — so treat it as two well-made drinks rather than a menu. It's a scenic, tourist-popular rooftop where a sober guest can still order something composed.

name: Rare Society
description: Rare Society is the retro steakhouse in chef Brad Wise's group, on Park Boulevard in University Heights, and its cocktail card carries a Spirit Free section of four. Three are built drinks: Fountain of Youth on a salted raspberry and chamomile sparkling with grapefruit and soda, Fool's Gold on a non-alcoholic Italian aperitif with lemon and a miso-ginger syrup served over a large cube, and Staycation on a white cane spirit alternative with pineapple, lime, orgeat, cranberry and mint. Best Day Brewing's non-alcoholic kölsch is eight dollars. What distinguishes the section is that it sits on the cocktail card among the classics rather than at the back with the sodas, and that three of its four entries are made to order rather than opened. Dinner runs nightly from five, until nine early in the week and ten on Friday and Saturday, in a room built to look like a mid-century Las Vegas steakhouse.

Everything on offer is 0.0%: Heineken 0.0 on draught alongside Guinness 0.0, Stella 0.0 and craft NA beer from Brulo, plus seven alcohol-free whiskies and AF gin, vodka, tequila and botanical spirits used in the bar's alcohol-free cocktails. name: R&D
description: R&D is a craft cocktail bar in Philadelphia's Fishtown neighborhood, opened in October 2018 in the former Root Restaurant & Wine Bar space at 1206 Frankford Avenue. It's run by Defined Hospitality, the group behind Suraya, Pizzeria Beddia, Condesa, and Kalaya; the cocktail program was built by Aaron Deary and is curated by bar manager Resa Mueller. R&D has won Best of Philly for Best Cocktail Bar. Beyond its acclaimed full bar, R&D maintains a permanent zero-proof presence on its menu, and bartenders also build custom non-alcoholic drinks on request. Mueller refreshes the zero-proof cocktails every few months, leaning on tiki-style builds with fresh juices, coconut, house-made syrups, small-batch sodas, and tannic teas. Named NA drinks have included the Virgin Piña Colada and a negroni-inspired build, plus NA beers from Athletic Brewing and Guinness 0.

name: Realm of the 52 Remedies
description: Realm of the 52 Remedies is a hidden cocktail bar in the Convoy District, themed on an ancient Chinese medical text and reached through an apothecary front. Its signature cocktails are twenty dollars, and every one of them is printed with the same line: available spirit free at fifteen. That makes the whole seasonal list — drinks such as the Sunomono, the Je Ju and Softly Spoken — orderable without alcohol, rather than a separate short section. The bar does not publish a separate ingredient list for those versions, so what arrives is its own rebuild of the drink without the spirit, at a five-dollar discount — worth asking which of the current list the bartenders think survives the swap best. The bar trades nightly from five, to midnight in the week and half past one on Friday and Saturday, and the room is small enough that a reservation is the safer plan.

name: 48 Record Bar
description: 48 Record Bar is a vinyl listening room and cocktail bar that opened in December 2023 on the second floor above Sassafras Bar in Old City, Philadelphia. It was founded by Donal McCoy, owner of Sassafras and the former Tin Angel music venue, with Joey Sweeney. Inspired by Tokyo's audiophile "kissa" bars, the roughly 45-seat room pairs a high-fidelity vinyl sound system with a menu of about 16 cocktails, plus beer and wine. The bar carries a small but genuine named zero-proof lineup alongside its full cocktail list, including the Polyester Dinosaur (pineapple, turmeric-honey syrup, ginger, tajín rim) and a Coconut Matcha Mojito (cream of coconut, lime, matcha), with seasonal additions like a Moroccan mint tea mocktail and a "hot mocklate" with pistachio orgeat. name: Red Feather Lounge
description: Red Feather Lounge on the 8th Street pedestrian block builds its alcohol-free drinks with the same technique as its cocktails, which shows most clearly in Well Orange You Sophisticated — orange vanilla syrup, lime and egg white foam. The foam is the detail worth noticing: it requires a hard shake and adds real time to the build, and it is the first thing most bars quietly drop from a zero-proof order. There is also I Know a Tiki When I See One, a pineapple, almond orgeat, cinnamon and lime build, and Dorothy, made with lavender soda and dry secco. It sits on the pedestrianised 8th Street block and runs to 1:30am on Friday and Saturday, later than almost anything else in this guide.

description: Redemption Bar is country artist Ashley McBryde's NA-forward bar, opened in August 2025 on the fifth floor of Eric Church's Chief's on Lower Broadway in downtown Nashville. Inspired by McBryde's own path to sobriety (she is nearly four years sober), the bar centers an 18-drink zero-proof cocktail menu "composed like a setlist," with each drink named after lyrics that carried her forward — including Flickerin' Flames of Hell, Martini McBryde, Gospel Night, and The Devil I Know. The bar takes its name from McBryde's song "Redemption." Alcohol is also served, since "everyone is welcome." Beyond the drinks, the space features an intimate troubadour-style stage built for solo or duo singer-songwriter sets. Billed by the venue as "Broadway's first NA-focused bar," it offers a sober-friendly alternative on a famously alcohol-soaked strip, with a full food menu alongside the zero-proof and alcoholic lists.

Time Out Singapore singles out Muri 'Passing Clouds' (about S$25) as a standout champagne alternative - floral, honeyed and pleasantly dry - making Republic a rare high-end Singapore bar where a non-drinker can order with the same care as everyone else.

description: One-Michelin-star Mod-Sin restaurant from chef LG Han where the Singapore-heritage tasting menu comes with a genuine non-alcoholic pairing option run course by course. The kitchen's zero-proof anchor is a house sparkling tea pairing that reviewers describe as floral, refreshing and not too sweet, offered as a full alternative to the wine flight rather than an afterthought. The room sits inside Esplanade Mall rather than a hotel or a shophouse, which undersells it: the cooking is a serious, narrative-led reading of Singaporean food, and the tea flight is built to track it course by course.

name: Restaurant Olivia
description: Restaurant Olivia is a pasta-focused Italian restaurant in Denver's Wash Park / South Gaylord neighborhood, opened in January 2020 by chef-proprietor Ty Michael Leon, beverage director and proprietor Austin James Carson and hospitality director and proprietor Heather Morrison. Its handmade pasta and beverage program have earned a place in the Michelin Guide Colorado, a James Beard nomination for Outstanding Hospitality and a 2025 Michelin Service Award. The non-alcoholic offering is a genuine part of the beverage list rather than an afterthought, though it currently runs through bottles and glasses rather than built cocktails: Codorniu Cava "Zero" is poured alcohol-free by the glass, Casa Emma's Zeero Bianco and Zeero Sangiovese carry the non-alcoholic wine section, and three Copenhagen Sparkling Teas are listed by the bottle. Seasonal zero-proof cocktails, including a clarified milk punch, appear on the menu at intervals through the year.

description: A Central West End fixture since 2015, Retreat Gastropub pairs elevated pub fare with one of St. Louis's most respected cocktail programs — and the current menu gives the zero-proof side its own dedicated Non-Alcoholic section. Alongside Giffard-based builds like the Nah-Perol Spritz and the tiki-leaning Jungle Birdie, you'll find a coffee-forward Cold Fashioned, the savory pineapple-and-bell-pepper Hush Pupper, a house shrub and soda, Athletic Brewing and Best Day NA beers, Gruvi's alcohol-free Dry Secco, and a Mighty Kind CBD seltzer. Now owned by longtime staffers Jennifer Anderson and Sydney Caldwell, Retreat serves dinner six nights a week plus a popular Sunday brunch.

name: Retrograde
description: Retrograde is a retro-futuristic cocktail lounge hidden behind the freezer door of Sweet Action Ice Cream on East 19th Avenue in Denver's Uptown. Guests flip a light switch by the door to signal staff, then enter a dim room styled with mid-century furniture, cosmic detailing and cult films projected on the walls. The cocktail list is named after B-movies, and the non-alcoholic list follows the same conceit: the current board, titled "Invasion of the Pod People", carries four built non-alcoholic cocktails rather than a single bartender's-choice option. They are Forbidden Texture (apple custard, toasted sugar, aromatic bitters, aqua faba), Low Orbit (apple, orange, marshmallow), The Thing on the Rocks (American oak tea, pear core, aromatic bitters) and The Day the Juice Stood Still (clarified orange juice, cold pear, lemon, sobacha, soda water). Retrograde is 21+, first-come first-served with no reservations, and caps parties at five.

A named recurring alcohol-free menu is a stronger commitment than a permanent line or two, because it creates an occasion rather than an accommodation: there is a night when not drinking is the point rather than the exception. name: Rhinegeist Brewery
description: Rhinegeist occupies the historic 1895 Christian Moerlein bottling plant in Over-the-Rhine, a soaring brick hall that has anchored Cincinnati's craft-beer revival since 2013. In fall 2025 the brewery brought its beer heritage to the sober-curious with Ghost, a dedicated non-alcoholic line brewed on Sustainable Beverage Technologies' BrewVo nested-fermentation process rather than dealcoholized after the fact. Ghost Pils, an NA German pilsner, took a bronze medal in the Non-Alcoholic Beer category at the 2025 Great American Beer Festival and a silver at the 2026 Craft Beer and Brewing NANA Cup; Ghost Haze pours as a full-flavored NA hazy IPA and is a year-round release in cans and on draft. Both sit at or below 0.5% ABV and sell in 12oz six-packs for taproom pickup and shipping. A West Coast-style Ghost Hops was announced for early 2026 but has not appeared on the brewery's beer list, so the Ghost line stands at two beers. The cavernous taproom pairs cornhole, ping-pong, and rooftop views with a genuinely award-winning zero-proof pour.
signatureDrinks: Ghost Pils (non-alcoholic German pilsner; 2025 GABF bronze, 2026 Craft Beer & Brewing NANA Cup silver)|Ghost Haze (non-alcoholic hazy IPA, year-round, cans and draft)

name: Rhody Roots
description: Rhody Roots on Main Street in Warren keeps a real bank of non-alcoholic spirits and non-alcoholic beers behind the bar — not a token can in the fridge — and will build any cocktail on its list without alcohol. Stocking finished NA spirits and NA beer alongside a make-anything-zero-proof policy puts it among the best-equipped rooms in the state for a non-drinker, twenty minutes down the bay from Providence.

name: Rich Table
description: Rich Table is a Hayes Valley fine-dining mainstay opened in 2012 by married chefs Evan and Sarah Rich, both alumni of acclaimed kitchens, who built a name on market-driven California cooking. Now in its 13th year, it ranked #3 on the San Francisco Chronicle's 2025 Top 100 Bay Area Restaurants and anchors a growing family that includes RT Rotisserie and, as of January 2026, RT Bistro. Its drink program treats non-alcoholic guests as first-class: the current list carries dedicated "Non-Alcoholic Refreshers" and "Non-Alcoholic Milk Wash" sections of house cocktails built on NA spirits and house ingredients, alongside a non-alcoholic beer from nearby Best Day Brewing of Sausalito. Named zero-proof pours — like The Remedy (NA agave spirit, pineapple, carrot, ginger, lemon, bitters), the Strawberry Fauxgroni, and Pod Culture — rotate with the seasons, mirroring the same farm-driven philosophy as the food.
signatureDrinks: The Remedy|Strawberry Fauxgroni|Pod Culture

name: Rigo
description: Rigo is a Spanish-Italian restaurant on Kapahulu Avenue, serving tapas, wood-fired pizzas, house-made pastas and grill plates. It trades as Rigo, not Rigo's — older coverage uses the possessive, and the current name does not. Its documented non-alcoholic drink is That Cucumber Thing, built from cucumber, mint, lime and soda: a dry, herbaceous, low-sugar build of the kind that is much rarer on Honolulu menus than the tropical-fruit default, and one that works with salty Mediterranean food in a way a pineapple drink does not. The restaurant sits on the Kapahulu strip between Waikīkī and Kaimukī, a few minutes from Da Cove.
signatureDrinks: That Cucumber Thing (cucumber, mint, lime, soda)

name: Ripple Wine Bar
description: Ripple Wine Bar's O'Bryonville outpost is a wine-focused room that treats non-drinkers as real guests rather than an afterthought. Alongside 40-plus wines by the glass, the bar pours Leitz non-alcoholic sparkling riesling and rosé — a genuine dealcoholized wine, not grape juice — plus rotating alcohol-free beer and wines. Two standing house mocktails round out the zero-proof list: the Ginger Garcia (ginger beer, apple, lime, soda) and the Althea (strawberry, pineapple, lemon, soda), both built to pair with charcuterie boards and flatbreads. It's the same menu run at the original Covington, KY location. Founded by Matt and Kathleen Haws in 2019, Ripple earned a spot on Wine Spectator's 2025 "Editors' Favorite Wine Bars" list, making it a comfortable, elevated place to order without the buzz.
signatureDrinks: Ginger Garcia (ginger beer, apple, lime, soda)|Althea (strawberry, pineapple, lemon, soda)|Leitz Non-Alcoholic Sparkling Riesling|Leitz Non-Alcoholic Sparkling Rosé

name: Rita's Seaside Grille
description: Hall family beachfront grille at the foot of Center Street near the Folly Beach Pier, run by the same group behind Halls Chophouse in Charleston. The kitchen serves scratch-made American fare, house-smoked barbecue, and coastal seafood. Its drink menu carries a small set of named mocktails priced at $7 alongside freshly brewed iced tea, sodas, frozen Jarritos, and cold brew coffee.

name: Ritual
description: Ritual, the late-night cocktail lounge that took over the former Alice space in Bryan Place in January 2026, gives non-drinkers a dedicated "Elixirs" section rather than a token Shirley Temple — four spirit-free cocktails built with the same intent as the full bar. The Elixirs were developed alongside the alcoholic list by Paul Ramon, named a Top 50 World Class U.S. Bartender in 2022, so they get the same modern-texture treatment (matcha cold foams, spiced infusions) as their spirited counterparts. The operating team frames the non-alcoholic program as a deliberate effort at "intentionality and inclusivity," not an afterthought.

name: Ritual Kava Lounge
address: 11127 N Dale Mabry Hwy, Tampa, FL 33618
description: Ritual is an alcohol-free kava lounge on North Dale Mabry in Carrollwood, open 10am to 1am every day, and it is programmed harder than most rooms in the category: silent discos, bingo nights and ping-pong tournaments run alongside the drinks. Seating is split between bean bags and bar stools, which suits both the study crowd in the afternoon and the social crowd at night, and the hosts, Dylan and Gloria, are the thing regulars mention first. The list covers kava, teas and coffee. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: kratom is served here alongside the kava. It acts on opioid receptors and carries real dependence and withdrawal risk, unlike kava, so it is worth asking which is in your cup.

name: River Club
hours: Mon-Tue 5pm-10pm; Wed 12am-10pm; Thu 5pm-10pm; Fri 5pm-11pm; Sat 11am-11pm; Sun 11am-10pm
description: River Club is a Mediterranean-coastal restaurant and bar on the Georgetown waterfront at 3000 K Street NW, serving mezze-style shareable plates drawn from Lebanon, Italy and Spain, with patio seating over the Potomac. It trades seven days with lunch, weekend brunch, dinner and a weekday happy hour. The drinks programme is notable for a dedicated zero-proof section, headed 0% Booze, whose cocktails mirror the food: a 0% Lemon Basil on basil-infused Seedlip Grove 42 with lemon, celery and celery salt; a 0% Sumac 75 on Freixenet alcohol-removed sparkling with sumac syrup, lemon and mint; and a 0% Farid Has to Drive with cucumber-and-fennel shrub and chinotto soda, all $15. Brunch adds 0% Aperol and Hugo spritzes on Undone. Peroni 0.0 is $9.

name: Ro Sham Beaux
description: Ro Sham Beaux is one of three Sacramento bars run by the Irish Hospitality Group, and all of them stock the same useful pair: the St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, a bottled non-alcoholic frizzante that is among the best ready-to-drink zero-proof products made, and Guinness 0. A group standardising its alcohol-free stock across venues is quietly valuable — it means you can walk into any of the three without checking first, which removes the research that usually precedes a night out for someone not drinking. Ro Sham Beaux is the Midtown J Street location, open from 2pm most days and noon at weekends.
signatureDrinks: Phony Negroni by St. Agrestis|Guinness 0

name: ROAM by San Chez
address: 250 Monroe Ave NW, Grand Rapids, MI 49503
hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 11am-8:30pm; Fri-Sat 11am-10pm; Sun closed
description: ROAM by San Chez is a downtown restaurant at 250 Monroe Avenue NW from the family behind San Chez, the long-running Grand Rapids tapas house. It keeps what Experience Grand Rapids calls an extensive non-alcoholic drink menu, and the range is broader than most: hot teas and house drip coffees at one end, horchata and rotating house-made Italian cream sodas in the middle, and composed zero-proof drinks such as the Rosemary-Elderflower Spritzer — herbal syrup, lemon, soda and butterfly pea tea — at the other. The kitchen team has said publicly that it is glad to see the city offering more alcohol-free options in order to be more inclusive, which reads as a statement of intent rather than a marketing line.
signatureDrinks: Rosemary-Elderflower Spritzer (herbal syrup, lemon, soda, butterfly pea tea)|Horchata|House Italian cream sodas (rotating flavours)

name: Rob Roy
description: Rob Roy is a Belltown cocktail bar at 2332 2nd Avenue, open since 2009 and owned by Anu Apte, who runs it with Chris Elford under their Canoe Ventures group alongside Navy Strength and Vinnie's Wine Shop. Rob Roy was a James Beard finalist for Outstanding Bar in 2023, and Apte herself was a James Beard semifinalist for Outstanding Professional in Cocktail Service in both 2025 and 2026. It was the first bar in Washington State to run its own ice programme. Its non-alcoholic drinks get a full printed section headed "Designated Drivers", six deep at $16–$17 and all marked 0% ABV: Silver Rush (Seedlip Spice 94, verjus, lemon, Giffard jasmine, salted honey), Cornucopia (Seedlip Notas de Agave, non-alcoholic Lucano amaro, Pathfinder, clarified in coconut), Ace of Cups (Three Spirits Livener, winter melon, Thai basil, ginseng), and three botanical elixirs — The Mood, Pick Me Up and Dream Maker. Bitburger Drive is $6. Note that three of those drinks use mood-active botanicals; see the full description. 21+ only.
signatureDrinks: Silver Rush ($16)|Cornucopia ($17)|Ace of Cups ($16)|The Mood ($17)|Bitburger Drive 0% ($6)

name: Rochambeau
description: Rochambeau is a French brasserie on Boylston Street in Back Bay, steps from Copley Square, with a street-level bar and a large dining room running from morning through late service. Its drinks list keeps a named non-alcoholic section rather than a token substitute, and the builds use real zero-proof products rather than juice. Red Lace is made with Tilden Lacewing, strawberry Persian rose, honey and egg white; Blueberries for Sal uses CleanCo non-alcoholic tequila with blueberry, mint, lime, orgeat and soda; the N/A Hugo Spritz is built on Giffard's alcohol-free elderflower with lime, mint and alcohol-free sparkling; and the Spritz Del Conte is an Italian-style alcohol-free spritz. The kitchen and bar also keep additional non-alcoholic wine, beer and spirits available on request.

name: Roll Up Herbal Bar
description: Roll Up Herbal Bar is a dedicated zero-proof cocktail lounge beside the Gateway to the Smokies arch on Main Street in downtown Waynesville, about thirty miles west of Asheville. It serves mocktails exclusively, crafted with herbal infusions and house-made mixes and designed to either calm or energise. Its owner, Sam, is unusually clear about why it exists: she started it for one reason, to provide culinary beverages for people who are not drinking alcohol but crave the complexity of a well-crafted cocktail. She is an experienced bartender, and also an artist and a former theatre kid, which she says is why the drinks are built to look as good as they taste. The room is a small oasis — comfortable seating, magical décor, and a patio shaded by tall oaks — and it is a sit-down tasting lounge rather than a pop-up, typically open Thursday to Saturday from noon. It anchors the alcohol-free scene at that end of the region.

name: Roosevelt's
description: Roosevelt's is a Cherry Street bar and restaurant in Tulsa, open 11am to 10pm through the week, to midnight on Friday and Saturday and from 10am at weekends — the widest hours of any venue in this city guide. Its alcohol-free drink is The Red Keep, built on blood orange, lemon, jalapeño and ginger beer: two sources of heat against citrus, which is a savoury rather than sweet approach and works alongside food. Being open from mid-morning to late seven days a week makes it the fallback when the evening-only rooms are shut. It shares Cherry Street with Nola's, which has the better zero-proof programme but keeps a narrower kitchen.
signatureDrinks: The Red Keep — blood orange, lemon, jalapeño, ginger beer

name: Root Awakening Kava Bar
description: Root Awakening opened in 2022 as New England's first kava bar and serves no alcohol at all. Owner Gregory Gately started it after losing his brother to alcohol, and built something that runs like a bar rather than a tea room: open to midnight on weeknights and 1am at weekends, with kava from Fiji, Vanuatu and elsewhere in the South Pacific, kava lattes, kava mocktails and kombucha on tap. The week is programmed the way a neighbourhood pub programmes it — movie night, ladies' night, trivia, a darts tournament, karaoke — with a games lounge and a free arcade cabinet. Kava contains no alcohol but is psychoactive and mildly sedating, and is not FDA-regulated.
signatureDrinks: Give Me Samoa ($13)|Kavarita ($12)|Kava Kolada ($12)|Chocolatta ($11)|Cold Brew Kava Latte ($12)

name: Root City Kava Bar & Lounge
description: Root City Kava Bar & Lounge bills itself as Maryland's first and only dedicated kava bar, a completely alcohol-free botanical lounge in a three-story historic building on Mount Vernon's Cathedral Street. Under new ownership, it serves traditional kava — your first shell is free — alongside kratom, teas, and botanical mocktails built on functional mushrooms, adaptogens, and herbal blends. The ground floor runs as a kava cafe, with a lounge for live music and events above it and a retro arcade gaming room on the top floor. It keeps genuine late-night hours, open until 2 a.m. Tuesday through Saturday, and fills the calendar with trivia, open mics, comedy, and wellness nights — all, as the bar puts it, powered by plants, not booze.

name: Root of Happiness Kava Bar | Davis
description: The Davis branch of Root of Happiness sits on F Street in the downtown grid, minutes from the UC Davis campus, and runs 11am to 1am seven days a week — a rare late alcohol-free option in a university town where the alternative is a bar crowd. Root of Happiness has traded since 2006 and describes itself as the original California kava bar, now six rooms across Northern California; two of them, in Midtown Sacramento and Rancho Cordova, are already listed here. The group's focus from the start has been sourcing: identifying exceptional kava from across the Pacific and building reliable ways to evaluate its quality. No alcohol is served, and no kratom appears on the published menu.

name: Root of Happiness Kava Bar | Roseville
description: The Roseville branch of Root of Happiness sits on Vernon Street in the middle of the town's revitalised downtown, and like the rest of the group it runs 11am to 1am every day of the week with no alcohol served. It covers the Placer County side of the Sacramento metro — Roseville, Rocklin and Granite Bay — where dedicated alcohol-free rooms are otherwise absent entirely. The group has traded since 2006, calls itself the original California kava bar, and built its reputation on sourcing exceptional kava from across the Pacific and evaluating it systematically. No kratom appears on the published menu, which sets it apart from most American kava operators.

name: Root of Happiness Kava Bar | Midtown
description: Root of Happiness Kava Bar's Midtown room opened in March 2023 in a warehouse space on the R Street Corridor, the newest of four Northern California locations run by Travis Lowin and Tyler Blythe, who started the company in Rancho Cordova around 2013. Nothing alcoholic is served. The bar prepares noble kava only, ground fresh and hand-prepared each day from fresh-frozen root sourced in Hawaii, Fiji and the company's own American farms, and serves it traditionally in shells alongside a house specialty coffee programme built on its Bula Blend and a list of functional botanical drinks and iced tonic pours. Kava is a psychoactive root drink from the South Pacific — alcohol-free, but sedating and intoxicating in its own right, which is why the bar serves it only to guests 18 and over with ID while keeping the coffee and botanical menu open to all ages. The room runs daily from 11am to 1am, with spray-painted street art across the walls, pink neon over the bar and regular live music.

name: Root of Happiness Kava Bar | Rancho Cordova
description: The Rancho Cordova room is where Root of Happiness began: Travis Lowin and Tyler Blythe opened it around 2013, which puts it ahead of the first kava bars in Berkeley and New York and makes it one of the older continuously operating kava bars in the continental United States. It is fully alcohol-free. The kava is noble root only, ground fresh and hand-prepared daily from fresh-frozen root sourced in Hawaii, Fiji and the company's own American farms, served traditionally in shells, with a specialty coffee list built on the house Bula Blend and a range of functional botanical drinks alongside. Kava is a psychoactive South Pacific root drink — no alcohol, but genuinely sedating — so the bar restricts it to guests 18 and over with ID while keeping coffee and botanicals open to all ages. Fifteen miles east of downtown Sacramento, it serves a suburban regular crowd rather than a night-out one, and runs 11am to 1am daily.
signatureDrinks: Traditional kava shell (noble root, ground fresh and hand-prepared)|Bula Blend specialty coffee|Functional botanical tonic pours

name: Rooted In Sanity Kava Lounge
description: Rooted In Sanity is Madison's first and only kava lounge, tucked at the back of the SolEscape Healing Arts Building on Williamson Street — lower level, down the ramp, following a painted teal line. Nothing served contains alcohol. It pours traditional kava by the shell alongside housemade mocktails, locally made teas and a full craft coffee menu, and furnishes the room for staying rather than drinking up: swinging chairs, couches and board games at the tables. It runs evening hours to 10pm most nights and 11pm at weekends, which makes it one of the very few genuinely alcohol-free rooms in Madison that is open when the bars are. Kava contains no alcohol but is psychoactive and mildly sedating.

name: Roots And Leaves: Mile High Kava Bar
description: Mile High Kava is the Westminster branch of the Roots & Leaves group, on the northwest edge of the Denver metro. The venue describes itself as "a unique 18+ non-alcoholic tea and kava bar experience, perfect for those who prefer to socialize without alcohol", and it is programmed like a bar rather than a tea room: a stage for open-mic nights and karaoke, two pool tables, Skee-Ball, darts, couches and a full-size bar. It also has a kid-friendly area with toys, and hookah is available. Drinks are house-brewed kava and a range of traditional and ethnobotanical teas, both psychoactive plant preparations rather than soft drinks. Happy hours run three times a day, including a late slot from 10pm to midnight.

name: Roots and Leaves: Peak Kava
description: Peak Kava is the Lakewood branch of Roots & Leaves, a seven-strong kava bar group operating across Colorado and New Mexico. The venue states its position without hedging: "Peak Kava is a non-alcoholic bar dedicated to nurturing social connections without alcohol", and the group markets itself under the line "join the sober shift". It is fitted out as a bar rather than a cafe — two pool tables, giant Jenga, a multicade, a fireplace, bar seating and lounge seating — and runs happy hours from 5pm to 7pm and again from 10pm to midnight. The drinks are kava and ethnobotanical teas, both psychoactive: the house tea blends include blue lotus, California poppy, wild lettuce and white willow, and the kava is served traditionally by the shell or CO2-extracted.

name: Roots and Leaves: Tanoan Kava
description: Tanoan Kava is the Albuquerque room of Roots & Leaves, a six-site group across Colorado and New Mexico whose Denver-area bars — Peak Kava in Lakewood and Mile High Kava in Westminster — are already listed here. The group describes itself as a sober kava bar and a social space that does not revolve around alcohol, and this room runs 10am to midnight every day of the week on 12th Street NW in the Near North Valley. The drinks are handcrafted kava and a range of botanical teas. It joins Luna's Kava Root downtown and Gaia's Kava Root on Central as the third dedicated kava room in Albuquerque, and it is the only one belonging to a multi-state group.

name: Rorschach Brewing Co.
neighborhood: Leslieville (South Riverdale, near the border of The Beaches)
address: 1001 Eastern Ave, Toronto, ON M4L 1A8, Canada
description: Rorschach Brewing Co. is a craft brewery and taproom on Eastern Avenue in Leslieville, near the border of The Beaches, with its own on-site kitchen. It brews its non-alcoholic beer in-house under the sub-brand Free Spirit, whose flagship Adventure IPA is sold on tap and in cans right alongside Rorschach's regular lineup rather than as an afterthought. The 0.5% ABV IPA is brewed with oats, wheat and Galaxy hops, and packaged to go in 355ml cans ($2.45) or 6-packs ($13.70) at the taproom.

name: Rosa Sky Rooftop
description: Rosa Sky is a rooftop bar and lounge on the 22nd floor of the dual-brand AC & Element Hotel Miami Downtown in Brickell, opened in 2022. Known for panoramic skyline views, globally inspired tapas, DJ-driven nights, and a popular Sunday Soirée bottomless brunch, it pairs handcrafted cocktails with a compact but genuine zero-proof section. The non-alcoholic lineup is built on Ritual Zero Proof spirit alternatives and Giffard syrups: Feeling Frisky (Ritual Whiskey Alternative, Giffard ginger, lemon), Rooftop Retreat (Ritual Tequila Alternative, Giffard pineapple, basil, coconut water, citrus), and Pom Pom (Ritual Gin Alternative, pomegranate, vanilla, citrus). The Pom Pom also appears as a zero-proof pour during the bottomless brunch. It's a full-service rooftop rather than a dedicated NA venue, but the named mocktails are real and ingredient-specific.

name: Rosalie Italian Soul
description: Rosalie Italian Soul is chef Chris Cosentino's Italian-American restaurant inside Downtown Houston's C. Baldwin Hotel, and its printed drink menu carries a standing Mocktails section built on Ritual Zero Proof spirit alternatives. The list runs a Ritual Margarita, a Ritual Espresso Martini, and a non-alcoholic Jungle Bird, each printed with full ingredients right alongside the restaurant's cocktail list rather than as an afterthought. A fourth mocktail, The Black Tie, appears under a repeated "Rosalie Mocktails" heading.

name: Rosemary's Wynwood
description: Rosemary's Wynwood is the Miami outpost of Carlos Suarez's beloved West Village Italian restaurant (Casa Nela group), which opened in New York in 2012; the Wynwood location debuted February 7, 2025 in a converted former shoe warehouse. Executive chef Craig Giunta (previously Mother Wolf, Macchialina) leads a seasonal menu of housemade pastas, antipasti, and seafood. A defining feature is the 3,500-square-foot indoor-outdoor space — nearly a third of it a living garden grown with Little River Cooperative, supplying herbs and produce used across the kitchen and bar. The beverage program runs an Italian spritz-forward cocktail list alongside a named zero-proof section: a Ghia Sour (Ghia aperitivo, lemon, egg white), a Hugo Fizz (elderflower cordial, Athletic Brewing Upside Dawn, club soda, mint, lime), and a Non #1 Bollicine Rosato, plus an Athletic Brewing Upside Dawn NA lager. Non-drinkers get composed, named options rather than an afterthought.

name: Rosette
description: Rosette is a small worker-owned bar and restaurant at 9262 57th Avenue S in Rainier Beach, opened in 2025 by members of the collective behind Jude's Old Town, Seattle's first worker-owned bar and restaurant, two doors down. It focuses on non-alcoholic cocktails, natural and biodynamic wine and small bites, and the room is petite — a rectangular space just under eleven feet wide. Worker-owner Mark Paschal's reason for building it is the clearest statement of the case we have found: for too long, people who don't drink alcohol have been treated as an afterthought in bar spaces, and at Rosette thoughtfully constructed non-alcoholic cocktails are meant to shine and offer a true bar experience without alcohol. The N/A Cocktails list is flat $15: In Bloom (Figlia Fiore, Lumette Bright Light, lemon, rose blossom, Woody's non-alcoholic sparkling), Minimal Intervention (DHOS vodka, lemon, strawberry-mint), Refined Prop Comic (Lumette LumRum, Ghia, lemon, orange-carrot) and Spirited Away (Free Spirits bourbon, Pathfinder, vermouth, bitters). PLEASE NOTE: a fifth, Pine for the Days, contains KAVA — a mildly sedative plant — under the same non-alcoholic heading. Happy hour 3–6pm; open Wednesday to Saturday.

name: Royal Kumete Kava Lounge
description: Royal Kumete is a Polynesian-owned and operated kava lounge on South Broadway, just north of Evans, and it is the only venue in the Denver metro that frames itself first as a cultural room and second as an alcohol alternative. The house line — where tradition meets tranquility — describes a programme built on the traditional serving of kava with a modern presentation, named for the kumete, the carved wooden bowl kava is prepared and shared from across the South Pacific. It is an evening venue rather than a café, opening at 5pm and running late, in a stretch of South Broadway otherwise given over to tattoo shops, vintage stores and bars. Kava is served; the lounge does not serve alcohol.

name: Royal Sushi & Izakaya
hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 5pm-10pm; Fri-Sat 5pm-11pm; Sun closed
description: Royal Sushi & Izakaya in Queen Village runs a front-of-house izakaya and a twelve-seat omakase counter behind it, and chef-owner Jesse Ito is himself sober — which shows in how the non-alcoholic side is handled. The Yuzu Spritz builds yuzu and lime with plum bitters and soda; the Ginger Mint Smash runs mint and a ginger syrup with lime. Beyond the house builds the fridge is unusually well chosen: Athletic's Upside Dawn at 0.5%, Leitz Eins Zwei Zero sparkling Riesling as a genuine alternative to sake or wine with the food, and Kimino sodas made with Japanese fruit. For a sushi restaurant, having a proper non-alcoholic pairing rather than green tea is the whole point.

name: RSVP Discount Beverage
description: RSVP on Forest Avenue is Portland's serious beverage store, and its non-alcoholic section has grown into the best place in the city to actually buy this category — alcohol-free beers by the shelf, mocktail-ready mixers, sparkling tonics and zero-proof bottles, alongside the beer and wine selection that made its reputation. It is not a dedicated dry shop, and that is worth saying plainly, but with Vena's now a weekday-only operation twenty minutes away in Westbrook, RSVP is the practical answer for anyone in Portland who wants to stock a fridge on a Sunday afternoon. It is a conventional beverage store with a strong alcohol-free section rather than a dedicated dry shop, which is worth knowing in advance.

description: Runner Up is a hidden rooftop bar and garden tucked above the Collingwood Yards creative precinct, reached via a small terrace and elevator off Johnston St. Alongside its cocktails it keeps a genuine no/low line-up: Heaps Normal XPA 0% and Drivers Non-Alc Lager on tap-style pours, NON7 Stewed Cherry & Coffee, a Lyre's Italian non-alcoholic spritz, and a rotating set of house mocktails. description: Søbr Market is a fully non-alcoholic bottle shop and tasting bar on the lower level of Wellington Market, the food hall inside The Well, in Toronto's King West/Fashion District. The Toronto location relocated here at the end of 2025 after opening on Richmond Street, and functions as a retail shop rather than a full bar - every bottle, can, and pour on the shelves is zero-proof. Shoppers can still sit at the in-store tasting bar to sample spirits and de-alcoholized wines before buying, including brands like Lyre's, Ghia, Free Spirits, and Dr. Zero Zero.

name: Saba
address: 5757 Magazine St, Suite A, New Orleans, LA 70115
hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed-Thu 5pm-8pm; Fri 11am-9pm; Sat 10:30am-9pm; Sun 10:30am-2:30pm & 5pm-8pm
description: Saba is chef Alon Shaya's modern Israeli restaurant on Magazine Street in Uptown New Orleans, the flagship of his Pomegranate Hospitality group (the name means "grandfather" in Hebrew). Known for blistered wood-fired pita baked steps from the table, it opened in 2018 and earned a 2025 Michelin Bib Gourmand. IMPORTANT CORRECTION: Saba's gazoz — the sparkling Israeli soda it is best known for — is served alcoholic on the current menu. All three seasonal builds are $18 and contain spirits: strawberry lemon with bourbon, cucumber agave with tequila, and pineapple shrub with white rum. Do not order a gazoz assuming it is zero-proof. The genuinely non-alcoholic offering is narrower: Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn ($6) is the only NA beer, and there is a carefully built coffee and tea list with Moroccan mint tea and a seasonal herbal tea ($10 each), an iced halva latte ($8), cold brew ($6) and a pot of coffee for two ($8). Dinner Wednesday to Sunday, brunch Friday to Sunday.

name: Sacred Springs Kombucha
address: 1059 Wealthy St SE, Grand Rapids, MI 49506
description: Sacred Springs is an urban kombucha micro-taproom at 1059 Wealthy Street SE, opened in December 2018 by Joel Andrus and Geoff Lamden after several years of brewing without a permanent home. Twelve rotating taps pour house kombucha, with bottles and howlettes to take away and a short food menu built on bagel sandwiches from Grand Rapids Bagel. Named brews include Root of Life, made with beets, ginger and turmeric; Flower of Life, with jasmine, elderberries and hibiscus; Thursday Knight, a chamomile lavender; Trop Hopics, a pineapple and hops build; and The Grapeful Harvest, made with concord grape. Note that the taproom also serves hard kombucha and mead, so it is not an alcohol-free room.

name: The Sacred Vortex Teahouse & Kombuchery
description: The Sacred Vortex is an alcohol-free teahouse, kombuchery and kava bar on Lorain Avenue in Ohio City. David Kovatch and his wife Julie Moran took the building that Platform Beer Co. had used as its original Ohio City taproom — one of the addresses that defined Cleveland's craft beer boom — and reopened it in late summer 2024 as a room where nothing served contains alcohol; the symbolism was not lost on anyone locally. Kovatch already ran Sacred Waters in Lakewood, Ohio's first kava bar, and this is the larger, more ambitious expression of the same idea, with a lengthy bar, soft seating, communal high-tops and a substantial patio. It serves kava by strain, kombucha brewed on site, botanical sodas, adaptogen drinks, tea and coffee, plus named alcohol-free mixed drinks, and runs to 2am most nights. Cleveland Scene readers voted it Best Alcohol-Free Bar in 2025 and 2026. Kava and kratom-based drinks are part of the menu.
