name: Sacred Waters Kava Bar
description: Sacred Waters is an alcohol-free ethnobotanical bar on Detroit Avenue in Lakewood, and the room that started Northeast Ohio's kava scene. David Kovatch opened it in 2022 as Ohio's first kava bar, with Mike Young and three further partners, after encountering kava while travelling and coming home to look for a space; it traded earlier as Muddy Waters Kava Bar, which is how some older listings still refer to it. Kovatch has been sober for more than a decade. It pours kava by the shell and by origin — Vanuatu, Tonga, Solomon Isle — alongside cold-brew kava lattes, spritzers, a kava mule, responsibly sourced botanical teas and coffee, and stays open to midnight or 1am seven nights a week. NOTE: it also serves kratom, kanna and blue lotus — psychoactive botanicals rather than alcohol substitutes, and worth knowing before you go.

name: Sadie's
description: Sadie's is a modern Mediterranean-American restaurant in Nashville's Edgehill Village, opened in September 2021 in the former Taco Mamacita space on the corner of Villa Place. It belongs to Red Pebbles Hospitality, the local group led by Howard Greenstone and Ken Levitan that also runs Adele's, The 404 Kitchen and Shep's Delicatessen, and the kitchen is mezze-driven and share-focused with vegetarian and gluten-free options throughout. For non-drinkers, Sadie's keeps a dedicated "Mocktails" section priced flat at $8 and built from fresh purées, citrus and house sodas rather than bought-in zero-proof spirits: Pathos (passionfruit, lime, hibiscus ginger beer), Pineapple Express (mint, almond orgeat, lime, pineapple soda) and Guava Ginger (guava purée, ginger, lime, guava soda). The list rotates — a Blueberry Butterfly and, more recently, a Strawberry Lemonade have both come and gone. Two non-alcoholic beers, Athletic Lite and an Untitled Art juicy IPA, round out the options, and mocktail specials are part of the weekday happy hour.

name: Sago House
description: Sago House is a Duxton Hill speakeasy from three industry veterans whose weekly-rotating, market-driven menu of six classic cocktail styles always leaves room for a genuine non-alcoholic build. Its most talked-about zero-proof drink is the Yo Soy Elotes, a mocktail inspired by Mexican street corn (elote) that tastes uncannily of warm, buttered popcorn. Because the drinks list is rebuilt each week from whatever the team finds in local markets, the specific alcohol-free option changes, but a mocktail is a standing part of the offer rather than an afterthought. Co-founder Desiree Jane Silva has said the bar was never about making the best drinks so much as being friendly and approachable, which is exactly the quality a non-drinker is looking for.

name: Saint Arnold Brewing Company
description: Saint Arnold Brewing Company, Texas' oldest craft brewery, backs its beer list with a genuine house-made non-alcoholic line at its Beer Garden & Restaurant: Hop Spring alcohol-free hoppy sparkling water, cane-sugar Root Beer, and Ginger Beer, called out in their own dedicated 'Non-Alcoholic' menu section. Hop Spring is brewed from just carbonated water, hops (Citra and Amarillo), and phosphoric acid — zero calories, zero ABV — and began life as taproom-only 'Hop2O' in 2018 before its 2023 relaunch, and it's now canned for Houston-area grocery and liquor stores. It's a full-alcohol production brewery and restaurant rather than an alcohol-free bar, but non-drinkers get real, dedicated products instead of a soda-gun afterthought.

description: Saint Eve's is a small, intimate cocktail bar on 12th Street in Park Slope, shortlisted at the inaugural NYC's Best Bars for NA Awards. It is deliberately tiny — the bar states it cannot take parties of six or more — which makes it the opposite of a destination and rather good as a place to sit and talk. It serves alcohol and does not publish a named non-alcoholic list, so the zero-proof drinking here rests on the bartender rather than on a printed menu; ask, and expect something built rather than poured. Open 5pm until close, seven nights. Mockingbird, South Brooklyn's dedicated alcohol-free bar, is a short walk away for anyone who wants a room with no alcohol in it.

name: Saint-Germain
address: 3054 St Claude Ave, New Orleans, LA 70117

description: Saint-Germain opened in 2018 in a Bywater double-shotgun house on St. Claude Avenue (the former Sugar Park pizza spot), founded by Drew DeLaughter, Trey Smith, and Blake Aguillard. It began as a French wine bar and small bistro and has since evolved into an intimate, multi-course tasting-menu destination, earning one Michelin star in 2025. The dining room runs by reservation a few nights a week, with an adjoining wine bar that takes walk-ins. The beverage program leans on natural wine, and the kitchen offers a curated, daily-changing mocktail menu built to complement the savory courses for guests who aren't drinking — a rotating zero-proof pairing rather than a fixed named list. It's one of the few Michelin-recognized New Orleans rooms that takes a non-alcoholic pairing seriously.

name: Sally O's
description: Sally O's is a corner bar at 3531 Gough Street in Highlandtown from chef Jesse Sandlin, a Top Chef alum who took over the longtime home of The Laughing Pint after it closed in autumn 2019 and named the place for her grandmother, Mildred O'Dethal, known as Sally O. The kitchen cooks from scratch, including its own ice cream, and Baltimore Magazine singled out a Crabonara that mixes blue crab into the pasta in place of pancetta. Its printed "Spirit Free" section runs three built drinks at $10 each: Szechuan Blush (Ritual zero-proof gin, rosemary-szechuan-cranberry syrup, lime), a Pathfinder Old Fashioned (Pathfinder NA amaro, marshmallow syrup, orange twist) and a Zero Proof Spritz (Mionetto NA bubbles, Mionetto NA aperitivo, soda). Athletic's Free Wave and Lite are $5, a non-alcoholic Guinness is $8 and a Mionetto alcohol-removed sparkling is $10. Dinner runs Monday to Saturday from 5pm with a late-night menu Thursday through Saturday. Sandlin also owns The Dive in Canton.

name: Saltbrush
description: Saltbrush on Grove Street keeps two named alcohol-free drinks whose names tell you what kind of bar it is: Queen of the Meadow — an old country name for meadowsweet, a bitter herb historically used in brewing — and Quivering Quinine, which points straight at tonic's defining bitterness. Both names advertise bitterness rather than fruit, which is unusual on a zero-proof list and a reliable signal that the kitchen is thinking about balance rather than sweetness. It sits a few doors from Tavolàta on the same block. Some local guides give a 6th Street address; the Grove Street address is the one recorded here — worth confirming before a trip. Closed Sundays.

name: SAMU Matcha House
description: SAMU is a fully alcohol-free Japanese matcha house and cellar door on Johnston Street in Collingwood, built entirely around stone-milled ceremonial matcha shipped direct from Japan. The room pours drink-in and takeaway matcha Thursday to Sunday and runs formal, appointment-only tea meditations led by a trained Chanoyu (Japanese tea ceremony) practitioner. There is no bar and no zero-proof cocktail list here, just single-origin tea as the entire ritual, which makes it one of Melbourne's clearest sober third-spaces. Samu is a Japanese matcha house on Johnston Street in Collingwood, milling its own stone-ground matcha from Kyoto and Kagoshima leaf and running formal, by-appointment tea meditations alongside its cellar door.

description: San Simón is a moody, candlelit bar tucked down Tin Pan Alley in downtown Bend, the sort of room built for a slow evening, and its zero-proof options are made to hold their own against the cocktail list rather than sit below it. Open daily from 3pm until midnight — the latest consistent hours of any bar in this guide.

name: Sana'a Cafe (Drumm Street)
description: Sana'a Cafe's Drumm Street location opened in 2026 in a former Starbucks unit near the Embarcadero, and trades 7am to 10pm every day of the week. It is entirely alcohol-free, and the Bay Area Telegraph singled the fifteen-hour trading day out as the point of the place, describing it as a genuine evening destination rather than a morning latte stop. The menu combines familiar cafe orders with Yemeni specialities: pistachio, rose and Yemeni lattes, qishr made from the dried husks of coffee cherries, Adeni chai, Arabic light roast coffee and mofawar, with honeycomb pastries, baklava, milk cakes and savoury turnovers from the counter. For Financial District workers it is one of very few post-work rooms that is not a bar.

description: Sana'a Cafe is an alcohol-free Yemeni coffeehouse at New Montgomery and Howard, named after the Yemeni capital and open from 6:30am to 10pm on weekdays and 8am to 10pm at weekends. CBS News Bay Area profiled it in April 2024, with manager Sam Mardaei explaining that the team's aim was to bring Yemeni culture to the city. The list runs to signature Adeni chai, Sana'ani coffee, qishr brewed from dried coffee cherry husks, mofawar and Spanish lattes, alongside pistachio and rose lattes and a pastry counter of saffron milk cake, Biscoff desserts, baklava and honeycomb bread. The room seats a steady evening crowd of downtown workers and students well after the surrounding coffee counters have closed.

name: Sandfish Sushi & Whiskey
description: A modern sushi-and-whiskey restaurant on 7th Avenue in the Melrose District of Phoenix, with a deeper non-alcoholic list than the format suggests. Several zero-proof drinks are built on Seedlip rather than juice: the Virgin Garden pairs Seedlip Garden with lemon, muddled cucumber and soda, and the Nordic Brace sets Seedlip Garden against hibiscus, lemon and a jalapeno-ginger note. The pairing logic is sound — the herbaceous, low-sugar register of a Seedlip Garden build sits alongside raw fish far better than the sweet mocktails most sushi restaurants default to. Open daily from 4:30pm in a neighbourhood worth arriving early for; the whiskey list remains the house identity.

name: Sans Bar
description: Founded in 2017 by Chris Marshall, Sans Bar is widely regarded as one of the first dedicated non-alcoholic bars in North America. Located one block south of the Texas Capitol, the downtown space is the cornerstone of Marshall's mission to create alcohol-free spaces that don't feel like substitutes. Marshall, a substance-use counselor since 2009 and sober since 2007, has been featured in The New York Times, Men's Health, USA Today, and has spoken at the Aspen Ideas Festival. Bar Manager Valentina, who joined in November 2022, overhauled the menu and now consults with bars and restaurants worldwide on their non-alcoholic programs. Beyond the bar itself, the Sans Bar Academy has helped launch over 40 alcohol-free bars and bottle shops across the United States, Canada, and Australia. The room hosts live music most Fridays at 8pm and rotating wellness collaborations through a partnership with Swift Fit Events.

name: Sasha's Wine Bar on DeMun
description: A DeMun-neighborhood fixture for more than two decades, Sasha's Wine Bar anchors a leafy Clayton block with a cellar of more than 4,200 bottles and a wine list curated by sommelier Denise Mueller. The zero-proof corner of that list is quietly excellent for a classic wine bar: NoZeco sparkling brut poured by the glass, Giesen alcohol-removed Sauvignon Blanc, and a trio of Leitz cans spanning sparkling Riesling, sparkling rosé, and Zero Point Five Pinot Noir. A dedicated N/A Cocktails section adds a house alcohol-free spritz, the St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, and Parch's Desert Margarita, while Athletic Brewing and Best Day cover non-alcoholic beer.

description: Saturn Room is Tulsa's tiki bar, on North Boulder downtown, and it opens at 4pm and runs to 2am every single day of the week — the most consistently available late-night room in this guide. Its alcohol-free build is the Apple Drop: a non-alcoholic apple vodka with pineapple, ginger, aromatic bitters, vanilla, lemon and cinnamon, which is a seven-component drink using a named zero-proof spirit as its base. Tiki suits this category unusually well, since the format is built on fresh juice, house syrups and spice with the rum as one element among many rather than the whole structure.

Its cocktail list is built on house ingredients — yaupon tea, house cordials, its own bitters — and the same components carry a handful of alcohol-free drinks, among them a spirit-free take on an old-fashioned made with yaupon tea and sugar bitters, a carrot, pineapple, coconut and lime colada, and a cold-brew-and-coconut build lengthened with tonic. It trades from mid-afternoon to midnight, later at weekends, and closes on Tuesdays.

The 2025 'Long Drawn Out Sip' menu spotlighted two alcohol-free originals among its 24 creations, led by the No-Cracker 0% (Amarico, Martini Vibrante and acorn soda) and the Lost & Found 0% (juniper hydrosol, Martini Vibrante, raspberry and iris cordial).

name: Schlafly Tap Room
description: St. Louis's original craft brewpub earns the title: when the Schlafly Tap Room opened in December 1991, it was the first brewery to open in the city since Prohibition. Three decades on, the restored brick landmark in Downtown West still anchors the Schlafly universe — and the brewery now makes two of its own non-alcoholic beers, NA IPA and NA Pale Ale, both under 0.5% ABV and part of the year-round lineup. The NA Pale Ale reimagines the 1991 flagship that started it all. Come for hefeweizen-battered fish and fries, Tuesday-night trivia and a genuine piece of American craft-beer history, alcohol optional.

Current alcohol-free serves include the Dove (rose, pink grapefruit soda, lime), El Ranchero (apple, nutmeg, lemon, vanilla, almond, soda), Fortuna (cranberry, ginger, raspberry, grenadine, lime) and a from-scratch Virgin Mary, alongside Lucky Saint 0.5%, homemade ginger beer and a spread of Fentimans.

name: Seasons Rotisserie & Grill
description: Seasons Rotisserie & Grill is a long-standing restaurant near Old Town on Mountain Road, with a rooftop cantina above the dining room, and its contribution to this guide is an elevated Shirley Temple — which sounds like a joke and is not. The Shirley Temple is the drink most often handed to adults who are not drinking, usually badly made from bottled grenadine and flat lemonade; a kitchen that takes it seriously enough to rebuild it properly is making a specific point about who it is serving. name: Seaworthy
description: Seaworthy is an oyster bar and seafood restaurant in a restored 1832 cottage on Carondelet Street in New Orleans' Central Business District, open since 2016. NOTE: it sits inside the hotel formerly known as the Ace Hotel New Orleans, which was rebranded The Barnett in 2024 and now operates under JdV by Hyatt — the restaurant kept its own name and continues to trade there. It built its reputation on wild-caught, sustainably harvested oysters from the Gulf and both coasts, plus an acclaimed cocktail program; executive chef James Whitehead came from sister property Maison de la Luz. Within the drinks list sit a handful of zero-proof options: Curious Elixirs No. 1, a non-alcoholic riff on a Negroni made with rhodiola and pomegranate, and a Lyre's Amalfi Spritz. Prices for the zero-proof drinks are not published online. Open 4pm to 10pm Sunday to Thursday and to 11pm Friday and Saturday, with an oyster happy hour daily from 4 to 6.

name: Seed Library
description: Seed Library is the Shoreditch cocktail bar from Ryan Chetiyawardana, the bartender better known as Mr Lyan, who reshaped London drinking in 2013 with White Lyan — the first bar to work with no perishables, no ice and no branded spirits. His later rooms, Dandelyan (named the world's best bar in 2018) and its South Bank successor Lyaness, have been fixtures of the World's 50 Best list. Opened in the basement of the One Hundred Shoreditch hotel at 100 Shoreditch High Street, Seed Library is pitched as his neighbourhood bar: less theatrical than the flagship, built around what the team call stripped-back analogue forms and a maker's touch — minimal fuss, maximum flavour, drawn from unexpected ingredients. It is a low-lit room with a pared-back, produce-led list. Its "Pathways" menu carries four dedicated non-alcoholic serves, and roughly half the full cocktail list can be rebuilt booze-free; named low- and no-alcohol drinks include the Hand-Rolled Spritz and Master Stock Plus.

The Midtown dining room keeps a short list of named zero-proof cocktails like the bittersweet, ginger-tinged Beautiful Genius and the cucumber-mint-citrus Instant Karma, alongside non-alcoholic beer, house hopped water, and the amaro-inspired Casamar Club leisure soda from a local maker.

name: Senia
description: Senia is a fine-dining restaurant on North King Street in Chinatown, listed by The World's 50 Best Discovery and one of the most decorated kitchens in Hawaiʻi. Its non-alcoholic offering is a single drink, Mike's Mocktail, but it is a rotating one — the build changes every other month, with a lavender-honey version among those reported. That rotation is the point: it means the drink is developed alongside the food each cycle rather than printed once and forgotten, which is a different kind of commitment from a long static list. Dinner runs Monday to Saturday from 5.30pm, and the restaurant is closed on Sundays.

name: SereniTea Lounge
description: SereniTea Lounge is a boba teahouse and cocktail bar on Milwaukee's East Side, occupying a long-vacant Downer Avenue landmark (the former Chancery) that it revived in January 2025 as the local brand's third location and first bar. By day it runs as a full teahouse with an extensive alcohol-free menu of fruit teas, milk teas and bubble-tea drinks built with tapioca pearls and bursting boba; by night it adds a cocktail program. For sober and sober-curious guests the entire boba/tea menu is non-alcoholic and available all day, with named drinks like the Horchata Taro and a house-brewed Sweet Thai. Because it also serves cocktails, wine and sake, it is a hybrid rather than a fully alcohol-free space.

description: Seroja is chef Kevin Wong's two-Michelin-starred Nusantara restaurant in the Duo Galleria at Bugis, and its non-alcoholic pairing is a genuine anchor of the beverage program rather than an afterthought. The roughly S$148 zero-proof flight is built to run alongside the S$288++ tasting menu, using fruit and vegetable trimmings that would otherwise be discarded. Named house infusions include a chestnut, watercress and lotus-root brew aged in an apple-wood barrel, and a pomegranate, mulberries and curry-leaf blend that plays sweet against savoury. This waste-conscious drinks work is part of what earned Seroja a Michelin Green Star. Chef Kevin Wong has said he could not connect with the other cuisines he trained in because they were not part of his DNA, and the drinks follow the same logic as the food.

The bar shakes its non-alcoholic drinks in house rather than buying them in, and — usefully — stays open all day even when the kitchen closes for a reset between 2:30pm and 4pm, so it is one of the few Capitol Square rooms where you can sit with a drink mid-afternoon. Happy hour runs every weekday from 2 to 6pm. Closed Sundays; open to midnight Friday and Saturday.

name: Seven Bro7hers Beerhouse (Ancoats)
description: Seven Bro7hers Beerhouse in Ancoats is the Manchester bar of the Salford family brewery run by seven brothers, opened in 2016 on Blossom Street in the regenerated Ancoats district. It qualifies because Seven Bro7hers brews its own alcohol-free beer — AF Pale, a 0.5% hoppy craft pale ale — which is stocked across all of the company's Manchester beerhouses, this one included. Set over several levels with a ground-floor bar, a downstairs lounge and an outdoor patio, it pairs rotating house taps of Honeycomb Pale, Easy IPA and Helles Lager with burgers, gyros and bar snacks. The non-alcoholic pour is the brewery's own beer rather than a bought-in afterthought.

name: Seviche, A Latin Restaurant
description: Seviche is chef Anthony Lamas's Latin restaurant on Bardstown Road in the Deer Park stretch of the Highlands, and one of Louisville's longest-standing serious kitchens — Lamas is a James Beard semifinalist and a familiar face from television. The bar makes a non-alcoholic mojito as standard and, more usefully, the staff will build a bespoke alcohol-free cocktail on request rather than pointing at the soft drinks. In a Latin kitchen that is a meaningful offer: the house already keeps muddled herbs, citrus, agave syrups and fruit purées for the cocktail list, so an alcohol-free drink starts from real components. Dinner runs seven nights from 5pm.

description: Sexy Fish is the glossy Japanese-inspired restaurant and bar that opened on Spinningfields Square in autumn 2023, inside the former Armani Emporium — a 200-plus-seat room designed as much as a bar as a restaurant, with large sea-creature sculptures by Damien Hirst and fish-shaped lamps designed by Frank Gehry. The kitchen turns out sushi, sashimi, seafood and robata-grilled fish and meat, and the bar earned a pin in the inaugural Pinnacle Guide 2024, one of only 37 bars selected worldwide. Its alcohol-free programme is treated as an equal rather than an afterthought: the Unity cocktail menu, launched in 2024, is built around 12 core flavour profiles, each printed side by side in an alcoholic and an alcohol-free version, so a non-drinker orders from the same list. Named zero-proof serves include a non-alcoholic Watermelon (£7) and a non-alcoholic Cacao (£10, on Everleaf Marine), alongside six low-ABV options.

name: Sexy Fish Miami
description: Sexy Fish Miami is the Brickell outpost of the London-born Caprice Holdings restaurant group, occupying a lavish, underwater-themed space featuring original Damien Hirst artwork. Beyond its Asian-influenced seafood menu, the bar program is notable for its structured non-alcoholic offering. In May 2024 the venue launched its "Unity" cocktail menu, built around 12 core flavor profiles each served in both a full-strength and a 0% ABV iteration — a near 1:1 alcohol-free mirror of the spirited list. The program was developed by Caprice Holdings' bar team, and the zero-proof builds lean on house-made tinctures and infusions plus named ingredients like Seedlip Garden 108 and London Essence Co. sodas. Miami-exclusive serves include Lime, Goldenberry, and Coffee (the latter inspired by the espresso martini and carajillo). It is one of Miami's most deliberately built NA cocktail experiences.

For non-drinkers the brand's calling card is its "Stripped" mocktail menu, including the Stripped Geared Mule (pineapple, lime, lemon, mint and ginger beer), plus packaged non-alcoholic seltzers — a deliberate nod to inclusivity in an otherwise beer-forward room (note it is 21+). The year-round three are the important part: seasonal menus that vanish in February are the standard failure in this category, and a permanent list is a much smaller promise kept properly. Fair Oaks sits about twenty minutes east of downtown, so this serves a suburb the central venues do not reach. Read the hours carefully though: closed Monday and Tuesday, and Sunday is an 11am-2pm brunch slot only.

It serves no alcohol, and it trades to midnight most nights and 2am on Friday and Saturday — genuinely late for this part of the metro, and the reason the room fills up with groups rather than laptops after dark. The menu covers classic Yemeni coffee served in the traditional style alongside espresso drinks, and a set of house specialities including the Shibam Royal, strawberry and raspberry mojitos built without alcohol, dragon fruit lemonade and a pistachio iced latte. Six named alcohol-free cocktails are printed beside the house cocktails at $10 to $14, running from Cloud Nine with coconut, lime and club soda to two Tilden-based drinks, the Lacewing and the Tandem, plus a Tea-groni built on Gnista wormwood with a non-alcoholic aperitif and black tea. The shop roasts its beans on site two or three times a week and pours single-origin Ethiopian coffees rather than blends - the Sidamo it is named for, the fruitier Yirgacheffe and the full-bodied Harar - alongside a wide tea selection. Its best-known fixture is the traditional Ethiopian coffee ceremony held every Sunday at 2pm, a ritual it has now run several hundred times. There is free Wi-Fi and a back patio. No alcohol is served.

name: Sitti
description: Sitti is a downtown Raleigh Lebanese restaurant on South Wilmington Street in the Warehouse District, and its drinks list carries a dedicated "Spirit-free Cocktails" section with all three builds at $5 — among the cheapest properly made non-alcoholic drinks in the city. The list draws on Lebanese drinking traditions rather than mimicking cocktails: pomegranate molasses with honey, lime, ginger ale and soda in the Pomegranate Spritz, the mint-infused lemonade Limon Nana, and a passionfruit-and-ginger Lebanese Iced Tea. Head mixologist Colleen Hughes, fifteen years with the restaurant group, was named Esquire's Cocktail Guru of the Year in 2022 and received a 2025 Michelin Guide American South Exceptional Cocktails Award. Her "Spirit-Free Cocktails" section runs four drinks, every one marked vegan on the menu: the Spirit-Free Italian Spritz ($13, Lyre's non-alcoholic Italian spritz, Freixenet non-alcoholic sparkling wine, soda, acid phosphate, orange), Golden Hour ($15, Sentia GABA Gold botanical, passionfruit syrup, ginger kombucha, containing adaptogens), Bright and Spritzy ($15, verjus blanc, Amethyst grapefruit basil, simple syrup, soda), and the Spirit-Free Amaretti Sour ($15, two Lyre's expressions with lemon stock and a vegan egg white). name: SÜRENITEA Wellness Kava Bar
description: SÜRENITEA is a fully alcohol-free wellness and kava bar in Miami's Wynwood Arts District, styled as a Pacific-island-inspired "oasis of calm" with a plant-filled interior and the tagline "Meditation in a cup." Instead of alcohol, the menu is built entirely around botanical and functional beverages: ceremonial-grade kava (including Vanuatu and Tongan varieties), kratom drinks, functional-mushroom "cocktails," nootropic and biohacking elixirs, brewed teas, and a range of fruit-forward mocktails, alongside vegan food. The venue emphasizes COA-tested ingredients and staff who help guests choose drinks by desired effect — relaxation, energy, or recovery. It operates as a community-focused space where locals work, socialize, and unwind without alcohol, and stays open late on weekends. SÜRENITEA holds a 4.9-star rating from roughly 100 reviewers and is frequently cited among Wynwood's notable kava and wellness bars.

name: Swamp Cow Kava Lounge
description: Swamp Cow was Seattle's first kava bar, opened on Denny Way in Uptown by a couple of locals with roots in the Florida sober nightlife scene — the part of the country where alcohol-free lounges were normal long before the Pacific Northwest caught up. It calls itself the one and only late-night alcohol-free lounge in Seattle, and it works as a retail shop and a hangout at the same time: a wide range of prepackaged and branded adaptogenic drinks including kava, blue lotus and kanna, plus kombucha, ginger beer, non-alcoholic beer, seltzers, teas, coffee and sodas. The room has ample comfortable seating, WiFi, a full sound system and a modest stage for local artists, and the calendar is dense — weekly trivia, a Thursday open mic, highlighted artists, video games, movie nights, sporting events, dance and art groups, and EP release shows. Kava, blue lotus and kanna are all psychoactive botanicals rather than soft drinks: no alcohol, but not inert either.

name: Swift Soho
description: Swift opened on Old Compton Street in November 2016, taking over the site of the long-running Soho drinking den Lab. It is the work of Bobby Hiddleston and Mia Johansson — a bartending couple who met while working at the celebrated, now-shuttered Milk & Honey — in partnership with Edmund Weil and Rosie Stimpson, the team behind Nightjar and Oriole. The name is a promise: an upstairs bar built for a quick, well-made drink before dinner or the theatre, with no booking required, and a dark cocktail den below for settling in. It has since grown into a small group with further bars in Shoreditch and Borough, and is a near-permanent fixture on the World's 50 Best Bars list. The walk-in upstairs room carries a dedicated non-alcoholic list alongside its aperitivo menu, and the sibling Swift Borough pours a named low/no serve, the Atopia, with spiced citrus, Botivo, strawberry and pink peppercorn.

name: Switchback Brewing Co.
description: Switchback is an employee-owned Burlington brewery on Flynn Avenue, best known for its unfiltered Switchback Ale, and since January 2026 it has been the most heavily invested non-alcoholic producer in Vermont. The brewery installed a BrewVo de-alcoholisation system to bring production of Switchback N.A. fully in-house after the beer outgrew its trial run, and the same equipment makes Burlington the East Coast production site for BrewVo-made beers on behalf of other breweries and drinks brands. The tap room pours the full range and is open Wednesday to Sunday from noon to 9pm, Tuesday evenings from 5pm, closed Monday.

name: Syndicate Kava Bar
description: Syndicate Kava Bar is a fully alcohol-free kava and kratom bar in Miami's Wynwood Arts District, founded by Joyci Borovsky and Joey Roberts. Built "for the community of locals by those same locals," it runs like genuine nightlife rather than a wellness cafe: open until 3am daily, with a rotating events calendar that includes Tuesday open-mic nights, Thursday comedy, and a Saturday cabaret show. The bar pours brewed Fijian kava and kratom by the glass or growler, plus green/red/gold teas on tap and a roster of house-made kava and kratom mocktails. Signature pours include the Slutty Nectar (kava lemonade with watermelon, mint, lime, agave), Bitches Brew (a kava mojito), the Skinny Bitch, and Dasha's Kava Milkshake. A second Syndicate location operates in South Beach. Every drink is zero-proof — the venue serves no alcohol.

name: Taano House
description: Taano House is a non-alcoholic trailer bar parked at 1109 E. 6th Street in Austin's East Sixth entertainment district, with late evening hours that have changed more than once since it opened, so check its channels before going. Opened August 15, 2024 by University of Texas professor Geoff Smith and Joe Wes — co-founders of Austin-based Taano Elevated Beverages — the bar offers an unusual take on non-alcoholic drinking. Rather than focusing on traditional mocktails, Taano builds drinks around legal psychoactive plants like kava, kanna, blue lotus, and Amanita muscaria, aiming to deliver the relaxation and euphoria of social drinking through botanicals rather than alcohol. The cocktail menu was developed with Shaun Meglen, a mixologist and product education director for beverage distributor Southern Glazer's. Standout drinks include the Egyptian Mule (built on blue lotus and Amethyst's cucumber-ginger-serrano NA spirit), the Molly Martini (kanna with Lyre's NA coffee liqueur), and a 'mushroom wine' pairing Amanita muscaria with Oddbird NA wine. Visitors in recovery or anyone with substance sensitivities should note that the menu emphasizes psychoactive botanicals — this is a non-alcoholic experience, not necessarily a fully sober one.

name: Table Wine
description: Table Wine is a neighbourhood wine shop on Atwood Avenue in Schenk-Atwood, and it carries what is generally reckoned the deepest non-alcoholic wine and spirits selection in the Madison metro — a distinction it inherited when Sober Social, the state's only dedicated all-NA shop, closed its Middleton storefront in February 2026. For anyone building a home bar rather than going out, that makes it the practical option: de-alcoholised wines, zero-proof spirits and aperitifs shelved alongside a serious conventional list, with staff who taste the range. It opens at noon daily and runs to 9pm Tuesday through Saturday, which is later than most bottle shops in this guide manage.

name: Taiyo Sun
address: 394 St Georges Road, Fitzroy North VIC 3068
description: Taiyo Sun is a tiny, light-filled Japanese kissaten-style cafe run by Tats Kawabata on St Georges Road in Fitzroy North. It is alcohol-free by nature: the drinks list is built around whisked matcha — among the more talked-about in Melbourne — alongside a genuine curated tea menu (lapsang souchong, grapefruit green, sakuranbo cherry and blossoming jasmine flower) and Wide Open Road coffee with St David's Dairy milk. It is a quiet daytime cafe stop rather than a go-out-for-a-drink destination, but the matcha and tea program is real and well made.

name: Taj A Sweet Cafe
description: Taj A Sweet Cafe opened on Westheimer Road in Greater Uptown in September 2025 and keeps the most consistent late hours of any alcohol-free room in Houston: seven in the morning to midnight, every single night, with no weekday drop-off. It is a Levantine and Turkish sweets house rather than a Yemeni coffeehouse proper, though it serves Yemeni tea — the Adani, available by the cup or in a shared pot. The rest of the list runs to Turkish coffee, pistachio and Spanish lattes, a house soothing tea, and dessert-led drinks including the Biscoff Cloud and Tiramisu Dream. The published menu spans hot and cold drinks, oriental sweets, crepes and chocolates, and contains no alcoholic item anywhere on it.

name: Takibi

By day it runs a ramen-focused lunch on long-simmered broths and snow-aged noodles; by night it serves wood-fired plates, sushi, sashimi, tempura and a rotating omakase with a vegan version alongside it, plus one of Portland's deepest sake lists, sourced from Niigata. The bar keeps a named non-alcoholic section of four drinks at $10–$13, built on real zero-proof bases rather than juice: Natsu Gori (Dr. Zero Zero amaro shaved ice, watermelon, lime, sweetened condensed milk), Swizzle Me This (Ghia, peach shrub, mint, salted lime soda), Early Bird (Seedlip, lemon, coconut cream, poppyseed, demerara, nutmeg) and Chura-Sun (Wilderton Earthen, caramelised pineapple, lime, demerara), with non-alcoholic beer at $6. Named an Esquire Top 25 US bar and a Portland Monthly Top 50 restaurant in 2022. The restaurant closed temporarily during 2024 and reopened that October.

description: Tall Order is a New American bar and restaurant at 70 Beacon Street in East Somerville, opened in March 2025 by Daren Swisher and Joe Cammarata, who also run Daiquiris and Daisies in Boston. It occupies the former Thirsty Scholar Pub, a fixture near the Somerville-Cambridge line for close to thirty years before it closed in 2024. The drinks menu is deliberately split into full-strength, low-ABV and a section headed No Alcohol, so the alcohol-free options sit on the same page and at comparable prices rather than being relegated. Three named zero-proof cocktails are listed at $12.36 each, backed by non-alcoholic beer, non-alcoholic sparkling rose, a canned zero-proof negroni, hop water and fountain soda.

Its non-alcoholic offering is short but well made: The Perfectionist at $13 combines DHOS bittersweet aperitif with Töst alcohol-free sparkling, citrus, lavender and rosemary — an aperitif-style build with real bitterness and two herbs that place it alongside the kitchen's cooking rather than against it. description: Tandem Coffee + Bakery occupies a converted 1960s filling station on Congress Street in the West End and is the most loved cafe in Portland — nationally written-up, permanently busy, and entirely alcohol-free. Will and Kathleen Pratt roast their own coffee and the bakery turns out biscuits and pastries that draw a queue most mornings. It is a daytime room in the strictest sense, open 8am to 1pm and not a minute later, but within those hours it is the easiest place in the city to meet someone over a drink that was never going to involve alcohol in the first place.

name: Tandem Coffee Roasters
description: The Anderson Street location is where Tandem actually roasts, in East Bayside among the breweries and distilleries that fill that end of Portland — which makes it a useful address to know. It opens at 7am and closes at 1pm, entirely alcohol-free, and it sits within a few minutes of several taprooms, so it works as the sober half of a morning in a neighbourhood otherwise organised around drinking. The coffee is the same carefully roasted product as the Congress Street bakery, in a plainer, more industrial room built around the roastery itself. It opens an hour earlier than the Congress Street bakery and closes on Sundays, so check the day before making the trip.

Service runs from midday Tuesday through Saturday, which makes it one of the few kitchens on this list open across a long afternoon rather than only from 4pm. Its non-alcoholic drinks are seasonal composed builds at $13, the same territory as the cocktails: a Petit Autumn of cider, vanilla, maple, ginger and cayenne finished with apple butter and a bruléed apple, and a Mon Petit Coeur built on alcohol-removed red wine with cider, cinnamon and maple.

description: Tavern of Tales is a board game cafe and bar on Tremont Street in Mission Hill, with a free curated game shelf, a full library catalogued on BoardGameGeek and private soundproof rooms available to book. Three house mocktails are $6.99: Red Flags, a fizzy strawberry drink with lime and ginger; Ticket to Ride, its version of an Arnold Palmer built with a house lavender syrup and honey; and Dispelled Magic, orange and cranberry juice with cinnamon. A house lavender lemonade, Barritt's ginger beer, George Howell cold brew and espresso, and a specialty latte list round it out.

name: Tavolàta
description: Tavolàta is the Boise outpost of Ethan Stowell's Italian restaurant group, built around long communal tables and handmade pasta, and it keeps two named alcohol-free drinks on the list: Donn's Fizz and White Sands. The communal-table format is quietly useful for a non-drinker — a long shared table with food at its centre makes the meal the event rather than the drinking, and nobody is counting rounds. It opens at 4pm seven days a week, which is more consistent than most of Boise's better options. In a city where the good alcohol-free drinks come with awkward schedules, a seven-day restaurant is the reliable default when plans change late.

description: Tazza Kitchen's Scott's Addition location is a wood-fired neighbourhood restaurant whose bar keeps thoughtfully constructed non-alcoholic drinks on the standing list — the Centerfold is the one local guides name. What makes it useful in this particular district is the split-service schedule and the food-first orientation: Tazza trades lunch and dinner with a break between, so it functions as a proper meal out rather than a drinking session, which is exactly what a group needs when it is anchoring an evening in Richmond's brewery quarter around someone who is not drinking. Scott's Addition is otherwise organised almost entirely around taprooms, and a wood-fired kitchen with a real dinner service is a scarce thing in it.

By day it runs as a quiet co-working tea lounge (a roughly five-hour day pass, around $37, with unlimited tea); by night it hosts late-night tea sessions (about 7–11pm, ~$35, unlimited refills) plus jazz nights, sound baths, tarot, and art workshops. Drinks are entirely zero-proof: premium loose-leaf teas like the caffeinated Moonlight White, the red-rooibos Leche de Tigre, and the floral Love Potion, alongside a kava pop-up station. Everything is by advance reservation; no alcohol is served.

name: Tea Chapter
description: Tea Chapter is Singapore's best-known traditional Chinese teahouse, occupying a pair of conserved shophouses at 9 and 11 Neil Road on the edge of Chinatown and trading since 1989. It is entirely alcohol-free, and it is one of the few tea rooms in the city that stays open into the evening — until 10:30pm on Fridays and Saturdays — which makes it a workable alternative to a bar rather than only a daytime stop. Guests sit at low tables in the upstairs rooms and brew their own leaf in gongfu sets with staff guidance, and the house runs formal tea appreciation classes. Queen Elizabeth II visited in 1989, and the seat she used is still marked.

The tea list is the point: loose-leaf blends sourced worldwide and served properly, among them Vanilla Rooibos, Honeybush, a Sparkling Wine herbal infusion, Earl Grey, Japanese Cherry green and Raspberry Champagne white, alongside coffee and a short breakfast and lunch menu. Catchings launched a bottled line into local grocery in 2023 and has used the cafés as a first-job pipeline for Indianapolis teenagers. Nothing it pours contains alcohol, and the framing is deliberately social rather than therapeutic: it exists so that people who do not drink, for any reason at all, have somewhere to go together. It runs as a residency and event programme rather than a nightly bar, including Dry January pop-ups, so check the current schedule before making the trip. It keeps no fixed hours, which reflects that format rather than any doubt about the venue.

name: TEN 3
description: TEN 3 sits at 10,300 feet on Sandia Peak, reachable only by the Sandia Peak Tramway, and it is the most spectacular place in New Mexico to order a drink of any kind — the room looks out over eleven thousand square miles of desert. Its mocktails are named for the setting: On Mountain Thyme and Elevation Elixir. Because the only way up is the tram, and the tram has a schedule, this is a planned outing rather than a stop, and it works particularly well as an alcohol-free one given that altitude amplifies alcohol considerably. Book the restaurant and the tram together, and check the weather, which closes the tramway at short notice.

name: That's Kava
description: That's Kava is an alcohol-free kava bar on South Broadway in Englewood, on the southern end of the Denver metro's Broadway corridor. The venue states plainly on its own site that "We are an alcohol free establishment" and describes itself as a sober bar. It trades from 8am until 2:30am, which makes it one of the latest-closing alcohol-free rooms in the metro, and it programmes trivia, bingo and board-game nights most evenings of the week. Readers should know what is actually being served: alongside kava, the traditional South Pacific root drink, That's Kava pours kratom and other psychoactive ethnobotanicals, and Colorado law restricts kratom sales to over-21s. The drinks list is organised into kava, teas, on-tap, shots, mocktails and a high-potency "extreme" section.

description: Hidden in the lower level of a circa-1927 building downtown, the Thaxton has been pouring Prohibition-style cocktails behind a password-protected door since 2007 — the weekly password drops on Instagram. Alongside the boozy classics, the menu carries a dedicated 'Temperance' section of zero-proof cocktails built on DHOS Gin Free, like the egg-white-frothed 20/20 Tim Vision and the Greek-yogurt-smoothed Razz But No Tazz, plus a Faux Blueberry Sage French 75 and NA beers including 4 Hands' non-alcoholic Incarnation IPA and Bud Zero. It's open Thursday through Saturday nights when not privately booked, with limited first-come seating — one of downtown St. Louis's most distinctive date-night rooms.

name: The 126
description: The 126 is a downtown cocktail bar on College Street whose alcohol-free drinks are printed as Temperance Cocktails — a deliberate joke, each one named after a leader of the Temperance Movement that brought in Prohibition, including a Carrie the Hatchet built in tribute to Carrie Nation. The structural decision behind the section is more interesting than the naming: the bar makes every house syrup and every batch of bitters without alcohol, so any drink on the list can be built alcohol-free without substitution or compromise. Co-owner Emily Morton insists on the Temperance label over the word mocktail. Open Tuesday to Saturday from 5pm, closed Sunday and Monday.

name: The Archives
description: The Archives is a downtown arcade bar on College Street — vintage cabinets, pinball, a long craft beer list and a cocktail programme that is a good deal more considered than the format suggests. Hotel Vermont's guide to drinking in Burlington names it as one of two bars in the city making creative N/A cocktails, alongside Devil Takes a Holiday. It is also the most useful room in this guide for anyone not drinking, for a structural reason: it opens at noon at weekends and runs to 2am every night, and there is something to do with your hands that is not a glass.

name: The Aviary
hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 5pm-11pm; Fri 5pm-1am; Sat 4:30pm-1am; Sun closed
description: The Aviary is the avant-garde cocktail bar of The Alinea Group — the Chicago restaurant empire of Michelin-starred chef Grant Achatz and partner Nick Kokonas — opened in 2011 in the Fulton Market District of the West Loop. It treats drinks with fine-dining rigor, using molecular techniques, custom glassware, and a dedicated ice chef. Critically, its non-alcoholic program is a first-class equal, not an afterthought: every experience, from multi-course cocktail progressions to the à la carte list, is available fully zero-proof, with a dedicated NA pairing menu. The kitchen's commitment runs deep enough that the Alinea Group published "ZERO: A New Approach to Non-Alcoholic Drinks," a book of nearly 100 alcohol-free recipes. Named NA pours include the 310 to Yuzu and the Fill Collins. Accolades include a James Beard Award for Outstanding Bar Program (2013) and repeated World's 50 Best Bars rankings.

name: The Baker's Table
hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed-Thu 5pm-9pm; Fri-Sat 5pm-10pm; Sun closed
description: The Baker's Table is chef Dave Willocks' farm-to-table tasting-menu restaurant in Newport's historic Monmouth Street district, and its non-alcoholic program is unusually serious for a fine-dining room. Alongside the six-course seasonal menu, guests can add a four-course Spirit-Free Pairing ($45) that runs parallel to the Wine Pairing ($60), matching a considered zero-proof beverage to the canapes, starter, pasta and main. The bar always keeps a rotating seasonal mocktail on hand -- past pours include The Petal (hibiscus, chamomile, egg white) and the wintry The Partridge (cider, pear, cinnamon) -- plus Athletic Brewing non-alcoholic beer. Willocks, a 2026 James Beard finalist for Best Chef: Southeast, brings the same California-farmers-market rigor to the drinks that regulars say gets as much thought as the wine.

name: The Bar at Saint Kate
description: The Bar at Saint Kate is the art-filled lobby bar of Saint Kate - The Arts Hotel in downtown Milwaukee's Theater District, where live music plays nightly amid rotating gallery works. It anchors one of the city's more serious hotel mocktail programs, originally built with Lost Whale mixologists Daniel Beres and Trip Duval, and it remains a fixture on Visit Milwaukee's Dry January mocktail trail. The crafted zero-proof list runs alongside full cocktails, wine and beer, so it is a hybrid rather than a fully alcohol-free room. Note that the Bar has recently added intoxicating THC-infused sips, which are separate from its genuinely alcohol-free mocktails.

name: The Bardo Coffee House
description: The Bardo Coffee House is the South Broadway flagship of a small Denver chain that bills itself as "Denver's Late Night Coffee House", trading 6am to midnight every day of the week one block north of Alameda. No alcohol appears anywhere on its menus; the drinks list is coffee, espresso, tea and a set of house-blended speciality drinks made in-house rather than from commercial syrups. That combination — midnight closing, seven days a week, on the SoBo strip — makes it a working alternative to a bar rather than a daytime cafe, and it is a rare one on a block otherwise dominated by licensed venues. The room runs on 100 percent wind power and offers free WiFi, ample seating, free customer parking and a public colour laser printer.

name: The Barnes
description: The Barnes is the restaurant and bar on Powell Street inside the Union Square hotel of the same name, open daily from 5pm to 11pm. Its beverage menu carries a named non-alcoholic section of three built cocktails priced at $16, the same as most of the alcoholic list: a Non-Alcoholic Negroni made with Ritual zero-proof gin, Lyre's Italian Spritz and orange; Your NA Poolside, combining Lyre's Italian Spritz with Ritual agave blanco, lime and almond syrup; and Never Been Kissed, built on Seedlip Spice with lime, hibiscus, ginger beer and mint. Athletic Brewing's Run Wild IPA is stocked at $8 alongside a non-alcoholic Asahi. The kitchen runs shareable plates, a superfood salad, burgers and steak frites.

Its two documented alcohol-free builds are unusually savoury: the Vacation Email uses orange spice tea with grapefruit, lime, cinnamon, tonic and coconut, and the Karate Kid runs carrot and ginger syrup against lime, ginger beer, ancho chili and mint. Two sources of heat and a vegetable base is about as far from a sweet mocktail as a bar can get, and it is what makes both drinkable across a long evening.

description: The Bay has been trading on Brandon Boulevard since 2014, which makes it one of the longer-running kava rooms in Hillsborough County, and it is the main alcohol-free option in Brandon itself rather than in Tampa proper. It opens at 9:30am and runs to 11pm through the week, later at weekends, with a pool table and comfortable seating for people staying a while, plus late-night community events and wellness-room sessions. The drinks are kava, herbal and botanical teas, and craft non-alcoholic builds. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: the lounge is known for an extensive kratom selection alongside the kava. Kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries dependence and withdrawal risk that kava does not, so order with that in mind.

name: The Berry & Rye
description: The Berry & Rye is the oldest craft cocktail lounge in Omaha, a dim Prohibition-styled room in the Old Market on Howard Street, and it has an explicit policy of welcoming guests who are not drinking and building custom mocktails for them on request. It is open 5pm to 2am seven days a week, from 3pm on Friday and Saturday. For a bar of this vintage and reputation the willingness to make something properly rather than pointing at the soda gun is the relevant fact, and it is stated openly rather than left to be discovered.

Its recommended alcohol-free drink is a non-alcoholic paloma built on grapefruit, lime and triple syrup, and the bar will make other mocktails on request. Combined with the late hours and its position a few doors from 330 Main, the fully alcohol-free kava bar, it makes the Southside the easiest part of the city to spend a whole evening in without drinking.

That vertical integration is the reason its mocktails hold up: a Spokane Mule, a zero-proof Old Fashioned and a White Linen are made from the same house components as their full-strength counterparts rather than from a separate bottle of cordial. Being all-ages makes it one of very few rooms in the metro where a family or an under-21 group can sit at a proper cocktail bar. Wednesday to Saturday, 3pm to 9pm.

description: The Bower is a seasonal, locally-sourced American restaurant and bar on Magazine Street in the Lower Garden District, opened in 2020 by Mark Latter of Latter Hospitality (the group behind Tujague's); an adjacent cocktail-focused Bower Bar followed in 2022. The kitchen and beverage programs are ingredient-driven, with menus shaped by produce, herbs, and flowers from Sugar Roots Farm. Under beverage director Mickey Mullins, the "field-to-glass" bar program extends to a dedicated non-alcoholic section, where house-made mocktails are built from the same fresh, garden-driven ingredients as the cocktail list rather than bottled zero-proof spirits. Current non-alcoholic offerings include Moody Judy (vanilla bean lemonade, butterfly pea flower), No-Loma (grapefruit, lime, soda), and Walk the Lime (sweet lime and coconut), all available at the daily happy hour.

description: The Breeze is a combined coffee bar and wine shop in Shelby Park, run by Sarah Height and Chelsea Moore next door to their natural wine bar Canary Club. It bills itself as Louisville's first and only coffee bar and wine shop, opening in the morning for espresso from Cincinnati roaster Deeper Roots and running through the day as a bottle shop for natural, low-intervention wine. For non-drinkers it is the closest thing Louisville has to a non-alcoholic bottle shop: alongside the natural wine the shop carries a range of non-alcoholic wines and spirits, including a non-alcoholic Kentucky bourbon — which in this city is the bottle people actually want. name: The Butcher's Wife
description: A gluten-free, Brazilian-inspired restaurant and natural wine bar tucked into Tiong Bahru, The Butcher's Wife gives non-drinkers a genuine fermented, sit-down option: the kitchen brews its own house kombucha with regularly rotating flavours, sold by the 450ml bottle (S$15). Beyond it, there is a short but real line of named mocktails built to order - the Roselle & Pineapple (hibiscus tea, pineapple, almond syrup), the Apple Lemon Mint (apple juice, lemon, mint, soda) and Dansel's Virgin (elderflower, lychee, cranberry, mint) - plus cold-pressed juices like the Wife's Cooler (watermelon, cucumber, coconut water). The gut-friendly, fermentation-forward kitchen means the zero-proof pours are part of the same philosophy as the food, not an afterthought.

description: The Butterfly Bar opened in February 2011 inside The VORTEX, a long-running non-profit live theatre in East Austin's Manor Road corridor, evolving from the theatre's small beer-and-wine cafe into a full-service bar after it secured a mixed-beverage license in 2013. Every drink purchased supports the resident performing artists. The bar pours from a historic bartop reportedly over 200 years old and opens onto a patio that is a certified monarch butterfly garden, with butterflies present in summer. Alongside craft cocktails, bar manager Kellee Broadway runs a dedicated, named mocktail menu priced around $8. Confirmed zero-proof drinks include Aphrodite's Kiss (pomegranate, pineapple, lime, ginger beer) and the Queen Bey, a strawberry-limeade mocktail dusted with tajín that Broadway created. The on-site Patrizi's food truck serves housemade Italian pasta in the garden, and the adjoining black-box theatre hosts live performance most Thursday through Sunday, plus trivia, improv, and movie nights.

name: The Café at Thistle Farms
description: The Café at Thistle Farms is a fully alcohol-free cafe, tea room and event space on Charlotte Avenue in West Nashville, run as a nonprofit social enterprise that employs women survivors of trafficking, prostitution and addiction. It sits on the Thistle Farms campus alongside the organisation's shop and body-care workshop. The kitchen serves locally sourced breakfast and lunch, and the cafe runs a daily seated tea service - by reservation, 1pm to 3pm - with a steeped pot, a china cup donated by a supporter or programme graduate, and six chef's-choice bites on a tiered tray. The loose-leaf list includes Earl Grey Lavender, Casablanca Twist, Cha Cha, Masala Chai and a house blend called Communi-Tea. No alcohol is served. Closed Sundays.

A full page is a different order of commitment from a couple of drinks at the foot of the cocktail list — it means the drinks have been developed, costed and trained on as a category in their own right. It is open noon to 10pm most days and to midnight on Friday and Saturday, seven days a week, which for a non-drinker makes it one of the few all-day options in the metro.

name: The Charles
description: The Charles is one of the Design District's most booked dining rooms — a dim, loud, Italian-leaning room that has traded on being hard to get into since 2018 — and its Summer 2026 menu carries a printed Mocktails section. The Blossom Spritz builds cherry blossom and grapefruit over Fre sparkling, the Nada Colada covers the creamy tropical end, and the Blueberry di Capri the fruit-forward one. None is built on a non-alcoholic distillate, which places the list a step below the Ritual and Lyre's programmes elsewhere in this guide. The quietly more useful entry is a separate N/A Sparkling listing: Fre Brut by the glass or the bottle, so a non-drinker can share a bottle at the table rather than order around the wine list. name: The Charlotte
description: The Charlotte on Henderson Avenue prints a boxed Zero Proof section, and unusually every drink in it is a martini variant — the format zero-proof lists almost always skip, because a drink served up with nothing to hide behind is the hardest kind to build without alcohol. The Dirty Martini runs Ritual's gin alternative with olive juice and blue cheese-stuffed olives; alongside it sit a Pornstar Martini made with vanilla, pineapple, passion fruit and non-alcoholic sparkling, an espresso martini and a pomegranate martini. The restaurant publishes no telephone number and no closing times, and its own Instagram says only that it opens daily at 11am, so check before a late visit.

name: The Chill Room

description: A fully alcohol-free bar and lounge on Broadway Road in Tempe, built around spirit-free cocktails, kava, Fijian extract, botanical root teas, herbal teas and coffee. What sets it apart from the metro's other kava rooms is the calendar: open mic nights, live music, DJs, movie nights, trivia and poker, run weekly rather than occasionally, which is what turns a bar into somewhere people come back to. Open daily from 2pm and to 2am on Friday and Saturday, it functions as a genuine third place for the sober and sober-curious in the East Valley. Kava and kratom are alcohol-free but psychoactive — alcohol-free is not substance-free.

name: The Chloe
address: 4125 St Charles Ave, New Orleans, LA 70115
description: The Chloe is a boutique hotel, restaurant, bar and lounge from New Orleans hospitality group LeBlanc + Smith, opened in 2020 inside a restored 19th-century St Charles Avenue mansion designed by architect Thomas Sully, with a front porch and a tiki-style pool bar. READ THIS BEFORE ORDERING: the bar's "Spirit Free" section mixes alcohol-free drinks with two hemp-derived THC drinks under the same heading — Louie Louie Blackberry Lemon and Reba Water Sparkling Water, each labelled "(THC 5mg)" and priced at $11. The genuinely alcohol-free options in that section are the Typhoon Lagoon ($13) with Ritual non-alcoholic rum, passionfruit, guava, pomegranate, papaya, pineapple and lemon; the N/Aperitif Spritz ($16) with Lyre's Classico sparkling and orange; a bottled St. Agrestis Phony Negroni ($13); and Lyre's Classico sparkling wine by the glass ($14). These are built on bottled non-alcoholic brands rather than made from scratch. Dining runs 11am to 10pm Monday to Thursday, later Friday and Saturday, with weekend brunch and free on-street parking.

name: The Church of Root Kava Bar
description: The Church of Root is a small alcohol-free kava bar on NE 15th Avenue in Portland's Sabin neighbourhood, open 4pm to 10pm every day of the week. It prepares traditional kava beverages from high-quality roots using time-honoured methods rather than instant powder, and rounds the list out with a varied menu of other non-alcoholic drinks. The stated purpose is narrower and more specific than most bars manage: a welcoming environment designed for socialising, conversation and genuine connection, built around authentic kava, a relaxing room and engaging conversation. It joins Bula Kava House, Kava Saia and Nalu in giving Portland one of the deeper kava scenes on the West Coast. Kava is a psychoactive root drink from the South Pacific — no alcohol in it at all, but genuinely relaxing and mildly intoxicating on its own terms, which is worth knowing before a first shell.

name: The Commoner
description: The Commoner is the American-tavern restaurant and bar inside the Kimpton Hotel Monaco at 620 William Penn Place in Downtown Pittsburgh, and the hotel's own site confirms it as the operating restaurant there. Its zero-proof programme is led by Kyle Turner, a sober bartender, who designs a rotating line-up of non-alcoholic cocktails built on the serious bottles — Seedlip, Pathfinder, Lyre's and Trejo's. Drinks including a Pandan Express, The Wandering Path, a Machete and an N/Aperol Spritz have appeared on the list. IMPORTANT PRACTICAL NOTE: The Commoner publishes its food menus online but not its cocktail list, so the current zero-proof line-up cannot be checked in advance and we could not confirm which of those drinks is pouring today — the programme is real and well regarded, but the specific drink is a question for the bar. The bar runs later than the kitchen, to 11pm most nights and midnight on Friday and Saturday, with a seasonal biergarten. Do not confuse it with The Commoner Corner, a small separate to-go concept at the same building that has closed. Parties of eight or more carry an automatic 20% gratuity.

name: The Crunkleton
description: The Crunkleton is a lodge-style craft cocktail bar and restaurant at 1957 E 7th Street in Charlotte's historic Elizabeth neighbourhood, opened in December 2018 as the second location from Gary Crunkleton, who began bartending in Chapel Hill more than twenty years ago. It runs a full kitchen — a prime New York strip at $74, crab cakes at $26, a house pecan pie — with dinner from 5pm nightly and weekend brunch from 11am. Its menu carries a printed "Non-Alcoholic Cocktails" section, of which three are genuinely free of both alcohol and anything else, all $13: the N/A Sour (A Cut Above non-alcoholic gin, elderflower syrup, lime, fresh ginger, cucumber), the Painlesskiller (fresh pineapple, coconut cream, lime, orange, demerara), and a Phony Negroni built on the Spiritless negroni alternative. description: The Dabney is a Michelin-starred Mid-Atlantic restaurant at 122 Blagden Alley NW, a tucked-away corner of Shaw, opened in October 2015 by chef-owner Jeremiah Langhorne. The 55-seat dining room is built around a ten-foot wood-burning stone hearth, and almost everything passes through it. Langhorne's hyper-regional cooking won a Michelin star in 2017, the first year the guide reviewed Washington, and the 2018 James Beard Award for Best Chef: Mid-Atlantic, on top of a place on Bon Appetit's Best New Restaurants of 2016. The bar, run by bar director Daniel Todd, keeps a dedicated spirit-free list available a la carte at the bar or paired alongside the tasting menu: a Fennel Sour built with toasted fennel, egg white, lime and lemon, and a Manhattan riff on a house sorghum-based faux whiskey with spicebush amaro and black walnut bitters.

Its drinks menu has a six-drink mocktail section — the Cucumber Cooler (basil, cucumber, lemongrass, coconut water, soda), a Passionfruit Lime Soda, a Strawberry Limeade, the Coco-Mo, a rotating daily shrub with club soda, and Blue Ridge Bucha ginger kombucha from Virginia — plus Athletic Brewing and Stella Liberte 0.0% in bottles and cans. Lunch starts at 11am on weekdays and brunch at 10:30am at weekends, and it serves until 9pm every day.

name: The Dandelion
description: The Dandelion is a British-style pub off Rittenhouse Square, part of the Starr Restaurants group, done in the full country-pub register — snugs, patterned wallpaper, fish and chips, a Sunday roast. Its non-alcoholic provision is bottled rather than mixed, but it is honestly labelled on the printed beer list: Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn golden ale at $7, marked non-alcoholic, and St. Agrestis's Phony Negroni. That is a shorter answer than a cocktail bar would give, and we grade it accordingly. What it offers instead is a proper pub that serves food all day and stays open to midnight on Friday and Saturday, where nursing a non-alcoholic pint attracts no attention whatsoever.

name: The Dive
description: The Dive is a Canton cocktail bar on Elliott Street whose standing menu keeps a built non-alcoholic option rather than a soda pour: the Mockingbird shakes cranberry, lime and cinnamon honey with aquafaba and tops it with ginger beer, the aquafaba giving it the frothed body of a properly shaken cocktail.

name: The Dog Bar
description: The Dog Bar pairs an off-leash private dog park with a full bar in St. Petersburg's Grand Central District — a USA Today "best dog bar in America" finalist. Alongside 30-plus rotating drafts, it keeps a genuinely curated non-alcoholic menu of mocktails and NA beers (plus a CBD seltzer), so dog owners who aren't drinking have more than a soda while their dogs run. The list runs to seven mocktails and eight non-alcoholic beers — the Nah'Chelada, Safe Sex On The Beach and a Virgin Mary among them — an unusually deep bench for a bar whose main draw is the dog park. A daytime crowd that has to drive a dog home is exactly the customer base most bars ignore.

name: The Donovan Bar at Brown's Hotel
description: The Donovan Bar is the World's-50-Best-listed cocktail room inside Rocco Forte's Brown's Hotel in Mayfair, run by maestro Salvatore Calabrese and Director of Mixology Federico Pavan. Its signature achievement for non-drinkers is structural: the menu is built so that every section pairs four alcoholic cocktails with one full alcohol-free serve, given equal billing and treated as a real drink rather than a placeholder. The zero-proof builds are engineered to match the character and flavour of their spirited counterparts, drawing on bases like Seedlip.

name: The Draftsman
description: The Draftsman opened on 21 June 2023 at 68 Patton Avenue downtown as the bar and restaurant of The Restoration Hotel, and it is a more relaxed proposition than a hotel bar usually is — there is a bowling alley in it, called Up Your Alley, run first-come-first-served by signing up at the bar rather than booked ahead. The kitchen is straightforward and well priced for downtown: deviled eggs with local farm eggs, pickled mustard seeds and bacon at $8, a short rib and chuck Draftsman Burger at $17, and a jalapeño buttermilk fried chicken sandwich with Alabama white sauce at $16. It builds its non-alcoholic drinks with the same care as the full list rather than treating them as an afterthought, leaning on zero-proof aperitifs like Ghia — the Clear Morning Spritz (Ghia Amaro, lemon, grapefruit, soda) and a spirit-free Phony Negroni — so the non-drinker gets a properly crafted cocktail in a real cocktail room. Open from 5pm Thursday and Friday and from 11.30am at weekends.

Athletic Brewing's non-alcoholic IPA is on the bottle list. Open daily until 1am.

The lineup runs from a Seedlip-based garden cooler to a dessert-like Butterscotch Espresso Notini, and the restaurant is a featured stop on Visit Milwaukee's Mocktail Trail.

name: The Eleanor
description: The Eleanor is a Warehouse District cocktail bar whose zero-proof drinks are built with the same architecture as its spirited list rather than being simplified into juice. The clearest evidence is the Pass The Buck, which layers Almave — the non-alcoholic blanco agave spirit — with Giffard bitter aperitif syrup, a strawberry and Thai basil syrup, ginger, lemon and barrel-smoked black pepper. That is seven components doing the work alcohol usually does: the bitter aperitif supplies the backbone, the smoked pepper the finish. Visit Austin's official zero-proof guide singles the drink out. The bar keeps late Friday and Saturday hours and is walkable from the Fifth Street hotel cluster.

name: The Elk Room
description: The Elk Room is a subterranean, speakeasy-style craft cocktail bar in Harbor East known for a serious spirit-driven program. Its zero-proof entry, the Penumbra, is a composed build rather than a sweet afterthought — a wine vinegar shrub with yuzu juice, blueberries, thyme, black pepper and soda water — the kind of savory, acid-forward drink the bar's cocktail list is built on.

name: The Epicurean
description: The Epicurean is an award-winning independent craft-beer bottle shop, and this Henry Street unit is the group's Ancoats flagship — its first city-centre store, opened in November 2021 next door to natural-wine merchant Kerb. Owner Simon Yarwood's shop packs more than 500 beers across nine fridges, and its low-and-no range is one of the deepest in Greater Manchester: a 'beer library' of alcohol-free options rather than a token shelf. Chilled 0.0–0.5% picks run from Big Drop's Galactic Stout and Beavertown's Lazer Crush to Tiny Rebel's Clwb Tropicana, Athletic Brewing's alcohol-free lager and Vandestreek's grapefruit IPA. It is a bottle shop rather than a bar, but for taking home a genuinely broad spread of alcohol-free craft beer it has few rivals in the city.

Several non-alcoholic drinks sit on the standing menu, led by the Little Green One at $10 — cilantro, lime, pineapple, mint and jalapeño lengthened with Fever-Tree tonic over a Tajín rim, so heat and salt do the work alcohol would in a spicy margarita. Two named builds are documented — one a calming lavender, chamomile, ginger and CBD drink, the other a watermelon shrub and lime build that reads like summer in a glass. It opened on 28 September 2017 from Bryan Rushton and Andrew Cook, longtime music-industry friends and Massachusetts natives, in a room fitted out with reclaimed wood from Nashville-area houses. Food & Wine named it one of the 10 Best U.S. Bars in 2023, Eater Nashville made it Bar of the Year the same year, and USA Today's 2026 list called it one of the city's strongest cocktail programs. Its non-alcoholic drinks are built with the same technique as the full menu and, importantly, they rotate with the seasons rather than sitting still — the current three are the East Coast Inferno (Sanbittèr Red, orange juice, Old Bay, habanero, lemon), Pêche Mode (Almave Ámbar non-alcoholic tequila, peach, lime, salted honey) and Duck Hunt (duck fat Lapsang Souchong, The Pathfinder, cherry, BBQ bitters), all $12.

It is a DC original from the Drinks With You group, which also runs Patina, Never Looked Better and The Mirror, and it pairs craft cocktails and fine food with a jazz-age room and recurring live programming, including regular jazz nights framed as an homage to Duke Ellington. Non-drinkers get their own headed menu, Beer, Wine & Non-Alcoholic, rather than a footnote: an Amaro Lucano & Soda built with N/A amaro, soda and lemon essence, and The Peacock Room, made with cider, lemon, sugar, NA bitters and sparkles, alongside non-alcoholic beer such as Kit NA Lager, plus NA ciders and wines.

Beyond its rum-forward classics like the Navy Grog, the bar keeps a dedicated "Virgin Cocktails" section on its menu, so non-drinkers get crafted zero-proof options rather than an afterthought. The lineup includes the Tropical Vertigo (Kalinago Caribbean tea, cream of coconut, pineapple, lime, vanilla and grated cinnamon), the Coconut Pick-Me-Up (espresso, cream of coconut, vanilla and club soda), and an N/A Painkiller built on Dole soft serve with creamy coconut and grated nutmeg. The standout is the No-Groni, a non-alcoholic Negroni riff made with Lyre's Rose botanical spirit, Giffard aperitif, Lucano N/A, lemon and Fee Brothers orange bitters. The venue is 21+ and was voted Best Chinatown Bar in Las Vegas Weekly's 2025 Readers' Choice awards.

name: The Green Door
description: The Green Door opened in April 2025 as Greater Cincinnati's first fully alcohol-free "dry" bar, created by founder Christian Perry-Watt and the team behind Kentucky Botanicals Co. Every drink starts zero-proof: fresh craft mocktails you can enjoy as-is or customize with kava, THC, CBD, adaptogens or blue lotus. The moody, speakeasy-inspired room fuses Art Deco and Art Nouveau, with signature pours like "That Lavender Haze" (blueberry, lavender, citrus) and "The Spicy Mock-arita" (mango, citrus, habanero), plus non-alcoholic riffs such as "Not Gin + Tonic" and "Whiskey-ish + Soda." There are also canned THC seltzers, kava seltzers and mushroom elixirs, a small bottle shop, and a calendar of live music, DJs and wellness events. It's a 21+ room, just across the river from downtown Cincinnati.

description: The Green Zone is a Middle Eastern craft cocktail bar at 2226 18th Street NW in Adams Morgan, founded by Chris Hassaan Francke, who opened the permanent bi-level space in July 2018 after running it as a pop-up. It draws on Levantine and Iraqi flavours - Francke sources rare ingredients such as sour grapes from Lebanese markets and visits his Iraqi family in Lebanon - and pairs house cocktails with Middle Eastern small plates. Because it is inspired by a region where many people abstain from alcohol for religious reasons, the bar treats the non-alcoholic list as a true equal, typically keeping at least eight no-ABV options on at any time: a Royal Jallab, a zero-proof Garibaldi, a Halal Spritz on St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, a Zeroodeh Swizzle and frozen mint or cucumber lemonade. Open to 3am on Friday and Saturday.

name: The Hills Market Downtown
description: The Hills Market Downtown is an independent grocer on North Grant Avenue in the Discovery District, and it is the closest thing Columbus has to a bricks-and-mortar zero-proof bottle shop. Rather than scattering non-alcoholic products through the beer and wine aisles, the store runs a dedicated end cap of nearly forty different alcohol-free wines, beers and spirits — non-alcoholic gin, whiskey, tequila and rum, ready-to-drink cocktails and gin and tonics, dry sodas and alcohol-free sparkling wine. That breadth matters in a city with no dedicated non-alcoholic retailer: it is the only place in central Columbus where a shopper can compare a range of zero-proof spirits side by side before buying. The market also serves prepared food and coffee and has run occasional happy hours.

name: The Horn Midtown
description: The Horn Midtown is the second site of the family-run Somali cafe that began in 2015 on Murfreesboro Pike, and like the original it serves no alcohol. It sits on Scarritt Place, on the Scarritt Bennett campus between Vanderbilt and Belmont, which makes it a student and staff room as much as a neighbourhood one. The counter runs on chai rather than espresso: Somali chai, brown sugar chai and a dirty chai pulled with a shot, plus a short coffee list including a cinnamon white mocha, with hand-folded sambusas alongside. Nashville Public Radio featured The Horn in 2025 in a report on Muslim-owned coffeehouses that reopen at night through Ramadan and want that alcohol-free evening culture to last all year. Outside Ramadan the hours are daytime.

It began in 2015, after the founder's father arrived from Somalia and sold sambusas out of his car, and it has grown into a two-site business hand-folding sambusas and brewing Somali chai daily. name: The Intan
description: The Intan is an award-winning Peranakan home museum in Joo Chiat whose by-appointment, 60-minute Tea Experience is a fully non-alcoholic affair: owner-curator Alvin Yapp guides guests through his collection before serving The Intan Signature Tea alongside a spread of traditional nyonya kueh. There is no bar and no alcohol here at all, only heritage tea service in a lived-in Straits Chinese home. Sittings run Friday to Sunday and cost S$64.20 for adults (S$32.10 for children under 12). Founder Alvin Yapp has spent more than four decades collecting Peranakan antiques and hosts the tea sessions in his own home himself, which is why the visit reads as a social gathering rather than a museum tour.

The no- and low-ABV list is treated as core rather than supplementary, built on house-made seasonal shrubs, non-alcoholic bitters and dealcoholized aperitifs. Current spirit-free pours include Asimov's Crater, the Bitter Orange Old Fashioned and The Maiden, alongside non-alcoholic beer and sparkling cider.

description: Appears to be closed for now, as of late October 2026: the lounge's own page has been taken off the company's website, its Locations menu no longer lists it, and its dated events stop in mid-October. No reason or reopening date has been published, so call (980) 237-6651 before you go. The Kanna Collective Lounge & Coffee Bar is a woman-owned, 21+ Amsterdam-style cannabis lounge on W Worthington Ave in South End, from a dispensary business founded in 2019, with the group's separate South End THCA dispensary in the unit next door. Every named beverage it sells is cannabis-infused — its Kanna Mocktail Seltzers carry 10mg Delta-9 hemp-derived THC and 10mg CBD per can and warn that use "may result in a failed drug test", and Queen City Nerve describes its signature drink plainly as "the cannabis-infused Pretty High for a Dry Guy mocktail". No fully non-psychoactive named drink is published anywhere on its menu. The consumption lounge is members-only ($5 day passes sold in person); the cafe and patio are open to the public. Despite the name, no kanna plant or kratom is sold.

Happy hour runs twice daily, 2pm to 4pm and again 7pm to 9pm. The menu covers kava, kratom and herbal teas. description: The Open Road is an alcohol-free bottle shop on Penn Avenue in Garfield, founded by Mel Babitz and widely described as the country's oldest non-alcoholic specialty retailer. Examples carried include a 10mg THC seltzer, a 20mg CBD seltzer, a hemp-and-lion's-mane soda at 3mg THC, and a kava spirit at 150mg kavalactones per serving. name: Thevar

Alongside a wine list of more than 400 labels, its tasting menu offers a fully composed non-alcoholic pairing (S$138) built course by course for teetotallers, sitting beside the S$248 alcoholic pairing. It is a genuine kitchen-driven zero-proof pairing rather than a token mocktail add-on, which is why teetotal diners can follow the full tasting experience. Time Out Singapore sums the kitchen up as modern South Indian cooking with spot-on seasoning, complex spice blends and stellar presentation.

The root beer float is the interesting inclusion: it is unapologetically a dessert drink rather than a cocktail imitation, and giving a non-drinker something that is straightforwardly good on its own terms is a different and often better move than approximating a Negroni. Its sibling bar, Bar Please!, occupies the suite above and keeps identical hours, so the building offers two rooms in one trip. Both run to midnight midweek and 1am at weekends, and both open Sundays, which is unusual downtown.

Its approach to alcohol-free drinking is unusually practical: rather than confining zero-proof options to a short list, the bar marks individual cocktails on the main menu as available as non-alcoholic, so the same builds are offered either way. Four of the shaken drinks carry that note, including the Yuzu Cute with elderflower, yuzu, pineapple, lemon and mint, the grapefruit-and-elderflower Pawloma, the house Third Rail with lemon, honey and orange bitters, and the smoky Evil Twin. Its non-alcoholic program is a formally named one — “Zero Proof, Zero Judgment,” created by bartender Anna Welker — and it runs as a full spirit-free menu rather than a single token pour. The drinks are built on gin and tequila alternatives with house ingredients like pineapple shrub and Aztec chocolate bitters; the signature Yellow Balloons layers cinnamon-infused ginger turmeric tea with pineapple shrub and grapefruit bitters. Rotating cans from the Baltimore non-alcoholic brand NOPE round out the list alongside NA beer and wine, and the program was successful enough to draw its own local TV coverage.
