The restaurant runs it under Sandoval's group-wide Art of Zero Proof programme, which the company describes as flavourful, beautifully crafted drinks showcasing culinary artistry, creativity and elevated indulgence without alcohol. Named builds include the Espresso Maíztini, a spirit-free reworking of the espresso martini, plus the Garden Grove and a Grapefruit Sour. Its bar program includes named zero-proof cocktails alongside the spirited list: the "Clear Headed," built on Ritual's rum alternative with Earl Grey and smoked vanilla, and a zero-proof piña colada made with hearth-roasted pineapple, mint, coconut water, and lime. description: IMPORTANT CLARIFICATION — UNBAR SERVES ALCOHOL. UnBAR Cafe is a Black-owned cafe and evening hangout on Larchmere Boulevard, opened on 20 January 2020 by Melissa Garrett-Hirsch and built around the social experience of a bar for people who are not drinking. We previously implied it was alcohol-free; it is not. It runs a wine offering alongside its non-alcoholic drinks, and the owner's own framing is precisely the point: people can bring their friends and have a good time, participate in karaoke, trivia and cards, and their friends can have the alcoholic beverage — but they don't have to. A mixologist who specialises in non-alcoholic work makes the drinks, and the rest of the menu runs to espresso, smoothies, soup and light, health-conscious food. The interior is deliberately domestic — green and purple walls, positive art, inspirational quotes lettered where you will read them — described by its owner as a loved one's living room, and the room programmes comedy, game nights, karaoke and poetry. PLEASE NOTE: its website is currently broken and its published phone numbers disagree across listings, so confirm hours on its social channels before travelling.

The aperitivo format is what matters here — an Italian café is one of the very few settings where ordering something soft in the early evening is completely unremarkable, because the room was serving cappuccino an hour earlier. The current card runs four at $10 under a Non-Alcoholic Cocktails heading: a Fauxspresso Martini on Switters nitro cold brew with vanilla clove, Defying Gravity (Seedlip Agave, Lyre's Italian Orange, lemon and house grenadine), a Not Aperol Spritz on Lyre's Italian Orange with NA sparkling wine, and a Free Spirit of grapefruit, ginger syrup, lime and ginger beer — alongside non-alcoholic beer from Athletic Brewing (Lite, Golden Dawn, and Run Wild IPA) and other NA pours. name: Urban South Brewery
description: Urban South Brewery, founded in 2016 by Jacob Landry and Kyle Huling, is the largest brewery by volume in New Orleans, anchoring a taproom on Tchoupitoulas Street in the Lower Garden District that welcomes families and hosts children's birthday parties. It was the first brewery in the city to brew a non-alcoholic version of its own beer. The NA program is built around two in-house 0.5% ABV brews: N.A. Holy Roller, a hazy IPA using the same Mosaic, Citra and Centennial hops as the flagship, and N.A. Charming Wit. PARENTS AND NON-DRINKERS SHOULD KNOW: the same beverage page also carries a "THC Beverages" section of nine hemp-derived THC seltzers at 5mg per can — Grapefruit, Black Cherry, Tangerine Ginger, Peach Spritz, Watermelon Spritz, NOLA Cola Classic, NOLA Cola Root Beer, Lemon Lavender and Lime — listed immediately above the "Non-Alcoholic" heading, with no warning or age-policy text published nearby. The two categories are labelled separately but sit side by side. The taproom serves smash burgers, with happy hour weekdays 3 to 6pm.

name: UrbanMama505 Kombuchery & Elixir Bar

description: UrbanMama505 is a kombuchery and elixir bar on Central Avenue run by Julie Morrell and Ted Archuleta, brewing its own kombucha from organic teas and pouring it as flights — lime, lavender, rose hips, and a Black Guatemalan made with cold-brew coffee. Nothing served contains alcohol. Morrell's framing of why it exists is the clearest statement of this directory's premise anyone has made: the culture always asks what you're drinking, and they want people to know that does not always mean alcohol. The hours are narrow — Friday and Saturday only — so plan around them. The building is a plain cement-block unit on Central, easy to drive past.

name: Valkyrie
description: Valkyrie is downtown Tulsa's serious cocktail bar, on Reconciliation Way, open 4pm to 2am six nights a week and closed only on Monday. It has treated zero-proof drinks as part of the programme for years rather than as a recent addition — a Don't Text Your Mex of spicy house ginger beer, strawberry syrup, lemon and basil appeared in local drinks writing back in 2020, and the current alcohol-free entry is the NWA, built on orgeat, cream and lemon. Both are house-made from the bar's own components. It is one of three downtown rooms in this guide keeping a 2am licence, which makes late sober nights in Tulsa genuinely possible.

name: Van Ryder
address: 131 S 300 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
description: An 11th-floor rooftop bar atop the Le Méridien Salt Lake City Downtown, opened in February 2023 with a Western-saloon aesthetic. Its non-alcoholic program is unusually deep: a dedicated "Proofless Cocktails" menu (the Honey Badger Redux and Meet Me in The Garden, both around $11) plus a separate "Proofless Beer" list. Director of Libations and Service Elyse Evan has put the zero-proof program at roughly 15% of total sales, with NA beer running 25-30% of all beer sales. The spirit-free builds get the same care as the full rooftop cocktail list, served against floor-to-ceiling skyline and Wasatch Range views.

address: 3570 S Las Vegas Blvd, Las Vegas, NV 89109
description: Vanderpump Cocktail Garden is reality-TV personality Lisa Vanderpump's glamorous open-air-style cocktail lounge at Caesars Palace, tucked between The Colosseum and the entrance to The Forum Shops on the Las Vegas Strip. The space is styled as an elaborately decorated garden with sparkling chandeliers, lush florals, and pink-hued opulent decor, and it draws a steady celebrity-fueled, Instagram-driven crowd. Beyond its hand-crafted signature cocktails, the menu includes a dedicated "Mighty Mocktails" section of zero-proof drinks, so non-drinkers get crafted options rather than an afterthought. House mocktails include the Garden Goddess (mint, matcha, pineapple, lemon, and aquafaba for a velvety foam) and the Caesars Berries (raspberry, mint, hibiscus, lemon, coconut, and soda), both made with the same garnish-forward attention as the alcoholic list. The kitchen pairs the drinks with decadent small bites, with the goat cheese balls a widely cited favorite.

It took gold for Best Rooftop Dining in CityScene Magazine's 2025 Best of the 'Bus reader poll. The cocktail menu carries a dedicated no-proof section rather than a single token drink, and the builds use proper non-alcoholic spirits: Everybody Loves Juniper is made with Lyre's London Dry, a house tonic syrup, lemon and soda; the Spice Orange combines Seedlip Citrus with fresh lime, orange and ginger beer; and the house VASO G&T is offered zero-proof with Seedlip Garden, bergamot, lavender, juniper and tonka bean over sparkling Mediterranean tonic. The bar opens at 4pm on weekdays and 2pm on Saturdays.

The taproom keeps a rotating bench of non-alcoholic beers — Bero's 0.0% West Coast IPA and Noon Wheat, Rationale Brewing's Japanese-Style Dry and Mexican Cerveza, and Sam Adams Just the Haze — alongside Noble Coyote nitro cold brew, kombucha, espresso and tea. name: Vena's Fizz House
description: Vena's Fizz House has been the centre of gravity for alcohol-free drinking in greater Portland since 2013, when it opened on Fore Street as a bar where every drink was zero-proof. That original room closed and the business moved to the Dana Warp Mill in Westbrook, where it now trades as a craft mixer and mixology shop — shrubs, bitters, syrups, tools and the ingredients that make a good non-alcoholic drink possible at home. It came close to closing entirely in 2025 after twelve years before new owners stepped in to keep it going, with the founders helping. Note the hours are strictly weekday business hours, and Westbrook is a twenty-minute drive from downtown Portland.

name: Verde
description: Verde is the restaurant and terrace inside the Pérez Art Museum Miami in Museum Park on Biscayne Boulevard, with a terrace looking straight across Biscayne Bay. Its alcohol-free list runs to three named builds rather than one — a Boba Passion Fruit, a Coconut Cooler and a Gingerberry Smash — all built around fresh fruit and spice rather than around substitutes for spirits. RESIDENT covered the restaurant in December 2025 and wrote that the drinks are part of the larger sensory experience and that the setting encourages guests to linger. The hours follow the museum rather than the restaurant trade: closed Tuesday and Wednesday, with a late Thursday service until 8pm.

name: Verdigris
description: Verdigris is an upscale cocktail bar and lounge inside the Park Place development in Leawood, Kansas, opened in spring 2020 by owners David and Noelle Manica with the team behind Kansas City's Monarch Bar. The room is themed around verdigris — the green patina of weathered copper — and the menu organizes drinks as classic, light, rich, and imperial cocktails. The non-alcoholic offering is built into the cocktail list itself: several signature drinks are explicitly marked "available non-alcoholic," meaning the bar builds spirit-free versions of named house cocktails to order. Confirmed spirit-free options on the 2026 menu include the Green Maiden (cucumber, snap pea, green tea, ginger, lime), the Ibisco (hibiscus, pineapple, lime, orgeat), the Aqua Regia (orange, turmeric, aperitif, strawberry seltzer), and the Whiskey Bramble. The packaged non-alcoholic pour is the 0.0% Lagunitas Hoppy Refresher. Verdigris was voted Best Johnson County Bar in Kansas City Magazine's Best of 2026.

Named alcohol-free options include the Not So Stormy, Bonito, a zero-proof Old Fashioned, Slo Gin Fizz, Paloma and a "Nigroni." name: Via Vecchia

Every element of that build is doing the job the alcohol would: gentian and cherry bark supply the bitterness Campari normally brings, juniper stands in for the gin, and the clear ice and garnish mean the drink arrives looking exactly like the one everyone else ordered. Dinner service runs from 4pm daily in one of the Old Port's grandest rooms.

name: Vibehaus Kava Bar & Lounge
address: 118 NE 1st Ave Ste g, Hallandale Beach, FL 33009
description: Vibehaus is an alcohol-free kava lounge in downtown Hallandale Beach, open 9am to 2am every day, with an outdoor lounge area and free parking for guests. It is programmed as a night-out venue rather than a cafe — live music and events run through the week — and the drinks are billed as signature kava and K-drink cocktails rather than as wellness shots. Two things are worth knowing before you go. Hookah is served, so the room is not smoke-free. And IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: the K-side of that cocktail list is kratom, whose alkaloids act on opioid receptors and carry a genuine dependence and withdrawal risk. Kava, the South Pacific root the venue is named for, does not work that way. Both are poured here, so ask which is in your glass.

name: Vice City Kava
description: Vice City Kava is a fully alcohol-free kava and kratom bar in Miami's Coral Way neighborhood, wrapped in an unapologetic 1980s "Miami Vice" aesthetic of neon, vaporwave lighting, and retro nostalgia. Its stated mission is to offer relaxation, energy, and euphoria through kava and kratom "minus the booze, pressure, and weird vibes." The bar pours traditional strained kava sourced primarily from Fiji, kratom teas, herbal infusions, and nitro cold brew, alongside light food like Belgian waffles and ramen. Beyond drinks, it leans hard into community: weekly trivia, open mics, live music, "Around the Tanoa" gatherings, and a free "Sound Library" of instruments and recording gear. The venue is listed by BestKavaBar as the #1 kava bar in South Florida. It operates daily, 9am–3am, and runs a second location ("The Warehouse") elsewhere in Miami.

The seasonal, farm-driven cooking that made Michael a Food & Wine Best New Chef in 2018 extends to the glass: Vicia offers a year-round non-alcoholic selection spanning mocktails, wines, and beers. The signature Garden Toddy stirs n/a bourbon with opal basil, green shiso, spearmint, marigold, honey, and lemon — a zero-proof drink as garden-obsessed as the food. Dinner runs Tuesday through Saturday in a light-filled space at Duncan and Boyle.

name: Vintage Books
description: Vintage Books is a speakeasy and restaurant hidden behind a vintage-bookstore facade on Waialae Avenue in Kaimukī — not Chinatown, as several guides have it. The styling is Prohibition-era with a tropical bend, and the spirit-free drinks are built to the same specification as the rest of the list rather than improvised. The Nogroni is the clearest evidence: Seedlip Garden, Giffard sirop aperitif and Lyre's aperitif rosso, finished with orange oil — three genuine zero-proof products layered to hold the bitterness a negroni drinker actually wants. The Kaimuki Cruise runs lychee, lemon, mango and Sicilian lemonade, and a botanical London Tonic sits alongside them.

It opens at 9am and runs to midnight, or 1am on Friday and Saturday. Kava flights are offered for anyone wanting to taste across preparations. Its standing locally rests on more than drinks: it hosts the annual Kava Campout, has been recognised by the Town of Weaverville, and served as a gathering space for the community during Hurricane Helene.

name: Virago Spirits
description: Virago Spirits is a Richmond distillery whose tasting room pours non-alcoholic versions of several of its own cocktails, built around flavours including smoked raspberry, vanilla, orange and pecan. A distillery is the last place most non-drinkers would expect to be catered for, which is exactly why it is worth knowing: the same people who develop the spirits build the zero-proof serves, using the syrups, infusions and technique the bar already has. It trades Wednesday to Sunday afternoons and evenings, closing at 9:30pm, and it makes the distillery tour circuit that runs through Scott's Addition workable for a mixed group — turning what is usually the worst afternoon of the year for a non-drinker into an ordinary one. Ask what they are pouring zero-proof when you arrive, as the serves follow the house list rather than a fixed menu.

name: Virtue
description: Virtue Restaurant & Bar is chef Erick Williams's acclaimed Southern restaurant in Chicago's historic Hyde Park neighborhood, opened in November 2018 as his first solo concept. Williams was named James Beard Foundation Best Chef: Great Lakes in 2022, becoming the first Black chef to win in that category, and Virtue is listed in the MICHELIN Guide. The kitchen centers thoughtful, hospitality-driven Southern cooking, and the bar carries a dedicated "zero-proof" section for non-drinkers. Current spirit-free offerings are house-made rather than bottled brands: the Sorrel Fizz (hibiscus, rosemary, vanilla, sparkling water), The Hummingbird (basil, lemon, soda), and the Coconut Woman (coconut cream, pineapple, lime). It's a smaller but real NA list at a full-service Southern restaurant, well suited to those who want a considered alcohol-free option alongside a notable dinner.

name: Volare Italian Ristorante
description: Volare is a long-running Italian restaurant on Frankfort Avenue in Clifton, named Best Italian Restaurant by readers of Louisville Magazine three years running, with a seasonal menu built on locally sourced produce and house-made pasta. Its place in a non-alcoholic guide rests on one thing done properly: the bar builds Spiritless Manhattans, using the Louisville-made non-alcoholic bourbon Kentucky 74 in place of rye or bourbon. A manhattan is a spirit-forward, stirred, undiluted drink — the hardest category to render without alcohol and the one most bars refuse to attempt — so a restaurant offering it as standard is making a real claim. Dinner runs seven nights from 4:30pm.

description: W.A. Frost & Company is a Cathedral Hill institution that opened in December 1975 inside the historic 1889 Dacotah Building, originally home to William A. Frost's pharmacy. Long known for its tree-canopied patio, award-winning wine list, and contemporary American cuisine, the St. Paul mainstay also runs a genuine zero-proof program. Its Cocktail Hour menu carries a dedicated "No Proof Cocktails" section priced at $8, currently listing the Blueberry Buzz Tonic, the Wilfred Spritz, and the Strawberry Gimlet. The bar additionally pours non-alcoholic and low-proof options such as the Evening At Frost, built on Gnista Wormwood and house-made spiced orange syrup. Set among the grand Victorian mansions of Cathedral Hill, the restaurant pairs its no-proof list with the same atmospheric, white-tablecloth setting that has made it a special-occasion destination for decades. description: Wallace Dry Goods is Ardmore's first fully non-alcoholic bottle shop, opened in early 2024 by owner Robin Cummiskey on the Main Line at 1 West Lancaster Avenue. Styled like a traditional bottle shop — shelves of "whiskey," wine, gin, and mixers — it stocks zero liquor; everything is alcohol-free. The shop sells NA spirits, beer, wine, cider, mixers, bitters, syrups, and ready-to-drink cans, plus barware, so non-drinkers have the same tools to build cocktails at home. Brands carried include Ghia, Ritual Zero Proof, Cut Above, Seedlip, Lyre's, Athletic Brewing, Abstinence, and Mingle Mocktails. A daily in-store tasting bar pours rotating samples and the occasional craft mocktail, and the shop hosts classes and events. Wallace Dry Goods was named Best Non-Alcoholic Bottle Shop in Philadelphia Magazine's 2024 Best of Philly awards.

name: Walrus Rodeo
description: Walrus Rodeo is a wood-fired restaurant on NE 2nd Avenue in Little Haiti, which describes its own cooking as contemporary wood-fired and is emphatic that it is not just a pizzeria. Dinner is the only service, 5:30pm to 10:30pm seven nights a week. Its documented alcohol-free build is the Rodeo Limonada, which blends strawberry, orgeat and lime — a short, straightforward drink that leans on the almond weight of the orgeat rather than on syrup. RESIDENT covered it in December 2025 and described the approach as easygoing and well made. It is one of the few documented alcohol-free drinks north of the Design District.
signatureDrinks: Rodeo Limonada (strawberry, orgeat, lime)

name: Warka Coffee

description: Warka Coffee is a fully alcohol-free Ethiopian specialty coffee house that opened in August 2025 at 500 New Jersey Avenue NW, in the National Association of Realtors building at E Street, a few blocks from Union Station and the Capitol. It is named after the warka tree, a symbol of shelter and gathering in Ethiopia, and the business runs the whole chain itself: long-term relationships with smallholder growers in Yirgacheffe and Sidama, direct importing, roasting at its own Rockville, Maryland roastery, and serving here. The cafe pours single-origin Ethiopian coffee sorted by taste rather than region - floral and clean, fruit-forward, chocolate and full, espresso - alongside signature drinks, breakfast and lunch. A second service point operates inside Georgetown Law. No alcohol is served.

name: Watch Hill Proper
description: Watch Hill Proper is a bourbon bar and restaurant in Norton Commons, the walkable development in Prospect north-east of Louisville, and it claims the largest bourbon collection in the country alongside the most extensive American whiskey menu it can assemble. That is exactly the sort of room a non-drinker usually writes off — which is why it matters that it also keeps Spiritless Kentucky 74, the non-alcoholic bourbon made in Louisville, on the menu. The bar runs later than the kitchen, to 11pm midweek and midnight at weekends, and a Tuesday night live music series gives the room a reason to be in it that is not the whiskey list.

name: Water Witch Tiki
description: Water Witch Tiki is a 21-and-over tiki bar in the Starland District, a dark, densely decorated room on Bull Street that takes its rum programme seriously and applies the same thinking to the drinks without any. Its menu carries a standing Non-Alcoholic section of four builds at $8 to $9, made with the same house syrups, shrubs and proprietary bitters as everything else — chamomile and green cardamom, tamarind-mango-mint purée, blueberry shrub, a Sichuan-hibiscus bitters the bar makes itself. Three Athletic Brewing alcohol-free beers sit in the cans list at $7. It opens at 5pm midweek and 11am on Friday and Saturday, and closes on Sundays.

name: Watershed Pub & Kitchen
description: Watershed Pub & Kitchen is a family-owned neighbourhood pub at 10104 3rd Ave NE in Northgate, opened in 2014 by Ben Curran, who wanted a pub for a district that had none and deliberately skipped the dark-bar-and-fried-food model for something family-friendly, fresh and local. Its non-alcoholic section is one of the more developed in Seattle: two zero-proof cocktails — The Honey Pot ($14, Empress 1908 0.0 indigo, lemon, honey) and the Kava Kalada ($8) — plus Best Day kölsch and west coast IPA at $7 each (both under 0.5% ABV) and house specialty drinks including a quinine cold brew ($9) and a peach-rosemary-thyme lemonade ($8). IMPORTANT: the Kava Kalada contains real kava, and the menu separately sells a Goldfinch ginger kava cocktail neat ($10) and an Ablis CBD drink ($9). All three are marked 21+ but carry no printed dosage. It is one of the most accessible venues we list: an ADA-accessible facility with limited-mobility drop-off from 3rd Ave NE, highchairs and boosters, a dog-friendly patio, free parking, and plant-based, gluten-free and alcohol-free options stated as standard.

description: Watr at the 1 Rooftop is the eighteenth-floor bar and restaurant on top of 1 Hotel South Beach, looking straight out over the Atlantic from Collins Avenue. It stays open to midnight on weeknights and 2am on Friday and Saturday, which makes it usable as a late destination rather than a sunset stop. The documented alcohol-free build is the Sunburnt on South Beach, mixing coconut water with mango, lime, mint and Fever-Tree ginger beer — long, hydrating and built for the heat rather than for imitation of a cocktail. The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau calls it one of Miami Beach's most refreshing ginger beer drinks and highlights the hotel's sustainability-led design.

name: Watts & Ward
description: Watts & Ward is a below-ground prohibition-themed cocktail lounge off Moore Square on South Blount Street, and its menu carries a "Zero Proof Cocktails" section headed "all the craftsmanship, none of the spirits". Four builds at $10 run across Mock One's non-alcoholic rum, tequila, gin and whiskey — a Faux Tai with lime and orgeat, My Little Secret on strawberry and lemon, Après Tout against a blueberry shrub and tonic, Village of the Deer with grapefruit and honey — and, more useful than the list itself, the bar will substitute Mock One for the spirit in any house cocktail for $5. That turns a four-drink section into most of the full menu. Open Tuesday to Saturday from four until two in the morning, Sunday from two until midnight. name: Wendigo Tea Co.
description: Wendigo Tea Co. is a fully alcohol-free (and substance-free) tea bar tucked beside Findlay Market inside Findlay Launch, the market's storefront accelerator. It's the second location for the Cincinnati company founded in 2013 by Sky White, keyboardist of the rock band Foxy Shazam, who fell for rare loose-leaf tea while touring the world. The Elm Street tea bar pours hot and iced service plus what the shop calls "absurd crafted teas," alongside retail tins of Wendigo's curated, organic, hard-to-source blends — signatures like Bigfoot Black Tea, FireBird Chai, Nessy Jasmine Tea and Siren Throat Health Herbal Tea. Tastings are free, the room is casual, and there is zero alcohol on the menu. A separate appointment-only tasting room operates on Warsaw Avenue in East Price Hill.

name: The Westside Local
description: The Westside Local is a farm-to-table New American restaurant that has anchored Kansas City's Westside neighborhood since 2009, set in a historic exposed-brick, wood-beam space with a grapevine-covered beer garden. Known for seasonal, locally sourced cooking, it also keeps a small but thoughtful named non-alcoholic drink list that runs alongside its beer and wine program. The zero-proof menu, highlighted in a 2023 KCUR guide to KC's mocktail scene, includes house-built drinks like the Aesop (red bell pepper and mango shrub, chamoy, Hellfire Bitters, Perrier, lime) and the Mother Goose (passion fruit, carrot juice, coconut water, lime, salted toasted coconut), plus a dealcoholized sparkling option, the Secco, made with Germany's Fritz Müller alcohol-removed semi-sparkling white. Guests are encouraged to ask their server about the mocktail menu.

There is no a la carte and no printed menu — the dishes shift day to day with the weather, the tides and the harvest. Crucially for non-drinkers, the wine flight has a genuine equal: a fully non-alcoholic juice flight built in-house from pressed and fermented juices, kombucha and botanical infusions, matched course by course. It is one of the UK's benchmark alcohol-free pairings, treated with the same seriousness as the cellar.

name: Whisler's
description: Whisler's is an award-winning craft cocktail bar on the historic East Sixth Street in Austin, opened in a hundred-year-old building that was originally a 1916 grain mill. The interior is candlelit and rustic-chic — described variously as "Gothic" and "castle-like" — with a large back patio, mist system for hot Texas summers, and palo santo greeting guests at the door. The cocktail program emphasizes handcrafted drinks made with fresh, high-quality ingredients. Mezcaleria Tobala, a weekend-only Oaxacan mezcal bar, sits upstairs. Award-winning Thai food from the Thai-Kun food truck is available on the patio (Thai-Kun was named to Bon Appétit's Hot 10 Best New Restaurants list in 2014). Non-alcoholic options are mentioned positively in recent reviews, though specific NA drinks are not publicly named.

name: Wicked Rabbit
description: Wicked Rabbit is a downtown Omaha cocktail bar open 5pm to 2am every single day of the week, and it runs the most locally rooted alcohol-free list in the city. Its zero-proof drinks are built on Sandhills Elixir — a small-batch range of non-alcoholic spirits made in Valentine, Nebraska from native prairie botanicals and water drawn from the Ogallala Aquifer — in drinks including the Sandhills Spiced Sour, alongside a Sunset in Wonderland and a Blushing Cow. Using a Nebraska-made zero-proof spirit rather than an imported one is a genuine point of difference, and it means the non-alcoholic order is as regional as the whiskey list. Harney Street puts it inside the walkable downtown cluster.

name: Wicked Sisters
description: Wicked Sisters is a neighbourhood tavern at 3845 Falls Road on the edge of Hampden and Woodberry, in the building that was McCabe's until a fire closed it. Charlie Gjerde took the space over in June 2015 and reopened it in late October 2016, naming it for his wife Lori Gjerde and Carrie Podles, who are real-life sisters. The white-brick, 150-seat room serves comfort food without pretension — Baltimore Magazine noted there is no concerted attempt to pass for healthy. Its drinks list carries two non-alcoholic headings. "Non-Alcoholic Spirit-Free Cocktails" holds Peachy Keen ($12, Lyre's NA tequila, Crodino, peach purée, lime, pineapple), Sunset Fizz ($13, Mionetto NA prosecco, Crodino, Mionetto spirit-free aperitivo, blood orange) and Gingerberry Snap ($11, Lyre's NA tequila, blueberry syrup, ginger, lime, soda). A second heading, "Non-Alcoholic Spikeable Options", lists a seasonal Wicked Lemonade at $8 and a Caramel Apple Mule at $9, either of which can take a spirit for $5 — useful for a mixed table. Owner Jay Sanders was named a James Beard semifinalist for Outstanding Professional in Cocktail Service in 2025 — the first Beard recognition for a Shawnee bar — and Bon Appétit named Wild Child one of the best new bars in America in 2024. Its zero-proof programme is the deepest in the Kansas City metro and unusually self-sufficient: Sanders distils his own non-alcoholic spirits in house, having worked out it was cheaper than buying them in. Nine drinks run $10 to $12, including an N/A Negroni built at full strength and then stripped of alcohol by atmospheric distillation, Up & At Em (Aplos Arise, clarified green apple, malic acid, pandan leaf), Bearing Fruit (de-alcoholised alpine liqueur, kiwi, Seedlip Garden, lime), Best Medicine (smoked-tea-infused NA ginger liqueur, local pear, maple foam) and an N/A Espresso Martini on espresso-infused non-alcoholic amaro. name: Wild Heaven Beer
description: Wild Heaven Beer was founded in 2010 by Georgia natives Nick Purdy and Eric Johnson, making it one of the state's earliest craft breweries. After opening its flagship in Avondale Estates in 2014, the company launched this West End location in late 2019 inside the Lee+White development, directly on the Atlanta BeltLine's Southwest Trail. The 21,000-square-foot brewery and restaurant pours its own craft beer, housemade cocktails, and Georgia farm wines, with food and coffee on site. For non-drinkers, Wild Heaven brews its own zero-proof option: Near Wild Heaven Non-Alcoholic IPA (0.5% ABV), poured on draft alongside the full-strength lineup. Made with Trident, Centennial, and El Dorado hops for grapefruit, pine, and citrus notes, it is also 99.9% gluten-free. Copresident and brewmaster Eric Johnson and head brewer Josh Franks developed the beer, which Atlanta Magazine highlighted in 2025.

The plant-filled room works as a specialty coffee bar by day, pouring beans roasted with Heights roaster Tenfold Coffee, and becomes a full bar at night alongside an in-house "Bud Bar" stocked with hemp-derived CBD products. Its drink program was created by Laurie Harvey and Kris Sowell of Ladies of Libation and centers on hemp-infused elixirs: the Pink Loco with raspberry, coconut, citrus and mint; the coffee-based Skywalker OG; and Marfa Days with hibiscus, Topo Chico, citrus and tropical fruit. Readers avoiding all intoxicants should note these carry 20mg of full-spectrum CBD, and the venue will not mix CBD with alcohol. The Montrose second location has closed.

Its bar prints three named mocktails as a fixed part of the drinks list: a Spicy Sage Lemonade of freshly squeezed lemon with jalapeño and organic sage leaves, a caramelised Pineapple Mojito with fresh orange, organic mint and soda, and a Blackberry Limeade built on muddled blackberries with fresh lime and simple syrup. All three are constructed from produce rather than mixers, which is what distinguishes a restaurant that has thought about the category from one that keeps a bottle of grenadine.

name: Wilder
description: Wilder is a three-story, 150-seat restaurant, bar, and private-event space that opened in March 2022 in Rittenhouse, inside the former Philadelphia Academy of Social Dance building at 2009 Sansom Street. It was founded by husband-and-wife team Brett Naylor and Nicole Barrick, who designed the eclectic interior and brought on executive chef Bob Truitt (formerly of Corton, Buddakan, and Morimoto). Because Barrick and Naylor are both sober, Wilder maintains one of the most developed non-alcoholic drink programs in Philadelphia, with zero-proof cocktails on both the regular and happy-hour menus, each around $10. Named alcohol-free options include Doctor's Orders (lapsang souchong, ginger, honey), One Last Question (sarsaparilla, vanilla, lime), and Top Shelf Bubbles (a spritz of orange, lime, and TÖST NA Sparkling). Visit Philadelphia and Philadelphia Magazine have both spotlighted the venue's zero-proof offerings.

Its non-alcoholic list is short but built with the same technique as the cocktails: Westword describes the El Corazón as melding coconut, lemon, orgeat and hoja santa, the Mexican herb whose flavour runs close to root beer, and the Padre Pio as combining chamomile honey, lavender and lemon. A sparkling green tea rounds out the list. The pairing of a hotel restaurant with an outdoor-focused hospitality group means the room draws a mixed crowd, and the drinks are priced and presented alongside the full-proof list rather than tucked away. Wildflower serves dinner Monday to Saturday and closes on Sundays.

Zero-proof builds lean on NA spirits and house ingredients — fresh juices, shrubs, kombuchas, and homemade extracts — including a Negroni AF (NA Ritual gin, melati amaro, house aperitivo, orange), a Love & Lavender (NA Ritual gin, lavender, butterfly pea tea, Wilderton citrus, fee foam), an NA Spicy Pineapple Margarita (jalapeño-infused NA tequila, pineapple, lime, Tajín), and a Serenity Spritz. description: Wildwood Kitchen & Bar at Pavilions builds its blood orange margarita on CleanCo alcohol-free tequila rather than leaving the spirit out, which is the difference between a margarita and a limeade. There is also a lychee Moscow mule mocktail and Heineken 0.0 for anyone who wants a beer in hand. Stocking a named non-alcoholic tequila is a purchasing decision with only one purpose — serving people who are not drinking — and it means the drink keeps the agave note that makes a margarita taste like one. It is out at Pavilions in Arden-Arcade rather than downtown, and opens from 10am at weekends for brunch.

Billing itself as "Nevada's only licensed kava bar" and the "unofficial Las Vegas Star Trek headquarters," it serves traditional Pacific Island kava in shells, quads, jugs and Tanoa bowls alongside botanical specialty teas and functional, non-alcoholic mocktails (no alcohol is served). name: Wooden City
description: Wooden City is the Birmingham room of a small restaurant group that also runs in Chattanooga and Tacoma, on Morris Avenue in the restored warehouse block downtown, serving wood-fired pizza and small plates seven nights a week from 5pm to 10pm. Its sibling in Chattanooga carries five separate zero-proof drinks on the printed menu, which is the deepest restaurant list in that city; the group's house approach to the category is the reason this room is listed here. The Morris Avenue setting — cobbles, iron canopies, no through traffic — makes it one of the more pleasant places downtown to eat without drinking.

name: Wooden City
description: Wooden City is a downtown Chattanooga restaurant on Broad Street serving wood-fired pizza and small plates, with a bar that carries five separate zero-proof drinks on the menu — the deepest printed alcohol-free list of any restaurant in the city. The one worth ordering is the Fizz, built on berries, coconut cream, cinnamon, nutmeg and soda, which uses warm baking spices and a fat to give an alcohol-free drink the weight most of them lack. It serves dinner seven nights a week from 4:30pm, running to 9:30pm and 10pm at weekends, with a daily happy hour from 4pm to 5:30pm.

Queen City Nerve readers voted it Best Brewery in 2024. Its taproom lists a Non-Alcoholic section holding an N/A Beer at $6, Walker Brothers kombucha at $6 and sodas from $2, plus a rotating shelf of non-alcoholic cans from Untitled Art and Athletic Brewing. IMPORTANT: three further items on that same Non-Alcoholic list — Five Flowers ($8), 420-Rita ($14) and Blueberry Yum Yum ($14) — are hemp-derived THC and CBD drinks rather than plain mocktails; Five Flowers is a THC/CBD cooler brand, and the bar's "Hightails" are built with a Calmezzi THC/CBD elixir. They contain no alcohol, which is why they appear there, but anyone avoiding intoxicants should order the N/A beer, kombucha, soda or coffee instead.

All its beers are gluten-reduced. Its non-alcoholic offer is broader than most taprooms': a house hop water at 0.0% built on Centennial and Au Tropical hops, canned non-alcoholic beer from Untitled Art and Deschutes, and — the part worth knowing — specialty non-alcoholic cocktails including a shrub seltzer, a hibiscus margarita and a dill seltzer, each of which can be ordered at 0% rather than only in its alcoholic version.

name: Worthy Brewing Company
description: Worthy's Hop Quencher is hop water — hop aroma and bitterness brewed without alcohol, calories or sugar — and it has become a warm-weather staple in Bend for exactly the moment a full beer is too much. The east-side brewery pairs it with a hop garden, an observatory and a big patio, open to 11pm at weekends.

name: Wren House Brewing Co.
description: A beloved neighborhood brewery on N 24th Street in central Phoenix, Wren House is known for some of Arizona's best IPAs — its flagship hazy, Spellbinder, took a Gold Medal in the Juicy/Hazy IPA category at the 2020 Great American Beer Festival. It also brews a zero-proof Non-Alcoholic Spellbinder at 0.5% ABV, built on the same Citra, Mosaic and Cascade hops with increased kettle hopping for bitterness and a dialled-in dry-hop ratio aimed at tangerine citrus. Axios Phoenix named it among the local non-alcoholic beers worth seeking out for Dry January. Note that the standard Spellbinder is alcoholic — ask specifically for the NA version.

name: Writers Bar

description: Tucked into the front corner of Raffles Hotel Singapore's Grand Lobby, Writers Bar runs a genuine printed list of eight non-alcoholic cocktails served in proper stemware. Bar manager Konstantine Arzumanov's zero-proof builds include the Emin Pasha, an Arabic-influenced old-fashioned of Seedlip Spice 94, miso, orgeat, gum and demerara syrups and orange-blossom water, and the Strike Slip, a clarified serve of Lyre's White Cane, sencha, soursop and calamansi. The NA drinks are composed with the same care as the bar's literary-themed alcoholic cocktails, not treated as an afterthought.

Alongside its always-changing house brews and roughly a dozen guest drafts, the inclusive beverage program lists meads, wine, non-alcoholic brews and "alcohol alternatives" so non-drinkers have real options. It bills itself as Charleston's only 21+ brewery, with a large yard where leashed dogs and kids are welcome.

name: Yacht Club
description: Yacht Club is a 2021-founded neighborhood bar in Denver's Cole neighborhood, co-owned by McLain Hedges and Mary Alison Wright. The 'anti-club club' concept sits at the crossroads of upscale cocktail haunt, natural wine bar, and beloved dive bar — with hot dogs and dim-sum-style snacks rounding out the food offering. The bar debuted on the World's 50 Best Bars list in 2023 and won the Ketel One Sustainable Bar Award at North America's 50 Best Bars the same year, recognized for sustainability initiatives including fermentation programs that extend the shelf life of seasonal ingredients. The non-alcoholic program is featured on the menu under 'soft bangers' and has been covered in detail by Visit Denver's December 2025 spirit-free roundup (the Paradise Waits — green pineapple, Lyre's white cane, celery, lime, curry leaf) and Sober Bars Finder's Denver mocktails feature (the Friends In Low Places — Three Spirit Nightcap, Late Harvest Verjus, coffee, N.O.T. Chocolate Vinegar). The split-based, wine-forward cocktail philosophy that defines the alcoholic menu extends to the NA program: thoughtful, ingredient-driven, and far from the standard mocktail playbook.

Its non-alcoholic side is genuine if moderate: alcohol-free beers from Melbourne's Hop Nation and zero-alcohol spirits from Four Pillars sit alongside AF spritzes, RTDs and mocktails. The riverfront room, all-local produce and skyline views make it an easy low-proof stop rather than a dedicated zero-proof destination. It is a floating bar on the Yarra, pouring Victorian-made drinks through a partnership with Drink Victorian, with non-alcoholic beer, cocktails and alternative wines all on the list.

name: Yellow Door Taqueria
description: The original Yellow Door Taqueria is in Lower Mills, the mill village at the southern end of Dorchester Avenue where Boston meets Milton, and it is the room that made the group. Cali-Mex food, a margarita-led bar and a dining room that runs to 11pm most nights and midnight Thursday through Saturday. The alcohol-free list is the same three named drinks the group pours across its restaurants, all $10 and made with fresh juice rather than a mix: Mango Vibes Only with mango, pineapple, coconut, agave and lime; Stitzer's Paloma with a house rosemary syrup, fresh grapefruit and lime juices and soda; and Sober Baddie with pineapple and hibiscus, vanilla, toasted coconut, lime and soda. Jarritos are $4.

Three named drinks are $10, all hand-squeezed rather than poured from a mix: Mango Vibes Only combines mango, pineapple, coconut, agave and lime; Stitzer's Paloma uses a house rosemary syrup with fresh grapefruit and lime juices and soda; and Sober Baddie layers pineapple and hibiscus with vanilla, toasted coconut, lime and soda. Jarritos in assorted flavours are $4.

Four alcohol-free cocktails hold a marked "(N/A)" spot on the menu at $10 — the Belly Bump, Piña Co-Nada, Toothless Tiger and Jungle Feather — drawing on the hydrosol "botanic waters" Wiggins developed so alcohol-free drinks keep real flavor and mouthfeel. address: 18006 Park Row Blvd, Suite 100, Houston, TX 77084

The signature drink is the areekano: a double espresso poured over chilled water, sweetened with a house-made syrup and topped with cream, cheddar cheese, honey and black sesame seeds, a translation of the Yemeni date-and-cheese dessert areeka into a cup. Alongside it sit a cafe de olla latte, an Adeni chai brewed with a house spice blend and piloncillo, and single-origin Yemeni pour-overs from Al-Haimah and East Haraz. description: Yeppa & Co. Beltline is an Italian bar and restaurant on Auburn Avenue in the Old Fourth Ward, directly on the BeltLine's Eastside Trail, from Pietro Gianni and Stephen Peterson of Storico Fresco and Forza Storico. The menu takes its cue from Rimini on the Adriatic coast, and the drinks list carries a zero-proof section that fits the aperitivo format properly rather than awkwardly. The house Spritz swaps prosecco and bitter liqueur for Lapo's non-alcoholic aperitif with soda, and Amore e Passione runs Floreale non-alcoholic aperitivo with passion fruit, lemon and soda. There is a large covered patio with fire-pit tables and outdoor seating alongside the trail, so the alcohol-free order works in the same setting as everyone else's.

name: Yeppa & Co. Buckhead
description: Yeppa & Co. Buckhead is the Buckhead Village outpost of the Rimini-inspired Italian bar and trattoria from Pietro Gianni and Stephen Peterson of Y Hospitality, and it keeps longer hours than the BeltLine original — open from 11:30am seven days a week and to midnight on Friday and Saturday. The room is a Formula One-themed bar and dining space in the Buckhead Village District. The same zero-proof section runs here: a Spritz rebuilt on Lapo's non-alcoholic aperitif with soda and no prosecco, and Amore e Passione made with Floreale non-alcoholic aperitivo, passion fruit, lemon and soda. Because the kitchen opens at lunch, this is one of the more reliable places in Buckhead to get a properly-built alcohol-free aperitivo in the middle of the day.

description: Yixing Xuan Teahouse is a Chinese teahouse and tea merchant at 78 Tanjong Pagar Road, founded in 1989 by Vincent Low, a former banker who came to tea through a friend, and run today with his daughter Charlene. It serves no alcohol at all. The tea menu runs to more than thirty Chinese and Taiwanese teas brewed gongfu-style at the table, from a S$8.50 Beauty of the East oolong the house calls its signature to three grades of Da Hong Pao, aged Gong Mei white tea and Feng Huang Dan Cong, with dim sum as pairing. Tea appreciation workshops run regularly and the shop sells around fifty loose-leaf teas and teaware. It opens until 9.30pm on Fridays and Saturdays.

Three named builds anchor it: She's Blushin', made with spiced rich cranberry, lime juice, mint leaves and club soda; Manila Bae, which puts pineapple juice with tamarind syrup, lime juice and citrus syrup; and Stamped Strawberry, muddled strawberry with lime, basil and club soda. Fever-Tree mixers are stocked for simpler orders.

Beverage director Ashley Sarkis built a dedicated mocktail menu anchored by premium NA spirits including Seedlip Garden and Amass Riverin, earning Yunta a spot on Yelp's top 25 mocktail programs in the U.S. in 2024 — the only North Carolina restaurant on that list. Guests can choose from named zero-proof cocktails like The Gardener and Isle del Sol alongside NA beer, making it one of Charlotte's strongest NA options in a full-service restaurant setting.

name: Z Tiki Kava Bar
description: Z Tiki is an alcohol-free tiki lounge in the Hourglass District, and it is a night venue in the full sense — closed Monday and Tuesday, open from 5pm midweek and from 3pm at weekends, running to 2am on Friday and Saturday. The room is fitted with soft lighting, plush seating and natural wood, and the entertainment is real rather than incidental: a blacklight pool table, karaoke every Friday from 10pm, and stand-up comedy nights. Kava is served at a notably low price point for the city. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: kratom is on the menu alongside it. Kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries dependence and withdrawal risk that kava does not, so order deliberately. (As of late September 2026 Z Tiki appeared to be temporarily closed, and the bar had not posted on Instagram since May, with no reason given — check before you go.)

Each January the bar layers in Dry January specials such as La Mora di Zanti, Marg No Rita, Panoma and Tiki Good. Rather than coffee or cocktails, the lounge is built around ethically sourced specialty kava — the calming Pacific-island root beverage — plus nootropic and hemp-derived botanical drinks, traditional teas, and snacks. It positions itself as a calm, mindful place to gather, read, or connect, marketing kava as "a social beverage without a next-day hangover," which makes it a genuine fit for sober and sober-curious guests. The menu blends prepared kava drinks served in traditional shells and bowls with espresso-style and tea options, plus sugar-free and dairy-free preparations and build-your-own blends. It carries a 4.9-star Yelp rating across 100-plus reviews, with praise for its sourcing, knowledgeable staff, and atmosphere.

description: Zén holds three MICHELIN stars in a restored Bukit Pasoh shophouse, and it runs one of the most serious non-alcoholic pairings in Asia. The zero-proof programme is priced at around S$250 per person — set against the wine flight rather than discounted below it — and it is rebuilt whenever the kitchen changes its menu, so it tracks the food course by course instead of recycling a fixed set of juices. The drinks are constructed rather than poured: a sparkling aperitif of heirloom tomatoes and red plums, a Peach with Pepper made from aged peaches juiced and fermented with oxalis stems, and a white wine alternative of fermented quince, apple, pear and lemon finished with toasted pecan and walnut water.

Her non-alcoholic menu is titled Zero Judgement, and the named pour from it is Butterflies on the Rail — butterfly pea flower, lemon, blackberries and an egg white foam that gives it the texture of a proper sour. The restaurant serves from 6:30am to midnight seven days a week, and a separate 32-seat room, Bar Z, pours the same drinks list.

name: ZERO ZERO
description: ZERO ZERO is a natural wine shop in Miami's Little River neighborhood, opened in June 2024 by Nicole and Adam Darnell, the couple behind Boxelder Craft Beer Market. Alongside its organic, biodynamic, and low-intervention wines, the shop houses "Zero Proof," a dedicated non-alcoholic micro-shop that the owners bill as "Miami's first and only retailer specializing in nonalcoholic beverage offerings." Rather than mixing drinks on site, Zero Proof is a walk-in bottle shop: the focus is "nootropic, adaptogenic, and functional beverages, as well as interesting offerings that feature a slug of flavor," spanning ready-to-drink spritzers and non-alcoholic wines, tequilas, and vodkas to take home. The Darnells frame the concept around inclusivity — providing those who don't drink with, in Adam Darnell's words, "equally exciting and delicious options." The shop also stocks goods and tinned fish, with parking behind the building.

name: Zhug
description: Zhug opened on Cedar Road in the Cedar Fairmount district of Cleveland Heights in 2020, the eastern-Mediterranean concept from Douglas Katz — one of the most influential chefs in Cleveland over the past twenty-five years, and the man behind Fire in Shaker Square before it — now operated with Todd Thompson under the Edgewater Hospitality banner. The cooking runs through hummus, wood-grilled vegetables and mezze built around the Yemeni chilli-herb sauce the restaurant is named for, and the dining room does dinner six nights a week, closing Sundays. Its drinks list gives non-alcoholic cocktails a permanent place in its own numbering rather than a separate mocktail box: two N/A builds on Ritual and Monday zero-proof spirits, a rotating pair of house gazoz — Israeli-style fruit-syrup sodas — plus non-alcoholic beer and sparkling rosé.

name: Zig Zag Café
description: Zig Zag Café is a landmark cocktail bar at 1501 Western Avenue on the Pike Place Market hillclimb, open since 1999 and housed in the 1910 Fix-Madore Building. It is internationally recognised as a pioneer of the classic cocktail revival, and it is where bartender Murray Stenson rediscovered the Last Word — a Prohibition-era drink that had fallen out of memory after the Second World War, which he found in a 1951 book and put back on a menu, from where it spread to New York, San Francisco, London and eventually everywhere. Its own description of the room is accurate: a low, sultry glow over the dining room, a verdant patio, and a house soundtrack of jazz, cumbia and highlife. Its non-alcoholic drinks are printed under "Zero Proof Drinks" at a flat $15: Daybreak (Yu No non-alcoholic gin, lemon, pineapple cordial, Giffard non-alcoholic spritz liqueur), Jardin Sauvage (mint, lime, ginger, Midnight Sun non-alcoholic aperitif), Rose-Colored Glasses (Roots non-alcoholic bianco vermouth, grenadine, grapefruit, bitters, non-alcoholic sparkling wine) and Dark Horse (Dr. Zero Zero non-alcoholic amaro, lime cordial, Giffard aperitif syrup). Open 5pm to midnight daily; 21+. Live jazz Sunday to Wednesday.

name: Zola
description: Zola is a live-music bar and restaurant on Main Avenue in downtown Spokane, a room built out of salvage and oddities with bands most nights. Its mocktail list is the most deliberately constructed in the city, and the reason is personal: head bartender Sheldon Moore expanded it after getting sober, and holds the alcohol-free drinks to the same standards as the cocktails — measured pours, proper technique and real non-alcoholic spirits, with Figlia among his preferred bases. His stated aim is drinks with some bitterness and structure rather than another sweet soda, which is the complaint most non-drinkers have about bar menus. Open from 4pm, to midnight midweek and 1am on Friday and Saturday, closed Sunday.

name: Zunzibar
description: Zunzibar is the coastal American restaurant and bar attached to Zunzi's on Drayton Street, with a large outdoor patio, live music programming and a dog-friendly policy, open from 11am to 11pm and later at weekends. Its bar keeps a mocktail list in regular rotation, and the house standard is the Pineapple Express — built on Ritual Zero Proof's non-alcoholic rum alternative with peach purée, pineapple, almond milk, cane sugar and lemon — which staff describe as the most-requested alcohol-free drink in the room. The long daily hours make it one of the easier places in the Historic District to get a considered zero-proof drink at lunchtime.

name: Zydeco Kitchen & Cocktails
description: Zydeco does elevated Southern-leaning comfort food in downtown Bend with a strong zero-proof lineup alongside its house cocktails, and it pours Crux's NØ MØ non-alcoholic IPA on the beer list — so both routes are covered for a non-drinker at dinner. Open daily from 4:30pm.
